A store to an entity's field, `=` or a compound one, `++` or `--`, evaluates the entity first, then the stored value, and makes the field's `ADDRESS` last, right before its `STOREP_*`: `QCC_PR_RefExpression` reads the left side as a reference, `QCC_PR_BuildRef(refbuf, REF_FIELD, QCC_RefToDef(lhs, true), ...)`, which loads the entity but not the field, then reads the right side, `rhsr = QCC_PR_RefExpression (&rhsbuf, priority, ...)`, and `QCC_StoreSRefToRef` makes the address when it stores. For a compound store the field is read after the right side: on id's opcodes no `ops_ptr` row is valid, so `lhsd = QCC_RefToDef(lhsr, false);` loads it before the operator. So in `self.health = g();` and `self.health += g();` the call to `g` comes before the `ADDRESS`, and in the second before the `LOAD_F` of `health` too, where id's `qcc` makes the `ADDRESS` first (QC-17.3). The pinned FTEQCC (`-Tid`) writes `CALL0 ADDRESS STOREP_F` for the first, `CALL0 LOAD_F ADD_F ADDRESS STOREP_F` for the second, `LOAD_F ADD_F ADDRESS STOREP_F` for `self.health++;`, and `CALL0 ADDRESS STOREP_F` for `self.origin_x = g();` (FTE-9.4). A call in the right side that changes the field is thus seen by a compound store's read, and one that changes `self` by `self.health = g();`, whose `ADDRESS` reads `self` after the call, but not by `self.enemy.health = g();`, whose entity is loaded before it.
`a % b` is the floating-point remainder of `a` divided by `b`. The rerelease uses it on floats (`rerelease-mg1/horde.qc` `self.wave % 3`).
Division by zero follows FTEQCC's generated code; the exact result is fixed when P2-06 implements the lowering and is checked against the rerelease's runtime behaviour in the differential suite.

Progs encoding: `%` has no vanilla opcode, so FTEQCC emits a short sequence of vanilla float opcodes (a division, truncation and multiply-subtract). The exact statements are fixed by P2-06 and recorded in this section's vectors then.
`cond ? a : b` evaluates to `a` when `cond` is true (QC-19) and to `b` otherwise. The rerelease uses it, including nested (`rerelease-mg1/ai.qc`, `rerelease-mg1/misc_fx.qc`).
`a` and `b` must have the same type; that is the type of the whole expression.
Progs encoding: lowers to an `IFNOT` over the two arms storing into a shared temporary, over vanilla opcodes; no new opcode is used.

`?:` is read at FTEQCC's `TERNARY_PRIORITY`, the assignment priority, which is tighter than `&&` and `||`: without `flag_cpriority`, `QCC_PrioritiseOpcodes` sets `priority_class[PC_LOGICAND] = 7;`, `priority_class[PC_LOGICOR] = 7;`, `priority_class[PC_TERNARY] = 6;` and `priority_class[PC_STORE] = 6;`, and `QCC_PR_RefExpression` tries `if (priority == TERNARY_PRIORITY && QCC_PR_CheckToken ("?"))` on the operand it read at the priority below. The right operand of `=` is read at its own priority and that of `&&` and `||` at the one below theirs, so each reaches the `?` first: `x = a ? b : c` assigns the conditional, and `a && b ? c : d` is `a && (b ? c : d)`, as is `a || b ? c : d` with `||`. A comparison, `a == b ? c : d`, is the condition. Both arms are read at `TOP_PRIORITY` (`val = QCC_PR_Expression(TOP_PRIORITY, 0);` for the middle and `QCC_PR_Expression(TOP_PRIORITY, EXPR_DISALLOW_COMMA)` for the last), so a conditional in the last arm nests to the right, `a ? b : c ? d : e` is `a ? b : (c ? d : e)`, and the last arm takes `&&` and `=`. This differs from C, where `?:` is looser than `||`; FTEQCC takes the C order only with `flag_cpriority` (`priority_class[PC_TERNARY] = 12;`), which is not its default.
On an expression of type `vector`, `.x`, `.y` and `.z` name its first, second and third float. The rerelease uses `.z` as an lvalue (`rerelease-ctf/hook.qc` `offset.z *= -1`).
A member is a float lvalue when its base is an lvalue, so it may be assigned and used with a compound operator (FTE-6).
Progs encoding: a vector's three floats are consecutive globals (QC-21), so `v.x`, `v.y` and `v.z` are the global at the vector's offset, offset plus one and offset plus two; no new opcode is used.

A store to a component of an entity's vector field, `e.v.x = f` or `e.v[0] = f`, stores through `ADDRESS` of the component's own field `v_x` (QC-11.12) with `STOREP_F`; a compound assignment or increment reads it first by `LOAD_F` of that field. The component is never a copy of the loaded vector. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseRefArrayPointer` (`fieldarrayindex`, `type_floatfield`).
`const T name = value;` declares a named compile-time constant of type `T`. The rerelease uses it heavily for float and string constants (`rerelease-mg1/lights.qc`, `rerelease-mg3/defs.qc`).
A `const` is folded at compile time where it is used; it may initialise another `const` (`rerelease-mg1/lights.qc` `const float LightStyles_MAX = LightStyles.length - 1`).
Assigning to a `const` is an error.
Progs encoding: a `const` that is only folded contributes no global of its own; its value is emitted as an immediate (QC-20) wherever it is used.

`var T name = value;` declares a mutable global of type `T` with an initial value, the opposite of `const`. The rerelease uses `var float` (`rerelease-mg1/defs.qc` `var float num_players = 0;`, `rerelease-rogue/newplats.qc` `var float elvButnDir = 0;`).
It differs from a bare `T name = value;` global by overriding FTEQCC's default that an initialised global is constant, so the name may be assigned to later.
Progs encoding: a global definition (QC-21) with its initial value, writable at runtime; no new opcode is used.
`nosave T name;` declares a global that the engine's save and load of the globals skips. The rerelease uses `nosave float` (`rerelease-mg1/defs.qc` `nosave float load_flag;`).
It is otherwise an ordinary global of type `T` (QC-21). The qualifier affects only savegames, which id's VM spec does not cover, so its only compile-time effect is to be accepted.
Progs encoding: an ordinary global definition (QC-21); the `nosave` flag lives in FTEQCC's extended def flags, which a version 6 progs does not carry, so it is a front-end-only qualifier here.

`T name[N] = { ... };` and `T name[] = { ... };` (size inferred from the initialiser) declare an array of `T`. The rerelease declares string and struct (FTE-14) arrays with an inferred size (`rerelease-mg1/lights.qc` `const string LightStyles[] = {...}`, `rerelease-mg1/misc_corpses.qc` `poseInfo poses[] = { ... }`).
`name[i]` subscripts the array with a float index `i`. The rerelease uses both a loop variable and a field as the index (`rerelease-mg1/misc_corpses.qc` `poses[i].mdl`, `poses[self.style]`).
`name.length` is the element count as a float constant (`rerelease-mg1/lights.qc` `LightStyles.length`, `rerelease-mg1/misc_corpses.qc` `poses.length` in a `for` bound).

Progs encoding: FTEQCC lays an array out as consecutive globals and compiles a subscript to its array-access helper over vanilla opcodes (it does not use a version 7 feature for the rerelease, FTE-1.1). The exact lowering is fixed by P2-06 and recorded in this section's vectors then.

**Withdrawn** 2026-10-30: it held each value of an aggregate initialiser to a literal, where FTEQCC copies any constant's words; replaced by FTE-13.10. An array of `N` elements of `T` takes `N` times `T`'s words in consecutive globals from the definition's offset; a vector array makes no `_x`, `_y` or `_z` definitions. An aggregate initialiser writes element `k` at word `k` times the element's words, each value a literal (a frame macro is its number). A literal never shares an array's word as it shares an initialised constant's (QC-20.2). Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseDefs`, `QCC_PR_ParseInitializerType`.

A subscript by a constant whole number `i` within the array is the global at the array's offset plus `i` times the element's words, with no statement: `QCC_RefNeedsCalls` returns false when `QCC_SRef_EvalConst(ref->index)` ("can short it"). A constant index outside the array, which FTEQCC warns of and reads anyway (WARN_BOUNDS), is not lowered. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseRefArrayPointer`, `QCC_RefNeedsCalls`.

**Withdrawn** 2026-10-30: it said a store through a subscript by a value is not lowered, which FTE-13.11 now lowers; replaced by FTE-13.12. A subscript by a float value on the vanilla opcodes, which have no `LOADA`, `GLOAD` or `FETCH_GBL`, calls the array's getter, `ArrayGet*NAME` of type `T(float)` (`QCC_LoadFromArray`, `accel` 0). The index is in words: `MUL_F` by the element's words when they are not 1 (`else if (t->size != 1)`), then `ADD_F` of a struct member's word (an `ADD_F` of 0 is left out here). The argument is stored with `STORE_F` to the first parameter and `CALL1` made; a vector array's index is divided by 3 first (`OP_DIV_F ... 3`); a value of more than one word is read a word at a time, the index plus `w` for word `w`, each result stored with `STORE_F` to a temporary. A store through a subscript by a value needs the array's setter (`ArraySet*NAME`), which is not lowered. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_LoadFromArray`, `QCC_PR_ParseRefArrayPointer`.

A getter is made at the first subscript that needs it and emitted after every file (`QCC_PR_EmitArrayGetFunction` from `qccmain.c`'s loop over `ArrayGet*` definitions): its parameter `__indexg`; with bound checks on (`boundchecks` is a default flag) `IF` of `__indexg < 0` to the bounds error; then `QCC_PR_ArrayRecurseDivideRegular` over the slots (the elements times their words, or a vector array's elements with a stride of 3): one slot `min` is `LT __indexg, min+1`, `IFNOT` over the next statement and `RETURN` of its word; more are halved at `mid = min + (max-min)/2`, and when more than four remain a `LT __indexg, mid+1` with `IFNOT` past the lower half. The bounds error calls `error` with `sprintf("bounds check failed (0 <= %g < %g is false)\n", __indexg, slots)` when the program defines `sprintf`, else with `"bounds check failed\n"`; then the last slot is returned and `DONE` ends the function. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_EmitArrayGetFunction`, `QCC_PR_ArrayRecurseDivideRegular`.

`name.length` is lowered as a float immediate of the element count. FTEQCC makes it an `int` constant (`QCC_MakeIntConst(arraysize)`), which the vanilla opcodes take only converted to a float, so the value read is the same; a deliberate divergence in the immediate's type. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseRefArrayPointer`.

An array of `N` elements of `T` takes `N` times `T`'s words in consecutive globals from the definition's offset; a vector array makes no `_x`, `_y` or `_z` definitions. An aggregate initialiser writes element `k` at word `k` times the element's words, each value a constant whose words are copied (`const int *srcdata = (const void*)QCC_SRef_EvalConst(tmp);`): a literal (a frame macro is its number), a constant's name, or an expression that folds to one, so `const float f[2] = { IT_AXE, IT_SHOTGUN };` holds the two constants' values. A literal never shares an array's word as it shares an initialised constant's (QC-20.2). Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseDefs`, `QCC_PR_ParseInitializerType`, `QCC_PR_GenerateInitializerType`.

On the vanilla opcodes a store to an element by an index that is a value calls the array's setter, `ArraySet*NAME` of type `void(float, T)`, made at the first such store and emitted with the getters after every file in the order the two kinds were made (`QCC_StoreToArray`; `qccmain.c` emits each `ArraySet*` definition by `QCC_PR_EmitArraySetFunction`): the index in words is read as a getter's is (FTE-13.12), then the value; a vector array's index is divided by 3 (`OP_DIV_F`); then `STORE_F` of the index to the first parameter, the value to the second by its type, and `CALL2`. A null value is a float 0, or `'0 0 0'` for a vector array. The setter has the parameters `indexs___` and `value___`; with bound checks on, `LT_F index, 0` and `IF`, then `GE_F index, slots` and `IF`, both to the bounds error; then `QCC_PR_ArraySetRecurseDivide` over the slots: one slot `min` is `LT_F index, min+1`, `IFNOT` over three statements (`st->b.ofs = 3;`), `STORE_V` of the value for a vector array or else `STORE_F` to the slot's word, and `RETURN`; more are halved at `mid = min + (max-min)/2`, with `LT_F index, mid+1` and `IFNOT` past the lower half when more than four remain. The bounds error calls `error("bounds check failed\n")`, and `DONE` ends the function. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_StoreToArray`, `QCC_PR_EmitArraySetFunction`, `QCC_PR_ArraySetRecurseDivide`.

A subscript by a float value on the vanilla opcodes, which have no `LOADA`, `GLOAD` or `FETCH_GBL`, calls the array's getter, `ArrayGet*NAME` of type `T(float)` (`QCC_LoadFromArray`, `accel` 0). The index is in words: `MUL_F` by the element's words when they are not 1 (`else if (t->size != 1)`), then `ADD_F` of a struct member's word (an `ADD_F` of 0 is left out here). The argument is stored with `STORE_F` to the first parameter and `CALL1` made; a vector array's index is divided by 3 first (`OP_DIV_F ... 3`); a value of more than one word is read a word at a time, the index plus `w` for word `w`, each result stored with `STORE_F` to a temporary. A store through a subscript by a value calls the array's setter (FTE-13.11). Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_LoadFromArray`, `QCC_PR_ParseRefArrayPointer`.

`typedef struct { T1 f1; T2 f2; ... } Name;` defines an aggregate type `Name` with the named fields, in declaration order. The rerelease defines one (`rerelease-mg1/misc_corpses.qc` `typedef struct { string mdl; float frame; } poseInfo;`).
`Name v;` declares a value of the type; `v.f` reads field `f`. The rerelease reads struct fields through an array element (`poses[self.style].mdl`, `poses[i].frame`).
A struct initialiser `{ a, b }` gives its fields in order, and an array of structs (FTE-13) is initialised with one such brace group per element.

Progs encoding: a struct value occupies the sum of its fields' sizes in consecutive globals; field access is a fixed offset. No version 7 feature is used for the rerelease (FTE-1.1); the exact layout is fixed by P2-06 and recorded then.

A struct value takes its layout's words (FTEF-6.13), and `v.f` is the global at `v`'s offset plus the member's word, read and stored with no statement of its own; an array element's member `a[i].f` is the element's word plus the member's (FTE-13.6, FTE-13.12). Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseRefArrayPointer`.

A struct value stored to another of its type is copied a word group at a time, `STORE_V` for each three words and `STORE_F` for the rest. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_StoreToRef`.

A struct's aggregate initialiser `{ a, b }` writes each member's value at its word in order, an array of structs one brace group per element (FTE-13.10). Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseInitializerType`.

`enum { A, B, C };` declares named float constants starting at 0 and increasing by one, like a sequence of `const float` (FTE-10). The rerelease uses the bare form and the typed forms `enum : int { ... }` and `enum class Name : int { ... }` (`rerelease-mg1/lights.qc`, `rerelease-mg3/defs.qc`, `rerelease-hipnotic/defs.qc`).

An explicit value `A = n` sets the running value; the next unvalued name is `n + 1`. QuakeC floats hold these, so `: int` and `enum class` names resolve to the same float constants; the `: int` and `class` are accepted and otherwise ignored for a version 6 target.
Progs encoding: each name is a folded float constant (FTE-10.4); an `enum` contributes no global of its own.

`enum Name { ... }` also names a type, `Name`, which declares parameters and variables of the enum: `QCC_PR_ParseEnum` reads the name (`name = QCC_PR_ParseName();`) and makes it a type (`enumtype = QCC_PR_NewType(name, basetype->type, true);`). The rerelease declares `enum UpgradeType { ... }` and `float GetUpgradeAmount(UpgradeType Type)` (`rerelease-mg3/defs.qc`, `rerelease-mg3/mg3_upgrades.qc`).

Each item of an `enum` is a constant global made in the order the items are written and initialised with the item's value. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseEnum`.

A named enum's type stands for its base type, and a typedef's name for its type, so a parameter `UpgradeType t` is a float: `QCC_PR_NewType(name, basetype->type, true)`. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseEnum`.

An `enum : int` item read where the vanilla opcodes take a float is the float its value converts to, C's `(float)` of the integer (`QCC_SupplyConversion` of a constant makes the converted constant). Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_SupplyConversion`.

A number literal initialising an `int` or `unsigned` global is the integer C's conversion of the float gives (`QCC_SupplyConversion` of a constant), not the float's bits. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_SupplyConversion`.

`#pragma name args` is a compiler directive. The rerelease uses `#pragma warning disable F317` and `#pragma warning enable F317` (`rerelease-mg1/misc_corpses.qc`), which turn one FTEQCC warning off and on around a block.

A `#pragma` this compiler does not recognise is accepted and ignored with a warning, so unknown build-time hints do not stop a compile. `#pragma warning` is recognised and adjusts whether the named diagnostic is reported.
`#pragma` produces no tokens and no progs output; it affects only diagnostics and the build.

`rettype name(params)` declares `name` with the function type `rettype(params)`: after the name `QCC_PR_ParseDefs` reads `if (QCC_PR_CheckToken("("))` ... `type = QCC_PR_ParseFunctionType(false, type);`. The type is the one `rettype(params) name` declares, so a C-style definition and a vanilla prototype (`void() InitLightStyles;` in `rerelease-mg3/world.qc`) are the same function (QC-11.5).

**Withdrawn** (P2-133, #574): it let a `[` right after a function declarator's name be its state header, but `QCC_PR_ParseDefs` reads the array suffix there first, for every type, so an array of functions was refused; replaced by FTE-17.7.

The `;` after a function declaration is optional: `QCC_PR_ParseDefs` ends with `if (type->type == ev_function) QCC_PR_CheckTokenComment (";", ...)`, which takes a `;` if there is one. A `;` before a definition is skipped (`while (QCC_PR_CheckToken(";")) ;` at the start of `QCC_PR_ParseDefs`), so `};` after a body is also accepted.

A builtin initialiser is `#number` or `#number:name`, and the number may be 0: `QCC_PR_ParseInitializerType` takes any integral immediate (`pr_immediate._float == (int)pr_immediate._float`), then `if (!*fname && QCC_PR_CheckToken (":")) QC_strlcpy(fname, QCC_PR_ParseName(), ...)`; the name is the engine's name for the builtin. The rerelease binds its `ex_` extensions this way.

A function's builtin initialiser may also start with `:` in place of `#`, and the engine name may stand in place of the number: a string literal after `#` or `:`, or a name after `:`, is the name, and the number is then 0. `QCC_PR_ParseInitializerType_Internal` (`qcc_pr_comp.c`, fte-team/fteqw@`f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e`), when `if (type->type == ev_function && pr_token_type == tt_punct)`, reads `if (QCC_PR_CheckToken ("#") || QCC_PR_CheckToken (":"))`, with `int binum = 0;`, then the number of FTE-17.4, `else if (pr_token_type == tt_immediate && pr_immediate_type == type_string) QC_strlcpy(fname, pr_immediate_string, sizeof(fname)); else if (pr_token_type == tt_name) QC_strlcpy(fname, pr_token, sizeof(fname));`, and a `:name` after it only `if (!*fname && QCC_PR_CheckToken (":"))`, so `#"a":b` and `:a:b` are errors. A name directly after `#` never reaches it: `QCC_PR_Lex` (`qcc_pr_lex.c`) reads `#` and a letter as a macro use, and with no such macro reports "Explicit precompiler usage when not defined %s"; this profile reports it as `E0209`. By FTE-17.2's `pr_token[0] == ':'` the `:` form may follow a function declarator with no `=`, and only a function takes it. The pinned FTEQCC, built by `cargo xtask oracles build`, compiles `void(string s, ...) bp = #"ex_bprint";`, `= :ex_bprint3;`, `= :5;`, `= :"ex_bprint4";`, `= :0:ex_bprint5;` and `void(string s, ...) bx :ex_bprint6;` with 0 warnings, and rejects `= #"ex_a":ex_b;`, `= :ex_a:ex_b;`, `= #ex_bprint2;` and `float fx = :ex_bprint7;`. The vanilla profile reads none of these forms (QC-13.3).

The number of a builtin initialiser is FTEQCC's `binum`, which depends on the literal's type (FTEF-3.1): a `float` literal is bound as in QC-13.10, `(int)` of its value once that value is whole and from -2^31 to 2^31 - 1, so `#123456789` is 123456792; an integer literal with the `i` suffix is its `int`, the whole number kept to 32 bits, so `#16777217i` is 16777217 and `#4294967313i` is 17; and a literal with a `u` or `l` suffix is "Bad builtin immediate" (`E0209`). `QCC_PR_ParseInitializerType_Internal` (`qcc_pr_comp.c`, fte-team/fteqw@`f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e`) reads `if (pr_token_type == tt_immediate && pr_immediate_type == type_float && pr_immediate._float == (int)pr_immediate._float) binum = (int)pr_immediate._float; else if (pr_token_type == tt_immediate && pr_immediate_type == type_integer) binum = pr_immediate._int;`, then the string and name of FTE-17.5, `else QCC_PR_ParseError (ERR_BADBUILTINIMMEDIATE, "Bad builtin immediate");`; `QCC_PR_LexNumber` (`qcc_pr_lex.c`) gives a number with no suffix and no fraction the type `float` (`pr_immediate._float = (float)(num*sign);`), an `i` suffix `type_integer` with `pr_immediate._int = num;`, and a `u` or `l` suffix `type_uint`, `type_int64` or `type_uint64`, which no branch takes. The pinned FTEQCC binds `#16777217i` as 16777217, `#0x1000001i` as 16777217 and `#4294967313i` as 17, and rejects `#16u`, `#16l` and `#16ll`; built for arm64 it binds `#2147483648` as 2147483647, where the x86 result of VM-9.2 is the rule.

A function declarator's body, state header or builtin may follow it without `=` once its array suffixes are read: after the name `QCC_PR_ParseDefs` runs `if (!arraysize && QCC_PR_CheckToken ("[")) { dynlength = QCC_PR_ParseDefArray(&type, name, istypedef, istypedef||isstatic);` for every type, and only then `isinitialised = QCC_PR_CheckToken ("=") || ((type->type == ev_function) && (pr_token[0] == '{' || pr_token[0] == '[' || pr_token[0] == ':'));`. So a `[` right after the name is the array suffix: `void() h = {}; void() g[2] = { h, h };` declares an array of two functions, as do `g[]`, `*g[2]`, `void(float a) g[2]`, with `static`, `var` or `const`, with `{ h }` or `{}`, a two-dimensional one with braces per dimension (`g[2][2] = { { h, h }, { h, h } }`, and `{ h, h, h, h }` is "expected {, found h", FTEF-19.8), through a typedef (`typedef void() fn; fn g[2] = { h, h };`, `fn *g[2]`, `typedef fn fns[2]; fns g = { h, h };`), and `g[0]()` calls an element; one with no initialiser, `void() x[2];`, holds functions with no body ("function x has no body", FTEF-17.11); `void() g [1, g] {};` and `$frame a1 void() g [$a1, g] { };` are refused, `1, g` being no array size. With no suffix the body, state header and builtin follow as before, in both orders, `void InitLightStyles() { ... }` and `void(entity e) remove { ... }` (`rerelease-mg1/defs.qc`), `void() g = [1, g] {};`, `void() g { };` and `void() g : 6;`. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseDefs`.

`...` may end a list after named parameters: each parameter begins with `if (QCC_PR_CheckToken ("..."))`, which, with no type after it, sets `ftype->vargs = true` and ends the list. The rerelease declares `void(string s, ...) bprint = #0:ex_bprint;`.

A parameter may have a default value, `type name = value`: `if (QCC_PR_CheckToken("=")) paramlist[numparms].defltvalue = QCC_PR_ParseDefaultInitialiser(paramlist[numparms].type);`. The rerelease writes `float(entity e) predicate = (float(entity e))SUB_True` (`rerelease-mg1/subs.qc`).

A parameter's type is read by `QCC_PR_ParseType`, so it may be a type name the program defined, such as the named enum (FTE-15.4) of `float GetUpgradeAmount(UpgradeType Type)` (`rerelease-mg3/mg3_upgrades.qc`).

A call reads every argument before it stores any to a parameter slot, a call's value among them copied out of the return global to a temporary when another argument follows (`QCC_PR_ParseFunctionCall` collects the arguments as references, which `QCC_PR_GenerateFunctionCallRef` copies to the slots); so a call in an argument overwrites no slot an earlier argument filled, and an argument past the last parameter is read and ignored. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseFunctionCall`, `QCC_PR_GenerateFunctionCallRef`.

A call's value as the left operand of a binary operator is copied out of the return global before a call in the right operand overwrites it: the value is an alias of `OFS_RETURN` (`QCC_GetAliasTemp`), and before each call `QCC_ClobberDef` copies the aliases still in use to temporaries. So `f() + g()` adds `f()`'s value to `g()`'s, where id's `qcc` adds `g()`'s to itself (QC-18.6). The pinned FTEQCC (`-Tid`) writes `CALL0 f`, `STORE_F` of the return global to a temporary, `CALL0 g` and `ADD_F` of the temporary and the return global for `x = f() + g();`, the same for `==` and `%`, and no copy for `f() + 2`, where no call follows. `qc-codegen` copies a call's left operand to a temporary whether or not a call follows, which reads the same values. The rerelease's `dog_bite` (`rerelease/monsters/rottweiler.qc`) sums `random() + random() + random()`.

FTEQCC's punctuation adds, among others, `->`, `~`, `^`, `<<`, `>>`, `&=`, `|=`, `^=`, `&~=`, `<<=`, `>>=`, `(+)` and `(-)`, tried before shorter punctuation as its table says: "longer symbols must be before a shorter partial match". `^` is exclusive or, `<<` and `>>` shift, and each `op=` stores `a op b` back to `a`; `&~=` clears the bits of its right side.
`pr_punctuationremap[]` reads three of them as others: "(+) -> |=", "-> -> ." and "(-) -> &~=". So `a (+) b` is `a |= b`, `a (-) b` is `a &~= b`, and `e->f` is `e.f`.

Without `flag_cpriority` (the default for the rerelease's `-Tid` build), `QCC_PrioritiseOpcodes` gives shifts, `&`, `^` and `|` the priority of `*` and `/` (`priority_class[PC_MULDIV] = 3; ... priority_class[PC_SHIFT] = 3; ... priority_class[PC_BITAND] = 3; priority_class[PC_BITXOR] = 3; priority_class[PC_BITOR] = 3;`), one tighter than `+` and `-` as in vanilla (QC-15.1). The compound assignments are in `PC_STORE`, with `=`: right-associative, at the assignment priority.

A term may start with `-`, `+` or `~`: `QCC_PR_RefTerm` reads `if (QCC_PR_CheckToken ("-")) { ... e = QCC_PR_Expression (UNARY_PRIORITY, EXPR_DISALLOW_COMMA);` and the same for `+`, with `#define UNARY_PRIORITY 1`, so the operand is a term with its postfix forms; `~` takes `QCC_PR_Expression (NOT_PRIORITY, ...)`, the operand of `!` (QC-15.6). `-e` negates, `+e` is `e`, and `~e` is the bitwise not.

A negative number where a binary operator belongs is a subtraction: `QCC_PR_RefExpression` "work[s] around (4-3) being parsed as 4 -3 with no operator between" by reading the token as `+` and the negative number after it, at the priority of `+`. The lexer still reads `-1` after a value as one number (QC-4.1). The rerelease writes `self.count -1` (`rerelease-mg3/mg3_sacrifice_triggers.qc`).

`(type) e` is a cast: `QCC_PR_RefTerm` reads `(`, then `newtype = QCC_PR_ParseType(false, true, false)`; if it is a type, `)` and `e = QCC_PR_Expression (UNARY_PRIORITY, EXPR_DISALLOW_COMMA); e = QCC_EvaluateCast(e, newtype, false);`. A parenthesis that does not open a type is a parenthesised expression, as in vanilla. This profile parses before names are known, so it takes a cast at a `(` followed by a type keyword or `.`; the rerelease casts to no type a program defines.

`a ^ b` of floats on the vanilla opcodes is `OP_BITXOR_F`'s emulation, `(a & ~b) | (b & ~a)`: `BITNOT_F b`, `BITAND_F a, ~b`, `BITNOT_F a`, `BITAND_F b, ~a`, `BITOR_F`, each `~x` as `OP_BITNOT_F`'s emulation `-1 - x`; `a ^= b` stores it to `a`. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_StatementFlags`.

`a % b` of floats on the vanilla opcodes is `OP_MOD_F`'s emulation: a `CALL2` of the program's `mod(a, b)` when it defines one (`QCC_PR_EmulationFunc(mod)`), else `a - b * (a/b | a/b)`, `DIV_F`, `BITOR_F` of the quotient with itself, `MUL_F` and `SUB_F`. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_StatementFlags`.

`v / f` of a vector and a float is `OP_DIV_VF`'s emulation, `v * (1 / f)`: `DIV_F 1, f` then `MUL_VF`. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_StatementFlags`.

`a && b` and `a || b` whose operands are not both floats are `OP_AND_ANY` and `OP_OR_ANY` on the vanilla opcodes: a vector operand is first `MUL_V` of it with itself under `vectorlogic` (a default flag), then `AND` or `OR` of the two words; a string's word is read as it is, `ifstring` being off by default. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_StatementFlags`.

`a << b` and `a >> b` of floats are `OP_LSHIFT_F` and `OP_RSHIFT_F`. Two constants fold, each truncated to an `int` and shifted (`QCC_MakeFloatConst (QCC_PR_RoundFloatConst(eval_a) << QCC_PR_RoundFloatConst(eval_b))`, `dialect-fteqcc.md` FTEF-26.2). Otherwise, on the vanilla opcodes, which have no `OP_LSHIFT_I`, they are emulated with the program's functions (`QCC_PR_EmulationFunc`): with `powf`, or else `pow`, and `floor`, `a << b` is `floor(a * pow(2, b))` ("a<<b === floor(a*pow(2,b))") and `a >> b` `floor(a / pow(2, b))`: `CALL2` of the power with the float 2 and `b`, `MUL_F` or `DIV_F` of `a` and its value, and `CALL1` of `floor`; else with `bitshift`, `bitshift(a, b)` and `bitshift(a, 0 - b)` (`SUB_F` of 0 and `b` first); else the warning "bitshift function not defined: cannot emulate OP_LSHIFT_F*", which this profile does not lower. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_StatementFlags`.

A `.` followed by a digit starts a number: `QCC_PR_Lex` dispatches `(c == '.'&&pr_file_p[1]!='.'&&pr_file_p[1] >='0' && pr_file_p[1] <= '9')` to `QCC_PR_LexNumber`. The rerelease writes `float DRAW_AI_SINGLE_FRAME = .1;` (`rerelease/defs.qc`).

A number may end in the float suffix `f` or `F`, which is not part of its value: after the fraction `QCC_PR_LexNumber` has `else if (c == 'f' || c == 'F') { pr_immediate_type = type_float; pr_file_p++; break; }`. The rerelease writes `1.0f` (`rerelease/client.qc`).

**Withdrawn** (P2-26, #82): it kept FTEQCC's escapes beyond one byte "Unknown escape char" under the FTEQCC profile, which now also reads the full dialect. Replaced by FTE-20.4 for the one-byte escapes and `dialect-fteqcc.md` FTEF-13.4 for the rest.

Besides `\n` and `\"`, the escapes that stand for one ASCII byte are `\r`, `\t`, `\a`, `\v`, `\f`, `\#`, `\\`, `\?` and `\'`, as `QCC_PR_LexEscapedCodepoint` maps them (`else if (c == 't') c = '\t'; //tab` and the rest). The rerelease uses `\t` (`rerelease-mg1/misc_corpses.qc`). FTEQCC's other escapes are the full dialect's (`dialect-fteqcc.md` FTEF-13.11).

A number's immediate is shared only with an immediate of its size and bits (`QCC_Make32bitConst`: `if (((QCC_eval_t*)cn->symboldata)->_uint == value) return QCC_MakeSRefForce(cn, 0, type);` over `floatconstdefstable`, else a new `"IMMEDIATE"` with `cn->constant = true;`), and a constant takes the immediate's place when its value folds (`dialect-fteqcc.md` FTEF-34.15). So a literal never shares a variable's word, unlike id's `qcc`, which shares any initialised definition's (QC-20.2): after `var float two = 2;` the literal `2` is its own immediate, and a store to `two` does not change it. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_Make32bitConst`.

A statement that starts with a type declares locals with no `local`: `QCC_PR_ParseStatement` passes a name for which `QCC_TypeForName(pr_token)` finds a type, or one of the words `float`, `vector`, `string`, `entity`, `var`, `const` and the other type and storage keywords, to `QCC_PR_ParseDefs`, and also a statement starting with `.` ("for local .entity without var/local"). Such a declaration may stand anywhere among the statements. The rerelease writes `float playerFlags = CheckPlayerEXFlags(playerEnt);` mid-body (`rerelease/weapons.qc`) and `poseInfo pose = poses[self.style];` (`rerelease-mg1/misc_corpses.qc`). This profile parses before names are known, so it takes a statement that starts with a name and then another name, `Type name`, for a declaration of a type the program defined; no expression statement starts that way.

A local may be a field or a function variable: FTEQCC's check is commented out, `// QCC_PR_ParseError ("Fields must be global");`. The rerelease declares `void() tutsh;` and `local void() pain_event;` in bodies (`rerelease-mg1/map_specific/mge2m2.qc`, `rerelease-mg3/monsters/boss_final.qc`).

A definition that is not a function may lack its `;`: `QCC_PR_ParseDefs` reports `QCC_PR_ParseWarning(WARN_UNDESIRABLECONVENTION, "Missing semicolon at end of definition");` and goes on. The rerelease's `local float color = bottom + top * 16` has none (`rerelease-ctf/teamplay.qc`). This profile reports `W0203` (QCD-7.18).
A block may be empty: `QCC_PR_ParseStatement` reads `while (!QCC_PR_CheckToken("}")) QCC_PR_ParseStatement ();`. The rerelease has `else { }` holding only a comment (`rerelease-mg3/mg3_upgrades.qc`).

A `;` alone is an empty statement: `QCC_PR_ParseStatement` takes it with `QCC_PR_ParseWarning(WARN_POINTLESSSTATEMENT, "Hanging ';'");`, unless a macro expansion produced it. A macro written `if (CheckContentsDamage()) return;` and used with a `;` after it makes one (`rerelease-mg1/ai.qc`, `rerelease-mg1/monsters/tarbaby.qc`). This profile reports `W0204` (QCD-7.19) for every one, since the parser does not see expansions.

A QuakeC function's record counts its parameters among its `locals`, so `PR_EnterFunction` saves them when a call enters the function again and `PR_LeaveFunction` restores them: `QCC_WriteData` sets `funcs[i].parm_start = local->ofs;` at the first parameter, adds each parameter's size, `funcs[i].locals += size;`, and then each used local that is not static and not an initialised constant. id's `qcc` counts only up to the end of the last `local` declaration, so a function with parameters and no `local` has `locals` 0 (QC-21.4) and a nested call of it overwrites the caller's parameters. In the rerelease `ai_run(12)` reaches `ai_run(16)` through `CheckAnyAttack`, `WizardCheckAttack` and `wiz_run1`, and then calls `movetogoal(dist)` with 12; the pinned FTEQCC's record of `ai_run` has `locals` 1. `qc-codegen` counts the parameters and every global from them to the end of the last `local` declaration, its temporaries among them.

A parameter or local is a new definition that shadows a global of the same name, whatever its type: when `QCC_PR_GetDef` allocates in a function's scope it skips global definitions, `if ( (def->scope || (scope && allocate)) && def->scope != scope) { ... continue; // in a different function }`. A use in the body finds the function's own definition first. The rerelease names a parameter `light` beside the spawn function `void() light` (`rerelease-mg3/mg3_weapons.qc`, `rerelease-mg3/lights.qc`). A second declaration of a name in the same function is still that definition again, or a type mismatch (QC-11.5).

**Withdrawn** (P2-26, #82): it made a second initialiser that is not a literal always "NAME redeclared", which the full dialect's corpus contradicts. Replaced by FTE-22.5 for literals and `dialect-fteqcc.md` FTEF-17.5 for the rest.

**Withdrawn** 2026-10-28: it kept "NAME redeclared" (QCD-3.6) for a differing literal by this profile's choice, but the pinned FTEQCC reports `"incompatible redeclaration"` there, and compares no value that is not a constant; replaced by FTE-22.6.

A name initialised twice with the same value is accepted: for a "dupe initialisation" (`basedef->initialized && !basedef->unused && !(flags & PIF_STRONGER)`) `QCC_PR_GenerateInitializerType` compares the two word by word and, when they differ, reports the fatal error `QCC_PR_ParseErrorPrintSRef (ERR_REDECLARATION, def, "incompatible redeclaration")`, `E0363` (QCD-4.64), but for the `parseentitydata` and builtin-after-body warnings (FTEF-17.9, QCD-7.49). The comparison is in the branch for a constant value only: a value that is not one is "initializer for 'NAME' is not constant" (QCD-3.14) and nothing more. The rerelease initialises `float SIGIL_E1 = 1;` in both `rerelease-mg1/defs.qc` and `rerelease-mg1/items_runes.qc`. So `float A = 1; float A = 2;`, `string A = "a"; string A = "b";` and `float B = 2; float A = 1; float A = B;` are "incompatible redeclaration", and `float x; float A = 1; float A = x;` is only "not constant"; other initialisers compare as FTEF-17.10 says. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_GenerateInitializerType`.

With `-Fautoproto` every top-level declaration of the program is visible in every function body: `qccmain.c` describes the flag as "Causes compilation to take two passes instead of one. The first pass, only the definitions are read. The second pass actually compiles your code." `rerelease-mg3` needs it (FTE-1.2). Between the passes `QCC_SetDefaultProperties` makes a new table of `#define`s (`Hash_InitTable(&compconstantstable, ...)`), so the second pass defines its macros again.

Frame macros (QC-8) carry from one file to the next: at the start of a file `QCC_PR_CompileFile` calls `QCC_PR_ClearGrabMacros (true)`, which with `newfile` set only restarts the numbering (`if (!newfile) pr_nummacros = 0; pr_macrovalue = 0;`). A `$frame` name another file defined takes the new value ("old file, override it"); one this file already defined keeps its first (QC-8.7). With `-Fautoproto` the frame macros of the first pass are still defined in the second, so a file may use a frame name a later file defines (`rerelease-mg3/misc_corpses.qc` uses `$CORPSEFRAME_PLAYER_6` from `rerelease-mg3/player.qc`).

Under FTEQCC a `#` opens a builtin only when the byte right after it is `"`, `-`, a digit, `)` or `,`. `QCC_PR_Lex` reads any other as a macro use: `if (c == '#' && !(pr_file_p[1]==')' || pr_file_p[1]==',' || pr_file_p[1]=='\"' || pr_file_p[1]=='-' || (pr_file_p[1]>='0' && pr_file_p[1] <='9'))) //hash and not number`, then `if (!QCC_PR_CheckCompConst()) { ... QCC_PR_ParseError(ERR_CONSTANTNOTDEFINED, "Explicit precompiler usage when not defined %s", pr_token); }`. So `= # 5;`, `= # "x";`, `= #'a';`, `= #.5;`, `= #+5;`, `= #(5);`, `= #/**/5;`, `= #\t5;` and `= #;` are errors, which this profile reports as `E0209`, and `= #5;`, `= #-5;` and `= #"x";` are builtins. `:` is plain punctuation, so `= : 5;`, `= :'a';` (97) and `= : "nmr";` (`nmr`) are builtins. The vanilla `#` is plain punctuation too (`pr_punctuation[]` in id's `qcc/pr_lex.c` lists `"#"`), and id's `qcc` binds `= # 5;` as 5, as the vanilla profile does.

An FTEQCC hex number with a fraction is C's `atof` of its text, which reads `0x` as a hexadecimal float: `QCC_PR_LexNumber` keeps the `0x` in `pr_token`, takes only decimal digits after the `.` (`if (c >= '0' && c <= '9') { pr_token[tokenlen++] = c; }`), and sets `pr_immediate._float = (float)atof(pr_token);`. The digits before the `.` are read in full, so `0x10000000000000005.0` is about 1.8e19 and binds no number. So `0x10.0` is 16, `-0x10.0` -16, `0x1.8` 1.5 and `0x1.08` 1.03125; `0x1.a` is `0x1.` (1) and then a name.

A `d` literal is a `double`, and FTEQCC binds no builtin number for it: the initialiser takes only `type_float`, `type_integer` and `type_string` immediates, and `QCC_PR_LexNumber` gives `type_double` to a `d` or `D` after a fraction (`else if (c == 'd' || c == 'D') { pr_immediate_type = type_double;`) and after the digits of base 8 or 10 (`else if (c == 'd' || c == 'D') { //note: conflicts with hex.`). So `= #16d;`, `= #16.0d;`, `= #0d;`, `= #010d;`, `= #0x1.5d;` and `= :16d;` are "Bad builtin immediate" (`E0209`), and `qc_syntax::builtin_binum` gives them no number. In base 16 `d` and `f` are digits (`c < 'a'+base-10`), so `#0x1d` is 29 and `#0x10f` 271; in base 8 or 10 `f` makes a `float`, so `#16f` and `#16.0f` are 16.

A `-` is part of a number only right before a digit (`QCC_PR_Lex`: `( c=='-' && pr_file_p[1]>='0' && pr_file_p[1] <='9')`), and FTEQCC binds a negative builtin number like any other (FTE-17.4): `#-5` and `:-5i` are -5, `#-0x10` -16. `= #- 5;`, `= #-.5;`, `= :- 5;` and `= :-.5;` read the `-` alone and are "Bad builtin immediate" (`E0209`).

Adjacent string literals are one string (FTEF-16.8): `QCC_PR_LexString` loops, skipping whitespace and comments with `QCC_PR_LexComment(&pr_token_precomment);` before each part, until `else if (first) { ... } else break;`. So `= #"ab" "cd";` binds the engine name `abcd`, `= :"x" "y";` `xy`, and the parts may stand on separate lines or around a comment. An empty string sets no name: `fname` stays empty, so the builtin is named after the definition (`QCC_PR_GenerateBuiltinFunction(def.sym, binum, *fname?fname:def.sym->name)`) with `binum` 0, and `if (!*fname && QCC_PR_CheckToken (":"))` still reads a name after it: `= #"";` is builtin 0 named after the function and `= #"":ex_b;` binds `ex_b`. After a non-empty string a `:name` is an error, as FTE-17.5 says.

An engine name is at most 255 bytes: `QC_strlcpy(fname, ..., sizeof(fname))` into `char fname[256];` keeps the first 255 of a longer string or name. It copies a C string, so a string's name ends at its first NUL byte: `#"ab\x00cd"` binds `ab`, and `#"\x00":ex_b` names nothing before the `:` and binds `ex_b`. Names are bytes, compared with `strcmp`, so two bronze names (`\b`, bytes of 0x80 and above) differ when their bytes do. A name after `:` is `pr_token`, which `QCC_PR_ParseName`'s "name too long" check does not see.
**Withdrawn** 2026-10-28: it gave the differing builtin reinitialiser `E0206`, but the pinned FTEQCC reports `"incompatible redeclaration"`, `E0363` (FTE-22.6); replaced by FTE-23.17.

A builtin initialiser makes a builtin function, numbered `binum` and named the engine name or, with none, the definition's name, unless it initialises a definition already initialised and FTEQCC finds one to reuse: `if (basedef && basedef->initialized)` it takes the first function, in the order they were made, with `functions[i].code == -1 && functions[i].builtin == binum` and `!strcmp(functions[i].name, fname)`, or with no `fname` `(!*functions[i].name || !strcmp(functions[i].name, defname))`; `if (!tmp.cast) f = QCC_PR_GenerateBuiltinFunction(def.sym, binum, *fname?fname:def.sym->name);`. The "dupe initialisation" comparison then reports `"incompatible redeclaration"` unless the function is the one the definition has. So a second builtin initialiser is the same value exactly when its number and engine name are those of the first and no function with them was made before the definition's: under this profile it is otherwise `E0363`. `#0:ex_a` then `#0:ex_b`, `#5:ex_a` then `#5:ex_b`, `#5` then `#5:ex_a` and `#0` then `:ex_a` are `E0363`; `:ex_a` then `:"ex_a"`, `#0:ex_a` then `:ex_a`, `#"ex_a"` then `:ex_a`, `#5` then `#5.0`, and, for a definition `f`, `#5` then `#5:f` and `#0` then `:f` are not. A builtin function's record, as `QCC_WriteData` writes it for id's format (`PST_DEFAULT`), has no parameter or local slots and its named parameters' count: `else if (functions[i].code == -1) { funcs[i].parm_start = 0; funcs[i].locals = 0; funcs[i].numparms = functions[i].type->num_parms; if (funcs[i].numparms > MAX_PARMS) funcs[i].numparms = MAX_PARMS; p = 0; }`, and then `while(p < MAX_PARMS) funcs[i].parm_size[p++] = 0;`. A `#` before a macro that stands for a number, `#define N 5` and `void() f = #N;`, initialises `f` with `5`, which FTEQCC cannot cast to a function: the error `E0213` "Cannot cast from float to void()" (`dialect-fteqcc.md` FTEF-19.31), as for `#__LINE__`, the line number. On the standard target a program is written in FTE's 32-bit layout (PROGS-20) when it has more than 65530 globals (`else if (numpr_globals > 65530) ... outputsttype = PST_FTE32;`) or a statement whose first operand is no symbol, a `GOTO`'s offset, is past `0x7fff` either way (`if (!statements[i].a.sym && ((int)statements[i].a.ofs > 0x7fff || (int)statements[i].a.ofs < -0x7fff)) break;`, the test written three times for `a`, so an `IF`'s or `IFNOT`'s offset in `b` is never tested); otherwise in version 6. Statements, globals and definitions are the same either way.

In version 6 each operand is written as its low 16 bits, `statements16[i].a = (unsigned short)PRLittleShort((unsigned short)a);`, so a global from 32768 to 65530 is written where id's `short` reads it as that global less 65536 (FTEQCC prints "Globals exceeds 32k - an enhanced QCVM will be required" and writes the file).

A FTEQCC corpus mod (`nuclide`, `freecs`, `freehl`) is accepted under the FTEQCC profile. Every full-dialect construct it contains is covered by a section of this file; the coverage check (`xtask/src/fteqcc_full_coverage.rs`) fails on a class no section names. This statement is what that check pins.

Unlike the rerelease subset, which fits version 6 (`dialect-fteqcc-rerelease.md` FTE-1.1), the full dialect's aggregate and pointer types (FTEF-6, FTEF-9) in general need FTE's version 7 progs format ([`progs.md`](progs.md) PROGS-19). Which construct needs version 7 and which lowers to version 6 is a code-generation question, fixed by L-01, not by this parse-and-resolve spec.
Codegen (later): the progs format and opcode set each construct emits are fixed by L-01 and recorded there, against FTEQCC's output. This spec does not state them.

`int` and `integer` both name a 32-bit signed integer type. FTEQCC defines them as `type_integer` (`QCC_PR_NewType("__int32", ev_integer, ...)`), and the two keywords `keyword_int` and `keyword_integer` both resolve to it (`QCC_PR_ParseType`, the C-type branch, `int`/`integer` set `bits = 32`). The corpus declares locals, globals, fields, parameters and return types of this type.

**Withdrawn** (P2-117, #545): it said `signed`, `char`, `short` and `long` are types, but their keywords are disabled by default (`nondefaultkeyword` in `compiler_flag[]`), so bare they are "not a type". Replaced by FTEF-2.7 and FTEF-2.8.
**Withdrawn** (P2-117, #545): it said `double` is a type, but `keyword_double` is disabled by default: the double is `__double`. Replaced by FTEF-2.7 and FTEF-2.8.

**Withdrawn** (P2-117, #545): it said the C words combine in any order C allows, but the loop takes a word only while its test holds (`long int` is 32 bits, `int long` ends at `int`). Replaced by FTEF-2.8 and FTEF-2.9.
**Withdrawn** (P2-117, #545): it said `volatile` is accepted, but `keyword_volatile` is disabled by default. Replaced by FTEF-2.11.
Codegen (later): how each width is stored and which need version 7 is fixed by L-01.

A C type word is matched as `QCC_PR_CheckKeyword(keywordenabled, string)` matches it: a token that starts with `__` matches its keyword in any case whether or not the keyword is enabled (`if (pr_token[0] == '_' && pr_token[1] == '_') { if (stricmp(string, pr_token+2)) return false; ...`), and a bare word only when its keyword is enabled, case sensitively. By default (`compiler_flag[]`) `int` and `integer` (`typekeyword`) and `unsigned` (`defaultkeyword`) are enabled, `float` and `_Bool` (`QCC_PR_CheckKeyword(true, "_Bool")`) always are, and `double`, `long`, `short`, `char`, `signed`, `register` and `volatile` (`nondefaultkeyword`) are not: `long l;`, `double d;`, `signed x;`, `short s;` and `char c;` are "\"WORD\" is not a type" (`E0203`), and `__long l;`, `__double d;` and `__CHAR c;` are types.

`QCC_PR_ParseType` first looks the word up with `QCC_TypeForName`, which finds the types `QCC_PR_NewType` registers (`float`, `__double`, `__int`, `__int32`, `__uint`, `__uint32`, `__int64`, `__uint64`, `__int8`, `__uint8`, `__int16`, `__uint16`, `__bint`, ...): such a word is the type alone, so in `__int unsigned x;` the name is `unsigned`. Else its loop over C words takes, after an optional leading `register`, each word whose test holds and stops at the first that fails: `signed` and `unsigned` when neither was read; `long` while no width is set, a second making the width `longlongbits` (64); `int` or `integer` while no width is set or it is 16, setting 32 when none is; `short` (16) and `char` (8) while none is set; `_Bool` while none is set and no sign was read, which ends the type as `type_bint` (`__bint`, the `int` keyword being enabled); `float` while no width is set and no `long` was read (32, a float); `double` while no width is set or after `long` (64, or 128 after `long`, a float). A word the loop does not take is the declarator's name, so `int int i;`, `unsigned unsigned u;`, `int float f;` and `__long __long int x;` are errors. With no width set the width is `longbits`, 64, after `long` and 32 otherwise (`flag_ILP32` is set only by `-std=c`); then a float of 64 bits or more is `__double` and else `float`, and an integer of more than 32 bits is `__int64`, of 8 or fewer `__int8`, of 16 or fewer `__int16` and else `__int32`, each unsigned (`__uint64`, `__uint8`, `__uint16`, `__uint32`) after `unsigned`. So `__long int` is `__int32`, `unsigned __long` is `__uint64`, `__short int` is `__int16`, `__register` alone is `__int32` and `unsigned float` is `float`. FTEQCC's `bool` is no keyword: it comes from the engine's extension headers (`fteextensions.qc`), a defined type.

An `unsigned` float is the warning `W0226` "ignoring unsupported unsigned keyword, type will be signed", and a float of more than 64 bits (`__long __double`) "long doubles are not supported, using double", in that order, at the type's first word. The integer branch's "long longs are not supported, using long" is never given: `long long` sets 64 bits, and only more than 64 warns.

In a function body a statement defines locals at a name `QCC_TypeForName` finds or at one of the bare words `QCC_PR_ParseStatement` tests with their keyword enabled (`integer`, `unsigned`, `int` and `_Bool` among the C words; FTEF-19.1 lists the others). `STRCMP` compares the bare word, so a `__` C word that names no registered type is a value there: `__long x;` in a body is "Unknown value \"__long\"", and `__int x;` defines a local.

A type may start with `const`, which `QCC_PR_ParseType` reads and ignores with the warning `W0226` "ignoring unsupported const keyword", and then with `volatile`, read and ignored, which by default only `__volatile` spells; a `*` may be followed by `const`, with the same warning (`if (QCC_PR_CheckKeyword(keyword_const, "const")) QCC_PR_ParseWarning (WARN_IGNOREDKEYWORD, "ignoring unsupported const keyword");`). A bare `volatile` is a name, so `void(volatile float v) f;` is an error. At file level `__volatile float v;` is a definition; in a body it is a value (FTEF-2.10). How `const` makes a constant is FTE-10.

An 8- or 16-bit integer, `__int8`, `__uint8`, `__int16` or `__uint16` (and the C words that make one, `char` and `short`), is `ev_bitfld` with the `parentclass` `int` or `uint` (`type_sint8 ->parentclass = type_integer;` and the others, `qccmain.c`). It is cast as its parent (`QCC_TryEvaluateCast` follows `parentclass`), so `c = "a"` is "Implicit cast from string to __int8" and `c = 3.5` "Numerical overflow. 3.500000 will be rounded to 3", and messages name it by its own name; a definition of it is read as a bitfield at bit 0 (`QCC_BitfieldToDef`), extended by `OP_BITEXTEND_I`, or `OP_BITEXTEND_U` for an unsigned one, with the mask of its bits, to a value of its parent's type; it is no bitfield's base ("bitfields must be integer types"); and a string initialises an array of 8-bit integers with no cast, a character to each element (FTEF-19.8). An element of an array of them at a constant index is the bitfield `index * bits` bits in (`ret.ofs += bitofs>>5; bitofs&=31;`), read extended and stored packed into its word (`QCC_PR_Statement_BitCopy`, FTEF-6.15); at another index it is read through its address (`QCC_PR_GenerateAddressOf`, which the id target refuses) by the narrow load of FTEF-27.10. A local of one is initialised packed at bit 0 (`QCC_PR_GenerateInitializerType`), and a local array of 8-bit ones from a string a character, then zeros, to each element. A field of one has no load: read, it is the fatal error `E0358` "QCC_PR_ExpandField: invalid field type __int8"; stored, its index is the error `E0359` "Unable to evaluate to numeric constant" (`QCC_Eval_Int` of the field), and the value is packed at bit 0 and stored through its address (FTEF-6.18). FTEQCC prints "INTERNAL: over-freed refcount to NAME" for such a local's initialiser, its own temporaries' bookkeeping, which the semantic model does not report.

A number may carry a type suffix: `f`/`F` float, `d`/`D` double, `i`/`I` integer, `u`/`U` unsigned, `l`/`L` long (and `ll`/`LL` long-long), in the combinations `QCC_PR_LexNumber` accepts (length and sign flags in either order). `12i` is an integer literal, `3.5d` a double, `1u` an unsigned.

`0x`/`0X` begins a hexadecimal literal and a leading `0` a base-8 (octal) one; `QCC_PR_LexNumber` reads the digits in that base and `QCC_PR_Lex` dispatches `0x` to it. FTEQCC warns "A leading 0 is interpreted as base-8." on an octal literal.

Without a suffix the type is chosen by the compiler flags: `flag_assume_integer` makes an un-suffixed whole number an integer (widening to `uint`/`int64`/`uint64` as its magnitude needs), otherwise it is a float (`QCC_PR_LexNumber`, the "assume base 10" tail). An un-suffixed number with a `.` is a float, or a double under `flag_assume_double`.
The built-in macro `__NULL__` expands to `0i` (`qcc_pr_lex.c`, `QCC_PR_CheckBuiltinCompConst`), an integer zero used as a null pointer or entity; the corpus uses it.
Codegen (later): how each literal type becomes an immediate is fixed by L-01.

`T *` is the type pointer-to-`T`; one `*` per level, parsed by the `*` loop of `QCC_PR_ParseType` building `QCC_PointerTypeTo`/`QCC_PR_PointerType`. `float *`, `entity *` and `__variant *` all occur. A cast `(T *)expr` reinterprets `expr` as that pointer type.
`&lvalue` is the address of an lvalue, of type pointer-to-its-type (the `&` token in `pr_punctuation[]`). The corpus takes the address of globals and of struct fields.
`ptr->member` dereferences a pointer and selects a member (the `->` token, remapped to `.` in `pr_punctuationremap[]`): `ptr->member` is `(*ptr).member`.

`*ptr` dereferences a pointer to its pointed-to lvalue. FTEQCC's internal dereference operator is `*^` (`QCC_PR_LexPunctuation` notes "fteqcc uses *^ internally"), and `**` is remapped to it under `flag_dblstarexp` for GMQCC compatibility with a warning; in FTEQCC source `*` before a value is the dereference.
Codegen (later): pointers need FTE's version 7 progs ([`progs.md`](progs.md) PROGS-19, PROGS-20); the lowering is fixed by L-01.

`T name[N];` declares an array of `N` elements, `N` a constant integer expression. `QCC_PR_ParseArrayType` reads `[N]` with `QCC_PR_IntConstExpr`, and errors "cannot cope with 0-sized arrays" on `N == 0`.
`T name[A][B]...` declares a multidimensional array; `QCC_PR_ParseArrayType` loops over each `[...]` and builds nested array types with `QCC_GenArrayType`. It errors "too many dimensions" past 64.

A sized array may be a struct (FTEF-6) or class member, a local, a global, a parameter (where FTEQCC may demote it to a pointer, FTEF-4) or a field; `QCC_PR_ParseStruct` and the function-type parser both call `QCC_PR_ParseArrayType`.
Codegen (later): array layout and subscript lowering are fixed by L-01 (and for the inferred-size subset, FTE-13.4).

`struct Name { T1 f1; T2 f2; ... };` and the anonymous `struct { ... }` define an aggregate with the named members in declaration order (`QCC_PR_ParseStruct` with `structtype == ev_struct`). `struct Name;` with no body is a forward declaration.
`union Name { ... };` is the same with `structtype == ev_union`: every member shares offset 0 and the union's size is its largest member (`QCC_PR_ParseStruct`, the `ev_union` offset branch).

`struct Child : Parent { ... }` inherits: the child begins at the parent's size and adds its own members (`QCC_PR_ParseStruct` reads `:` then the parent name, and sets `newt->size = newt->parentclass->size`). The parent must be a previously defined struct.

A member may itself be an array (FTEF-5), a pointer (FTEF-4), a function type, or a bitfield `T name : bits;` on an integer type (`QCC_PR_ParseStruct`, the `:` bitfield branch, which promotes to 64-bit when `bits > 32` and errors "bitfields must be integer types" otherwise). `v.member` selects a member.
`access.member` on a struct value or through a pointer (FTEF-4.3) reads or writes the member; a brace initialiser `{ a, b }` gives members in order (as FTE-14.3 for the typedef-struct subset).
Codegen (later): struct and union layout, and which need version 7, are fixed by L-01.

`QCC_PR_ParseStruct` reads a body's members in a loop, and this profile reads them so: a `}` ends it, with "missing semi-colon" when a member's type is still open (`if (newparm) QCC_PR_ParseError(ERR_EXPECTED, "missing semi-colon");`); a `;` closes the open type (`newparm = NULL;`); a `,` goes on with the same type and is "element missing type" when none is open; any other token starts a new type, which is "missing semi-colon" while one is open, and begins with `public`, `private` or `protected` and `QCC_PR_Expect(":")` (`QCC_PR_CheckKeyword(1, "public")`, then `continue`), or `static` or `virtual`, then `QCC_PR_ParseType(false, false, true)`, which makes the type of a nested `struct`, `union`, `enum` or `class` whether or not a declarator follows, then any `*`, then either a `;` (`//annonymous structs do weird scope stuff`: a member of the name "", a warning "declaration does not declare anything" unless its type is a struct or union) or `(` and an optional `*` and a name and `)`, or a name, then `[` array dimensions, `(` and a parameter list (else "expected function arg list"), `:` and a width, and `=` and a default value. A body is `struct S { public: float a; private: float b; };`, `struct S { struct T { float a; }; float b; };`, `struct S { enum { A }; float a; };`, `struct S { struct { float a; }; float b; };`, `struct S { float; };` and `struct S { float a, *b; };`. A member written at column 0 is a member (FTEF-18.34). A `static` member is a global, not counted among the members (`numparms`), and a body with none is "struct %s has no members" (`QCC_PR_ParseError (ERR_NOTANAME, "%s %s has no members", ...)`), as `struct S { };`, `struct S { ;; };` and `union U { };` are, and so is a body whose every member the parent has with the name and type (`oldparm = QCC_PR_FindStructMember(newt, parmname, &ofs, &bitofs)`, which is then the parent's), `struct P { float a; }; struct S : P { float a; };`. A member whose type takes a `(` with `*` after it, `float (*fp)(float);` with `qcfuncs` on, is "expected function arg list": `QCC_PR_ParseType` took the `(`. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_lex.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseStruct`.

After `struct` or `union`, `QCC_PR_ParseStruct` reads `{` for an anonymous type (`<struct>`, `<union>`), else the tag with `QCC_PR_ParseName`, so `struct *p;` is "not a name"; a struct (`structtype == ev_struct`) then reads `:` and a parent, which a union does not, so `union U : P { float b; };` is an error at the `:`; a parent needs the body (`if (parenttype) QCC_PR_Expect("{");`), so `struct S : P;` is "expected {"; with no parent a tag without `{` names the type and returns (`else if (!QCC_PR_CheckToken("{")) return newt;`), so `struct S x;` is a variable of the type, and `struct S;` declares it; the type is the one `QCC_TypeForName(tname)` finds, so `struct float x = 1;` is a `float`. A named union is an `ev_struct` type like a struct. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_lex.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseStruct`.

A member's `:` is followed by `QCC_PR_IntConstExpr()`; "too many bits" for more than 64; the type must be `ev_integer`, `ev_uint`, `ev_int64` or `ev_uint64`, else `QCC_PR_ParseWarning(ERR_BADNOTTYPE, "bitfields must be integer types")`, an error, so `struct S { float a : 3; };`, a `char`, a `short` and a `string` field are refused and `int a : 3;`, `unsigned a : 3;` and `long a : 3;` and `int a : 40;` (promoted to 64 bits) are not. The width's names are values (`int a : b;` with no `b` is "Unknown value"), a literal with a fraction is "Value is not an integer constant" (`int a : 1.5;`), and `(1 + 2)` is a width. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_lex.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseStruct`.

`QCC_TypeForName(tname)` finds the type of a struct's name; a struct given a body when the name is a type with a size (`if (newt->size)`: a struct defined, or `float`, a class, an enum, a typedef) is a new type compared with the old after its members (`typecmp_strict(newt, oldtype)`), "struct %s redeclared differently" when they differ in a name, type, array size, bit width or order of a member, and the same members are accepted: `struct S { float a; }; struct S { float a; };`, but not `struct S { float b; };`, nor `struct float { float a; };`. A parent that is not yet a type is "Parent type %s was not yet defined", one that is no struct "Parent type %s is not a struct" (a typedef of a struct is the struct, `typedef struct P { float a; } PP; struct S : PP { float b; };`), and a struct that has a parent or a size given another is "Redeclaration of struct with different parent type". A direct member whose type is the struct itself, or a struct with no body so far, is "type %s not fully defined yet" (`if (type == newt || ((type->type == ev_struct || type->type == ev_union) && !type->size))`, `QCC_PR_ParseWarning(ERR_NOTANAME, ...)`). A struct written in a function's body is compared with the struct of its name as any is, and lasts to the body's end (`QCC_PR_ParseStruct` with `pr_scope`, dropped with the block's locals), so a struct of its name after the body is another. The struct's own name is no parent of it (`newt = QCC_TypeForName(tname)` comes after the parent is found): `struct S : S { float a; };` is "Parent type S was not yet defined", and `struct S; struct S : S { float a; };` never ends in FTEQCC. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_lex.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseStruct`.

The member after `.` of a struct is `QCC_PR_FindStructMember`'s: the members of the struct are searched, with `stricmp` under `-Fcaseinsens` and `STRCMP` otherwise, those of an anonymous struct member too, and more than one found is "multiple members found matching %s.%s"; a member declared again with its name, type and size is one; none found in the struct goes on to its parent. `union U { float a; float A; }; U x; ... x.A = 1;` is refused under `-Fcaseinsens` and accepted otherwise; a name no struct of the chain has is `QCC_PR_ParseWarning(ERR_BADMEMBER, "%s is not a member of %s", ...)`, an error, `S s; s.b = 1;` after `struct S { float a; };`; a struct's name is no scope of its members or of a nested enum's values, `float y = S::A;` after `struct S { enum { A }; float a; };` is "Unknown value"; and an array takes `.length` and no other member, "expected length, found a" for `S x[2]; x.a = 1;`. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_FindStructMember`.

A struct or union is cast to and from nothing but itself: `QCC_TryEvaluateCast` takes a cast of a type to itself (`if (!typecmp(src.cast, cast))`) and a constant 0 to any type but a struct or union (`else if (QCC_SRef_IsNull(src) && totype != ev_struct && totype != ev_union)`), and has no case for a struct, so `QCC_EvaluateCast` ends in `QCC_PR_ParseError(0, "Cannot cast from %s to %s", ...)`: `struct S { float a; }; S s = 1;`, `S s = 0;`, `S s; float x = s;` and `(struct S)0` in a body are "Cannot cast from float to struct S" and "from struct S to float". A struct's initialiser is an aggregate, `S s = { 1 };` (`else if ((type->type == ev_struct || type->type == ev_union) && QCC_PR_CheckToken("{"))` in `QCC_PR_ParseInitializerType_Internal`), or a value of the same type, `S t = s;`. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_TryEvaluateCast`, `QCC_EvaluateCast`, `QCC_PR_ParseInitializerType_Internal`.

A type has a size in words, `size`, and in bits, `bits`, with an alignment in bits, `align` (`QCC_PR_NewType`: `type_size[]` words, aligned to 32): one word for a float, a string, an entity, a field, a function, a pointer and a 32-bit integer, two for a 64-bit integer and a double, three for a vector and a `variant`; `__int8` and `__uint8` take 8 bits aligned to 8, `__int16` and `__uint16` 16 aligned to 16. `QCC_PR_ParseStruct` lays out a struct's members bit by bit after its parent's words, skipping a `static` member and one the parent has with the same name, size and type: a member with bits is aligned to its alignment, a bitfield (`int x : N`, of an integer's size and alignment, an `int` wider than 32 bits made 64) only where it would cross it, any other member to a word, and each takes its bits, or 32 a word, times its array's elements. A union's members all start at 0 and it takes the largest. The tail is padded to the largest alignment, the size is the bits rounded up to words, and the type keeps its bits when that alignment is no whole word. `sizeof` is the bits over 8 when they are no whole words, else 4 bytes a word: `struct { __int8 a[3]; }` is 3, `struct { __int8 a; __int16 b; }` 4, `struct { int a : 30; int b : 5; }` 8. The model lays out a struct whose array sizes and widths are numbers. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_lex.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseStruct`; `engine/qclib/qccmain.c`, `QCC_PR_NewType`, `type_size`.

A bitfield member (`int a : N`, FTEF-6.13) narrower than 32 bits is `ev_bitfld` with its bit offset in its word, `bitofs`, as the layout places it. Read, its word is read and extended (`QCC_BitfieldToDef`, `OP_BITEXTEND_I` for an `int`, `OP_BITEXTEND_U` for a `uint`, with `QCC_MakeUIntConst((bitofs<<8)|bits)`, which on a target without them is a left and a right shift, FTEF-27.7). Stored, but through a pointer, the word is read and the value packed into it (`QCC_PR_Statement_BitCopy`): `OP_BITCOPY_I` as a plain statement when the target has it, else `OP_BITAND_I` of the word with `~(((1u<<bits)-1u)<<bitofs)`, `OP_BITAND_I` of the value with `(1u<<bits)-1u`, `OP_LSHIFT_I` by `bitofs` and `OP_BITOR_I`, each folded or emulated as any: on the id target `x.a = 1;` for `struct S { int a : 3; } x;` is the two refused opcodes `BITAND_I` and `BITOR_I`, and `x.b = i;` for a second member at bit 3 also the `MUL_I` of the shift. Through a pointer it is loaded by its width (`QCC_LoadFromPointer`): `OP_LOADP_I8` or `OP_LOADP_U8` for 8 bits, the 16-bit loads for 16, and any other width the fatal error `E0353` "ptr-to-bitfld has unsupported bit depth". A pointer to `__int8`, `__uint8`, `__int16` or `__uint16` is read by the same loads (FTEF-27.10), its index made an integer first and 0 when there is none.

A struct's `static` member is no member but the global `STRUCT::NAME` of its type ("static members are technically just funny-named globals", `QCC_PR_GetDef(type, membername, ...)`, a constant only for a function), so `S::a = 1;` stores it, `float x = S::a;` is "initializer for 'x' is not constant", and `S::b` of an instance member is "Unknown value \"S::b\"". An array's only member is `length` (FTE-13), its elements' struct's members none, so `x.length` of an array of structs is its length and `x.a` "expected length, found a".

A struct member's array sizes are each `QCC_PR_IntConstExpr()` (`QCC_PR_ParseArrayType`), an integer constant, and a 0 is the fatal error `E0356` "cannot cope with 0-sized arrays": `float a[0]`, `a[0x0]` and `a[2][0]` are refused, `a[2.0]` and `a[-1]` are not, `a[1.5]` is `E0262` "Value is not an integer constant", and a name the module does not define, there or as a bitfield's width (FTEF-6.9), is "Unknown value \"A\"." and then that error. A defined name is taken as a constant; an expression of more than a literal or a name is not folded (FTEF-19.63).

A store through a pointer (`QCC_StoreToPointer`, the type the source's when the pointer points at a `variant`): to an 8- or 16-bit integer or a bitfield by `OP_STOREP_I8` or `OP_STOREP_I16`, any other width the fatal error `E0353` "ptr-to-bitfld has unsupported bit depth", a bitfield that does not start its word first the error `E0357` "left operand (NAME) has a bit offset" (not fatal). Otherwise, with an index on a target whose stores take no offset (`QCC_OPCode_StorePOffset`: FTE's formats before revision 5712 and DarkPlaces' before 20241108) the index is first added to the pointer by `OP_ADD_PIW`. A float, vector, entity, string, function or field is stored by its `OP_STOREP_*`; an integer by `OP_STOREP_I`, or else `OP_STOREP_FLD`; a 64-bit value by `OP_STOREP_I64`, or else two `OP_STOREP_FLD`, the second at the index plus 1 by `OP_ADD_I`, or with no offset the pointer plus 1 by `OP_ADD_PIW`; a pointer by `OP_STOREP_P`, `OP_STOREP_I` or else `OP_STOREP_FLD`. A struct or union (and any other type) is stored word by word: where stores take an offset, `OP_STOREP_V` for each three words when the target has it, then `OP_STOREP_I` (or else `OP_STOREP_F`) for each word left, each word's offset added to an index by `OP_ADD_I`; else the pointer offset to each by `OP_ADD_PIW` and `OP_STOREP_V` for each three, `OP_STOREP_I64` for each two when the target has it, and `OP_STOREP_F`. Each store is a `QCC_PR_SimpleStatement`, an opcode the target lacks the fatal error `E0320`. An 8- or 16-bit store the target lacks is emulated (`QCC_PR_Statement_SmallStore`): for `OP_STOREP_C` the value made a `uint`; the index (0 when there is none) split into the place in its word, `& 3` or `& 1`, and the word, `>> 2` or `>> 1`; the word read by `OP_LOADP_I`; the value masked by `0xff` or `0xffff` and shifted by `OP_LSHIFT_I` to its place (`OP_MUL_I` of the place by its bits), the mask shifted and inverted (`OP_BITNOT_I`), the word's bits there cleared by `OP_BITAND_I` and the two joined by `OP_BITOR_I`; and the word stored by `OP_STOREP_I`, or `OP_STOREP_F` when the target lacks it. Each is folded or emulated as any opcode (FTEF-27): on the id target `*pc = c;` for an `__int8 *pc` is the `memgetval` and `OP_LOADP_I` errors, two `OP_BITAND_I` and an `OP_BITOR_I`.

A member reached through a pointer is at an index (`QCC_PR_ParseRefArrayPointer`): its offset in units of its alignment (a word, or a byte or two for an 8- or 16-bit integer), with no index before it; with one, the index made an integer and multiplied by `OP_MUL_I` into the member's units when it is narrower than a word, then, unless the offset is 0, `OP_ADD_I` of it and the offset when the target has `OP_ADD_I`, else `OP_ADD_F` of it made a float and the offset as a float (times `32/align`). On the id target `pt[i].v = w;` for a `struct { float f; vector v; } *pt` is `OP_MUL_I` of `i` by 4 (FTEF-31.7), the index made a float for `OP_ADD_F` ("itof emulation") and made an integer again for the store ("ftoi emulation").

A member of a struct or union that is a value, not reached through a pointer (`st.f`, `sarr[1].f`), is the struct's own definition at the member's word (`QCC_PR_BuildRef` of its `sym` with the member's `ofs`), no temporary: its address is the struct's, refused on the id target with "Address-of operator is not supported in this form without extensions" and on the FTE target a pointer to the member, and `st.n == st.n` of an `int` member is the same operand twice, "Result of comparison is constant" on the id target (FTEF-28.1), where `st.n == st.m` is not.

An 8- or 16-bit integer read through its address (`OP_LOADP_I8`, `OP_LOADP_U8`, `OP_LOADP_I16`, `OP_LOADP_U16`) is a value of the opcode's type, `int` or `uint`, as its extension at a constant index is (FTEF-2.12): `x_s = carr[i];`, `x_s = *pc;` and `x_s = ps->c;` of `__int8`s warn "Implicit cast from __int32 to string", of `__uint16`s "from __uint32"; a bitfield read so keeps its type.

An 8- or 16-bit integer member of a struct is `ev_bitfld` (FTEF-2.12), read and stored as a bitfield of its width at bit 0 of the word that holds it (the member's `bitofs` is 0): on the id target `st.h = 1;` of a `__uint16 h` is the `OP_BITAND_I` and `OP_BITOR_I` of `QCC_PR_Statement_BitCopy`, with no shift, a read is `OP_BITEXTEND_U` by `(0<<8)|16`, and its address and a pointer's index to it count its bytes (FTEF-6.19).

A struct's member array named bare is its head (`REF_ARRAYHEAD`), with the member's first size as its length: `s.a[4]` of a `float a[3]` is "(constant) array index out of bounds (0 <= 4 < 3)". Its index is added to the member's word in the struct (`QCC_PR_ParseRefArrayPointer`'s `idx`, an `int` on a target with `OP_ADD_I` and else a float): `OP_ADD_F` when both are floats, else `OP_ADD_I` of both made integers, so on the FTE target `s.a[3.5]` warns "Numerical overflow. 3.500000 will be rounded to 3" and on the id target `s.a[i]` is `OP_ADD_I`'s refusal. An element at an index that is no constant is read by the struct's `ArrayGet` into its return, which for a struct of more than three words is returned through storage `OP_PUSH` makes, refused on a target without it. Through a pointer the element is read and stored through the pointer at that index (`ps->a[i]`), and the head is the pointer plus the member's offset in bytes by `OP_ADD_I`.

A call through a struct's function member reads the parameters of the member's type (`QCC_typeparam_s`): a parameter with a default may be left out, and a call that leaves out one with none warns "too few parameters on call to NAME, PARAM will be UNDEFINED", NAME the struct's definition, the member's `sym`: `w.get()` of a `float(entity e = __NULL__) get` is no warning, `w.two()` of a `float(float a) two` names `w`.

An error FTEQCC raises about an element of an aggregate initialiser that is itself braced stands where its `{` does, the token the parser has read: "inherited structs must use designated initialisers" and "member U.b was already ininitialised" are on the `{`'s line, whatever follows it on the next.

A bitfield's width is the signed `int bits` `QCC_PR_IntConstExpr()` gives, kept in the unsigned `bitfld->bits`: a negative width is no error ("too many bits" compares the signed value with 64, and no promotion to 64 bits happens for it), and the struct's layout adds it in C's unsigned arithmetic (`unsigned int bitsize`), which wraps: `struct S { int a : -1; int b; };` puts `b` at bit 0 and is one word, and `struct S { int a : -1; };` is of size 0.

A member of a struct or union of size 0 (`!t->size`), one named with no body yet or one laid out to no word, is the fatal error `E0362` "NAME was not defined yet" (`QCC_PR_ParseRefArrayPointer`), before any member is looked up: `struct T; T *pt;` makes `pt->a` that error, and `struct T2 { }; T2 t;` makes `t.a` "T2 was not defined yet", not "a is not a member of T2".

A struct or union with no tag (`struct { ... } x;`, `typedef struct { ... } T;`) is a type of its own, with its members and its layout, named `<struct>` or `<union>`: `t.zz` of one is "zz is not a member of <struct>", `sizeof(T)` of `typedef struct { float a; vector v; } T;` is 16, and since `typecmp` compares a struct by its size and name, two of them with the same size cast to each other (`A a; B b; a = b;` for two `typedef struct { float a; }`), and of different sizes are "Cannot cast from struct <struct> to struct <struct>".

A struct or union read through a pointer is read word by word (`QCC_LoadFromPointer`, `case ev_struct: case ev_union:`): `OP_LOADP_V` for each three of its words and `OP_LOADP_I` for each word after them, each a `QCC_PR_SimpleStatement`, which emulates nothing and refuses an opcode the target lacks with the fatal error `E0320` "Opcode \"=|LOADP_V\" not valid for target. ..." (the first refused ends the statement); with an index, each word's offset is added to it by `OP_ADD_I`. A member reached through a pointer, `p->a`, `p.a`, `(*p).a` or `p[0].a` for a `struct S *p`, is read by the load of its own type at its offset (FTEF-27.10), the pointer read first, so `(*pp)->a` loads `*pp` with `OP_LOADP_I` and then `a` with `OP_LOADP_F`. On the id target `local S y = *p;` is "Opcode \"=|LOADP_I\" not valid for target" for a one-word `S`, and `OP_LOADP_V` for one of four words.

A struct or union member that is a type with nothing after it but `;`, other than a struct's or union's, whose members it nests, is the warning `W0204` "declaration does not declare anything (TYPE)" (`WARN_POINTLESSSTATEMENT`), and declares nothing: `struct S { float; };`. A `virtual` member that is no function is the error `E0369` "[non]virtual members must be functions", which goes on (`if ((isnonvirt || isvirt) && type->type != ev_function)`; FTEQCC reads no `nonvirtual` in a struct). Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_lex.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseStruct`.

A name as a member's array size or bitfield width (`QCC_PR_IntConstExpr`) is an integer constant only when it names a constant: `float y; struct S { int a : y; };` and `float a[y];` are "Value is not an integer constant", as an unknown name is. An unknown name read there is defined a global `variant` (FTEF-19.71), "Unknown value \"NAME\".", so `float u = A;` after `struct S { float a[A]; };` is only "initializer for 'u' is not constant". Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_IntConstExpr`, `QCC_PR_ParseValue`.

`typedef OldType NewName;` defines `NewName` as another name for `OldType`. `QCC_TypeForName` resolves a name to its real type, following an `ev_typedef`'s `aux_type`. The corpus typedefs function types, pointer types and enum/struct types (187 `typedef` occurrences across the three mods).
A typedef name is usable wherever a type is (`QCC_PR_ParseType` resolves it through `QCC_TypeForName`): as a member type, a parameter type, a cast, or the base of a pointer or array.
