Codegen (later): a typedef is a front-end alias and emits nothing of its own (its underlying type's codegen applies); confirmed by L-01.

`QCC_PR_ParseDefs` loops over its declarators after `typedef` as it does after any type (`do { ... } while (QCC_PR_CheckToken (","));`), each one defining a type, with its `*`s, parameter lists, `(*name)(params)` and array dimensions, and no initialiser or body (`if (istypedef) { ...; def = NULL; continue; }`): `typedef float t, u;`, `typedef float t, *u;`, `typedef void() fn, fn2;`, `typedef struct S { float a; } T, *PT;` and `typedef enum { A } E, F;` define two types each. `typedef` is read among the qualifiers (`istypedef=true;` in the loop of storage classes) before or after the others and any number of times, so `typedef typedef float tt;` defines `tt`, and `local typedef float t;` in a body defines `t` there. After `typedef` the declarators are those of any definition: `typedef class C { float a; } CC;` is `QCC_PR_ParseEntClass`'s type (FTEF-9.8). Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseDefs`.

A definition whose type is a typedef of a function type is a function: `QCC_PR_ParseDefs` reads the type with `QCC_PR_ParseType`, which finds the typedef's type (`QCC_TypeForName`), and then tests the type, not its spelling (`type->type == ev_function`), so `{`, `[` and `#` after the declarator are the function's body, state header and builtin, and `= {` its body: `typedef void() fn; fn g = { return; };`, `fn g = #6;`, `fn g : 6;`, `fn g = [1, g] {};`, `typedef float(float) fn; fn g = { return 1; };`, `typedef void(float a) fn; fn g = { a = 1; };`, with `static` or `var`, in a body, as a class member or a struct's `static` or `virtual` member, in `extern "C"` and `extern "QC"` blocks, through a chain `typedef fn fn2;`, through a macro, and from a typedef a body makes, under no option, `-Fcaseinsens` and `qcfuncs` off; `fn g = { 1 };` is a body missing a `;`. The typedef's declarator may be C's `(*name)(params)` (FTEF-21.7) or `name(params)`, which make the function type. A typedef whose declarator is `(name)` is a function type whose parameter `name` is no type, "expected function arg list" as `T (name);` is (FTEF-19.35): `typedef float (t);` and `typedef float t; typedef t (u);` are refused. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseDefs`; `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_lex.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseType`.

`enumflags { A, B, C };` declares named constants whose unvalued members double rather than increment: FTEQCC's `QCC_PR_ParseEnum(flags=true)`, described in `qccmain.c` as "like enum, but doubles instead of adds 1." So `A, B, C` are 1, 2, 4. The corpus uses it for bit masks.

`enumflags`, like `enum`, takes an explicit value (`A = n`) that sets the running value, and an optional element type (`: int`); the typed and `enum class` forms resolve as FTE-15.2 states. A bare `enum`'s increment-by-one semantics are FTE-15.1.
Codegen (later): each enum name is a folded constant and the enum contributes no global of its own (as FTE-15.3 for the subset); confirmed by L-01.

An `enum` or `enumflags` where a type belongs always has its body: `QCC_PR_ParseType` sends both keywords to `QCC_PR_ParseEnum` (`else if (QCC_PR_CheckKeyword(keyword_enum, "enum")) type = QCC_PR_ParseEnum(false);`), which reads an optional `class`, a name or legacy base type and an optional `: type`, then `QCC_PR_Expect("{");` on every path that has not already read the `{` (`qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseEnum`). So `enum colour_e c;` and `typedef enum colour_e C;` are "expected {" errors; an enum is named elsewhere by its type name alone (FTE-15.4), `colour_e c;`.

`enum class` needs its base type: after `strictenum = QCC_PR_CheckName("class");` and the name, `QCC_PR_ParseEnum` reads `:` and the type, `else if (strictenum) QCC_PR_Expect(":");`, so `enum class E { A };`, `enum class { A };` and `enum class E;` are "expected :, found {" (or `;`), and `enum class E : float { A };` is an enum; FTE-15.2's `enum class` names are those of an enum with a base type. The declarators follow the body as they follow any type (FTEF-15.6): `enum E { A } x;` is `E x`, `enum { A } x;` a `float x` (the base), and `enum class E : float { A } x;` an `E x` that no float takes (FTEF-19.10). Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseEnum`.

A named enum that is not `enum class` makes a type of its name with its base's basic type, the first declaration's (`enumtype = QCC_TypeForName(name); if (!enumtype) ... enumtype = QCC_PR_NewType(name, basetype->type, true);`), while its names stay of the base type: a value of it casts as the base does and prints by its name, so `enum EN { A }; EN e; string s = e;` is `E0213` "Cannot cast from EN to string", `enum EN : int { A }` makes it `W0220` "Implicit cast from EN to string", `int i = e;` warns "ftoi emulation" as a float does, and `string s = A;` casts the null constant. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseEnum`.

`class Name { ... };` and `class Name : Parent { ... };` define an entity subtype whose members are entity fields, inheriting the parent's fields (`QCC_PR_ParseEntClass` reads an optional `: Parent`, requires the parent be a class/entity type, and sets `newt->parentclass`). `class Name;` with no body is a forward declaration.

A member function is declared with `virtual`, `nonvirtual` or `static` (`QCC_PR_ParseEntClass`'s keyword loop). A `virtual` function becomes an entity field that can be overridden per instance; a `nonvirtual` or `static` function is a global named `Class::member`. FTEQCC warns "`%s::%s` was not qualified. Assuming non-virtual." when a member function has no qualifier. `nonvirtual:` and `virtual:` as a label set the default for the following members (the "fteqcc-specific" `assumevirtual` path).

A non-function member is a field of the entity (`QCC_PR_ParseEntClass` builds an `ev_field` type per member and unions it into the class's field layout). `self.member` or `this.member` selects it. `const`, `var`, `static`, `ignore`/`strip` and the access labels `public`/`private`/`protected` are accepted qualifiers; access control is not enforced (the labels are read and ignored).

A member function body `Class::member = { ... }` or `= [frame, think] { ... }` defines it. A `nonvirtual`/`static` member has no implicit `this`; a `virtual` or plain member receives `this` as a pointer to the class (`QCC_PR_MakeThiscall` prepends a `this` parameter). A member whose name equals the class name is a constructor; FTEQCC warns if it is not `void`, takes arguments, or is `static`.
For each class with a constructor FTEQCC defines a `spawnfunc_Name` function so maps can spawn it (`QCC_PR_ParseEntClass`'s trailing `QCC_PR_GetDef("spawnfunc_%s", ...)`).
Codegen (later): the field layout, vtable and `this`-call lowering, and the version 7 requirement, are fixed by L-01.

`QCC_PR_ParseEntClass` reads a class's parent with `QCC_TypeForName`, so after `:` a name that is no type is the error `E0240` "Parent class NAME was not yet defined" (`QCC_PR_ParseError(ERR_NOTANAME, "Parent class %s was not yet defined", parentname);`), also for the class itself (`class C : C {`), and a type that is no entity (`if (fieldtype->type != ev_entity)`), a struct, an enum or `float`, is `E0241` "Parent type NAME is not a class/entity"; `entity`, a class and a typedef of one are parents. A class given its members again with a parent other than the first is `E0242` "Parent class changed on redeclaration of NAME" (`if (redeclaration && fieldtype != newt->parentclass)`). Under `-Fcaseinsens` the parent is found in any case (FTEF-19.33), so `class D : c` after `class C` is a class of `C`.

`QCC_PR_ParseType` reads `class` with `qcfuncs` on as the type `QCC_PR_ParseEntClass` makes (`if (flag_qcfuncs && QCC_PR_CheckKeyword (keyword_class, "class")) type = QCC_PR_ParseEntClass();`), wherever a type stands, and the declarators follow it as they follow any type. `class Name` with no `{` returns the type, a forward declaration (`forwarddeclaration = !QCC_PR_CheckToken("{")`), so `class C; class C x;`, `class C { float a; } x;`, `void() g = { class C x; };`, `class C *p;` and `void(class C x) h = #6;` define a variable; a parent needs the body (`QCC_PR_Expect("{")`), so `class D : C;` is "expected {"; a name `QCC_TypeForName` finds is that type, `class float x;` a `float` named x; and the name `QCC_PR_ParseName` reads must be one. A class given a body in a function's body is "Declaration of class %s%s%s within function". Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_lex.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseEntClass`.

In `QCC_PR_ParseEntClass`'s loop over a member's keywords `public:` and `private:` read one `:`, and `protected:` reads two (`QCC_PR_Expect(":"); ... QCC_PR_Expect(":");`), so `protected: float b;` is "expected :, found float" and `protected: : float b;` is a label; `virtual` and `nonvirtual` are labels only when a `:` follows (`firstkeyword && QCC_PR_CheckToken(":")`); a label is followed by the member (`basetype = QCC_PR_ParseType(false, false, false)` is "In class %s, expected type"), so a label at the `}` is "is not a type"; and a `;` where a member starts is "is not a type". A first token `,` is "member missing name". Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_lex.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseEntClass`.

A member given a value with `=` is read as a function's body or value (`havebody = true`); "Can only initialise member functions" when it is not of function type and not `static` (`const` makes a member static), unless the value is `0` or `0i` (`isnull`): `class C { float a = 1; };` is refused, `class C { float a = 0; };`, `class C { static float a = 1; };` and `class C { const float a = 1; };` are not, and `var` does not make one static. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_lex.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseEntClass`.

A member whose type is a `struct` or `union` is "Struct or union in class %s" (`if (basetype->type == ev_struct || basetype->type == ev_union)`), a pointer to one is not. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_lex.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseEntClass`.

`QCC_PR_ParseEntClass` finds the class's name with `QCC_TypeForName(classname)`: a type with members (`if (newt && newt->num_parms != 0) redeclaration = true;`), a struct or union among them, is a redeclaration, "Parent class changed on redeclaration of %s" when its parent is not the one given (`if (redeclaration && fieldtype != newt->parentclass)`): `struct S { float a; }; class S { float b; };`. Another type with a size, `float`, a typedef or an enum, is taken as the class (`if (!newt)` makes none) and given the members, and its `spawnfunc_NAME` is declared (`QCC_PR_GetDef(type_function, membername, NULL, true, 0, GDF_CONST)`) and, the type being no entity, never given a body, "function spawnfunc_float has no body" (FTEF-17.11): `class float { float a; };`, `typedef float T; class T { float b; };` and `enum E { A }; class E { float b; };` are refused, which this profile reports at the class's name as "Parent class changed on redeclaration of NAME" (`E0242`), the program being refused either way. A class given its members again in another case under `-Fcaseinsens` is the class (FTEF-19.33), whose members are compared (FTEF-9.7): `class C { float a; }; class c { float b; };` is "Incompatible redeclaration of class c. b differs." with it and two classes without. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_lex.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseEntClass`.

A class given its body again is compared with the first, member by member in order (`if (newt->params[i].arraysize != parms[i].arraysize || typecmp(newt->params[i].type, parms[i].type) || strcmp(newt->params[i].paramname, parms[i].paramname))`), "Incompatible redeclaration of class %s. %s differs." at the first that differs in name, type or array size, and "Incompatible redeclaration of class %s." when the count differs (`if (newt->num_parms != numparms)`): `class C { float a; }; class C { float b; };` and `class C { float a; }; class C { };` are refused, `class C { float a; }; class C { float a; };` and a forward `class C;` before either are not; under `-Fcaseinsens` `class c { float b; }` after `class C { float a; }` is the class given again (FTEF-9.12). A member's type is a type (`basetype = QCC_PR_ParseType(false, false, false)`, "is not a type"), and a struct or union by its name is "Struct or union in class" as by its keyword (FTEF-9.11): `class O { T x; };` with no type `T`, and `struct S { float a; }; class O { S x; };`, are refused. A `nonvirtual`, `static` or `ignore` member is a global of the class's or nothing, not among the members compared (`continue` before `parms[numparms]` is filled), and a member's array size is compared (`newt->params[i].arraysize != parms[i].arraysize`): `class C { float a; }; class C { float a[2]; };` and `class C { float a; }; class C { ignore float a; };` are refused. The constructor is the member named exactly as the class (`!strcmp(parmname, classname)`), under `-Fcaseinsens` too: `class c { C(); };` is "function c::c has no body" with it, the name `C` being the class's type there and no constructor. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_lex.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseEntClass`.

A class is an entity type (`QCC_PR_NewType(classname, ev_entity, ...)`), and an implicit cast between two entity types, a class either side, is made (`QCC_TryEvaluateCast`, `totype == ev_entity && src.cast->type == ev_entity`): with the warning `W0220` "Implicit cast from A to B" when neither the value's type nor a class it derives from is the target to `typecmp_lax` (`for (t = src.cast; t; t = t->parentclass) if (!typecmp_lax(t, cast)) break;`), a class with no parent class deriving from the entity. `typecmp_lax` compares no class names but a class's members, its `params`, as a function's parameters: as many on each side (`if (!a->params[t].optional) return 1;` past the shorter), each of one basic type, an entity or struct by its name and anything else by `typecmp_lax`; the members are those a redeclaration compares (FTEF-9.13), the class's own, no parent's, no `nonvirtual`, `static` or `ignore` one, and an entity has none. A type is itself (`if (a == b) return 0;`), so a class with a member of its own type compares. So `C c = e;` for an entity `e` warns "Implicit cast from entity to class C" when `C` has a member and not when it has none; a class to `entity` never warns, its chain ending at the entity; `D d = c;` for a `C c` and `class D : C` does not warn (`D`'s own members, `float b` against `C`'s `float a`, are one), and two unrelated classes warn when their members differ, `class C { float a; }` from `class D { string b; }` or from `class D { float a; nonvirtual void() m; }` with `C`'s `m` virtual. A cast written out, `(C)e`, never warns. A global initialised with one of a variable, `C c = (C)e;`, is no constant (FTEF-34.9).

A member function made `virtual` that a parent class has as a nonvirtual function is the error `E0350` "NAME defined as virtual in CLASS, but nonvirtual in PARENT" (`QCC_PR_ParseEntClass`, the first parent up the chain with a global `PARENT::NAME`), and the member is not defined: `class C { nonvirtual void() m = {}; }; class D : C { virtual void() m = {}; };` is refused.

A member function's qualifiers (`QCC_PR_ParseEntClass`): the member named exactly as the class, the constructor, warns `W0265` "Constructor CLASS::TOKEN should not be static." under `static` or `const`, "Constructor CLASS::TOKEN does not return void." when it returns a value and "Constructor arguments are not supported at this time CLASS::TOKEN. Use named fields instead." when it has parameters or `...`, TOKEN being the token after its name and array suffix (`pr_token`, as `=`, `;` or `,`). Any other member function with none of `virtual`, `nonvirtual`, `static` and `const`, and no `virtual:` or `nonvirtual:` label before it in the class (`assumevirtual == 0`), warns `W0265` "CLASS::NAME was not qualified. Assuming non-virtual." and is nonvirtual; one with more than one of `virtual`, `nonvirtual` and `static` or `const` is the error `E0351` "Multiple conflicting qualifiers on CLASS::TOKEN." (`if (isvirt+isnonvirt+isstatic != 1)`). A member function, virtual or not, that nothing defines is "function CLASS::NAME has no body" (FTEF-19.41), by the name it is defined as; an array of member functions is an array of fields and is not reported.

A class's `vector` data member, no array, is a `.vector` field, which has its components' fields too, `NAME_x`, `NAME_y` and `NAME_z` (`QCC_PR_GetDef` of a vector field makes them), so `c.v_x = 1;` stores one and `c.v_w` is "Unknown field \"v_w\" in class \"C\""; a `vector v[2]` member has none.

A class member that is no function written `virtual` or `nonvirtual` is "virtual keyword on member that is not a function", and one written `inline` "inline keyword on member that is not a function"; an `inline` member function with no body, or a virtual one, the class's default included, is "inline keyword on function prototype or virtual function". Each is a `QCC_Error`, which ends FTEQCC, the fatal error `E0379`, and a typedef of a function type makes a function. The words are those written, not the class's `virtual:` or `nonvirtual:` default. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_lex.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseClass`.

A `static` or `const` data member is the global `CLASS::NAME` of its type, no field, a `const` one a constant (`GDF_CONST`), and `CLASS::NAME` names a member through the class (`QCC_PR_GetDef` of `CLASS::NAME`): a data member that is no global is the field, of type `.TYPE`, and a function, `virtual` or not, the function `CLASS::NAME`, a constant. So `float x = C::a;` is "Cannot cast from .float to float" for `float a`, "initializer for 'x' is not constant" for `static float a`, and accepted for `const float a = 1`; `void() x = C::m;` is accepted for any member function `m`.

The `0` or `0i` a member that is no function may be given (FTEF-9.10) is the token's text (`QCC_PR_CheckImmediate("0") || QCC_PR_CheckImmediate("0i")`, a `STRCMP` with `pr_token`), not its value: `0x0`, `00`, `0.0` and `-0` are "Can only initialise member functions". A vector immediate is lexed component by component into `pr_token`, which keeps the last component's text, so `'1 0 0'` and `'0 0 0'` are taken and `'0 0 1'` is refused.

`accessor Name : Base { get ...; set ...; };` defines a type `Name` that is stored as `Base` (its parent type) but whose reads and writes go through get and set functions (`QCC_PR_ParseType`'s `accessor` branch builds an `ev_accessor` type whose `parentclass` is `Base` and whose size matches `Base`). `accessor Name : Base;` with no body declares the handle type alone, as `fteextensions.qc` does.

A `get` member defines the read function and a `set` the write (`QCC_PR_ParseAccessorMember`, keyed by `setnotget`); an optional `[IndexType]` makes it an indexed accessor (`name[i]` calls the getter or setter with the index). `inline` and `&`/`*` on the member select by-reference or by-pointer forms. The functions are named `Name::get_field` and `Name::set_field`.

Inside a `class` (FTEF-9), `get` and `set` members declare accessor members of that class (`QCC_PR_ParseEntClass` dispatches `isget`/`isset` to `QCC_PR_ParseAccessorMember`). Virtual and static accessors are rejected ("virtual accessors are not supported", "static accessors are not supported").
**Withdrawn** (P2-136, #587): it left an accessor's reads and writes to code generation; the check stage reads them. Replaced by FTEF-10.7.

`QCC_PR_ParseType` reads `accessor` among the types (`QCC_PR_CheckKeyword (keyword_accessor, "accessor")`), wherever a type stands: `typedef accessor B : float;`, `static accessor A : float;` and `accessor A : float x;` define or declare with the declarators that follow. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_lex.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseType`.

`accessor Name : Base` reads the base with `QCC_PR_ParseType(false, false, false)`, "is not a type" when it is none, and `QCC_PR_ParseError(ERR_NOTANAME, "Accessor %s cannot be based upon %s", ...)` when it is a struct or union (`if (!type || type->type == ev_struct || type->type == ev_union)`): `accessor A : struct S { float a; };` and `struct S { float a; }; accessor A : S;` are refused, `accessor A : float *;` is not. A name that is another type is "Type %s cannot be redefined as an accessor" (`if (newt && newt->type != ev_accessor)`), `typedef float A; accessor A : float;`, while a variable's name is free, `float A; accessor A : float;`. A later `accessor A : Base` with another base is "Accessor %s basic type mismatch (%s, expected %s)" (`else if (type != newt->parentclass)`), `accessor A : float; accessor A : vector;`, and with the same base is accepted; under `-Fcaseinsens` `a x;` after it is a variable of the accessor (FTEF-19.33). An accessor declared with its base where a class member's type stands, `class O { accessor A : float x; };`, ends FTEQCC too, which this profile reports as "Accessor A declared with its base in class O" (`E0258`). An accessor with no `:`, `accessor A;` or `accessor A : float; accessor A;`, reads the null `type` (`newt->size=type->size;`, `TypeName(type, ...)`) and ends FTEQCC, which the oracle records as refused; this profile reports "Accessor A cannot be based upon ??", the message of the path where `parentname` is "??". Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_lex.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseType`.

A member of a value whose type has accessor members, by name (`QCC_PR_ParseField`), is a reference to it (`QCC_PR_BuildAccessorRef`, `REF_ACCESSOR`), of the type of the member declared first, read-only as the value is; a member that takes an index is given one by `[...]`, and an accessor's nameless indexer by `value[...]`. A read calls its `get` function with the value and the index, made the indexer's type (`QCC_SupplyConversion`, "Implicit type mismatch. Needed float, got string.") or an integer 0 with none; with no `get` it is the fatal error `E0348` "Accessor NAME has no get function". A store calls its `set` function with the value, the index and the stored value, which is cast to the `set` member's type as an argument is ("Cannot cast from float to string"); with no `set` it is the fatal error `E0349` "Accessor has no set function". A name no member of the type has, on a type that is no entity, is `E0261` "NAME is not a member of TYPE" (`QCC_PR_ParseWarning(ERR_BADMEMBER, ...)`, so the read goes on), and the member is a `void` 0: `a = h.nope;` is then "Cannot cast from void to float".

An accessor type and its base cast to each other with the warning `W0264` "Implicit cast from A to B" (`QCC_EvaluateCast`, `cast->parentclass == src.cast`, the warning of code 0), a literal of the base's own type to the accessor too (`a = 1;` for an `accessor A : float`, not `a = 1i;`); a value of an accessor type is otherwise cast as its base's, and a cast to one is checked against its base, "Cannot cast from string to float" for an `accessor H : string`. No opcode takes an accessor (`(*op->type_a)->type != lhsd.cast->type`), so an operator's operand of one is cast to the opcode's type, `a * f` warning "Implicit cast from A to float", and `-a` is the fatal error "type mismatch for -" (FTEF-30.4). A member that takes an index is followed by its `[` (`QCC_PR_Expect("[")`), `a.z = f` the fatal error "expected [, found =". A member's body is a function (`QCC_PR_GenFunctionType`) whose `this` is of the accessor's type, whose index is of its indexer's and whose `value`, for `set`, is of the member's, and is checked as any function's body is: `bufstr_get(this, idx)` with a `float` parameter warns "Implicit cast from strbuf to float".

`QCC_PR_ParseAccessorMember` reads a member's type as a type's name and its `*`s, so a parameter list after it stands where the `=` is expected: `get float() x = {};` and `set void(float v) y = {};` are the fatal error `E0204` "expected =, found (".

In a class, `get` and `set` are among the qualifiers `QCC_PR_ParseClass` reads before a member's type, in any order with `nonvirtual`, `virtual`, `static`, `const`, `var`, `ignore`, `strip` and `inline`, and either makes the member an accessor's, a `set` one when `set` is among them: `virtual get float x = { ... };` and `get virtual float x`. `virtual` among them is the error `E0377` "virtual accessors are not supported at this time", which reads on, and `static` or `const` the fatal error `E0378` "static accessors are not supported". A name after the type is the member's, `get` and `set` included. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_lex.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseClass`.

An accessor member whose value is a name, `get float x = g;`, declares that function with the member's function type (`QCC_PR_GetSRef(functype, funcname, NULL, true, 0, GDF_CONST)`): `this` of the accessor's or class's type, then the index and for `set` the value, returning the member's type or for `set` nothing. So a definition of the name with another type, before the member or after it, is "Type mismatch on redeclaration of g. float(A this), should be float()", in the order the two are read, and a name nothing defines is a function with no body. The name stays a reference to the function. The `=` is required (`QCC_PR_Expect("=")`): a member with neither a body nor a function is "expected =, found ;". This profile compares an accessor's or class's type with any other as `fteqcc_same` does, so a function that differs from the member's only in such a parameter is not reported. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_lex.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseAccessorMember`.

A second `get` or `set` member of one name defines its function again: `QCC_PR_ParseAccessorMember` parses the body into the definition with no test that it has one (`f = QCC_PR_ParseImmediateStatements(...); def.sym->initialized = 1;`), so `get float x = { return 1; }; get float x = { return 2; };` in an accessor or a class is no "redeclaration of function body". A function defined twice outside an accessor still is. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_lex.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseAccessorMember`.

`__variant` is a type that any other type is compatible with: `typecmp_lax` returns "equivalent" whenever either side is `ev_variant` ("variants and args don't make sense, and are considered equivelent(ish)"). It is used for generic parameters and return values, and `__variant *` (FTEF-4) for untyped memory.
An assignment or call that mixes `__variant` with a concrete type resolves without a type error, because of FTEF-11.1; the concrete type governs the operation.
Codegen (later): how a `__variant` value is stored and dispatched is fixed by L-01.

FTEF-11.1 holds only after `typecmp_lax` compares the two types' `aux_type`s (`if (typecmp_lax(a->aux_type, b->aux_type)) return 1;` comes before the `ev_variant` return), so a `__variant` differs from a pointer or a function, whose `aux_type` it lacks: `float **p; __variant *q; q = p;` and `void() *r; q = r;` are `W0220` "Implicit cast from float** to __variant*", as is `p = q;`, while `__variant **t; t = p;` and `string *s; q = s;` cast with no warning.

`#pragma TARGET name` chooses the output target (`QCC_PR_Precompiler`, the `TARGET` case, calling `QCC_OPCodeSetTargetName`); it warns "Unknown target ... Ignored." and lists `ID, HEXEN2, FTE, FTEH2, KK7, DP(patched)` for an unknown one. The corpus uses it 28 times.

`#pragma PROGS_DAT path` (and the lowercase `progs_dat`, and `#pragma output`) sets the output file unless the command line named one (`QCC_PR_Precompiler`, the `PROGS_DAT` and `output` cases, calling `QCC_JoinPaths` into `destfile`). `#pragma PROGS_SRC` is accepted and silently ignored. The corpus uses `PROGS_DAT`/`progs_dat` 26 times.

`#pragma sourcefile path` registers an additional source file to compile (`QCC_PR_Precompiler`, the `sourcefile` case, calling `QCC_RegisterSourceFile` for each parsed name). The corpus uses it 9 times.
**Withdrawn** (P2-116, #544): it gave the form as `#pragma flag name on|off`, but `QCC_PR_Precompiler` reads the state first and then the names. Replaced by FTEF-12.11.

`#pragma forcecrc n` forces the progs definitions CRC ([`progs.md`](progs.md) PROGS-5) to `n` (`QCC_PR_Precompiler`, both the `#pragma forcecrc` sub-case and the top-level `#forcecrc` directive, setting `ForcedCRC`). The corpus uses it 4 times.

`#pragma noref n` and `#pragma nosave n` set the file-wide defaults for the `noref` and `nosave` qualifiers (`QCC_PR_Precompiler`, setting `defaultnoref` and `defaultnosave`); `nosave` is FTE-12's qualifier applied by default. The corpus uses `noref` 2 times.

FTEQCC recognises further `#pragma` names the corpus does not currently use but which the FTEQCC profile must accept without error (`QCC_PR_Precompiler`'s remaining sub-cases): `optimise`/`optimize`, `opcode`, `autoproto`, `once`, `file`, `line`, `includedir`, `defaultstatic`, `framerate`, `compress`, `copyright`, `wrasm`, `DONT_COMPILE_THIS_FILE`. An unrecognised `#pragma` is accepted with the warning "Unknown pragma '%s'" (as FTE-16.2), not an error.
**Withdrawn** (P2-42, #429): it said a later `#pragma autoproto` reports nothing, but FTEQCC warns for it. Replaced by FTEF-12.10.

**Withdrawn** (P2-132, #569): it said a `#pragma autoproto` is taken only before any definition and otherwise warns, but `numpr_globals` is `RESERVED_OFS` for the whole parse, so FTEQCC takes it wherever it stands and never warns. Replaced by FTEF-12.18.
**Withdrawn** (P2-116, #544): it said a `#pragma` does not affect the token stream, but `#pragma flag` turns on and off flags `QCC_PR_Lex` reads. Replaced by FTEF-12.12.

The build pragmas are read as `QCC_PR_Precompiler` reads them, against FTEQCC's tables (`qc_preproc`'s `fte_tables.rs`, written out of `qccmain.c` and `qcc_pr_comp.c`), each warning FTEQCC gives being its Q120 (`WARN_BADPRAGMA`, `W0113`) unless said otherwise. `#pragma flag STATE NAME ...`, and `keyword`, reads its text with `QCC_COM_Parse`: STATE `enable` or `on` turns each NAME on and `disable` or `off` off, in any case; any other STATE is "compiler flag state not recognised" and sets nothing. Each NAME is the first row of `compiler_flag[]` whose `abbrev` it is in any case (`QC_strcasecmp`), "keyword/flag NAME not recognised" when none is, and "Cannot enable/disable keyword/flag via a pragma" when the row lacks `FLAG_MIDCOMPILE` (`acc`, `parms`, `autoproto`, `wasm`, `caseinsens`, `int`, `integer`). The flags start as `QCC_main` sets them, `FLAG_ASDEFAULT` on, and `QCC_SetDefaultProperties` does not set them again, so a pragma's setting holds into the second autoprototyping pass (`qc_preproc::FlagSettings`). `#pragma optimise` (or `optimize`) with a level `0` to `3`, or a text starting `addon` or `mutator` in any case, sets the optimisations; any other text, after an optional `no-`, is matched in any case against `optimisations[]`' `abbrev` and `fullname`, "pragma NAME: TEXT unsupported" when it matches none (NAME the pragma's name as written). `#pragma opcode STATE NAME ...` takes `enable`, `on`, `disable` or `off` ("opcode state not recognised" for any other) and names `pr_opcodes[]`' `opname`s in any case, "opcode NAME is internal" for one past `OP_NUMREALOPS` and "opcode NAME not recognised" for none. `#pragma TARGET NAME` takes its first token, a `targets[]` name in any case with an optional `_` and revision (`fte_5768`): an unknown one is "Unknown target 'NAME'. Ignored." and a line "Valid targets are: ID, HEXEN2, FTE, FTEH2, KK7, DP(patched)", and a revision past the format's highest "target revision N is unknown, assuming revision M", both warnings with no name (`W0117`). Any pragma name `QCC_PR_Precompiler` does not know is "Unknown pragma 'NAME'". The pinned FTEQCC (`fteqcc -Tid`) gives each of these warnings with this text for `#pragma foo`, `#pragma flag enable foo`, `#pragma flag maybe hashonly`, `#pragma flag enable acc`, `#pragma optimise foo`, `#pragma opcode foo`, `#pragma opcode on STORE_F foo`, `#pragma TARGET XYZ` and `#pragma TARGET fte_99999`. Two warnings depend on what the compiler has made so far, which the preprocessor does not know, and are not modelled: `optimise` inside a function ("unable to change optimisation options mid-function") and a `TARGET` that switches to or from Hexen II after the first statement. The pragmas' effects on the build are the compiler's (FTEF-12.17).

Seven of the flags `#pragma flag` sets (FTEF-12.11) change how FTEQCC lexes, and hold from the token after the directive: `QCC_PR_Lex` reads each token as the parser asks for it, with the flags of that moment (`qc_lexer::LexFlags`, `qc_lexer::lex_flagged`). The pinned FTEQCC (`fteqcc -Tid`) gives each result below. `qcfuncs` (`flag_qcfuncs`, on by default): with it off, `\0` to `\7` in a string are C's octal escape, the digit and up to two more octal digits (`if (flag_qcfuncs) c = 0xe012 + c - '0'; ... else //C compat`), and `\8` or `\9` is the error "Bad character code \8" (`E0103`). `qccx` (`flag_qccx`): a `:` after a string part, comments before it passed over, writes a NUL into the string and reading goes on (`if (flag_qccx && *pr_file_p == ':') { pr_file_p++; pr_token[len++] = 0; continue; }`), so `"a":"b"` is the string `a`, NUL, `b`; a character constant is a float whose bits are its code, with "char constant: denormal" (F313, `WARN_DENORMAL`, an error by default, `W0121`); `%` before a digit or `-` is "denormalized immediate" (F313) and a float whose bits are the `int` `QCC_PR_LexInteger` reads after it, `atoi` of `0x` and the digits, `a` to `f` and `.` that follow, so a hex `%0x5` is 0; and a hex number with no suffix goes to `qccxhex`: a float whose bits are the number's low 32 bits, with "numerical overflow" (`W0111`) where those bits are not the number and are no negative `int`. `utf8` (`flag_utf8strings`): a plain string is read and written as `u8"..."` is (`stringtype = flag_utf8strings?2:0;`), so a byte that starts no UTF-8 sequence is "Input string is not valid utf-8". `ILP32` (`flag_ILP32`): a number needs `ll` to be 64 bits (`islong >= (flag_ILP32?2:1)`), so `0x100000000l` is an `int` with "numerical overflow". `ssp` (`flag_dblstarexp`): `**` is the token `*^`, with "** is unsafe around pointers, use *^ instead." (F321, `WARN_GMQCC_SPECIFIC`, `W0118`). `assumeint` (`flag_assume_integer`): a number with no suffix and no `.` is an integer, with no float's "numerical overflow ... will be rounded", and a character constant is an integer, `qccx` aside; its value stays a float (FTEF-13.5), and "Numerical truncation" when such an integer becomes a float is the compiler's. `macroinstrings` (`flag_macroinstrings`): a `#` in a string starts a name that runs to white space or one of `)(+-*/\|&=^~[]"{};:,.#`; `QCC_PR_CheckCompConstString` looks it up and then looks up each macro's text as a name again for as long as it names a macro, and the text it ends on is written into the string as it is, trailing spaces and tabs dropped, with "Macro NAME expansion in string" (`WARN_MACROINSTRING`, `W0122`); a name of no macro writes the `#` as a byte and is "Unable to expand string macro NAME" unless empty, and a string the text would take to 8191 bytes or more is "String length exceeds 8191" (`E0502`). So with `#define FOO bar` and two spaces and `#define BAR FOO`, `"a#BAR.c"` is `abar.c`. A deliberate divergence: the lookup stops after 64 macros, as FTEQCC's recursion has no bound and never returns for a macro whose text names itself. The preprocessor lexes the rest of a text again when the flags change, or under `macroinstrings` when a macro is defined or undefined, and marks each change by token in `FileOutput::flags`, which `qc_syntax::parse_preprocessed_flagged` reads to lex the preprocessed text again as FTEQCC lexed it.

Two flags change the preprocessor's reading. `hashonly` (`flag_hashonly`): a name is a macro's or a built-in constant's only after a `#` (`if (flag_hashonly || !QCC_PR_CheckCompConst()) QCC_PR_LexName ();`), so with `#define FOO 5`, `FOO` is the name `FOO` and `#FOO` is `5`. `nofileline` (`flag_nopragmafileline`): `#pragma file` and `#pragma line` change nothing (`if (!flag_nopragmafileline)`).

**Withdrawn** (P2-118, #549): it said `caseinsensitive` and `assumedouble` are not modelled, but the semantic model reads them (FTEF-19.24, FTEF-19.25), and the command line that sets `acc` and `caseinsens` is read (FTEF-14.71). Replaced by FTEF-12.15, itself replaced by FTEF-12.16.
**Withdrawn** (P2-119, #554): it said the keyword flags are not read, but the parser reads each keyword with the flags in force at its token (FTEF-20). Replaced by FTEF-12.16.
**Withdrawn** (P2-121, #556): it said `cpriority` is not modelled, but the parser reads the priorities it sets (FTEF-21.4). Replaced by FTEF-12.17.

The other flags `qcc_pr_lex.c` reads are not modelled, as they belong to the compiler or its console output rather than to the tokens or the definitions: `acc` (its `|` in a string as a line feed, and reacc's type names and keywords, FTEF-19.63, FTEF-20.13); and `msvcstyle` and `debugmacros`, which change only what FTEQCC prints. The keyword flags, which `#pragma keyword` and `#pragma flag` set with the others, are FTEF-20's, and the flags the parser and the semantic model read, `cpriority` among them, FTEF-21's. A pragma emits no progs output of its own (as FTE-16.3); its effects on the output (the target format, the CRC, the flags) are realised by codegen (L-01).

`#pragma autoproto [N]` is taken wherever it stands in the first pass. `QCC_PR_Precompiler` reads it as `if (!autoprototyped) { if (numpr_globals != RESERVED_OFS) QCC_PR_ParseWarning(WARN_BADPRAGMA, "#pragma autoproto must appear before any definitions"); else autoprototype = *msg?!!atoi(msg):true; }`, and no definition changes `numpr_globals`: only `QCC_FinaliseDef`, which `QCC_UnmarshalLocals` runs when `QCC_FinishCompile` ends the compile, and `QCC_FinaliseTemps` add to it (`numpr_globals += def->symbolsize;`), `#merge` itself calling it "not normally changed until after compiling". So `void() f = #5;`, `float x;`, `typedef float t;` and a function with a body before the pragma leave it as it was, and the warning is never given while FTEQCC parses (this profile gives none; `W0108` is only the class `#pragma warning` names, FTEF-14.63). `autoprototype` starts false (`parseonly = autoprototyped = autoprototype = false;` in `QCC_main`, once per `progs.src`) or as `-Fautoproto` sets it (FTEF-14.72), and as a list-form `progs.src`'s pragma sets it: that file is read through the preprocessor (`QCC_ContinueCompile` calls `QCC_PR_LexWhitespace(false)` before each entry), so its pragma, as Copper's has, holds for the whole module. Each `#pragma autoproto` of the first pass then sets it from the token after it, across the module's files and `#include`s in compilation order, `autoproto 0` off and any other number or none on. FTEQCC makes the second pass if the flag is on when the first ends (`if (autoprototype) { qccmsrc = originalqccmsrc; autoprototyped = autoprototype; QCC_SetDefaultProperties(); autoprototype = false; ...`), and in the second pass the pragma is skipped without a word (`if (!autoprototyped)`). So `float x; #pragma autoproto` is a two-pass compile, `#pragma autoproto` and then `#pragma autoproto 0` is a one-pass compile, and `-Fautoproto` with a last `#pragma autoproto 0` is a one-pass compile whose functions are all skipped (FTEF-12.19).

The first pass reads each declaration with `autoprototype` as it is at its `=`. While it is on, `QCC_PR_ParseDefs` makes the definition and skips what initialises it (`if (autoprototype || dostrip || ...) { //ignore the code and stuff`): a frame header `[ ... ]`, a body `{ ... }` balanced, a string's `_("...")`, or the tokens to the next `,` or `;`, a builtin's `#` and number among them, and then `QCC_FreeDef`s it. The definition is made as the written `=` decides its constness (`isinitialised = QCC_PR_CheckToken ("=") || ...`, then `GDF_CONST` unless `assumevar`), and is not initialised, so `float x = 5; float y = x;` is read as it is without the pragma, and the value is not checked: a name used in a skipped body or value is not looked up, and the lexical errors of its tokens are still the lexer's. While it is off, the declaration is compiled in full, so an error in it, such as `Unknown value "h"` for a name defined after it, is the first pass's, and a function body in it is compiled. The second pass compiles everything again with every name the first pass made defined: a function with a body from the first pass that is given a body again is "redeclaration of function body" and "incompatible redeclaration" (a builtin, a prototype or a body the first pass skipped is not), and a value is compared with the first pass's as FTE-22.6 says. When no second pass follows, a function whose body was skipped is "function NAME has no body" (`ERR_NOFUNC`), which this profile reports as QC-11.8's "NAME was not defined" (`E0211`). This profile reads the first pass as its own file (its flags, keywords and warning settings, FTEF-12.20), declares what it skips uninitialised, and reports once what both passes report, but for the parse diagnostics of the skipped initialisers.

The second pass starts with what the first pass ended with, but for what `QCC_SetDefaultProperties` sets again: the compiler flags, which `QCC_main` set once (FTEF-12.11), the keywords (FTEF-20.1), the operator priorities (FTEF-21.4), the pragma defaults `noref` and `nosave` (`defaultstatic` is 0, FTEF-21.14) and the definitions the first pass made carry; the macros (FTE-22.3), the warning settings (FTEF-14.63) and the target (FTEF-20.3) are the command line's again. The preprocessor marks the second pass's first token with the flags the first pass ended with, and the second pass is lexed, parsed and its definitions made with them: `#pragma autoproto` and `float x = 5; float y = x;` followed by `#pragma flag enable assumevar` is the redeclaration of x as non-constant (F329) and not "is not constant", `string s = B;` after an enum of `float` names, with `assumeint` on at the end, reads `B` as an `__int32` (F314), and `[[eraseable]] float x;` before a last `#pragma flag enable attributes` is refused by the first pass, where `attributes` is off.

The first pass gives a parameter no default that names a definition: `QCC_PR_ParseDefaultInitialiser` reads it, and of a value not initialised `if (autoprototype) return nullsref;`, and the pass initialises no definition (FTEF-12.19). The definition keeps the first pass's type, which the second pass's, with the default, matches (FTEF-19.7), so a call that leaves the parameter out warns "too few parameters" (FTEF-32.3). A literal default is initialised and stays. Copper's `T_RadiusDamage` takes `float dmgtype = DMGTYPE_EXPLOSION`.
`::` is one token. `pr_punctuation[]` lists `"::"` before `":"`, as its rule says: "longer symbols must be before a shorter partial match".

A `\` directly before a line break joins the lines: the token is skipped with the break, in `QCC_PR_LexPunctuation`'s `if ((unsigned char)*pr_file_p == (unsigned char)'\\' && pr_file_p[1] == '\r' && pr_file_p[2] == '\n') pr_file_p+=3;` and the same for a lone `\r` or `\n` (`pr_file_p+=2`). The corpus continues declarations this way (`const string g_spray_mat_1 = \`, `shared/environment/Spraylogo.h`).

A `'` opens a character constant when the next byte is `\` (an escape, FTEF-13.13), a byte of 0x80 or more (a UTF-8 sequence, FTEF-13.14), or a byte followed by `'`: `QCC_PR_LexVector` reads `if (*pr_file_p == '\\') {//extended character constant`, the `utf8_check` branch, and `else if (pr_file_p[1] == '\'') {//character constant`. Its value is the character's code, a float unless `flag_assume_integer`. Otherwise the `'` opens a vector, which may stop after two components, the third 0, with FTEQCC's warning "2d vector" (`if (*pr_file_p == '\'' && i == 1)`).

**Withdrawn** (P2-72, #475): it said every code above one byte is written to a string as UTF-8, which only a UTF-8 string does, and that `\{` stops quietly at a byte that is no digit. Replaced by FTEF-13.8 to FTEF-13.11 for strings and FTEF-13.12 for character constants.

This parse-and-resolve profile keeps every number token of FTEF-3 as a float holding its value (an integer rounded to the nearest float), and every character constant as a float holding its code: the literal's FTEQCC type (FTEF-3.1, FTEF-3.3) matters only to type checking and code generation, which are later (L-01).

A vector's components are read by `QCC_PR_LexFloat`, which takes the bytes of a number and then skips one lowercase `f` only: `if (*pr_file_p == 'f') pr_file_p++;` (`qcc_pr_lex.c`, `QCC_PR_LexFloat`). So `'1f 2f 3f'` is the vector `'1 2 3'`, and an `F` after a component is no suffix: it is read as the next component, and the vector is bad (QC-5.2).

A string literal starts at `"`, and at `R"`, `Q"`, `u"`, `U"` and `u8"`: `QCC_PR_Lex` has `if (c == '\"' || ((c == 'R' || c == 'Q' || c == 'u' || c == 'U') && pr_file_p[1] == '\"') || (c == 'u' && pr_file_p[1] == '8' && pr_file_p[2] == '\"')) QCC_PR_LexString ();`. `QCC_PR_LexString` reads parts in a loop, skipping white space and comments before each (`QCC_PR_LexComment`), and takes those prefixes and `L"` too (`(*pr_file_p == 'U' || *pr_file_p == 'u' || *pr_file_p == 'L') && pr_file_p[1] == '\"'`), so `L"..."` is a string only after another part: `"ex_" L"a"` is `ex_a`, and a lone `L"a"` is the name `L` and a string. The prefix belongs to the part's token, and the parts join as FTEF-16.8 says. The vanilla dialect reads each prefix as a name.

A part's prefix sets its `stringtype`: a plain string, with no `-Futf8` (`flag_utf8strings` is off by default), and `R"..."` are 0, "quake output, input is 8bit"; `Q"..."` is 1, "quake output, input is utf-8"; `u8"..."`, `u"..."`, `U"..."` and `L"..."` are 2, "utf-8 output, input is utf-8" (`u`, `U` and `L` with the warning "char32_t/char16_t/wchar_t strings are not supported, treating as u8 prefix (as utf-8)"). A byte of 0x80 or more starts a UTF-8 sequence only in types 1 and 2, read by `utf8_check`: two bytes for 0 (modified UTF-8) or 0x80 to 0x7FF, three for 0x800 to 0xFFFF (surrogates included), four for 0x10000 to 0x10FFFF; any other byte is itself. Type 2 writes each code as UTF-8 (`forceutf8`), in as many bytes as its size needs with no check that it is a Unicode scalar; types 0 and 1 write it as one Quake byte (`forcequake`): a code from 0xE000 to 0xE0FF as its low byte, Quake's glyph, any other as its low byte too (`pr_token[len] = c;`), above 0x7F with the warning "Cannot convert codepoint %#x to quake's charset". So `"\["` is the byte 0x10 and `u8"\["` the three bytes of U+E010, `Q"é"` is 0xE9 and `u8"é"` C3 A9, `"\{256}"` is a NUL and `u8"\xc0\x80"` written as bytes is one NUL. A code of 0x80000000 or more given to `forceutf8` (`\U80000000` or more, in any string, FTEF-13.11) makes FTEQCC loop for ever: `t <<= 5` reaches 0 and `while (c >= t)` never ends; this profile writes it in 7 bytes, and `cargo xtask oracles builtins` counts the pinned FTEQCC, killed after 20 seconds, as differing as this statement says.

A raw string, `R"delim(...)delim"`, takes the bytes up to `(` as its delimiter, at most 62 (`char rawdelim[64]` from index 1, "EOF while parsing raw string delimiter. Expected: R\"delim(string)delim\"" at the end of the file or the 63rd byte, `E0101`), skips a `\` and line break right after the `(` ("generally part of the C preprocessor"), and then keeps every byte as it is, line breaks, backslashes and `"` included, up to the first `)` followed by the delimiter and `"`; the end of the file first is "EOF inside quote".

In a string that is not raw, `\s` and `\b` stand for no character and toggle bronze text for the characters after them (`texttype ^= 0xe080`). A byte read as itself (FTEF-13.8) from a space up gets the high bit (`if (c >= ' ') c |= texttype;`), so a tab stays a tab and a byte of 0x80 or more is unchanged; in types 1 and 2 an ASCII character from a space up becomes the code `0xE080` with it (`cp|0xe080`), a Quake glyph, and a character above ASCII keeps its bytes ("Unable to mask non-ascii chars. Attempting to mask bytes"). So `"\ba"` is 0xE1 and `u8"\ba"` the UTF-8 of U+E0E1. `\.` is `0xe01c | texttype`; the codes of the other escapes take no bronze.

An escape in a string is read by `QCC_PR_LexEscapedCodepoint`: `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, `\a`, `\v`, `\f` and `\#`, `\"`, `\\`, `\?`, `\'` (FTE-20.4); `\[` and `\]` 0xE010 and 0xE011; `\.`, `\<`, `\-` and `\>` 0xE01C to 0xE01F; `\(`, `\=`, `\)` and `\+` 0xE080 to 0xE083 ("quake specific"); a digit 0xE012 plus the digit under `flag_qcfuncs`, on by default ("yellow numbers"); `\{n}` and `\{xN}` the decimal or hex code up to the `}`, with "Bad character code" at any other byte, the end of the file included; `\u` and `\U` up to four or eight hex digits, then `if (nibbles) QCC_PR_ParseWarning(ERR_BADCHARACTERCODE, "Unicode character terminated unexpectedly");`, which the pinned FTEQCC reports as an error; since `while (nibbles --> 0)` leaves `nibbles` at `UINT_MAX` when every digit is read, the only form with no error stops one digit short (`\u041` and a byte that is no hex digit); `\x` one or two hex digits, "Bad character code" with none; a `\` before a line break that break; a `\` before CR the byte after the CR; anything else "Unknown escape char". This profile reports "Bad character code" as `E0103`, the code of "Unknown escape char" (QCD-2.3). The code of `\u` and `\U` is written as UTF-8 in any string ("\u is a utf-8 code regardless of output encoding") and that of `\x` as one byte in any ("an explicit byte regardless of encoding"); any other as FTEF-13.8 says for the string's type.

**Withdrawn** (P2-75, #480): it said this profile takes a character constant's escape with no code of its own as its byte, with no error, and reports no "Bad character code" there. Replaced by FTEF-13.13.

A character constant's escape, `'\c'`, is read as a string's is (FTEF-13.11), errors included: `QCC_PR_LexVector` reads `if (*pr_file_p == '\\') {//extended character constant` and then `pr_immediate._float = QCC_PR_LexEscapedCodepoint();` (`_int` under `flag_assume_integer`), the function a string's escapes go through. The constant's value is the code: `'\n'` is 10, `'\['` 0xE010, `'\.'` 0xE01C and `'\x4'` 4. "Unknown escape char" (`'\s'`, `'\b'` and `'\q'`: only a string reads `\s` and `\b`, as bronze, FTEF-13.10), "Bad character code" (`'\{6z}'`, `'\xg'`) and "Unicode character terminated unexpectedly" (`'\u0041'`; `'\u041'` is 65) are errors, `E0103` as in a string. The end of the file right after the `\` is "EOF inside quote" (`E0101`), and no other error; after a `\` and CR FTEQCC takes the NUL as the byte after the CR (`c = *pr_file_p++;`) and reads on past it, and this profile reports `E0101` there too. Any other byte than `'` after the escape is "Bad character constant" (`if (*pr_file_p != '\'') QCC_PR_ParseError (ERR_INVALIDVECTORIMMEDIATE, "Bad character constant");`, `E0104`). FTEQCC stops at its first error; this profile goes on after the escape, and so may also report "Bad character constant" after a bad one.

A character constant at a byte of 0x80 or more is read by `utf8_check` (FTEF-13.8): `int b = utf8_check(pr_file_p, &pr_immediate._int);` then `pr_file_p+=b+1;`. Its value is the sequence's code, a surrogate or the modified UTF-8 NUL included, and the byte after the sequence is skipped unread, as the closing `'` it should be, so `'éx` is 233. A byte that starts no sequence `utf8_check` takes (`*value = 0xFFFD; return 0;`) is the code 0xFFFD and is skipped alone, so a `'` after it opens a vector. Recorded with the pinned FTEQCC (`fteqcc -Tid` on `void() f = :'...';`, reading `f`'s `first_statement`): `'é'` (C3 A9) and `'éx` bind 233, `'\xed\xa0\x80'` 55296, `'\xc0\x80'` 0 and `'\xf0\x90\x80\x80'` 65536; `'\xff;` binds 65533; `'\xff'`, `'\xe9'` and `'\xc1\x81'` are "Bad vector" at the `'` after the byte. The bytes are written here as `\x` escapes.

White space between tokens is only what FTEQCC's `qcc_iswhite` takes, `#define qcc_iswhite(c) ((c) == ' ' || (c) == '\r' || (c) == '\n' || (c) == '\t' || (c) == '\v')` (`cmdlib.h`), where id's lexer takes every byte up to the space as a signed `char` (QC-2.1). So under this profile any other control byte, a form feed or 0x01, and DEL, starts no token and is "Unknown punctuation: '\x%x'" (`QCC_PR_LexPunctuation`, `QCC_PR_ParseWarning (ERR_UNKNOWNPUCTUATION, "Unknown punctuation: '\\x%x'", *pr_file_p);`), `E0105` with FTEQCC's text, the byte in lowercase hex: the pinned FTEQCC refuses `float` and a form feed before `x;` ("Unknown punctuation: '\xc'"), and accepts two vertical tabs between definitions. Reading goes on after the byte, as FTEQCC's `pr_file_p++; QCC_PR_Lex();` does. A byte of 0x80 or more is a name's (FTEF-13.16), never white space.

A name starts at an ASCII letter, `_` or a byte of 0x80 or more (`QCC_PR_Lex`, `if ( (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') || c == '_' || (c & 0x80))`) and `QCC_PR_LexName` reads it a character at a time, each a UTF-8 sequence `utf8_check` reads (FTEF-13.8, ASCII bytes one each), while the byte after is a letter, a digit, `_` or of 0x80 or more. So `float é;` and `float xéy;` define the names, written as UTF-8. A byte that starts no sequence (`if (!b)`) is the error "Invalid UTF-8 code sequence before WORD. Lead byte was 0xNN" (`ERR_NOTANAME`, `E0123`): NN the byte in lowercase hex, WORD the bytes up to white space from the first byte after it that starts a sequence, or, when only white space but a line feed stands between that byte and the line's end, "Invalid UTF-8 code sequence at end of line. Lead byte was 0xNN". The pinned FTEQCC refuses `float x` 0xC3 `;` ("... before ;. Lead byte was 0xc3") and `float` 0xA0 `x;`, the non-breaking space of Latin-1. FTEQCC stops at the error; this profile makes no token of the name and reads on at that byte, where FTEQCC leaves `pr_file_p`. The vanilla dialect keeps QC-1.3: such bytes are white space.

After a number `QCC_PR_LexNumber` reports "bad suffix on number TEXT" when a letter, a digit, `_` or a byte of 0x80 or more follows it (`checkjunk:`, `if ( (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') || c == '_' || (c >= '0' && c <= '9') || (c & 0x80)) QCC_PR_ParseWarning(ERR_NOTANUMBER, "bad suffix on number %s", pr_token);`), an error as its code is an `ERR_` one, `E0124`. TEXT is `pr_token`: the number's bytes, a `-` first included, `0X` written `0x`, and a type suffix included except an `f` or `d` after a fraction, which is passed over unwritten: `5abc` is "bad suffix on number 5", `5fx` "... 5f", `1.5e3` "... 1.5" and `08` "... 0" (after FTEF-13.19's warning). The letters after it are then read as a name of their own, as FTEQCC reads on. A vector's components, which `QCC_PR_LexFloat` reads, and the numbers of directives (`QCC_PR_LexInteger`) are not checked.

White space and comments before a token are read as `QCC_PR_Lex` reads them: `QCC_PR_LexComment` first, which reads white space up to and including the first line ending (`qcc_islineending`: a LF, or a CR not before a LF), or a `//` comment up to and including its LF (`while (*pr_file_p && *pr_file_p != '\n')`), after which `QCC_PR_NewLine` passes over the next line's spaces and tabs and only a `//` after other white space there, a VT, is read in the same way, or the first `/* */` comment; then `QCC_PR_LexWhitespace`, whose `//` comment ends at any line ending (`while (*pr_file_p && !qcc_islineending(pr_file_p[0], pr_file_p[1]))`). So a lone CR ends a `//` comment only after a line ending since the token before it: the pinned FTEQCC refuses `// c`, a CR and `float y = ;` on the line after a definition, and `float x; // c`, a LF, `// e`, a CR and `float y = ;`, and accepts `float x; // c`, a CR and `float y = ;`, which is all comment, and the same with a VT before `// e`. A `/* */` comment's `*/` is looked for from the byte after the `*` (`pr_file_p+=1; do { pr_file_p++; ... } while (pr_file_p[0] != '*' || pr_file_p[1] != '/');`), so `/*/` opens a comment that runs on, where id's closes it (QC-2.3): FTEQCC accepts `/*/ float x; */`. A `/*` inside one is the warning "\"/*\" inside comment" (`WARN_NESTEDCOMMENT`, F325, `W0112`, at the `/*`), and a comment with no `*/` is "EOF inside comment" (`E0501` with FTEQCC's text). A `\` before a line break, `\` CR LF taken whole, joins the lines and the reading starts again after it (FTEF-13.2).

`QCC_PR_LexNumber` accumulates the digits in a `long long num` (`num*=base; num += c-'0';`), which wraps on the two's complement builds FTEQCC runs on, and writes `(float)(num* sign)`: the pinned FTEQCC binds `#18446744073709551621` to builtin 5. It warns "A leading 0 is interpreted as base-8." (`WARN_OCTAL_IMMEDIATE`, named `octal`, `W0110`, at the `0`) for a `0` and then a digit, and "numerical overflow" (`WARN_OVERFLOW`, F312, `W0111`, at the number) where the value it stores is not the number: after an `f` or `d` suffix when `(longlong)` of the float or double differs from `num`; after an `i` or `u` suffix with no `l`, when the low 32 bits it keeps (`pr_immediate._int = num`) differ from `num` and are not negative, so `4294967313i` warns and `0xffffffffi` does not; and with no suffix in base 16 only, "numerical overflow %lld will be rounded to %f", `0x100000001` giving "numerical overflow 4294967297 will be rounded to 4294967296.000000". A float past `long long`'s range converts with C's undefined behaviour; this profile saturates, as arm64 does.

FTEQCC's token buffer is `char pr_token[8192];` (`FTEQCC_MAX_TOKEN`): a string, its parts joined (FTEF-16.8), of more than 8191 bytes is "String length exceeds 8191" (`QCC_Error(ERR_INVALIDSTRINGIMMEDIATE, "String length exceeds %u", ...)`, which ends the compile; `E0502` with FTEQCC's text), and a name or number that long runs past the buffer, which FTEQCC does not check, and is `E0502` "token too long" here, a deliberate divergence from that undefined behaviour. A name of 256 bytes or more is the parser's "name too long" (FTEF-15.7). So a string of 3000 bytes, which id's `qcc` cannot hold (QC-27.4), is accepted.

In a string whose input is UTF-8 (`Q"`, `u8"`, `u"`, `U"`, `L"` and, with `-Futf8`, `"`, FTEF-13.8) a byte that starts no sequence `utf8_check` reads is the error "Input string is not valid utf-8", and a byte of 0x80 or more starting a sequence inside bronze text (FTEF-13.10) "Unable to mask non-ascii chars. Attempting to mask bytes", each `QCC_PR_ParseWarning(ERR_BADCHARACTERCODE, ...)` and so an error, `E0103` with FTEQCC's text; FTEQCC reads on, writing the byte as FTEF-13.8 says. An unknown escape is "Unknown escape char %c" with the byte after the `\`.

FTEQCC's F301 (`WARN_NOTUTF8`) and F311 (`WARN_FTE_SPECIFIC`), off by default (FTEF-14.63), are reported once a `#pragma warning` turns them on: F301 for a `u"`, `U"` or `L"` string, "char32_t/char16_t/wchar_t strings are not supported, treating as u8 prefix (as utf-8)", for a code a Quake string cannot hold, "Cannot convert codepoint %#x to quake's charset", and for a UTF-8 one past U+10FFFF, "Bad unicode character code - codepoint is above 0x10FFFFu" (`W0119`); F311 for a vector of two components, "2d vector" (`W0120`).

A vector's components are read with `QCC_PR_LexWhitespace` before the first and after each (`QCC_PR_LexVector`), not with `QCC_PR_LexComment`, so a comment before the first component is passed over and a `//` comment between components ends at a lone CR: the pinned FTEQCC accepts `'/*c*/1 2 3'` and `'1 // c`, a CR and `2 3'`.

Under FTEQCC the punctuation is `pr_punctuation[]`, tried in its order, the first that matches the input winning ("longer symbols must be before a shorter partial match"), which has, besides the vanilla tokens and those of FTE-19.1, `<=>`, `*^`, `><`, `@` and `^^` (`qc_lexer::Punct::FTEQCC_TABLE`); a byte it does not list is FTEF-13.15's "Unknown punctuation". So `a<=>b` is `a`, `<=>`, `b` and `a><b` is `a`, `><`, `b`. `QCC_PrioritiseOpcodes` gives `*^` (`POW_F`) and `><` (`CROSS_V`) the priority of `*` (`PC_MULDIV`) and `<=>` (`SPACESHIP_F`) that of `==` (`PC_EQUALITY`), as this parser does. `@` (a `qccx` unary in `QCC_PR_Term`) and `^^` (which no opcode has) are tokens the parser of this profile reads as no operator.

In a string, `\` before a CR is the byte after the CR (`c = *pr_file_p++;` in `QCC_PR_LexEscapedCodepoint`), and when that byte is no LF FTEQCC warns `"Hanging \\\\\r"` (`WARN_HANGINGSLASHR`, `W0123`), the text `Hanging \\` and a CR: the pinned FTEQCC gives it for `"a`, `\`, a CR and `b"`. A `\` before a CR and an LF is the LF, with no warning.

`#if expr`, `#elif expr`, `#elifdef NAME` and `#elifndef NAME` choose a side as the project graph does (PRJ-5.5): `QCC_PR_Precompiler` evaluates `#if` with `eval = ParsePrecompilerIf(PPI_TOPLEVEL);`, and `QCC_PR_FalsePreProcessorIf` takes the first `#elif`, `#elifdef` or `#elifndef` that is true, or the `#else`, only while no earlier side was (`if (!hadtrue && !strncmp(pr_file_p, "elif", 4) && level == 1)`). An `#if` inside a skipped side only nests (`if (!strncmp(pr_file_p, "if", 2)) level++;`). The expression is evaluated by the one evaluator the graph uses, so the graph and the preprocessor take the same sides.

**Withdrawn** (P2-81, #492): it said a `//` comment ends a directive, which holds for the directive's text but not for the line `QCC_PR_SkipToEndOfLine` skips after it. Replaced by FTEF-14.30 and FTEF-14.24.

**Withdrawn** (P2-94 to P2-99, #507 to #512): it said a `#warning` or `#error` text is the rest of the line, where `#error`'s stops at a tab too and both start right after the directive's name. Replaced by FTEF-14.38.
**Withdrawn** (P2-94 to P2-99, #507 to #512): it said a `#endlist` with no list open is accepted, where FTEQCC reads it as no directive. Replaced by FTEF-14.41.

A macro parameter list whose last parameter is `...` makes the macro variadic: `if (nl == 3 && s[0] == '.' && s[1] == '.' && s[2] == '.') { cnst->varg = true;`. The arguments after the named ones, with the commas between them, replace `__VA_ARGS__` in the body (`if (*pr_file_p == ',' && c->varg && param >= c->numparams) extraparam++;`); a use may give no variadic argument. A use with fewer arguments than named parameters is "macro NAME expects N arguments, found M" (QCD-8.9), as FTEQCC's "Not enough macro parameters" is.

**Withdrawn** (P2-78, #484): it said every macro body reads `#param` as a string and `a ## b` as one token, which only a function-like macro's does, and that a paste is always one token. Replaced by FTEF-14.14 to FTEF-14.16.

When no macro of the name is defined, `QCC_PR_CheckBuiltinCompConst` expands `__NULL__` to `0i`, `__FILE__` to the file's name as a string, `__LINE__` to the line number and `__LINESTR__` to it as a string, `__FUNC__` and `__func__` to the function's name as a string, `__TIME__` and `__DATE__` to strings, `__RAND__` to a number and `__QCCVER__` to a string. The preprocessor does not know the function a use is in, so this profile expands `__FUNC__` to an empty string; the value is a compile-time string and does not change resolution.

**Withdrawn** (P2-94 to P2-99, #507 to #512): it said the build directives produce no token and read only their line, where `#package` ends the text and `#pack` and `#forcecrc` may read into the next line. Replaced by FTEF-14.39.

A use of a function-like macro may give one argument more than its parameters, which is unused: `QCC_PR_ExpandPreProcessorMacro` checks the count only at a comma, after counting the argument before it, with `if (param == MAXCONSTANTPARAMS || param > c->numparams) QCC_PR_ParseError(ERR_TOOMANYPARAMS, "Too many parameters in macro call");`, so the last argument is never counted against the parameters. Two or more extra arguments are "macro NAME expects N arguments, found M" (QCD-8.9). The corpus relies on it (`EVALUATE_FIELD(mins, 0, PLAYER_SIZE)` for a two-parameter macro, `shared/game/Player.qc`).
**Withdrawn** (P2-94 to P2-99, #507 to #512): it said a taken side left open is closed at the end of its file, where FTEQCC's count of open sides runs on into the next file. Replaced by FTEF-14.37.

**Withdrawn** (P2-94 to P2-99, #507 to #512): it said a line continuation in an `#if` expression reads as a space and that an expression FTEQCC reports as an error is only false, where FTEQCC stops at the `\` and the preprocessor reports the error. Replaced by FTEF-14.33.

A deliberate divergence: this profile's `#if` reader nests at most 64 levels (`MAX_DEPTH` in `qc-preproc`'s `cond.rs`), each parenthesis, each `!` and each right side of an operator one level deeper (`ParsePrecompilerIf` calls itself for each), and an expression nested deeper is false, as one FTEQCC reports as an error is. FTEQCC's `ParsePrecompilerIf` recurses with no limit; this profile bounds it so that no input can exhaust the stack, as PRJ-5.10 bounds the vanilla reader and QC-27.15 the parser.

A name is a macro use only when the word `QCC_PR_CheckCompConst` reads at it ends with the name: `QCC_PR_Lex` calls it for every name (`if (flag_hashonly || !QCC_PR_CheckCompConst()) QCC_PR_LexName ();`), and it takes the word up to the first NUL, `qcc_iswhite` byte (space, CR, LF, tab, VT) or one of `)(+-*/|&=^~[]"{};:<>,.#` (`for (end = pr_file_p; ; end++)`) and looks that word up (`pHash_Get(&compconstantstable, pr_token)`, then `QCC_PR_CheckBuiltinCompConst`). So a macro's name, or a built-in constant's (FTEF-14.7), followed directly by any other byte, such as `!`, `?`, `%`, `@`, `$`, `'`, `` ` ``, `\`, a control byte, DEL or a byte of 0x80 or more, is a name: with `#define N 5`, `x = N!=5;` is "Unknown value \"N\"" (`E0301`) and `x = N==5;` is `x = 5==5;`. The byte is the one FTEQCC reads after the name: in a macro's body the body's next byte as stored (QC-9.16), and after an argument the body's byte after the parameter, so `#define A(a) a!=5` used as `A(N)` leaves `N` a name; at the end of an expansion the word ends. FTE-23.10 reads the word after a `#` in the same way, in an expansion as in the source: `#define K #/**/N` then `K` is `5`, as FTEQCC stored the body `#N` (the pinned FTEQCC: "Cannot cast from float to void()" for `void() f = K;`, FTE-23.11). The vanilla preprocessor expands every name that is a macro (QC-9.4).

In a function-like macro's body `a ## b` writes `b`'s text right after `a`'s, with the white space before the `##` dropped (`*bufferlen = whitestart;`), and the result is lexed again with the rest of the expansion: a text that lexes as one token is that token (`x ##_net` with `x` given `health` is the name `health_net`, `#1##6` the builtin 16), and one that lexes as more is the tokens of that text, each against the one before (`J(a, +)` with `#define J(a, b) a ## b` is `a+`, the name and `+`). Either side may be empty, so `##` at the start or end of the body, or beside an empty argument, leaves the other side as it is, and an empty argument after `##` joins nothing to what follows it: `#define P(a, b) a##b` used as `P(#5, )` or `P(, #5)` is `#5`. `##` is two `#` that touch as the body was stored (`if (pr_file_p[1] == '#')`); `# #` is a `#` before a word (FTEF-14.31). An argument beside `##` is copied whole: one after it by `noargexpand`, one before it because `start[0] == '#' && start[1] == '#'`, each with what stands before its `,` or `)`. So the right argument's later tokens touch the joined one (`P(l, bl:)` writes the label `lbl:`), and white space or a comment after the left argument stays between the sides, as `*bufferlen = whitestart` drops only the body's white space: `P(x , y)` is `x y`. A paste whose text opens a comment (`/` and `/`, or `/` and `*`) writes nothing more: the comment runs to the end of the chunk.

**Withdrawn** (P2-80, #491): it said an argument that comes from another expansion's text is written into a `#` string as its tokens touch, one space where they do not, where FTEQCC keeps that text's white space; this profile now keeps it too. Replaced by FTEF-14.31.

An object-like macro's body is included as it was stored (`QCC_PR_IncludeChunkEx(c->value, ...)`), and `QCC_PR_ExpandPreProcessorMacro`, which reads `#` and `##`, runs only for a macro with a parameter list (`if (c->numparams>=0)`). So in an object-like macro `#` and `##` are tokens like any other: `#define P #5:ex_##a` is refused, the pinned FTEQCC reporting it at the `##`.

A macro is not expanded in the chunk of its own expansion (`if (c && (!currentchunk || currentchunk->cnst != c))`, "macros don't expand themselves"), and otherwise is, while fewer than 8 chunks of it are open for an object-like macro (`if (c->inside >= 8)`) or at most 8 for a function-like one (`if (c->inside>8) return false;`). The open chunks are the expansion a token comes from and those that expansion was used in, back to the source: a chunk stays open until its last token is read. So a macro used again through another is expanded again: with `#define A #5 B` and `#define B :A`, `A` is `#5 :#5 :...` eight times over, which the pinned FTEQCC refuses, where QC-9.4's rule leaves `#5 :A`. A built-in constant's value (FTEF-14.7) is a chunk of its own (`QCC_PR_IncludeChunkEx(tok, true, NULL, NULL)`), so it touches neither token beside it. This profile reads FTEQCC macros by this rule and keeps no hide set for them; the vanilla dialect keeps QC-9.4's.

**Withdrawn** (P2-81, #492): it said a comment before a function-like macro's `(` leaves the name as it is, which holds for the source and for an argument's text but not for a macro's stored body, where `QCC_PR_PreProcessor_Define` dropped the comment. Replaced by FTEF-14.29.

**Withdrawn** (P2-83, #494): it said this profile's expansions write at most 2^22 tokens, which it checked before each expansion and counted after it, so one expansion could write far more. Replaced by FTEF-14.28.

In an argument that is not copied whole (FTEF-14.14), `QCC_PR_ExpandPreProcessorMacro` reads each token with `QCC_COM_Parse2` and writes a built-in constant's value in its place (`end = QCC_PR_CheckBuiltinCompConst(qcc_token, retbuf, sizeof(retbuf));`, "we should be testing all defines instead of just built-in ones"), in the macro's own chunk: so with `#define K(x) x`, `K(#__LINE__)` is `#` and the line number touching, a builtin, where the line number of a built-in constant read anywhere else is a chunk of its own (FTEF-14.17). Other macros in an argument are expanded only when the expansion is read.

**Withdrawn** (P2-87, #504): it said this profile keeps a file's name whole in `__FILE__`, escaping it, a deliberate divergence while the name was the host's path. The name is now FTEQCC's, written as FTEQCC writes it. Replaced by FTEF-14.32.

A function-like macro's arguments are found in the text after its `(`, which `QCC_PR_ExpandPreProcessorMacro` reads a byte at a time: after the white space and comments that follow the `(` (`QCC_PR_LexWhitespace(false)`), a `"` string is passed over (`do { pr_file_p++; } while( (pr_file_p[-1] == '\\' || pr_file_p[0] != '\"') && *pr_file_p && *pr_file_p != '\n' );`), `(` and `)` nest (`plevel`), and a `,` or `)` outside them ends an argument (`paramoffset[param++] = start;`), the white space and comments after a `,` being skipped before the next. Every other byte, a character constant's or a comment's, is part of the argument, so a `,`, `(` or `)` in one ends an argument or nests as any other does: with `#define E(n) :n`, `E(',')` gives `E` the arguments `'` and `'`, and FTEQCC refuses `void() f = E(',');` ("Bad vector"); with `#define M(x) x`, `M(#5 /* ) */)` ends at the `)` in the comment, so its argument `#5 /* ` opens a comment the expansion ends inside, and `M(#5 // )`, a line break and `)` ends at the `)` in the `//` comment; a comment right after the `(` or a `,` is skipped first, so `M(/* ) */ #5)` is `#5`. With `#define S(a) #a`, `:S(e'x)` binds the name `e'x`. The string skip ends only at a `"` with no `\` right before it, a `\\` before it included, so a string whose last byte is a `\` runs on past its `"` to the next `"` or the line's end, and the argument with it: with `#define E(n) n`, `E(:"ex\\")` runs to the end of the file, which FTEQCC reports as "EOF on macro call" (FTEF-14.29), and `E(:"ex\\") ")"` takes `:"ex\\") "` as its argument. A line break, or a `\` before one, is part of an argument like any byte. Reading of the text the use stands in goes on after its `)`, read again from there where a token of the text as first read stood across it. The arguments' text is read as code only where the expansion writes it, so its lexical errors are reported there and nowhere else.

`QCC_PR_PreProcessor_Define` reads a macro's name with `QCC_PR_SimpleGetToken`, up to white space, `,`, `;`, `(`, `)`, `]` or `//`, and a parameter list from a `(` right after it as bytes: each parameter runs from after the spaces and tabs that follow the `(` or a `,` to the next `,` or `)`, its trailing spaces and tabs dropped, and the first byte after a `,` and its spaces is passed over before a delimiter is looked for (`if(!*pr_file_p++)`), so `(a,)` reads on past its `)`. A parameter given twice is refused ("duplicate macro paramter name '%s'"), as are a 33rd parameter (`MAXCONSTANTPARAMS` = 32, "May not have more than %i parameters to a macro"), a name of 32 bytes or more (`MAXCONSTANTPARAMLENGTH` = 32, "parameter name is too long"), a `...` that is not last ("varadic argument must be last") and a list the text ends in ("missing ) in macro parameter list"): this profile reports each as "bad parameter list for macro NAME" (`E0115`) and defines nothing. So `#define E(n, n) n` and `#define E(n,n) n` are refused, and `#define E( n ) n` names `n`. `()` is one parameter with no name, so `#define E() #5` takes one argument, and a second (FTEF-14.9). A parameter is its bytes: one that is no word, such as `a b`, is never matched in the body.

`QCC_PR_PreProcessor_Define` stores a body from after the spaces and tabs that follow the name or the `)` to a line break, the end of the file, or a `//` outside a quote; it drops each `/* */` comment outside a quote ("multi-line c style comments become part of the define itself. this also negates the need for \ at the end of lines. although we don't bother embedding.") and each `\` before a line break (LF, CR or CR LF) with the line break ("read over a newline if necessary"), storing the byte after it whatever it is, and drops the spaces and tabs at the end. Its quote flag flips at every `"`, an escaped one included (`if (*s == '\"') quote=!quote;`), so `#define N :"ex\"_a//"` stores `:"ex\"_a`, whose string the expansion leaves open, and FTEQCC refuses `void() f = N;`. After a `\` and line break, a line whose first byte after spaces and tabs is `#` keeps its line break, and so does the next continued line ("#define hacks however, require that it becomes foo\nbar\nmoo"). `QCC_PR_SkipToEndOfLine` then reads to the end of the directive's line, passing over `/* */` comments, strings before any `//`, and each `\` and line break, in a `//` comment too, so after `#define H 1 // c \` the next line is part of the directive and never read. The directive's text is read as code only where an expansion writes it. A function-like macro's name and a `(` that only dropped comments and continuations stand between in a body are apart only by the spaces and tabs around them, so `#define K M /**/ (#5)`, `#define K M/**/ (#5)` and `#define K M \`, a line break and `(#5)` call `M` (FTEF-14.29). `#append NAME ...` (FTEF-14.39) is read the same way and adds a space and its body to the macro's stored body when the parameters are the macro's; with others ("different number of macro arguments in macro append", "arguments differ in macro append") it defines the macro again, with the warning `W0102`.

In a function-like macro's body, and in an argument copied a token at a time (FTEF-14.20), `QCC_COM_Parse2` reads each token after white space and `//` comments: a number (digits and `.`, or `0x` and hex digits and `.`), a word (a letter or `_`, then letters, digits and `_`), or one byte, each kept to its first 1023 bytes (`char qcc_token[1024]`, `if (len >= sizeof(qcc_token)-1) ;`). A parameter is a word that is its name (`!STRCMP(qcc_token, c->params[p])`), so in `#define E(a) #5a` and `#define E(a) #5.a` the `a` is the parameter, and in `#define E(a) #0x5a` it is a hex digit (the builtin 90). A string right after `#` or `##` is read by `QCC_COM_Parse2` too, which writes its text with the escapes `\"`, `\\` and `\n` read and no quotes, and goes on one byte past the closing `"`: so `#define S(a) #"5"` writes `#5`, `#"5"x a` writes `#5` and the argument, the `x` passed over, and `a##"5"` given `#` writes `#5`.

In a variadic macro's body `__VA_COUNT__` is FTEQCC's count of the variadic arguments, `QC_snprintfz(tmp, sizeof(tmp), "%i", param-1+extraparam);`: the arguments found less one, and the commas after the named ones. So with `#define V(...) :__VA_COUNT__`, `V()` and `V(a)` are `:0` and `V(a, b)` is `:1`, and with `#define V(a, ...) #5:__VA_COUNT__`, `V(a, b)` is `#5:1`, which FTEQCC refuses ("not a name"); its "__VA_COUNT__ without any variable args" is never reached, since fewer arguments than named parameters are "Not enough macro parameters" first (FTEF-14.5). `__VA_ARGS__` is the variadic argument when one was given (`if (param-1 == c->numparams)`); when none was, after `##` it takes away a `,` written right before it (`if(*bufferlen>0 && (*buffer)[*bufferlen-1] == ',') *bufferlen-=1;`), the white space the `##` drops gone first, so `#define V(a, ...) a,##__VA_ARGS__` and `a , ## __VA_ARGS__` used as `V(#5)` are `#5`, while `a,__VA_ARGS__` keeps the `,`. An empty variadic argument is its text, commas and all: `#define E(...) #5 __VA_ARGS__` used as `E(, )` writes `#5 , `, the declaration `#5` and a `,` before the `;` (FTEF-15.8).

A built-in constant an argument copies as its value (FTEF-14.20) is written in place of the white space and `//` comments `QCC_COM_Parse2` passed over before it too (`end` is written, not `argstart` to `argend`), so with `#define E(n) n`, `E(# __LINE__)` is `#2`, the builtin 2, as `E(#//`, a line break and `__LINE__)` is the builtin 3. The line a built-in constant has is `pr_source_line`, or in a macro's chunk `currentchunk->currentlinenumber`, the line FTEQCC was reading when `QCC_PR_IncludeChunkEx` included the chunk (`chunk->currentlinenumber = pr_source_line;`). A use in a file includes its expansion at the line of its `)`, or of its name for an object-like macro, which is also the line of a constant its arguments copy; reading a chunk counts its lines from 1 (`pr_source_line = 1;`), so a use in a chunk includes its expansion at 1 and a line for each line break of the chunk before the use's end, and a constant its arguments copy has the line of the chunk the use is in. So `#define L :__LINESTR__` and `#define M L` used as `M` on line 3 bind the name `1`, and `#define M(x) :__LINESTR__ x` used as `M(`, a line break and `)` from line 2 binds `3`.
