A deliberate divergence: FTEF-14.17 lets an expansion grow exponentially (`#define A B B` and `#define B A A` expand to 2^16 names), and one expansion of a body that names its parameter `n` times, given an argument of `m` tokens, writes `n` times `m` (a body of 8000 `x` given 8000 tokens is 64000000), and FTEQCC builds it all. So this profile makes at most `FTE_MAX_EXPANSIONS` = 2^20 macro expansions in one file and writes at most `FTE_MAX_EXPANDED_TOKENS` = 2^22 tokens with them: an expansion's text is written only while it holds no more bytes than the tokens left under the bound, a token being at least one byte, and its tokens are counted when it is lexed. The first use past either bound is reported once, as "macro expansion too large" (`E0120`), and it and later uses are left as written. No program of the corpus comes near it. The vanilla dialect has the same bound (`language.md` QC-9.18).

A function-like macro takes its arguments only from the text of the chunk its name is in: `QCC_PR_CheckCompConst` skips spaces and tabs after the name (`while(*pr_file_p == ' ' || *pr_file_p == '\t')`) and expands it only `if (*pr_file_p == '(')`, so a line break or a comment before the `(`, in the source or in an argument's text copied into an expansion, or the end of the expansion the name is in, leaves the name as it is (`M\n(#5)` is the name `M`; with `#define N M`, `N(#5)` is too), while in a macro's stored body the comments and continuations between a name and its `(` are gone (FTEF-14.24); and `QCC_PR_ExpandPreProcessorMacro` reads the arguments up to the `)` within that text (FTEF-14.22), reporting "EOF on macro call" (`if (!*pr_file_p) QCC_PR_ParseError(ERR_EOF, "EOF on macro call");`) when it ends first. This profile reports that as "unterminated argument list for macro NAME" (`E0117`): with `#define L(x) x:` and `#define LL L(lbl`, `LL) goto lbl;` is `E0117`, as is the end of the file inside a use's arguments.

**Withdrawn** (P2-94, #507): it said only `#define` and `#append` read on past a `\` and line break in a `//` comment, a known difference for the other directives. Every directive now ends its line where `QCC_PR_SkipToEndOfLine` ends it. Replaced by FTEF-14.35.

In a function-like macro's body `#param`, `param` a named parameter, is a string of the argument's text as written, from after the white space and comments that follow its `(` or `,` (`QCC_PR_LexWhitespace(false)`) to its `,` or `)`: `QCC_PR_ExpandStrCatMarkup` copies `paramoffset[p]`, white space and comments included, with `\` before each line break, `\`, NUL and `"`. So `#define S(a) #a` used as `S( ex_a )` is `"ex_a "`, `S(ex a)` is `"ex a"`, `S(ex/**/a)` is `"ex/**/a"`, `S(ex\a)` is `"ex\\a"` and `S()` is `""`; every byte is kept, one of 0x80 or more included; the argument's text is a string's, so no lexical error in it is reported unless the body also writes the argument as code. `...` has no name (the loop compares `c->params[p]`), so `#__VA_ARGS__` is a `#` before the word `__VA_ARGS__`. A `#` before a word that is no parameter writes `#` and that word with nothing between (`QCC_PR_ExpandStrCat(..., "#", 1);` then `qcc_token`), so `#define S(a) # 5` is `#5`, a builtin; a `#` at the end of the body writes nothing (`if (!pr_file_p) break;`). An argument that comes from another expansion's text is that text as the expansion wrote it, white space and all.

**Withdrawn** (P2-95, #508): it said the semantic model gives the preprocessor each file's path as its input names it, the `progs.src` entry only where the caller makes it so, but the semantic model now gives an FTEQCC graph's files by their names (FTEF-14.75). Replaced by FTEF-14.74.

A built-in constant (FTEF-14.7) is the text `QCC_PR_CheckBuiltinCompConst` writes for it, read as a chunk of its own (FTEF-14.17): `0i` for `__NULL__`, the line (`%i`) for `__LINE__` and in quotes for `__LINESTR__` (FTEF-14.27), `""` for the constants this profile does not know, and for `__FILE__` `QC_snprintfz(retbuf, retbufsize, "\"%s\"", s_filen);` in `char retbuf[256]`, so at most 255 bytes, ended at its first `:` (`erk = strchr(retbuf, ':'); if (erk) { erk[0] = '\"'; erk[1] = 0; }`) with nothing in the name escaped: a `\` in the name starts an escape, a `"` ends the string, a line break is "newline inside quote" (`E0102`) and a name of 254 bytes or more leaves the string open. Its lexical errors are reported at the constant's name. `s_filen` is the name of the file being read: for a compiled file the name it is compiled by (`QCC_PR_CompileFile (char *string, char *filename)`), which the preprocessor takes as its caller gives the path, so a caller gives it as `progs.src` wrote it; for an `#include`d file the bytes between its quotes joined by `QCC_JoinPaths` to the compiled file's name, after its last `/` or `\`, or alone when they start with one (`QCC_FindBestInclude(msg, compilingfile, false);`), so a file another included file includes is named beside the compiled file; and from a `#pragma file(NAME)` or `#pragma file NAME` (any case of `file`) to the end of that file, NAME (`s_filen = e = qccHunkAlloc(strlen(m)+1);`), the pragma's text being bytes to the end of its line, read from after a space or tab or from a `(`, its trailing white space dropped and, from a `(`, ended at the first `)`, and never lexed as code. In a macro's chunk `s_filen` is the file's name, the line and the macro's name joined by `:` (`QC_snprintfz(p, b, "%s:%i:%s", ...)`), which the `:` cut ends at the file's name. So with `progs.src` listing `t.qc`, `void() f = :__FILE__;` binds the name `t.qc`, after `#pragma file(ex_a:b)` `ex_a`, and after `#pragma file(e\\x)` `e\x`; with `progs.src` listing `src/a.qc`, which includes `x/b.qh`, which includes `c.qh`, the pinned FTEQCC names them `src/a.qc`, `src/x/b.qh` and `src/c.qh`. The semantic model gives the preprocessor each file's name as FTEF-14.73 says.

An `#if` or `#elif` expression is read as `ParsePrecompilerIf` reads it, not with the C precedence of PRJ-5.5, by the preprocessor and by the graph of a module of this dialect. `||` and `&&` share one level and group to the right, the right side read first: `eval = ParsePrecompilerIf(level)||eval;` and `eval = ParsePrecompilerIf(level)&&eval;` under `case PPI_LOGICAL:`, so `0 && 0 || 1` is `0 && (0 || 1)`, 0, where C makes it 1. The comparisons `<=`, `>=`, `<`, `>`, `!=` and `==` share the level below in the same way (`eval = eval <= ParsePrecompilerIf(level);` under `case PPI_COMPARISON:`), so `1 < 2 == 1` is `1 < (2 == 1)`, 0. A value (`PPI_VALUE`) is a parenthesised expression, `!` and a value, `defined` and a name with or without parentheses, or a word as `QCC_PR_SimpleGetToken` reads it, up to white space, `,`, `;`, `(`, `)`, `]` or `//`, whose macro's text, or else the word itself, is read with `atoi`: `1||0` is one word, 1. The reader starts after `#if`'s name (`pr_file_p = directive+2`) or `#elif`'s, reads within the line, as its white space is all but a line break (`qcc_iswhite(*pr_file_p) && *pr_file_p != '\n'`), and stops after the whole expression; a `\` is a byte like any other, so `#if 0 \`, a line break and `|| 1` is 0, and the line's end is then read as FTEF-14.35 says, which makes the `\` there "unexpected tokens at end of line". Where FTEQCC reports an error, "unclosed bracket condition", "unclosed defined condition" or "unexpected end-of-line" (`#if` with nothing after it), the preprocessor reports it (`E0121`) and takes the expression as false; the graph takes it as false.

**Withdrawn** (P2-103, #520): it said the preprocessor reports FTEQCC's "Explicit precompiler usage when not defined NAME" as `E0121` for a `#` that stands first on its line of the output, where the semantic model would drop the line as a directive's. The semantic model now parses the output with no directive lines (QC-9.19). Replaced by FTEF-14.52.

After a directive's operand `QCC_PR_SkipToEndOfLine` reads to its line's break, passing over `/* */` comments, which may span lines, strings before any `//`, and each `\` and line break (LF or CR LF), in a `//` comment too, so after `#undef X // c \` or `#ifdef X // c \` the next line is part of the directive, never read as code. For `#define`, `#append`, `#undef`, `#if`, `#ifdef`, `#ifndef`, `#else`, `#endif`, `#package`, `#pack`, `#forcecrc`, `#merge`, `#includelist`, `#include`, `#output`, an `#elif` that is taken (FTEF-14.37) and `#endlist` (FTEF-14.41) it is called with `errorifnonwhite`, so a byte outside a comment and before any `//` that is no white space, a string's `"` included, is the error "unexpected tokens at end of line" (`E0121`; `QCC_PR_ParseWarning(ERR_UNKNOWNPUCTUATION, ...)` reports an error code as an error): `#ifdef X Y`, `#endif X`, `#else X` and `#include "b.qh" X` are refused. A `#pragma`'s line ends at its break (FTEF-14.43). Reading goes on at the break, which ends the line, so the next line may start a directive.

**Withdrawn** (P2-116, #544): it said this profile does not report FTEQCC's warnings for `#undef` of no macro and for an `#if` form with no white space after its name, which are on by default. Replaced by FTEF-14.57.

FTEQCC counts the sides that are open and taken in one `static int ifs`, kept from file to file of a module, included files and the second autoprototyping pass included: a true `#if`, `#ifdef` or `#ifndef` adds one; a false one is skipped by `QCC_PR_FalsePreProcessorIf(false, ...)`, which adds one if it stops at a side it takes. That function reads a line at a time: after spaces and tabs a `#` and spaces and tabs before a word starting `endif` closes a level and one starting `if` opens one (`if (!strncmp(pr_file_p, "if", 2)) level++;`); at the block's own level, while no side was taken, a word starting `else` takes the next side, its line read with `errorifnonwhite`, and one starting `elif`, `elifdef` or `elifndef` is tested, which needs a space or a tab after `elif`, `elifdef` or `elifndef` ("malformed #elif", `E0121`), and is taken when true, its line read with `errorifnonwhite` after the test; every line ends where `QCC_PR_SkipToEndOfLine` ends it, so a `//` comment ending in `\` hides the next line's `#endif`, and the end of the text is "#if with no endif" (`E0110`) at the conditional. On a taken side `#else` and `#elif` (and `#elsewhere`) take one from the count, read their line (`#else`'s with `errorifnonwhite`) and skip to the block's end with `QCC_PR_FalsePreProcessorIf(true, ...)`, which takes no side, so a second `#else` there is skipped too; `#endif` takes one. Either with nothing open is "#else outside of #if" or "unmatched #endif" (`E0109`). A taken side left open at the end of a file is closed by an `#endif` in a file read after it, and is not reported.

`#error` is the error `E0118` "#Error: TEXT" (`QCC_PR_ParseError(ERR_HASHERROR, "#Error: %s", msg);`), `#warning` the warning `W0103` "#warning: TEXT" and `#message` reports nothing. TEXT is the bytes from right after the directive's name, a space before the text included, to the first NUL or line break, at most 1023, and for `#error` to a tab too (`pr_file_p[a] != '\t' && pr_file_p[a] != '\n'`), for `#warning` and `#message` to a CR too; the line is then read without `errorifnonwhite`. So `#warning Toggle doesn't work` is "#warning: Toggle doesn't work", and no `'` in it opens a vector.

The build directives change the build, not the text read, but each reads its line as FTEQCC does: `#copyright` and `#message` read it without `errorifnonwhite`; `#forcecrc` reads a number with `QCC_PR_LexInteger`, which takes the byte after the name whatever it is and then digits, `.` and `a` to `f`, so `#forcecrc` at a line's end takes the line break and reads the next line as its own; `#pack id` passes over `id` and one byte more, and `#pack N` reads `N` with `QCC_PR_LexInteger` and one byte more, a number above 5 being "No more than 5 packs are allowed" (`E0121`); `#output` and `#merge` read a string with `QCC_PR_SimpleGetString`; and each then reads its line with `errorifnonwhite`. `#package` reads its line so and then ends the text (`pr_file_p += strlen(pr_file_p);`), as `#eof` ends it (`pr_file_p = NULL;`). `#datafile` reads a string, one byte more, and the bytes to the next line break. `#append NAME text` adds `text` to the body of macro `NAME`, or defines it when it is not defined (`append with no previous define is treated as just a regular define`).

`#include` takes the bytes between `"` and `"`, or `<` and `>`, after the spaces and tabs after its name ("Not a string literal (on a #include)" for another byte, "#include continued over line boundry" for a line break first, each `E0113`), reads its line with `errorifnonwhite`, and `QCC_FindBestInclude(msg, compilingfile, false)` finds the file: the bytes joined with `QCC_JoinPaths` to the name of the file being compiled, then to each include directory in order, the first that names a file being read (`if (FileSize(fullname) == -1) { includepath++; continue; }`), none being "Couldn't open file" (`E0111`). The file being compiled is the one `progs.src` or an `#includelist` lists, never an included one, so a file an included file includes is found beside the compiled file: with `progs.src` listing `src/a.qc`, which includes `x/b.qh`, which includes `c.qh`, the pinned FTEQCC reads `src/c.qh` and refuses the program when only `src/x/c.qh` exists. An empty name includes nothing, and a name `#pragma once` marked is not read again (FTEF-14.70). The file is read next, as text of its own, after the directive's line. The vanilla dialect keeps QC-9.2.

`#includelist` reads its line with `errorifnonwhite`, then words: before each, white space and comments are read as `QCC_PR_LexWhitespace(false)` reads them, which runs the directives at the starts of their lines (FTEF-14.45); a word is what `QCC_PR_SimpleGetToken` reads, a byte it stops at with no word is passed over, and the word `#endlist`, wherever it stands, ends the list, its line read with `errorifnonwhite`. Every other word names a file the graph compiles (PRJ-5.3); the preprocessor produces no token for the list. The end of the text before `#endlist`, reached or made by a directive in the list (`#eof`, `#package`, `DONT_COMPILE_THIS_FILE`), is FTEQCC's "eof in includelist", which the preprocessor reports as `E0406` "#includelist without #endlist" at the `#includelist`. `#endlist` outside a list is no directive (FTEF-14.52).

`QCC_PR_DefineName` refuses a macro name of 64 bytes or more (`if (strlen(name) >= MAXCONSTANTNAMELENGTH || !*name) QCC_PR_ParseError(ERR_NAMETOOLONG, "Compiler constant name length is too long or short");`, `#define MAXCONSTANTNAMELENGTH 64` in `qcc.h`), for `#define` and `#append`: this profile reports it (`E0121`) and defines nothing. A name of 63 bytes is defined. `QCC_PR_PreProcessor_Define` reads the directive's own word first with `QCC_PR_SimpleGetToken` and the name after it, so `#defined N 5` defines `N`, `#defineN 5` defines `5` and `#define/**/N 5` defines `5`, and a refused definition's line is read with no error of its own, as FTEQCC's compile stops at the first.

`#pragma`'s name is the bytes after its spaces and tabs up to the first space, tab or `(` met while the name read so far is empty, and its text the bytes after (from the `(`, or after the space or tab) to the line's break, its white space at the end dropped; a pragma's name is matched in any case (`QC_strcasecmp`). `#pragma line(N)` and `#pragma line N` number the line after the pragma `N`: `pr_source_line = strtoul(m, &m, 0)-1;`, `m` the text after a `(` it starts with, and the pragma's line break adds one. `strtoul` reads a sign, `0x` and hex digits, `0` and octal digits, or decimal digits, nothing being 0, a value too large `ULONG_MAX` and a `-` negating it, on a 64-bit `unsigned long`, and FTEQCC's `int` keeps its low 32 bits: so `#pragma line 0x10` numbers the next line 16, `#pragma line 010` 8, `#pragma line -1` -1 and `#pragma line 4294967297` 1. The lines after it count on from there to the end of the file or chunk the pragma is in, which `__LINE__` and `__LINESTR__` write (FTEF-14.27) outside a macro's expansion (in one, FTEF-14.46), and an `#include`d file's numbering ends with it (`QCC_PR_UnInclude` restores `pr_source_line`). FTEQCC's diagnostics report the line too; this profile's diagnostics keep the place of their text, a deliberate divergence, as a span in the file says more than a line FTEQCC was told.
**Withdrawn** (P2-116, #544): it said this profile keeps only F303's warning setting and does not report "Unknown pragma". Replaced by FTEF-14.70.

`QCC_PR_LexWhitespace(false)`, which reads the white space and comments after a function-like macro use's `(` and after each `,` of its arguments (FTEF-14.22), and before each word of an `#includelist` and each byte `DONT_COMPILE_THIS_FILE` passes over, calls `QCC_PR_NewLine(false)` at each line ending, which runs a directive at the next line's start (FTEF-14.52): so with `#define M(x) x`, `M(`, a line break, `#define Y #5`, a line break and `Y)` defines `Y` and expands to `#5`, and `M(`, a line break, `#ifdef Q`, `zz`, `#endif` and `#5)` is `#5`. The directive's line is no part of the argument, which starts after the white space. A line break in the middle of an argument is part of it (FTEF-14.22), so a directive on the next line is the argument's text, run where the expansion holds it (FTEF-14.46). A directive that ends the text, `#eof` or `#package`, ends the arguments, which is "EOF on macro call" (`E0117`), and the pinned FTEQCC crashes on `#eof` there. A use refused with its arguments read, for "EOF on macro call", too many parameters (`E0116`) or the bound of FTEF-14.28, is an error where FTEQCC's compile stops; this profile then reads the use again as it is written, unless a directive ran among its arguments, when reading goes on after the text the arguments took (after the `)`, or at the end of the text), so that no directive runs twice: with `#define M(x) x`, `M(`, a line break, `#append A 2`, a line break and `1, 2, 3) A` appends to `A` once.

A macro's expansion is read as a chunk of text (FTEF-14.17), and a `#` that starts a line of it, after a line break in it and spaces and tabs, is a directive there, where its text's line breaks are those `QCC_PR_PreProcessor_Define` kept in the body before a continued line starting with `#` (FTEF-14.24) or an argument held; a `#` at the chunk's start is none. Such a body is FTEQCC's warning F303 "preprocessor directive within preprocessor macro NAME" at the first such `#`, once for the definition (`if (!cnst->evil)`), an error by default (`qccwarningaction[WARN_EVILPREPROCESSOR] = WA_ERROR;`, `E0122`), a warning after `#pragma warning enable F303` (`W0109`) and nothing after `#pragma warning disable F303`. With F303 off, `#define D \`, a line break, `#define Y #5 \`, a line break and `Y` makes `D` define `Y` and expand to `#5`. In the chunk a `#pragma file` names, and a `#pragma line` numbers, the rest of that chunk only, and `#eof` and `#package` end it; the pinned FTEQCC crashes on `#eof` in a chunk, where this profile ends the chunk. The chunk's own `__LINE__` and `__LINESTR__` still write the line of its use (`if (currentchunk && currentchunk->cnst) line = currentchunk->currentlinenumber;`), so the lines a `#pragma line` numbers there are those of the uses after it in the chunk, whose expansions write them: with F303 off, `#define L __LINE__`, a `D` whose body is `#pragma line(30)` and `L __LINE__` on lines of their own, and `D __LINE__` on line 6, are `30 6 6`.

Deliberate divergences of this profile's directives: an `#include` met among a use's arguments, in a macro's expansion, in an `#includelist` or in the text `DONT_COMPILE_THIS_FILE` passes over is refused, as "#include where this profile does not follow it" (`E0121`), where FTEQCC reads the file as the text it goes on reading there, which ends the arguments or list it is in; an `#eof` run anywhere but at the start of a file, in a chunk too, ends the text it is in, where the pinned FTEQCC crashes, as `QCC_PR_LexComment` and `QCC_PR_LexWhitespace` read on from the null `pr_file_p` it leaves (`cargo xtask oracles builtins` counts those cases as differing as this statement says: an FTEQCC case that holds `#eof` after its first byte, refused by FTEQCC and accepted here with no error); an `#include` of a file already being read is "recursive #include of PATH" (`E0112`), where FTEQCC reads it again until it runs out of memory; a macro name in an `#includelist` is read as a file's name, where FTEQCC expands it (`QCC_PR_CheckCompConst()`), as the graph reads the list (PRJ-5.3); `#merge` and `#datafile` open no file, where FTEQCC refuses a missing one, as the files are the build's; and a directive met while 64 others are being run inside the readings they started, an `#includelist` or `DONT_COMPILE_THIS_FILE` inside another, is "directives nested too deeply" (`E0121`) and ends the reading, where FTEQCC's recursion has no bound, so that no input can exhaust the stack.

Before the first file FTEQCC's `QCC_SetDefaultProperties` defines `FTEQCC` and `__FTEQCC__` with empty bodies (`QCC_PR_DefineName("FTEQCC", NULL); QCC_PR_DefineName("__FTEQCC__", NULL);`), so `#ifdef FTEQCC` is true and `#if FTEQCC` 0, and `#undef` removes them. It runs again before the second autoprototyping pass (FTE-22.3), which so starts with those two macros only, no include directory but the module's (FTEF-14.49), no `#pragma once` mark (`QCC_PR_CloseProcessor`), and F303 an error again; the count of open sides (FTEF-14.37) is kept, being `QCC_PR_Precompiler`'s own.

A module's include directories (PRJ-5.2) are FTEQCC's `-I` options: `QCC_PR_CommandLinePrecompilerOptions` gives each to `QCC_PR_AddIncludePath(name)` (`else if ( !strncmp(myargv[i], "-I", 2) )`), which keeps it as `#pragma includedir` does (FTEF-14.70): a `/` after it unless it ends in one, at most 8. `QCC_SetDefaultProperties` calls it after `QCC_PR_CloseProcessor`, so they are the first include directories, before any `#pragma includedir` adds one, and they are there again for the second autoprototyping pass (FTEF-14.48). `QCC_FindBestInclude` tries them after the file being compiled (FTEF-14.40), so with `progs.src` listing `src/a.qc`, which includes `x/b.qh`, which includes `c.qh`, and only `src/x/c.qh` there, `-Isrc/x` reads it, as Rad-Therapy's `client/Makefile` gives `-I../shared` for `shared/defs.h`'s `#include "Weapon.h"`.

FTEF-14.43's `strtoul` is the host C library's, and the pinned FTEQCC reads a `#pragma line` number otherwise where `unsigned long` is 32 bits (LLP64, 64-bit Windows): there a value of 2^32 or more is `ULONG_MAX` = 4294967295, so `#pragma line 4294967297` numbers the next line -1, where an LP64 host (64-bit Linux and macOS) numbers it 1. This profile reads the number as an LP64 build does on every host, a deliberate divergence from the LLP64 build, so that a project reads the same wherever it is opened; the builtin differential records the LP64 outcomes and lists the cases a 32-bit `strtoul` reads otherwise as expected where the oracle ran on an LLP64 host.

Under this profile the syntax tree, which shows a file as written and runs no directive (both sides of a conditional are parsed), makes a directive node of the text the preprocessor reads as one directive (`qc_preproc::fte_directive_end`). It starts at a `#` that `QCC_PR_NewLine` reaches (FTEF-14.52), the file read as one being compiled, so a `#` after spaces and tabs on its first line starts one too, and it ends where the preprocessor reads on after it with nothing run: at the end of its line as `QCC_PR_SkipToEndOfLine` ends it (FTEF-14.35), after the operand the directive reads, a `#define`'s body (FTEF-14.24) or an `#if` expression (FTEF-14.33) among them, and for an `#elif`, `#elifdef` or `#elifndef` after its test, as `QCC_PR_FalsePreProcessorIf` reads one after the side before it was skipped (FTEF-14.37), so `#elif (1/*)` ends at its `)`; at a `#pragma`'s line break (FTEF-14.43); after the word of an `#if`, `#ifdef` or `#ifndef` with no white space after its name (`#if(1)`, FTEF-14.57); and at an `#eof`'s line break, as FTEQCC reads nothing after it. So `#undef X // c \`, a line break and `float y;` is one node of two lines, and `#pragma p // c \` ends at its line break. A `#` after a `/* */` comment on its line or in the middle of a line, and a `#` whose name matches no directive (`#foo`), are read as code (FTE-23.10). Unless only white space stands between the end and the token before it, the text from the end is lexed again as the preprocessor lexes it where it reads on (`qc_preproc::relex_from`, FTEF-14.22), so `#if"a b"` is a node `#if"a` and the code ` b"`. A lexical error the first lexing found in a node's text, as the unclosed string of `#define X "a`, is reported by neither, as the preprocessor reads that text as bytes. The text an `#if` or `#else` skips, an `#includelist`'s list (FTEF-14.41) and what `#eof`, `#package` and `DONT_COMPILE_THIS_FILE` leave unread are parsed as code. The vanilla dialect keeps QC-9.1's node: a `#` first on its line before a name on that line, to the first line break after it. A rendering of the preprocessor's output has no directive lines in either dialect (QC-9.19).

`QCC_PR_Precompiler` reads a directive at a `#` that `QCC_PR_NewLine` reaches: the first byte after a line ending (LF, or a CR not before a LF, `qcc_islineending`) that the white-space reader passes, a `//` comment's included, and the spaces and tabs after it (`while (*pr_file_p==' ' || *pr_file_p == '\t') pr_file_p++;`), or the start of a file being compiled after its spaces and tabs (`QCC_PR_CompileFile` calls `QCC_PR_NewLine` first). An `#include`d file is read with `QCC_PR_Precompiler()` at its first byte and no spaces skipped, so ` #define N 5` on its first line is no directive. A `#` after a `/* */` comment on its line, or after one that spans lines, or in the middle of a line, is none. After the `#` every byte up to `' '` but a line break is passed over (`for (directive = pr_file_p+1; *directive; directive++)`, `if (*directive > ' ') break;`, a byte of 0x80 or more too, as FTEQCC's `char` is signed), so `# define` and `#` and a tab or a vertical tab before `define` are directives; a line break first is "Hanging # with no directive" (`E0121`). The name is matched by its first bytes (`if (!strncmp(directive, "define", 6))`), in FTEQCC's order: `define`, `append`, `undef`, `if`, `else` and `elif`, `endif`, `eof`, `error`, `warning`, `message`, `copyright`, `package`, `pack`, `forcecrc`, `merge`, `includelist`, `include`, `datafile`, `output` and `pragma`. So `#defined`, `#iffy`, `#elsewhere`, `#endiff`, `#eofx`, `#errors`, `#includes` and `#pragmas` are those directives. A name that matches none, `#endlist` and `#foo` among them, leaves the `#` to be read as code (FTE-23.10), `#NAME` a macro's use, and FTEQCC's "Explicit precompiler usage when not defined NAME" when `NAME` is no macro, which this profile refuses where the parser reads the `#`, first on its line of the output too (QC-9.19): `E0209` in a builtin initialiser (FTE-23.10), the parser's other errors elsewhere. Each directive's operand is read from its name's end as its own name's length gives it (`pr_file_p = directive+5;` for `undef`), so `#undefine N` undefines `ine`.

In code a `\` directly before a line break joins the lines (FTEF-13.2) with no `QCC_PR_NewLine`: `QCC_PR_LexPunctuation` passes over both (`else if ((unsigned char)*pr_file_p == (unsigned char)'\\' && (pr_file_p[1] == '\r' || pr_file_p[1] == '\n')) pr_file_p+=2;`, and `pr_file_p+=3;` for a CR LF) and calls `QCC_PR_Lex()`, whose white-space reader meets no line ending before the next line's first byte, so a `#` there, after spaces and tabs too, is no directive (FTEF-14.52) but code: the pinned FTEQCC refuses `float g; \`, a line break and `#define N 1`, `#undef N` or `#include "b.qh"` ("Explicit precompiler usage when not defined define", and `undef` or `include`), and with `#define undef 6;` and `#define N`, `float g = \`, a line break, `#undef N` and `#ifdef N` takes the `#ifdef`'s side. A `\` in a `//` comment joins nothing, as the white-space reader ends the comment at its line break and calls `QCC_PR_NewLine`; nor does a `\` that another line ending follows before the `#`, which the white-space reader passes, nor one in a directive's text, after which reading goes on at or after the line break (FTEF-14.35, FTEF-14.43). The rule holds wherever FTEQCC lexes code: a file the preprocessor reads, a macro's expansion, whose text holds a `\` and a line break only from an argument (FTEF-14.22, FTEF-14.24), so with `#define M(x) x`, `void() f = M(#5 \`, a line break, `#define Y 6` and `);` is refused, and the project graph's code (PRJ-5.13); the syntax tree makes no directive node of such a `#` (FTEF-14.51).

**Withdrawn** (P2-116, #544): it said this profile does not add the line feed `QCC_LoadFile` writes after a file's text, and the end of `#if`, `#ifdef` and `#` alone at a file's end showed that its readers do not take the text's end for a line's. Replaced by FTEF-14.64.

FTEQCC's `atoi` is the host C library's, and this profile reads it as an LP64 host (64-bit Linux and macOS) does, on every host: `(int)strtol(s, NULL, 10)` (glibc `stdlib/atoi.c`, `return (int) strtol (nptr, (char **) NULL, 10);`; Apple Libc `stdlib/FreeBSD/atoi.c`, `return (int)strtol_l(str, (char **)NULL, 10, __current_locale());`, FTEQCC setting no locale), which passes over the bytes the C locale's `isspace` takes (space, tab, LF, VT, FF and CR), reads a sign and decimal digits, holds a value past a 64-bit `long` at `LONG_MAX` or `LONG_MIN`, and keeps the low 32 bits in the `int`. It is the `atoi` of each FTEQCC reading that names one: an `#if` value (FTEF-14.33), whose `int eval` (`eval = atoi(pr_token);`, `eval = atoi(c->value);`) is compared and negated as an `int`; `#pack`'s number (`QCC_PR_LexInteger`, `return atoi (pr_token);`, FTEF-14.39); the `noref` and `autoproto` pragmas (FTEF-12.6, FTEF-12.10); and `$framevalue` (`pr_macrovalue = atoi(pr_token);`, FTEF-18.16). So, as the pinned FTEQCC reads them on macOS arm64, `#if 4294967296`, `#if -99999999999999999999` and `#define X 4294967296` then `#if X` are false; `#if 4294967297 == 1`, `#if 2147483648 < 0`, `#if -2147483649 > 0` and `#if 99999999999999999999 == -1` are true; `#if` or a `#define X` body of U+00A0, U+3000 or U+0085 before `1` is false, as `strtol` passes over none of their bytes; `#pack 4294967296` is one pack; and `$framevalue 4294967301` numbers the next frame 5, `$framevalue 99999999999` 1215752191. Where `long` is 32 bits (LLP64, 64-bit Windows) `strtol` holds a value past an `int` at `INT_MAX` or `INT_MIN`, so there `#if 4294967296` is true: a deliberate divergence from that build, as FTEF-14.50's, so that a project reads the same wherever it is opened, and the builtin differential lists a case whose directive holds a number the two read otherwise as expected where the oracle ran on an LLP64 host, a project graph case among them (PRJ-5.13). The vanilla dialect's expressions keep PRJ-5.5.

Under this profile the syntax tree reads its directive nodes (FTEF-14.51) in the text `QCC_LoadFile` gives (FTEF-14.64), at the file's own offsets (`qc_preproc::qcc_load_in_place`), so that it makes a node of each directive the preprocessor runs and stays the file's bytes: each NUL byte is read as a space, so the text goes on past it and a directive on a later line is a node, and a directive's start is found in the text after a UTF-8 byte order mark at the file's start, so `#define N 1` on the first line after one is a node, after spaces and tabs too. Only that first mark is skipped: after a second one the `#` starts no line, as FTEQCC reads it. The NUL and the mark stay in the tree as white space, and a value read from a token's text, an engine name's string among them (`ast::Builtin::engine_name`, FTE-17.5), reads a NUL as that space. Text a preprocessor wrote (`qc_syntax::parse_preprocessed`) is no file the loader read and still ends at its first NUL. A file that starts with a UTF-16 or UTF-32 byte order mark is read by the tree as its bytes to the first NUL, as under the vanilla dialect (QC-1.1): the preprocessor reads its decoded text (FTEF-14.64), whose offsets are not the file's, so how such a file is shown is the semantic model's choice, not the tree's. The vanilla dialect keeps QC-1.1.

`#undef` reads a name with `QCC_PR_SimpleGetToken` after the spaces and tabs after its name and removes the macro; a name of no macro, the empty one included, is FTEQCC's warning "Precompiler constant NAME was not defined" (`WARN_UNDEFNOTDEFINED`, with no name, `W0114`), on by default, which comes before any "unexpected tokens at end of line" of its line. `#ifdef` and `#ifndef` read a name in the same way, after a white-space byte that must follow their name; a missing name is no macro's, so `#ifdef` alone is false and `#ifndef` alone true. `#if`, `#ifdef` or `#ifndef` with a byte that is no white space right after the name (`if (!qcc_iswhite(*pr_file_p))`), as in `#ifdefX`, `#iffy` and `#if(1)`, is the Q120 warning "Unknown pragma" (`W0113`) and opens no block: reading goes on as code after the word `QCC_PR_SimpleGetToken` reads from the name, so `#if(1)` leaves `(1)`. FTEQCC's warning names `qcc_token`, the last word any `QCC_COM_Parse` or `QCC_COM_Parse2` read, a macro's expansion or a `progs.src` entry included (the pinned FTEQCC prints "Unknown pragma 't.qc'" for `#iffy` in `t.qc`); this profile names the word, `'iffy'`, a deliberate divergence, as the word FTEQCC prints stands for nothing in the directive. At the end of a file `#if`, `#ifdef` and `#ifndef` read FTEQCC's line feed after the text (FTEF-14.64).

`QCC_PR_PreProcessor_Define`'s errors have FTEQCC's texts: "No name defined for compiler constant" (`E0114`), and for a parameter list it refuses (FTEF-14.23) "May not have more than 32 parameters to a macro", "parameter name is too long (max 32)", "varadic argument must be last", "duplicate macro paramter name 'NAME'" and "missing ) in macro parameter list" (`E0115`). Its warnings are F315's (`WARN_DUPLICATEPRECOMPILER`, `W0115`) and F316's (`WARN_IDENTICALPRECOMPILER`, `W0116`, off by default), at the macro's name: an `#append` of a macro whose parameter count or `...` differs is "different number of macro arguments in macro append", and one whose names differ "arguments differ in macro append", each then defining the macro anew; a definition of a macro that already has one, an `#append` defining anew included, is "Alternate precompiler definition of NAME (OLD -> NEW)", OLD and NEW the stored bodies, when they differ, and "Identical precompiler definition of NAME" when they do not, the parameters not compared (`if (strcmp(oldcnst->value, cnst->value))`); and a body's `/*` with no `*/` before the text's end is "EOF inside quote in define NAME". So `#define A 1` then `#define A() 1` is F316's, and `#define F(a) a` then `#append F(b) 2` gives "arguments differ in macro append" and "Alternate precompiler definition of F (a -> 2)", as the pinned FTEQCC prints them.
**Withdrawn** (P2-116, #544): it gave "Include path too long." for a `#pragma includedir` of 2048 bytes, which FTEQCC's `char msg[1024]` cannot hold (FTEF-14.66). Replaced by FTEF-14.68.

In a function-like macro's body a `#` before a token that names no parameter, read with `QCC_COM_Parse2`, is written as `#` and the token, and is FTEQCC's warning "'#TOKEN' is not a macro parameter in NAME" (`QCC_PR_ParseWarning(0, ...)`, the warning of code 0, with no name, `W0117`), at the `#`, for each expansion, unless the body holds a directive (`if (!c->evil)`, FTEF-14.46). So `#define E(x) #5:x` used as `E(ex_a)` warns "'#5' is not a macro parameter in E", as the pinned FTEQCC does.

FTEQCC's `QCC_PR_DefineName` warns "Duplicate definition for Precompiler constant NAME" (Q207) when a `-D` option gives a macro defined before, `FTEQCC` and `__FTEQCC__` included, another body; it prints it against no file, "cmdline", and this profile, which defines a module's `defines` as FTEQCC's `-D` options (FTEF-14.48), does not report it. `#define` removes the macro before it defines it, so it never gives this warning.

FTEQCC's warnings are reported as its `qccwarningaction` sets each, `WA_IGNORE` not at all, `WA_WARN` as the warning and `WA_ERROR` as an error, which FTEQCC prints as "werror" (`QCC_PR_PrintWarning`, `else if (qccwarningaction[type] == 2)`): `E0125` with the warning's text, F303's `E0122` (FTEF-14.46). The settings start as `QCC_SetDefaultProperties` makes them, every warning `WA_WARN` but F208, F209, F300, F311, F330, F322, F301, F302, F331, `localptr` and F316 `WA_IGNORE` and F303 and F313 `WA_ERROR` (`qccwarningaction[WARN_FTE_SPECIFIC] = WA_IGNORE;` and the rest), and again before the second autoprototyping pass (FTEF-14.48). `#pragma warning STATE NAME ...` reads its text with `QCC_COM_Parse`: STATE `enable` or `on` warns, `disable`, `off` or `ignore` ignores, `error` errs and `toggle` sets `!!` of the setting, so a warning stays one and an error becomes one (`qccwarningaction[wn] = !!qccwarningaction[wn];`), in any case (`stricmp`); any other STATE is the Q120 warning "warning state not recognised" (`W0113`) and changes nothing. Each NAME is looked up in `warningnames[]` in any case (`QCC_WarningForName`, `stricmp(name, warningnames[i].name+1)`): `Q100` to `Q302`, `F129`, `F207` to `F211`, `F300` to `F335`, `field-redeclared`, `deprecated`, `bounds`, `octal`, `unimplemented`, `localptr` and `largereturn`; one it does not know is "warning id not recognised" (`W0113`, as the settings stand when FTEQCC reads it). A setting holds for the rest of the module, the files read after it included, and a warning is reported as the settings stand where FTEQCC reads its bytes: so `#pragma warning disable F325` before a `/* /* */` comment drops `W0112`, and `#pragma warning error octal` makes `float y = 017;` after it `E0125`, which the pinned FTEQCC refuses ("werror octal: A leading 0 is interpreted as base-8."). Warnings FTEQCC gives no name are always reported. The settings in force from each token on are in the preprocessor's output (`qc_preproc::FileOutput::warnings`), for the warnings the parser and the semantic model report.

A source file is read as the text FTEQCC's `QCC_LoadFile` (`qcc_cmdlib.c`) hands its lexer, by the preprocessor and by the project graph (PRJ-5.13), a compiled file and an `#include`d one alike. `QCC_SanitizeCharSet` decodes a file that starts with the byte order mark of UTF-32LE (`ff fe 00 00`), UTF-32BE (`00 00 fe ff`), UTF-16LE (`ff fe`) or UTF-16BE (`fe ff`), tested in that order, to UTF-8 with `decodeUTF`, skips a UTF-8 one (`mem += 3;`), and leaves any other file as it is. `decodeUTF` reads whole code units only (`chars = inbytes / w;`), joins a high surrogate to a low one after it (`if (inc >= 0xd800u && inc < 0xdc00u && i+1 < chars)`), writes any other surrogate in three bytes as any value of U+0800 to U+FFFF, and makes a value past U+10FFFF U+FFFD (`if (inc > 0x10FFFF) inc = 0xFFFD;`). Then every NUL byte of the text is a space (`else if (!mem[check])`, `mem[check] = ' ';`), so the text goes on past a NUL where QC-1.1 ends it: the pinned FTEQCC refuses `void() f = #5;`, a line break, a NUL and `zz zz zz` ("\"zz\" is not a type"), refuses `#define N #5`, a NUL, `zz`, a line break and `void() f = N;`, and binds `f` to builtin 5 after `#ifdef Q`, a line break, `zz`, a NUL, a line break and `#endif`. A NUL first in a compiled file is a space `QCC_PR_NewLine` passes over, and first in an included file a byte before its `#`, so no directive starts there (FTEF-14.52). After a UTF-8 byte order mark a directive starts a compiled file's first line, after spaces and tabs too, and an included file's first byte; FTEQCC binds `f` to builtin 5 from `#define N #5` and `void() f = N;` after one, with and without two spaces before the `#`, and from `void() f = #5;` written as UTF-16LE after its mark. FTEQCC warns "file contains null bytes N/LEN" once for a file with a NUL, N the first NUL's offset in the text and LEN the text's length (`QCC_PR_Warning(WARN_UNEXPECTEDPUNCT, filename, line, "file contains null bytes %u/%"pPRIuSIZE, check, len)`), a warning with no name, `W0117`. `QCC_LoadFile` then writes a line feed after the text (`mem[len] = '\n';`), and this profile's readers read it too, so every directive and token at a file's end meets a line's end before the text's: the pinned FTEQCC refuses a file that ends in `#if` ("unexpected end-of-line"), in `#ifdef` ("#if with no endif") or in `#` ("Hanging # with no directive"), and calls a string that the file's end leaves open "newline inside quote" (`E0102`), as this profile does. A diagnostic's place in the file is the bytes its text came from: 3 bytes on after a UTF-8 mark, in a decoded file the code unit each byte came from, and the file's end for the line feed (`qc_preproc::SourceFile::file_span`). The vanilla dialect keeps QC-1.1: a file's bytes, its text ending at the first NUL.
**Withdrawn** (P2-116, #544): it left a `#pragma` line of 1024 bytes or more unmodelled, which this profile now reports as an error (FTEF-14.66). Replaced by FTEF-14.70.

`QCC_PR_SimpleGetToken`, `QCC_PR_SimpleGetString` and `QCC_PR_LexMacroName` read into `pr_token` and stop the compile with `QCC_Error (ERR_INTERNAL, "token exceeds %i chars", i)` at a 1024th byte (`if (i == sizeof(qcc_token)-1)`), and `QCC_PR_SimpleGetString` with "new line inside string" at a line break in its string. So a name of 1024 bytes after `#define`, `#undef`, `#ifdef`, `#ifndef`, `#elifdef` or `#elifndef`, a word of an `#if` or `#elif` expression, an `#includelist` word or a list's output (PRJ-4.9), and a string of 1024 bytes or with a line break after `#output`, `#merge` or `#datafile`, are each an error, `E0121` with FTEQCC's text, and a frame macro word of 1024 bytes is `E0502` with it; 1023 bytes are read. A `#pragma`'s name, or its text after the name, of 1024 bytes runs past `char msg[1024]`, which `msg[a++] = *pr_file_p;` fills with no bound. That is undefined behaviour, and the pinned builds differ. On macOS the build stops at the overrun (exit -6, for `#pragma foo` with 1024 bytes of text too, so it is `msg` and no path limit), and on Windows too; the Linux build of CI reads on and compiles the program for texts of 1024 and 1025 bytes. This profile reports `E0121` "#pragma name or text longer than FTEQCC's 1023 bytes" for each, a deliberate divergence. The differential takes such a case's other outcome on Linux as this statement's (`Overrun::Unseen`), and a recording there keeps the stopping build's outcome. `QCC_COM_Parse` keeps 1023 bytes of a longer word and drops the rest (`if (len >= sizeof(qcc_token)-1) ;`), which a pragma's words and a list's files are read with. After such an error FTEQCC's compile stops: the preprocessor reads no more of the file and the graph no more of it, but the lexer reads on after a frame word, so diagnostics FTEQCC would not reach may follow it. The pinned FTEQCC (`fteqcc -Tid`) gives each error at 1024 bytes and none at 1023.

`QCC_PR_LexWhitespace` reports a `/* */` comment the text ends in with `QCC_PR_ParseError(0, "EOF inside comment\n");` where it reads white space outside the lexer's tokens: after a use's `(` and each `,` (FTEF-14.22), before each `#includelist` word (FTEF-14.41) and before each word of a list-form `progs.src` (PRJ-4.9). This profile reports it as `E0501` "EOF inside comment" at the comment's `/*`, and the reading ends at the end of the text; the pinned FTEQCC gives it for a list `progs.dat`, `t.qc /* open`.

`QCC_PR_AddIncludePath`'s warnings have no name (`WARN_STRINGTOOLONG`, `W0117`): "Too many include dirs. Ignoring and hoping the stars align." for a ninth directory a `#pragma includedir` adds, and "Include path too long." for a directory that with its `/` has 2048 bytes or more, as the copy is bounded by the whole table (`sizeof(qccincludedir)`, `char qccincludedir[MAXINCLUDEDIRS][256]`), the directory then not kept. A `#pragma includedir` cannot name one so long: its text past 1023 bytes runs past FTEQCC's `msg` (FTEF-14.66), and `QCC_COM_Parse` and `char newinc[1024]` hold 1023 bytes of it. Only a module's `-I` option (FTEF-14.49) can, and FTEQCC prints its warnings against no file (`s_filen` "cmdline"), which this profile does not report. A name of 256 to 1023 bytes runs on into the next slots of FTEQCC's table, which this profile does not model: it keeps the name whole, as a later directory FTEQCC adds overwrites the bytes.

`#copyright` copies into `msg` only the bytes after its name that are white space (`for (a = 0; a < sizeof(msg)-1 && qcc_iswhite(pr_file_p[a]) && pr_file_p[a] != '\0'; a++)`), at most 1023, so its test `if (strlen(msg) >= sizeof(QCC_copyright))` against `char QCC_copyright[1024]` never holds and "Copyright message is too long" is never given; this profile gives no diagnostic for a `#copyright` of any length. The pinned FTEQCC gives none for 2000 bytes of text or of spaces.

Of the other pragmas, these change what the preprocessor reads: `DONT_COMPILE_THIS_FILE` passes over the rest of the text a byte at a time after white space read as `QCC_PR_LexWhitespace(false)` reads it, so the directives at the starts of its lines still run, an `#error` refusing the program; `once` marks the file being compiled (`strcpy(onced->name, compilingfile);`), not the file it is in, so a header's `#pragma once` keeps nothing from being read twice; `includedir` adds the directory its first token (`QCC_COM_Parse`) names, a `/` after it unless it ends in one, joined to the file being compiled, after the others, at most 8 (`MAXINCLUDEDIRS`, FTEF-14.68); `noref` and `autoproto` take their text with `atoi` (FTEF-12.6, FTEF-12.10), so `#pragma noref(1)` is 0; `warning STATE NAME ...` sets FTEQCC's warning settings (FTEF-14.63); and `flag` and `keyword` set the compiler flags (FTEF-12.11). The rest, `COPYRIGHT`, `compress`, `forcecrc`, `framerate`, `file` (FTEF-14.74), `line` (FTEF-14.43), `nosave`, `defaultstatic`, `wrasm`, `optimise` and `optimize`, `sourcefile`, `TARGET`, `PROGS_SRC`, `PROGS_DAT` and `opcode`, change the build, with the warnings of FTEF-12.11, and an unknown one is the Q120 warning "Unknown pragma 'NAME'" (`W0113`). `#pragma COPYRIGHT`'s warning "Copyright message is too long" needs a text of 1024 bytes or more, which overruns FTEQCC's `char msg[1024]` first, as `#copyright`'s, which copies only the white space after its name (`qcc_iswhite(pr_file_p[a])`), cannot reach it; a pragma line of 1024 bytes or more is that undefined behaviour, which this profile reports as an error (FTEF-14.66).
**Withdrawn** (P2-119, #554): it said `-std=` is not read, but `-std=` sets the keywords the parser reads (FTEF-20.1). Replaced by FTEF-14.72.

First `QCC_CheckParm ("-Fqccx")`, in any case (`QC_strcasecmp`), ignores F313 and F314. An argument that starts with `-W` in any case (`strnicmp(myargv[i], "-W", 2)`) is a warning option, its text after `-W` compared in any case: `all` makes each ignored warning a warning but F208, F209, F311, F330 and F332 ("these warnings require -Wextra to enable"), and F319, Q205, F312, F307, F320, F322, F321, Q208 and F211 only while F321 is not ignored; `extra` makes every ignored warning a warning; `none` ignores every warning; `error` sets `werror`; `no-mundane` ignores F306, Q207, F319, Q201, F300, F208, Q302, Q205, Q120, F316, the warning of an `#undef` of no macro, F209, F301 and F331; `error-NAME`, `no-NAME` and `NAME` set the warning `QCC_WarningForName` finds for NAME (FTEF-14.63) to an error, ignored or a warning, and a NAME it does not find changes nothing. `-Farithmetic-exceptions` makes F332 an error and `-Fno-arithmetic-exceptions` ignores it. After every argument, with `werror` set, each warning not ignored is an error (`if (qccwarningaction[j]) qccwarningaction[j] = WA_ERROR;`). An argument that starts with `-F` or `-K` in any case turns on, or after `no-` off, the first row of `compiler_flag[]` whose abbreviation it names in any case, whether or not the row has `FLAG_MIDCOMPILE`, so only the command line sets `caseinsens`. The command line's warnings for arguments it does not recognise ("Unrecognised warning parameter", printed against "cmdline") are not reported: they belong to no file of the module. A `-F` NAME no row of `compiler_flag[]` has is a compatibility flag: `short-logic` sets the `lo` optimisation, `correct-logic` `ifvector` and `vectorlogic`, and `false-empty-strings` `ifstring`, each turned off after `no-`. An argument that starts with `-std=` in any case sets every flag and keyword to its default (`*compiler_flag[p].enabled = !!(compiler_flag[p].flags & FLAG_ASDEFAULT)`) and then a dialect's, in order with the `-K` and `-F` options: `C`, `c89`, `c90`, `c99`, `c11` and `c17` in any case "set up for greatest C compatibility" (`for`, `goto`, `extern`, `static`, `auto`, `switch`, `case`, `default`, `int`, `typedef`, `struct`, `union`, `enum`, `float`, `double`, `long`, `short`, `char`, `signed`, `unsigned`, `register` and `volatile` on; `asm`, `accessor`, `class`, `var`, `inout`, `optional`, `state`, `inline`, `nosave`, `shared`, `noref`, `unused`, `used`, `local`, `nonstatic`, `ignore`, `strip`, `vector`, `entity`, `string`, `integer`, `enumflags`, `thinktime`, `until` and `loop` off; `ILP32`, `lo`, `assumevar`, `subscope`, `cpriority`, `assumeint`, `assumedouble` and `iffloat` on and `qcfuncs`, `macroinstrings` and `boundchecks` off; and F302 a warning, Q101, Q105 and Q106 errors, and F306, `octal` and Q205 ignored), `c++` the same with `class` and `inline` then on; `c23` none of them, being missing from the test of the C names; and, compared exactly, `qccx` (`qccx` on, F313 and F314 ignored), `preqcc` (`hashonly` and `macroinstrings` on), `reacc` (`acc` on, `macroinstrings` off), `frikqcc` (`state` on, `macroinstrings` off), `fteqcc` (none), `qcc` and `id` (`ifvector`, `vectorlogic`, `asm`, `break`, `continue`, `for`, `goto`, `const`, `var`, `inout`, `optional`, `state`, `inline`, `nosave`, `extern`, `shared`, `noref`, `unused`, `used`, `static`, `nonstatic`, `ignore`, `strip`, `switch`, `case`, `default`, `accessor`, `class`, `vector`, `entity`, `float`, `string`, `int`, `integer`, `typedef`, `struct`, `union`, `enum`, `enumflags`, `thinktime`, `until`, `loop`, `wrap` and `weak` off, and F320 an error), `hcc` and `hexenc` (the same off but `break`, `switch`, `case` and `default`, with `macroinstrings` off and `thinktime`, `until`, `loop`, `switch`, `case`, `default` and `break` on), and `gmqcc` (`ifvector`, `vectorlogic`, `ssp`, `attributes`, `assumevar`, `subscope`, `cpriority`, `allowuninit`, `reciprocal-math`, `undefwordsize` and `lo` on, `boundchecks` and `macroinstrings` off, `asm`, `inout`, `optional`, `state`, `inline`, `nosave`, `extern`, `shared`, `unused`, `used`, `nonstatic`, `ignore`, `strip`, `accessor`, `class`, `vector`, `entity`, `float`, `string`, `int`, `integer`, `struct`, `union`, `enumflags`, `thinktime`, `until`, `loop`, `wrap` and `weak` off and `enum`, `break`, `continue`, `for`, `goto`, `typedef`, `switch`, `case`, `default`, `const`, `var`, `static` and `noref` on; and F208, F319, Q205, F312, F307, F320, F322, F302, F321, `octal`, Q208, F211 and F333 ignored and Q106 an error); any other is "Unrecognised std parameter", the flags already at their defaults. The macros `-std=` defines for the C dialects (`__STDC_HOSTED__`, `__STDC_VERSION__` and the rest) are not read, as the profile reads no `-D` of the command line: a module's defines are the project graph's (PRJ-5.4). The module is compiled as `fteqcc -Tid` with these options after it (PRJ-3.4), so its target is the standard one, which the `-h2`, `-fte`, `-fteh2` and `-dp` that `QCC_SetDefaultProperties` reads before the options cannot change, and then that of each `-TNAME` that names one of `targets[]` (`QCC_OPCodeSetTargetName`, FTEF-12.11), in order, `-Tparse` none. The `/W`, `/F` and `/K` spellings FTEQCC reads only on Windows (`WINDOWSARG`) are not read: the pinned oracle is not built for Windows.

Under `-Fcaseinsens`, which only the command line sets (FTEF-14.72), FTEQCC searches its macro table in any case: `pHash_Get = &Hash_GetInsensitive;` and `QCC_PR_CheckCompConst`, `QCC_PR_DefineName` and `QCC_PR_UndefineName` look a name up with `pHash_Get(&compconstantstable, name)`. So after `#define Foo 5` a use of `foo` or `FOO`, `#ifdef foo`, `#ifndef foo`, `#if defined(foo)`, `#if foo == 5` and a macro whose body names `foo` find it, and without `-Fcaseinsens` they do not; a definition in another case finds the old macro (`oldcnst = pHash_Get(&compconstantstable, pr_token);`) and replaces it. `#undef` finds the macro the same way, with no "was not defined" warning, but removes it with `Hash_Remove(&compconstantstable, name)`, which hashes the name as written and compares it exactly: `#undef foo` of a macro defined as `Foo` leaves it defined, and `#undef` of a name with an upper case letter, or a redefinition of a macro that was defined with one, looks in a bucket the macro was not added to, which the pinned FTEQCC reads when it is empty and ends with a segmentation fault (measured on macOS arm64, the differential's host). This profile removes a macro only when the `#undef` names its spelling, finds it in any case, and never ends; the differential holds no program that makes FTEQCC read an empty bucket. The macros FTEQCC defines itself, `FTEQCC` and `__FTEQCC__`, are added before the search is switched, to the buckets of the name as written, so under `-Fcaseinsens` `#ifdef FTEQCC` is false, as is `#ifdef fteqcc` (measured); this profile finds no built-in macro there.

The semantic model (`Db::analyze_module`) gives the preprocessor each file it compiles at the path the database holds it by and named by the name its input holds for it, which for an FTEQCC module's graph (`ModuleInput::from_graph`) is the graph's name (PRJ-6.7), and the preprocessor opens each name an `#include` is joined to (FTEF-14.40) as the file of that name in the input's directory, the graph's (PRJ-6.8). So `__FILE__` (FTEF-14.74) in a listed file and in each file it includes is the name FTEQCC gives it, compiled in the source's directory: with `progs.src` listing `src/a.qc` it binds `void() f = :__FILE__;` to `src/a.qc` in that file, to `src/x/b.qh` in the `x/b.qh` it includes, to `src/c.qh` in a `c.qh` that one includes, to `src/y/c.qh` after `#pragma includedir y`, to `src/./b.qh` in a `b.qh` that `src/./a.qc` includes, and to `inc/c.qh` in a `c.qh` found with `-Iinc` or `-Iinc/`; with it listing `sub\top.qc`, to `sub`, a tab and `op.qc`, the `\t` an escape (FTEF-14.74), and in a `tab.qh` that file includes, to `sub`, a tab and `ab.qh`. A file with no name in the input is named by its path. The named projects of `cargo xtask oracles builtins` (`NAMED_PROJECTS` and `NAMED_DIR_PROJECTS` in `xtask/src/oracles/builtins/directives.rs`) hold these cases, the profile reading every FTEQCC case with no `progs.src` of its own through its graph in a directory of its own (`graph_input`), and the run of 2026-10-22 (macOS arm64) bound each as the pinned FTEQCC does.

A declaration may start with qualifiers, read by the loop at the start of `QCC_PR_ParseDefs`: `extern`, `static`, `shared`, `const`, `var`, `nonstatic`, `noref`, `nosave`, `strip`, `inline`, `wrap` and `weak`, and also, written with a leading `__`, `auto`, `register`, `unused`, `used`, `ignore`, `accumulate` and `deprecated`, which may take a `("reason")`. `QCC_PR_CheckKeyword` matches any keyword written with `__` whether or not it is enabled ("lets just always go insensitive with a leading underscore pair"). Then comes a type. At file level a name that is no statement word starts a declaration when a name, a `*` or a parameter list follows it, since a type name is followed by its declarator; a name alone is still "not a type" (FTE-21.1).

A function's return type may be any type: `QCC_PR_ParseType` ends with `if (flag_qcfuncs && QCC_PR_CheckToken ("("))` after any type, a user type or a pointer included. A function may be initialised with a value as well as a body or a builtin, as `QCC_PR_ParseInitializerType_Internal` does with `tmp = QCC_PR_Expression(TOP_PRIORITY, EXPR_DISALLOW_COMMA);`: another function, or `0`.

A parameter (`QCC_PR_ParseFunctionType`) has optional qualifiers `optional`, `__in`, `__out` and `__inout`; a type; an optional `&` ("accept c++ syntax"); then a name, a function pointer `(*name)(params)`, or nothing, since `else if (pr_token_type == tt_name) name = QCC_PR_ParseName ();` takes a name only when there is one; array suffixes; and a default value. A lone unnamed `void` is no parameter (`else if (paramlist[numparms].type->type == ev_void) break; //float(void) has no actual args`). `...` ends the list, after a type or alone, and may be followed by the name of the argument count. A `*` after a function type makes a pointer to it, `void(void() *a) h = #6;`.

A function type has at most `MAX_PARMS+MAX_EXTRA_PARMS` parameters ("Too many parameters. Sorry. (limit is %i)"), with `#define MAX_EXTRA_PARMS 128` and id's `MAX_PARMS` of 8 (`LIMIT_MAX_PARMS`, QC-27.7): 136 under this profile, not 8.

`wrap`, `weak` and `accumulate` let a function be defined again: a `wrap` definition replaces the one before it and may call it as `prior` (`PIF_WRAP`, "wrapper function does not wrap anything" when there is none), a `weak` one gives way to a later definition, and an `accumulate` one is extended by later ones. `extern` says the body is elsewhere ("function is external, don't error or warn if the body was not found"). A `var` function-typed name is a variable that holds a function, not a function to define: `QCC_PR_ParseDefs` makes "functions and fields ... always ... consts even when not initialised", unless `var`.
`T a, *b` declares `b` a pointer, and `struct { ... } a[4], *p;` declares variables of an unnamed struct, as C does; each `*` before a declarator's name is a level of pointer (FTEF-4.1).

A name is "name too long" (`E0202`) from 255 bytes, not id's 63 (QC-3.3): `QCC_PR_ParseName` (`qcc_pr_lex.c`) reports `if (strlen(pr_token) >= MAX_NAME-1) QCC_PR_ParseError (ERR_NAMETOOLONG, "name too long");` with `#define MAX_NAME 256` in `qcc.h`. So a name of 254 bytes is accepted in a declaration, after `#number:`, in an expression and after `::`, and one of 255 is the error; the pinned FTEQCC, built by `cargo xtask oracles build`, gives the same for `float n...;`, `void() f = #5:n...;` and `x = n...;` in a body, at 254 and 255 bytes. The name after a lone `:` is no `QCC_PR_ParseName` (FTE-23.6), so it has no limit. The vanilla dialect keeps QC-3.3.

A declaration's declarators may end with a `,` before its `;`: `QCC_PR_ParseDefs` (`qcc_pr_comp.c`) reads them in `do { ... } while (QCC_PR_CheckToken (","));`, each starting with `if (QCC_PR_CheckToken (";"))`, which ends the declaration. So `void() f = #5, ;` and `void() g, f = #5,;` declare `f` the builtin 5, as the pinned FTEQCC compiles them, and so does `#define E(...) #5 __VA_ARGS__` used as `E(, )` (FTEF-14.26); `void() f = #5, , ;` is refused, a `,` being no name. The vanilla parser is unchanged.

With `qcfuncs` on, after a function type, `(name)` followed by `;`, `=`, `,` or `[`, `name` no type, is C's parenthesised name: `QCC_PR_ParseDefs` tries `QCC_PR_ParseFunctionType` after the `(`, which finds no type there, and its C-style branch reads the name with no `*` (`isvar |= isptr>0`, so no variable). So `typedef void() (fn);` and `typedef float() (fn);` define `fn` a function type, `void() (g) = {};` defines `g`, and `void() (g), (h);` declares two functions with no body. With `qcfuncs` off the list is a QC parameter list and the declarator has no name, `";" - not a name`, as it has for a type's name (`typedef float t; void() (t);`).

A parameter whose type writes a struct, union or enum (`void(union { float a; vector v; } u) f`, `void(enum { EA } e) f`) has that type, read with the type (`QCC_PR_ParseType`), so the function's type prints it (`void(union <union> u)`) and the parameter is a value of it in the body.

A `wrap` definition's body takes over the record of the function it wraps, which moves to a new record at the end of the function table named `prior*NAME` (`QCC_PR_GenerateQCFunction`: `prior = &functions[numfunctions++]; memcpy(prior, func, sizeof(*prior));` and `strcpy(prior->name, "prior*");`), so the name keeps its function number and the wrapped body is called through `prior`: a constant of the function's type whose value is the moved record's number (`QCC_MakeUniqueConst(type_function, &funcref)` with `funcref = numfunctions-1`, and a static constant `prior` over it in the wrapper). So after `void() f = { a(); }; __wrap void() f = { prior(); b(); };` calling `f` runs `b` after `a`. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_GenerateQCFunction`, `QCC_PR_ParseImmediateStatements`.

A statement declares locals when it starts with a qualifier (FTEF-15.1), a C type word (FTEF-2), a `.`, or a name followed by a name, by `*`s, a name and a `;`, `=`, `,` or `[`, or by a parameter list and a name. FTEQCC decides by `QCC_TypeForName`; no expression statement has these shapes, except a product `a * b` alone, which this profile reads as an expression unless a declarator's end follows.

`(type) e` is a cast to any type: `QCC_PR_RefTerm` reads `(`, then `newtype = QCC_PR_ParseType(false, true, false)`, and, after `)`, `e = QCC_PR_Expression (UNARY_PRIORITY, EXPR_DISALLOW_COMMA);` or, before `{`, an initialiser of the type. This profile takes a cast where `(` holds a type word, a `.` or a C type word; or a name and `*`s or a function type's parameter list, closed by `)` and followed by a term; or a lone name in parentheses followed by a term. `(visible(head))` and `(sin(x))` stay parenthesised calls.

`[x, y, z]` builds a vector of three expressions, the missing ones 0 ("and to not need the 2nd/3rd parts if you're lazy - [5] or [5,6]"); a fourth is an error, since `QCC_PR_Expect("]")` follows the third.

`Class::member` names a member of a class or its parents, `super::member` one of the parent of the class whose member function it is, and `::name` a name of the global scope (`if (QCC_PR_CheckToken("::")) { assumeclass = NULL;`).
`if not (e)` takes the statement when `e` is false: `int negate = QCC_PR_CheckKeyword(keyword_not, "not")/*hexenc*/;`.
A call may be followed by a subscript, a member or another call; in vanilla a call ends the term (QC-15.8).
A term may start with `++` or `--` (`QCC_PR_RefTerm`'s `preinc`), `&` (an address, FTEF-4.2) or `*` (a dereference, FTEF-4.4); the operand is a term with its postfix forms.
Adjacent string literals are one string: `QCC_PR_LexString` reads strings in a loop that skips whitespace and comments and ends only where no `"` follows (`else if (first) ... else break;`).

A clause of a `for` header may hold several expressions separated by `,`, and the first clause a declaration after them (`v = 0, int i = 1`). `QCC_PR_ParseStatement_For` reads the first clause with `type = QCC_PR_ParseType (false, true, false)`, so any type starts a declaration there, `for (accessor A : float i; ; )` and `for (enumflags E { A } i; ; )` among them, which a statement's `accessor` and `enumflags` do not (FTEF-20.14).
A call's result may be assigned to, as in the chain `a = f() = b` the corpus writes; FTEQCC reports no error there, so neither does this profile.
An aggregate initialiser may name the member each value initialises, `{ .name = value, ... }`.
A `case` or `default` label may stand in a block nested in the `switch` body, as C allows; the corpus does so (`client/viewmodel.qc`).

Any expression may stand left of an assignment operator: `QCC_PR_RefExpression` reads the left side as a term whatever it is, and an assignment to a value that is no variable is checked, not refused by the parser (FTEF-29.1). `~a = 1`, `1 = a` and `(a = 2) = 3` each give the two "Assignment to const" warnings, not a syntax error (the pinned FTEQCC, 2026-10-27), so this profile's parser reports none; vanilla's E0508 (QC-27.10) stays.

`local` starts no declaration in a `for` header: `QCC_PR_ParseStatement_For` reads the first clause with `QCC_PR_ParseType (false, true, false)`, which takes no `local`, so the word is a name there, made a `variant` by `QCC_PR_GetDef` with the warning `W0221` "\"local\" keyword used as variable name - coexisting" and then "Unknown value \"local\"." (FTEF-19.45), and the type word after it is "expected ;, found float". The warning is given for any unknown name that is a keyword in force (FTEF-20.4).

`(NAME)` where `QCC_PR_ParseType` finds no type of the name is no cast but the value in parentheses, an unknown name a `variant` (FTEF-19.69), and what this profile's parser read as the cast's operand follows it (FTEF-16.2): `- e`, and a negative number, which the lexer splits after a value (`QCC_PR_IncludeChunk`), is a subtraction, `(x) -1` as `x - 1`; `(args)` calls the value, "not a function" of a `float`; `[i]` is an index the value does not take (FTEF-18.37, FTEF-18.38); and a number or a name is "Expected punctuation" (`WARN_UNEXPECTEDPUNCT`), then "expected ;, found TOKEN", or in a definition's value the end of the value, "Missing semicolon at end of definition" and at global scope "\"TOKEN\" is not a type". So `(x)[1] = 2;` of a `float x` is "Statement does not do anything" and "expected ;, found [", `y = (x) 1;` "Expected punctuation" and "expected ;, found 1", and no `(x)` is "\"x\" is not a type". Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_RefTerm`, `QCC_PR_RefExpression`.

A class, struct, union, typedef, enum or accessor names a type, and its name may be used where a value is (`spawn(ncTimer)`, `sizeof(graphNode_t)`). A type's name may be declared again: a class forward and then with its body, a typedef in two headers.

**Withdrawn** (P2-133, #574): it said a name in a member function's body is found among the members of its class, but `QCC_PR_ParseValue` reaches a field as `this.field` through the global `self`, without which FTEQCC ends; replaced by FTEF-17.14.

The name after `.` or `->` is a member of the class of what the access is made on, when that is known from a name's declared type, `this`, a cast or a call's return type; else an entity field the name defines; else a member of any class with the name. A vector's `x`, `y` and `z`, `.length`, and a field of a struct or accessor name no definition, and a name that is a value but no field is not checked; any other name is "Unknown value" (QCD-4.1).

`this`, `super` and, in a `wrap` function, `prior` are no names a program defines, and neither are the intrinsics `QCC_PR_ParseRefValue` declares on demand ("intrinsics, any old function with no args will do"): `nil`, `randomv`, `alloca`, `entnum`, `autocvar`, `used_model`, `used_sound`, `va_arg` and `_`, with `sizeof` and `_length`. `autocvar(name, default)` takes the cvar's name, which is no value, and `sizeof` may take a type word.
**Withdrawn** 2026-10-20 (P2-70): it compared a builtin by its number alone, but FTEQCC reuses a builtin function only for the same number and engine name; replaced by FTEF-17.10.

A name initialised again is accepted when the "dupe initialisation" comparison finds the two values equal word by word: this profile compares two literals by value (FTE-22.6), a builtin by its number and engine name as FTE-23.17 says, any other initialiser, a builtin FTEQCC binds no number for among them, by its text, token for token. An enum's names are never redeclared: `QCC_PR_ParseEnum` makes each with `QCC_PR_DummyDef`, which looks for no earlier definition. A function body is never equal to another.

**Withdrawn** (P2-117, #545): it took every type name for one whose meaning the model does not follow, but a typedef's name is the type it names (`QCC_TypeForName`, FTEF-19.9). Replaced by FTEF-17.12.

**Withdrawn** (P2-84, #495): it said a function with no body is an error only where the module refers to it, but the check's `d->unused` is the `noref` mark, so FTEQCC reports every bodyless function that is not both `noref` and unreferenced. Replaced by FTEF-17.11.

A definition marked `noref` or `unused`, by its qualifier or a `#pragma noref 1` before it (FTEF-12.6), may be initialised again with another value: the "dupe initialisation" comparison runs only `if (basedef->initialized && !basedef->unused ...)`. The corpus's `fteextensions.qc` sets `#pragma noref 1` and a later file binds `getgamedirinfo = #0` again.

A function that has a body, given a builtin number again, keeps its body, with the warning `W0206` "incompatible redeclaration. Ignoring replacement of qc function with builtin.": the "dupe initialisation" comparison of `QCC_PR_GenerateInitializerType` has `else if (!def.sym->arraysize && def.cast->type == ev_function && functions[QCC_SRef_DataWord(def, i)->_int].code>-1 && functions[QCC_SRef_DataWord(tmp, i)->_int].code==-1)` before its "incompatible redeclaration" error. As FTEF-17.8, the comparison is not made for a definition marked `noref`. Copper's client module defines `sin` in `maths.qc` and then reads `float(float angle) sin = #60;` in `csdefs.qc`.

A function with no body is an error ("function %s has no body", `E0211` here) unless it is marked `noref`, by its qualifier or a `#pragma noref 1` (FTEF-12.6), and the module does not refer to it: FTEQCC's check (`qccmain.c`) skips a definition only `if (d->unused && !d->used)`, `unused` being the `noref` mark, before `QCC_PR_Warning(ERR_NOFUNC, d->filen, d->s_line, "function %s has no body",d->name);`. So `void() f = #5;` then `void() g;` is an error, as are `void() f = #5, g;` and `#define V(a, ...) a,##__VA_ARGS__` used as `V(#5, g)`, and the pinned FTEQCC refuses each; `noref void() g;` compiles, and a `noref` function that is called is an error. A member function is not checked, and a class's `spawnfunc_Name` (FTEF-9.5), whose body FTEQCC writes when the program does not, is never undefined.

**Withdrawn** (P2-132, #569): it said a pointer is a type the model does not follow, but FTEQCC compares pointers by what they point to, and `float *a; float a;` is a mismatch. Replaced by FTEF-17.13.
**Withdrawn** (#84): it said a redeclaration involving a class, struct, union, accessor or enum type was never a mismatch; FTEQCC's `typecmp` compares those types too, and FTEF-17.21 replaces it.

A class's members are found through the class and its parents (`QCC_PR_ParseEntClass` keeps each class's members, with `newt->parentclass`). `Class::member` defines the member the class or a parent declares, or adds one, and its name refers to the member's declaration. In a member function's body a name is the function's own local or parameter, then a member of its class or a parent, then a global. A field, a `virtual` function among them, is read as `this.field` (`if (pr_classtype && expandmemberfields && d.cast->type == ev_field)`), `this` being made from the global `self` (`QCC_PR_DummyDef(pr_classtype, "this", pr_scope, 0, QCC_PR_GetDef(NULL, "self", NULL, true, 0, false), ...)`), so `entity self; class C { float a; void() m = { a = 1; }; };` and `void() C::m = { a = 1; };` after it compile; with no `self` defined FTEQCC ends in that `QCC_PR_GetDef` (the oracle records the program as refused), which this profile reports as "Unknown value" at the name. `this.a = 1;` needs no `self`, and `m()` calls a nonvirtual `m`. A class's own name there is the class, as `spawn(Thing)` takes it, not its constructor. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseValue`.

A member function written with its body inside its class is compiled where it stands, so a member the class declares after it is not there yet: `n();` is "Unknown value \"n\"." and `this.n` or `this.a` "Unknown field \"n\" in class \"C\"" for a later `n` or `a`, which a body written after the class sees. `this` there is the entity as the class's type (FTEF-17.14), so `local float f = this;` is "Cannot cast from class C to float".

`TYPE Class::member` of a member the class or a parent declares is `QCC_PR_GetDef` of `Class::member` with TYPE, so a TYPE that `typecmp` tells from the member's is the error `E0205` "Type mismatch on redeclaration of Class::member. TYPE, should be MEMBERTYPE", and the definition is not read on. Parameter names do not count, a class is told from the entity and another class, and a typedef is its type: `void() C::m` and `float(float x) C::m` for `void(float x) m` are refused, `void(float y) C::m` is not. A constructor declared `C();` is of type `void()` (`QCC_PR_GenFunctionType(type_void, ...)`), so `C() C::C = {};` is "C(), should be void()" and `void() C::C = {};` defines it. The types are named as `TypeName` names them, a class as `class NAME`, inside a function's parameters too.

`autocvar(name, default[, "description"])` is the global `autocvar_name`, made by the call with the default's type and value (`QCC_PR_GetSRef(e.cast, autocvarname, NULL, true, 0, GDF_USED)`), so the call is a value of that type: `string s = autocvar(sv_x, 1);` is "Cannot cast from float to string". A default that is no constant is the error `E0367` "autocvar default value is not constant", and one that differs from the value the global was given before, by its definition or an earlier call, is the fatal error `E0368` "autocvar NAME was already initialised with another value". The global is a definition as any other: the rest of the module refers to it, a global `autocvar_name` of another type is "Type mismatch on redeclaration", before the call or after it, and a later one given another value is "incompatible redeclaration". Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseFunctionCall`.

In a member function, `self` not after `::` is `this`, the function's class: `QCC_PR_ParseValue` warns `WARN_SELFNOTTHIS` (`F331`, off by default) "'self' used inside OO function, use 'this'." and reads `this` in its place, so `self.x` is the class's member `x`. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseValue`.

FTEQCC keeps a list of the sounds, models, textures and files the program names: the first argument of a `precache_sound`, `precache_model`, `precache_texture` or `precache_file` function (any name with that prefix), the second of `setmodel` and `localsound`, the third of `sound`, and the argument of `used_sound` and `used_model`, each a string immediate or a constant string. A path that is new to its list and has a backslash warns "backslashes in path names are non-portable - PATH", with the path's escapes read, and no command-line flag turns it off; a path the list has already warns no more. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PrecacheSound`, `QCC_PrecacheModel`, `QCC_SetModel`, `QCC_SoundUsed`, `QCC_PrecacheTexture`, `QCC_PrecacheFile`, `QCC_PR_ParseFunctionCall`.

A call of a function named `spawn` that takes no parameters is `spawn(CLASS, field: value, ...)` or `spawn(e, CLASS, ...)`, which is a value of the class (`result.cast = rettype`); `spawn()` is a call as any other. `QCC_PR_ParseType` reads the class, else an expression, then a `,` ("expected ,, found )" when the call ends) and the class; a name there that is no type is the fatal error `E0373` "Spawn operator with undefined class: NAME", and a type that is no entity's ends at the token after it, `")" - not a name`. Each argument after the class is a field, `QCC_PR_ParseValue(rettype, ...)`: a member of the class or its parents, else a definition of the name; a name the class has no member of and nothing defines is "Unknown field NAME in class CLASS", and anything that is no field is the fatal error `E0374` "Named field is not a field.", a positional value among them. The field's name is followed by `:`, or by `=` with the warning `W0318` "That = should be a :", and then its value, an expression of any type. The parser reads such an argument, a name and `:` or `=` after `spawn`'s first argument, as a `NamedArg` node. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseFunctionCall`.

A redeclaration's type is the earlier one's by `typecmp`, with each typedef's name read as the type it names (`QCC_TypeForName`, FTEF-19.9) and a named enum that is no `enum class` as its base type: a class, struct, union or accessor is its own type, the same as another only by name, so `C c; entity c;`, `void(entity e) f; void(C e) f;` and two classes' parameters are "Type mismatch on redeclaration", and an `enum E` and a `float` are one type. `__bint` and `__bfloat` are one type, and no other (FTEF-23.8). Failing that, `typecmp_lax` decides between a warning and the error (FTEF-19.7): an accessor is its base there, so `accessor box : float; box b; float b;` is "Optional arguments differ on redeclaration of b. float, should be box", but a parameter's kind is compared before its contents, `ev_accessor` being no other kind, so `float(float h) g` redeclared as `float(box this)` is a mismatch. A pointer is compared with a pointer by what each points to and is never the type of a non-pointer: `float *a; float a;` is "Type mismatch on redeclaration of a. float, should be float*" (`E0205`), `float *a; float *a;` none, and `float *a; string *a;` one. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_lex.c`, `typecmp`, `typecmp_lax`; `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_GetDef`.

A definition's initialiser may be any expression: past its special cases `QCC_PR_ParseInitializerType_Internal` reads `tmp = QCC_PR_Expression(TOP_PRIORITY, EXPR_DISALLOW_COMMA); tmp = QCC_EvaluateCast(tmp, type, true);`, so `float IT_ALL = IT_AXE | IT_SHOTGUN;` is a global with a folded value. A global's value must still be constant: `QCC_PR_GenerateInitializerType` reports "initializer for '%s' is not constant" when `!tmp.sym->constant`. This parse-and-resolve profile parses any expression there and checks only the names in it (FTE-10.2, P2-34); whether it folds is checked with constant folding (P2-06).

A function-typed local may be given a body inside a function body: the `if (pr_scope)` branch of `QCC_PR_ParseInitializerType_Internal` saves the outer function's locals, calls `QCC_PR_ParseImmediateStatements` for the inner body ("generate a goto statement around the nested function, so that nothing is hurt"), and restores them, so the inner function is a function of its own, `void() g = { ... };` with or without `local`.

A state's frame and next function are expressions: `QCC_PR_ParseState` reads `s1 = QCC_PR_Expression (TOP_PRIORITY, EXPR_DISALLOW_COMMA);` for the frame, converted to float, and then `def = QCC_PR_Expression (TOP_PRIORITY, EXPR_DISALLOW_COMMA);` for the next function, which is "Type mismatch" unless it is a function or null. A missing `,` between them is the warning "missing comma in state definition" (`WARN_UNEXPECTEDPUNCT`), not an error.

**Withdrawn** (P2-39, #423): it called a constant range against its direction a warning, but FTEQCC raises it with `QCC_PR_ParseWarning(ERR_STATETYPEMISMATCH, ...)`, and `QCC_PR_PrintWarning` prints any code `if (type >= ERR_PARSEERRORS)` as an error and counts it in `pr_error_count`. Replaced by FTEF-18.19.
