An expression statement may hold several expressions separated by `,`, each evaluated and the last one kept: `QCC_PR_ParseStatement` ends with `QCC_PR_DiscardExpression (TOP_PRIORITY, 0);`, and `QCC_PR_RefExpression` continues `if (!(exprflags&EXPR_DISALLOW_COMMA) && priority == TOP_PRIORITY && QCC_PR_CheckToken (","))`, warning "Statement does not do anything" when the expression before the `,` has no effect. Initialisers, arguments, state parts and `case` values pass `EXPR_DISALLOW_COMMA`, so a `,` there separates rather than sequences.

**Withdrawn** (P2-42, #429): it gave a function defined inside another labels of its own, but FTEQCC shares one list between them and clears it at the end of either. Replaced by FTEF-18.23 and FTEF-18.24.

`return = e;` sets the value the function returns without returning: "return = foo; sets the value that will be returned when the function finally exits, without returning now. return; returns that value now". A return type larger than a vector is the error "'%s' not supported when returning %s".

`if !(e)` takes the statement when `e` is false, like `if not (e)` (FTEF-16.5): `if (!negate && QCC_PR_CheckToken("!"))` sets `negate = 2`, with the warning "if !() is specific to fteqcc" (`WARN_FTE_SPECIFIC`).
**Withdrawn** (P2-119, #554): it said `until` is a keyword only for the Hexen II targets, but a `#pragma keyword` or a `-K` option turns it on too. Replaced by FTEF-18.31.

A `case` label may give a range, `case a .. b:`, matched when the value is from `a` to `b` inclusive: after the first value `QCC_PR_ParseStatement` tries `if (QCC_PR_CheckToken(".."))` and reads a second with `QCC_PR_RefExpression (&pr_casesref2[num_cases], TOP_PRIORITY, EXPR_DISALLOW_COMMA);`, and for a float the switch tests `OP_GE_F` against `a` and `OP_LE_F` against `b`.

`a ?: b` is `a` when `a` is true and `b` otherwise, `a` evaluated once: after `if (priority == TERNARY_PRIORITY && QCC_PR_CheckToken ("?"))` the conditional tries `if (QCC_PR_CheckToken(":"))` before reading a middle operand.

`sizeof` takes a type or an expression, with or without parentheses: `QCC_PR_RefTerm` reads `pbool bracket = QCC_PR_CheckToken("("); t = QCC_PR_ParseType(false, true, false);`, and when no type follows, `r = QCC_PR_RefExpression(&refbuf, TOP_PRIORITY, 0); //formulas are accepted weirdly enough, its not just terms.` The value is the size in bytes, an unsigned integer constant; for a string literal it counts the terminating NUL.

A frame macro reference (`$name`, QC-8.5) ends at whitespace or at the first `,`, `;`, `&`, `|`, `(`, `)`, `]` or `..`: `QCC_PR_LexMacroName` copies bytes `while ( (c = *pr_file_p) > ' ' && c != '\n' && c != ',' && c != ';' && c != '&' && c != '|' && c != ')' && c != '(' && c != ']' && !(pr_file_p[0] == '.' && pr_file_p[1] == '.'))`, where id's qcc stops only at whitespace, `,` and `;` (QC-8.6). So `$a||x`, `($b)` and `[$a, th]` name the frames `a` and `b`.

`$framesave` defines frame names exactly as `$frame` does (QC-8.2): `QCC_PR_LexGrab` takes `if (!STRCMP (pr_token, "frame") || !STRCMP (pr_token, "framesave"))` to `QCC_PR_ParseFrame`, which numbers each name on the line from the running frame count.

A function type may return a function: after the type, `QCC_PR_ParseDefs` loops `while(QCC_PR_CheckToken ("("))` over parameter lists ("qc-style function... possibly returning a function."), so `float(float)(string) f;` declares `f` as a function taking a string and returning a `float(float)` function.

Besides `$frame` and `$framesave`, `QCC_PR_LexGrab` knows these `$` commands, each followed by words read as frame macro names are (FTEF-18.13). `$cd`, `$origin`, `$base`, `$flags`, `$scale` and `$skin` are ignored with their words: `while (QCC_PR_LexMacroName ()) ;`, which stops at the end of the line or at the first word that ends at once, where id's qcc drops the rest of the line (QC-27.14). `$flush` numbers the next frame name 0 (`QCC_PR_ClearGrabMacros(true)`); `$frame_reset` also forgets every frame macro (`QCC_PR_ClearGrabMacros(false)`, "full reset of all frame macros"); `$framevalue N` numbers the next one `N` (`pr_macrovalue = atoi(pr_token);`); `$framerestore NAME` numbers it as the macro `NAME` is, which must exist ("Unknown frame macro"); and `$modelname NAME` first makes the previous model name a frame macro of the current number (`QCC_PR_MacroFrame(pr_framemodelname, pr_macrovalue, true)`), then takes `NAME` as the model name and, when `i = QCC_PR_FindMacro(pr_framemodelname)` is not 0, numbers the next frame `i`, which is -1 for a name with no macro. Under the vanilla profile each of these is a frame macro reference (QC-8.5). Copper's `m_knight.qc` begins with `$flush`.

Frame macros are kept from file to file (FTE-22.4), and the number of the next frame name, `pr_macrovalue`, starts at 0 in each file (`QCC_PR_CompileFile` calls `QCC_PR_ClearGrabMacros (true);`) and goes up by one for each name (`QCC_PR_MacroFrame(pr_token, pr_macrovalue++, false)`), a name already defined in the same file keeping its first number. The limit is on the macros of the whole program, not of one file: with `#define MAX_FRAMES 8192`, `QCC_PR_MacroFrame` reports `if (pr_nummacros >= MAX_FRAMES) QCC_PR_ParseError(ERR_TOOMANYFRAMEMACROS, "Too many frame macros defined");`, which this profile reports as `E0504` (QCD-6.4) at the name that reaches it. Under the vanilla profile the limit stays 256 frames in one file (QC-27.5). Arcane Dimensions' `mon_bossmammoth.qc` defines more than 256 frames.

`..` is one token: `pr_punctuation[]` lists `"...", "..", "."`, longest first. So `..T` is a field of a field, which `QCC_PR_ParseType` reads `if (QCC_PR_CheckToken (".."))` as two field levels ("so we don't end up with the user specifying '. .vector blah'"), and a number ends before `..`: `QCC_PR_LexNumber` takes a fraction only `else if (c == '.' && pr_file_p[1]!='.')`, so `1..5` is `1`, `..` and `5`.
**Withdrawn** 2026-10-20 (P2-93): it named its form after the withdrawn FTEF-18.4; replaced by FTEF-18.28.

The sequences of FTEF-18.5 are read wherever FTEQCC reads an expression with no `EXPR_DISALLOW_COMMA` at `TOP_PRIORITY`: a returned value and `return =` (`e = QCC_PR_Expression (TOP_PRIORITY, 0);`), the conditions of `if`, `while`, `until`, `do` and `switch`, a parenthesised expression (`r = QCC_PR_RefExpression(retbuf, TOP_PRIORITY, 0);` before `QCC_PR_Expect (")")`), a subscript (`tmp = QCC_PR_Expression (TOP_PRIORITY, 0);` after `QCC_PR_CheckToken("[")`), the middle of `?:` (`val = QCC_PR_Expression(TOP_PRIORITY, 0);`) and the expression of `sizeof` (FTEF-18.12). The last arm of `?:` passes `EXPR_DISALLOW_COMMA`.

A frame macro is looked up by its name and then, when no macro has it, by the name in any case: `QCC_PR_FindMacro` searches `for (i=pr_nummacros-1 ; i>=0 ; i--)` with `STRCMP` and then again with `stricmp`, the second time with the warning `W0104` "Case insensitive frame macro (using %s)" (`WARN_CASEINSENSITIVEFRAMEMACRO`), so the macro defined last of those that match is used. The lookups of a reference, `$framerestore` and `$modelname` (FTEF-18.16) are all `QCC_PR_FindMacro`'s.
**Withdrawn** (P2-94 to P2-99, #507 to #512): it cited the withdrawn FTEF-18.4 for an error code `QCC_PR_PrintWarning` prints as an error. Replaced by FTEF-18.29, which cites FTEF-18.28.

A statement may be a label, written `name:` (the C style, taken `if (pr_token_type == tt_name && pr_file_p[0] == ':' && pr_file_p[1] != ':')`) or `:name` (the FrikQCC style, `if (QCC_PR_CheckToken(":"))`), and `goto name;` jumps to one (`goto` is a default keyword in the `qccmain.c` keyword table); a label name that is not a name is "invalid label name". FTEQCC keeps one list of labels, `pr_labels`, which the end of every function clears (`if (num_labels) num_labels = 0;` in `QCC_PR_ParseImmediateStatements`), a function defined inside another (FTEF-18.2) included: that one is read by the same `QCC_PR_ParseImmediateStatements` in the middle of the enclosing body, with the note "FIXME: make sure gotos/labels/cases/continues/breaks are not broken by this." So a label read since the end of the last function is the warning `W0312` "Duplicate label NAME" (`QCC_PR_ParseWarning(WARN_DUPLICATELABEL, "Duplicate label %s", pr_token);`) at its name, and is not added again: a label of the enclosing function read before an inner function is a duplicate for a label of that name in the inner one, and is forgotten after it. The preprocessed text this profile parses keeps a name and the `:` after it together when the source does, so the C style is found there too.

**Withdrawn** (#84): it had the parser check each `goto`'s label at its label name; FTEQCC checks the statements generated, so a `goto` a stripped `if` arm took back is not checked, and the error is fatal at the function's end. FTEF-34.12 replaces it.

FTEQCC's flag `qcc_usefulstatement` says whether the expression being read does something: a call sets it (`if (priority == FUNC_PRIORITY && QCC_PR_CheckToken ("(") ) { qcc_usefulstatement=true;`, before the arguments are read), and so do an assignment of any of the operators of FTE-6 and FTEF-16, once its right side is read, a prefix `++` or `--` (`QCC_PR_RefTerm`), and a postfix `++` or `--` still pending when the expression is discarded (`QCC_PR_DiscardRef`), that is, the expression itself, in parentheses or as the last of a sequence. A discarded expression with none of these is the warning `W0313` "Statement does not do anything" (`WARN_POINTLESSSTATEMENT`, on by default) at that expression: - an expression statement, and the first and last clauses of a `for`: `QCC_PR_DiscardExpression` saves the flag, clears it, reads the expression, and warns `if (ref->cast->type != ev_void && !qcc_usefulstatement)`, then restores the flag. The first clause's expressions, separated by `,`, are each discarded so (`QCC_PR_DiscardExpression(TOP_PRIORITY, EXPR_DISALLOW_COMMA);` in a `do ... while(QCC_PR_CheckToken(","))` loop); the last clause is one sequence. This profile takes an expression as `void` only when it is a cast to `void` (`QCC_TryEvaluateCast`: "anything can be cast to void, but only do it explicitly."), or one in parentheses; - each expression before the `,` of a sequence (FTEF-18.5, FTEF-18.20), wherever the sequence is: `QCC_PR_DiscardRef(lhsr); if (!qcc_usefulstatement) QCC_PR_ParseWarning(WARN_POINTLESSSTATEMENT, "Statement does not do anything"); qcc_usefulstatement = false;`, with no exception for `void`. Outside an expression statement and a discarded `for` clause the flag then carries what came before, a call in an earlier condition included, since only the discarding and the `,` clear it; this profile keeps the flag over one file.

**Withdrawn** (P2-130, #567): it counted the operators, casts, `sizeof`, `*`s and parameter lists but not an `extern` block, whose `QCC_PR_ParseDefs` recursion nested without a limit. Replaced by FTEF-18.32.

**Withdrawn** (P2-133, #574): it ended a struct's, class's or accessor's body at any declaration line, but FTEQCC reads each body to its `}`, so a member at column 0 was refused; replaced by FTEF-18.34.

A frame cycle, `[++ first .. last]` or `[-- first .. last]` (`if ((isinc=QCC_PR_CheckToken("++")) || QCC_PR_CheckToken("--"))`), has `first` and `last` as expressions separated by `QCC_PR_Expect("..")`; `(w)` or `(W)` after the `++` or `--` cycles `weaponframe` instead of `frame` (`OP_CWSTATE`). Two constant frames against the direction, `if (first->_float > last->_float)` after `++` or `<` after `--`, are the error `E0212` "Forwards State Cycle with backwards range": FTEQCC's `QCC_PR_ParseWarning` with `ERR_STATETYPEMISMATCH`, an error code, prints an error. This profile compares two frames written as single numbers.

FTEQCC tells the readings of source apart by `s_filen`, a string it makes anew (`qccHunkAlloc`) for each compiled file (`QCC_PR_CompileFile`), each `#include` of a file, and each macro expansion (`QCC_PR_IncludeChunkEx`, given a `CompilerConstant_t`), and it compares the pointers, so each of these is a reading of its own; the file that includes another is the same reading again after the include. A frame macro keeps the reading that defined it (`pr_framemacro[].file`), and: - a use of a frame macro that another reading defined is the warning `W0105` "Stale macro used (NAME, defined in FILE)" (`WARN_STALEMACRO`, on by default), where FILE is the defining file's path: `QCC_PR_FindMacro` checks `if (pr_framemacro[i].file != s_filen)` after each of its two lookups (FTEF-18.21), for a reference, `$framerestore` and `$modelname` alike; - a frame name the same reading already defined keeps its first number with the warning `W0106` "Duplicate macro defined (NAME). Rename it." (`WARN_DUPLICATEMACRO`): in `QCC_PR_MacroFrame`, `if (pr_framemacro[i].file == s_filen && !force)`; a name another reading defined takes the new number and this reading silently ("old file, override it"), and so does the model name `$modelname` defines, with `force` set (FTEF-18.16). This is what "the same file" of FTEF-18.17 and FTE-22.4 means; - a new frame name of 64 bytes or more is the error `E0119` "Name for frame macro NAME is too long" and is not defined: `if (strlen(name)+1 > sizeof(pr_framemacro[0].name)) QCC_PR_ParseWarning(ERR_TOOMANYFRAMEMACROS, ...)`, with `char name[64];`, an error code, which `QCC_PR_PrintWarning` prints as an error (FTEF-18.28). The frame number still goes up by one for it; - a `$modelname` of 64 bytes or more is cut to its first 63 with the warning `W0107` "$modelname name too long": `if (!QC_strlcpy(pr_framemodelname, pr_token, sizeof(pr_framemodelname))) QCC_PR_ParseWarning (WARN_STRINGTOOLONG, ...)`, with `char pr_framemodelname[64];`.

A frame macro whose number is below 0 is unknown where it is expanded: a reference and `$framerestore` take their number from `QCC_PR_ExpandMacro`, which refuses any negative one as it refuses a name with no macro, `QCC_PR_FindMacro`'s `-1`: `int i = QCC_PR_FindMacro(pr_token); if (i < 0) QCC_PR_ParseError (ERR_BADFRAMEMACRO, "Unknown frame macro $%s", pr_token);`. So `$framevalue -5`, `$frame a` and `x = $a;` is the error `E0106` "Unknown frame macro $a" at `$a` (QCD-2.6), as is a `$framevalue` whose `atoi` is negative (FTEF-14.55): `-99999999999` is -1215752191 and `2147483648` is -2147483648 on an LP64 host. The lookup's warnings (FTEF-18.21, FTEF-18.29) come first, as `QCC_PR_FindMacro` gives them. A refused `$framerestore` leaves the number of the next frame name as it was. `$modelname` calls `QCC_PR_FindMacro` itself (FTEF-18.16), so a negative model name macro still numbers the next frame. Under the vanilla profile frames are numbered from 0 (QC-8.5) and none is negative. The cases are in the directive family of `cargo xtask oracles builtins` (`FRAME_VALUES` in `xtask/src/oracles/builtins/directives.rs`).

`until (e) s` repeats `s` while `e` is false, and `do s until (e);` is the `do` loop with the test reversed: `wasuntil = QCC_PR_CheckKeyword(keyword_until, "until"); if (wasuntil || QCC_PR_CheckKeyword(keyword_while, "while"))`, and in `do`, `until = QCC_PR_CheckKeyword(keyword_until, "until"); if (!until) QCC_PR_Expect ("while");`. `until` is a keyword when its flag is on: by default only for the Hexen II targets (`nondefaultkeyword` in the keyword table, forced on `if (qcc_targetformat == QCF_HEXEN2 || ...)`, FTEF-20.3), and after `#pragma keyword enable until`, `-Kuntil` or a `-std=` that sets it (FTEF-20.1); or when written `__until`, which `QCC_PR_CheckKeyword` matches whether or not the keyword is enabled (FTEF-20.2); otherwise `until (e)` is a call of a function named `until`.

Under this profile the nesting limit of QC-27.15 counts the FTEQCC constructs too: the operand of a prefix `-`, `+`, `~`, `++`, `--`, `&` or `*` (FTE-19.4, FTEF-16.7), of a cast (FTEF-16.2) and of `sizeof` (FTEF-18.12) is one level inside it, as the operand of `!` is, each `*` and each parameter list of a type (FTEF-4.1, FTEF-18.15) nests the type one level deeper, and so does each `*` before a declarator's name (FTEF-15.6); and each `extern` block (FTEF-21.17) is one level for the definitions it holds, braced or not, at file level, in a body and behind `local`, since `QCC_PR_ParseDefs(NULL, false)` calls itself for them. So `extern "C" { extern "C" { ... float y; } }` and `extern "C" extern "C" ... float y;` nest to the limit and no further, whether the braces close or not. QC-27.16 then holds as for vanilla: a prefix `++` or `--` it unwinds through is read as no postfix one, a type or a declarator takes no further `*` or parameter list, and a block past the limit is one error token, its `extern`. FTEQCC has no such limit. The tests parse every construct that nests, repeated, under both profiles, so that no recursive entry of the parser is without its level.

The body of a `switch` is any statement: after `QCC_PR_Expect (")")`, `oldst = numstatements; QCC_PR_ParseStatement ();` reads one, so `switch (1) ;` and `switch (1) break;` are read, and the labels of its block are those of the statement. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseStatement`.

With `qcfuncs` on, `QCC_PR_ParseType` takes one parameter list after a type; a further one is `QCC_PR_ParseDefs`'s (`while(QCC_PR_CheckToken ("("))`), and the declarator it starts then needs a name (`name = QCC_PR_ParseName ()`): `void()();` and `void() (float);` are the error `E0201` `";" - not a name`, and `void();` declares nothing.

Where FTEQCC's expression ends at a `[` or `.` after a value that takes neither (FTEF-31.2, FTEF-24.1), the statement it has read is that value alone when the value starts the statement, so `x[1] = 2;`, `x.y = 2;` and `3[1] = 2;` warn "Statement does not do anything" before "expected ;, found [", as a value that calls nothing and stores nothing does (FTEF-18.25); `g()[1] = 2;` does not, nor does `y = x[1];`, whose statement starts elsewhere. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_DiscardExpression`, `QCC_PR_ParseStatement`.

In a definition's value the same `[` ends the value before it, which the definition then reads whole: cast to its type, "initializer for 'NAME' is not constant" at global scope when the value's definition is no constant (`tmp.sym->constant`, which a field is), and a refused cast's fatal error ends it there. The `[` is then where the definition wants its `;`: "Missing semicolon at end of definition", and at global scope `"[" is not a type` as it reads the next definition, in a function "Statement does not do anything" of the statement the `[` starts, which this profile does not check further. So `float q = x[1];` of a global `float x` gives all three, `.float q = ff[1];` of a field the last two, `local float q = x[1];` the warnings, and `float q = e[1];` of an entity only "Cannot cast from entity to float". Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseDefs`, `QCC_PR_GenerateInitializerType`.

This profile's error recovery (QCD-1.4) ends the body of a struct, class, accessor, `switch` or function at a declaration line, a token at column 0 that has a declaration's shape or is one of `typedef`, `class`, `accessor`, `enum`, `enumflags`, `struct` and `union`, only when no `}` stands ahead to close it, since FTEQCC reads each body to its `}` and a member or a local at column 0 is one. So a body that lost its `}` damages no declaration after the next, and a body that has its `}` is read whole whatever its columns. Under the vanilla profile a function's statements end at a declaration line as before, where a declaration needs `local`.

A duplicate C-style label (FTEF-18.23) is warned of and its name read, but not its `:` (`QCC_PR_ParseWarning(WARN_DUPLICATELABEL, ...); QCC_PR_Lex(); return;`), so the `:` starts a FrikQCC-style label: `l: ; l: x;` defines `x`, and `l: ; l: ;` is the error `E0201` `invalid label name ";"` (`QCC_PR_ParseError(ERR_BADLABELNAME, "invalid label name \"%s\"", pr_token);`), which a `:` before any token that is no name is.

Parameters and locals are found in their function first (`QCC_PR_GetDef` scans `localstable` when `scope` is set). A parameter given twice, or named as a component of an earlier vector parameter, is the error `E0215` "Duplicate definition of NAME.": the parameters are made with `QCC_PR_GetSRef (type->params[u].type, pr_parm_names[u], pr_scope, 2, 0, 0)`, and `if (allocate == 2) QCC_PR_ParseErrorPrintDef (ERR_TYPEMISMATCHREDEC, def, "Duplicate definition of %s%s%s.", ...)`. A vector parameter after a parameter named as its component is no error: `QCC_PR_DummyDef` makes the components with no lookup. A local declared again with its type is the warning `W0207` "NAME duplicate definition ignored", or "nonstatic redeclaration of NAME ignored" after a `static` one, and the same definition; a `static` local declared again is neither; another type is `E0205`. A new parameter or local named as a global of the same kind of type (`def->type->type == type->type`) is the warning `W0208` "Local \"NAME\" hides global with same name and type"; a global of another kind gives none. A parameter of a function with a body that has no name is the warning `W0222` "Parameter N of NAME is not named", N counted from 1; a lone `void` is no parameter (FTEF-15.3). In a function body a statement defines locals when it starts with `local`, a type, a type name, `.`, or one of the words `QCC_PR_ParseStatement` tests with their keyword enabled: `var`, `noref`, `static`, `extern`, `const`, `typedef`, `class`, `struct`, `union` and `enum` (`register`, `volatile` and `auto` are disabled keywords, `nondefaultkeyword`); `shared`, `nosave`, `inline` and the `__` words start no definition there, so `shared float x;` is "Unknown value \"shared\"".

**Withdrawn** (P2-122, #558): it gave every cast among pointers, strings and functions the warning `W0220`, but `QCC_TryEvaluateCast` makes those to and from `void*` and between a string and a pointer to an 8-bit integer with none, and a pointer to another with none when they point to one type; and it read the flags that change the casts as off. Replaced by FTEF-19.31.

A definition is a constant when its first declaration makes it one, `GDF_CONST`: `const`, or at file level and not `var`, initialised, a function or a field (`if (isconstant || (!isvar && !pr_scope && ((isinitialised && !flag_assumevar) || type->type == ev_function || type->type == ev_field)))`); an enum's value and a `const` local are constants, a `static` local and an `autocvar_` are not. A later declaration does not change it (`// def->constant = isconst;` is commented out) and warns `W0212` "Redeclaration of NAME would change to const." (or "non-const.") when initialised, "Redeclaration of NAME changes const." when not; a new definition is compared with the constness it gets, which differs only for an initialised `autocvar_` (FTEF-19.16), so `float autocvar_x = 1;` gives the warning too. A name initialising a global or a `static` that is no constant is the error `E0214` "initializer for 'NAME' is not constant" (`QCC_PR_GenerateInitializerType`, `if (!tmp.sym->constant)`); a plain or `const` local's initialiser is not checked. A constant that has no value yet gives the warning `W0219` "initializer for NAME is not initialised yet, NAME will be treated as 0", and the value 0; a field always has its value (fields are "initialised behind the scenes") and a function not yet defined is filled in once it is (`$relocf`), so neither warns.
**Withdrawn** 2026-10-28: it gave the "incompatible redeclaration" after "redeclaration of function body" as `E0206`, which is `E0363` (FTE-22.6); replaced by FTEF-19.57.

A body given to a definition already initialised, by a builtin, a body, `extern` or `shared`, is the error `E0216` "redeclaration of function body" (`else if (basedef->initialized == 1 && !(flags & PIF_STRONGER))`), reported before the "incompatible redeclaration" the two different functions then give (`E0363`); a body after a `weak` one, or for an `accumulate` function, is none, and a body after a `wrap` one is. A body replacing the builtin of `anglemod` or `crossproduct` is the warning `W0217` "NAME already declared as a builtin" instead, and the builtin is marked unused. A `wrap` body with nothing initialised to wrap is the error `E0222` "wrapper function does not wrap anything", and one that does not use `prior` the error `E0223` "Wrapper function \"NAME\" does not refer to its prior function". An `accumulate` declaration of a function initialised before without it is the warning `W0218` "NAME redeclared to accumulate after initial declaration".
**Withdrawn** 2026-10-28: it gave a differing word `E0206`, which is "incompatible redeclaration", `E0363` (FTE-22.6); replaced by FTEF-19.58.

The "dupe initialisation" comparison of FTE-22.6 and FTEF-17.10 compares the words the two initialisers give: a number literal's value as FTEQCC's lexer reads it, so `0x10` and `16` are equal; a constant's name, the constant's value (`float y = 2; float x = y; float x = 2;` compiles); a vector's components, which `QCC_PR_DummyDef` gives the vector's initialised state and words (`d->initialized = def->initialized;`), so `vector v = '1 2 3'; float v_x = 1;` compiles and `float v_x = 2;` is `E0363`; and a `const` or `static` local's, as a global's. `parseentitydata` given another builtin after `#608` or `#613` is accepted with the warning `W0223` "incompatible redeclaration. Please validate builtin numbers. parseentitydata is #613" ("dpextensions is WRONG").

A default value must be a constant (`if (!ref.sym->constant) QCC_PR_ParseError(0, "Default value not a constant\n");`, `E0217`) with a value (`QCC_PR_ParseError(0, "Default value not initialized yet\n");`, `E0218`, but with autoprototyping), cast to the parameter's type (FTEF-19.31). Two function types are the same only if, where both give a default value, the values are equal (`typecmp`, `(a->type == ev_function && (a->params[i].defltvalue.cast && b->params[i].defltvalue.cast))`), so `void(float a = 1) g;` and `void(float a = 2) g = #6;` are `E0205`; a value given on one only is no difference. A parameter with a default value is not `optional`.

At file level a redeclaration whose type differs (`typecmp`) but agrees under `typecmp_lax`, the return types and the shared parameters agreeing and every parameter one list has beyond the other `optional`, whether either is variadic aside, is the warning `W0209` "Optional arguments differ on redeclaration of NAME. A, should be B", unless the two have the same parameters and only the first is variadic, and the definition takes the type with more parameters. A redeclaration of `droptofloor`, `callfunction` or `trailparticles` with another type is the warning `W0210` "NAME builtin was wrongly redefined as TYPE. ignoring later definition", and in a file named `*extensions.qc` (any case) of a function "NAME builtin was redefined as TYPE. ignoring alternative definition": the first type stays and the declaration goes on. A global marked unused that nothing refers to, `def->unused && !def->referenced`, is replaced by a declaration of another type, with the warning `W0211` "Type redeclaration of TYPE NAME replaces existing variable": a builtin a body replaced (FTEF-19.57) is one. A `noref` mark is a reference too (`if (noref) { def->unused = true; def->referenced = true; }`), so a `noref` global declared again with another type is `E0205`. A function declared again as `T(...)` with no parameters is no difference ("c89-style dumb redeclarations"). Any other difference is `E0205`, with FTEQCC's text "Type mismatch on redeclaration of NAME. A, should be B".

A redeclaration's array size, where it gives one, is the definition's: `if (def->arraysize != arraysize && arraysize>=0)` is the error `E0220` "Array sizes for redecleration of NAME do not match (A->B)" (in a function body "(A -> B)"), a declaration that is no array giving 0, so `float x[2]; float x;` is the error. `[]` gives no size, and an unsized definition takes the size a later one gives; an unsized array's initialiser sizes it (`QCC_PR_ParseDefArray` counts the elements of `{ ... }`, and a string's bytes and its terminator, `dim[0] = pr_immediate_strlen+1;`). A size that is no number literal is not compared (FTEF-19.63). An array is initialised with `{ ... }`, or an array of an 8-bit integer (`__int8`, `__uint8`, `__char`: `def.cast->type == ev_bitfld && def.cast->bits == 8`) with a string: anything else is the error `E0204` "expected {, found X" (`QCC_PR_ParseInitializerType_Internal`, `QCC_PR_Expect("{");`). A string of more bytes than the array's size is the error, not fatal, `E0233` "initializer-string too long" (`if (pr_immediate_strlen > arraysize) QCC_PR_ParseWarning (ERR_BADARRAYSIZE, ...)`), so `__char c[2] = "ab";` is no error.

A `typedef` of a name a typedef already names must name the same type, as `QCC_TypeForName` resolves a typedef to its type (`if (t && t->type == ev_typedef) return t->aux_type;`): else the error `E0219` "Cannot redeclare typedef NAME from A to B", so `typedef float t; typedef int t;` is the error and `typedef float t; typedef t t;` is not. A redeclaration compares a typedef's name as the type it names (`typedef float t; t x; vector x;` is `E0205`). A typedef with a storage qualifier is the error `E0224` "bad combination of modifiers with typedef (defining NAME)", `static`, `noref` and `nosave` among them when no `#pragma` makes them the default (FTEF-21.14); `typedef;` and `typedef float;` define nothing, with the warning `W0215` "typedef defines no types". A `typedef` in a function body is a definition statement (FTEF-19.1), checked as one at file level, whose type name this profile reads as any other type name.

An enum's names are constants of the enum's base type, `float` unless `: type` gives another, made with `QCC_PR_DummyDef`. A name's value is the one after its `=`, a number or a numeric constant converted to the base type, or the one before it plus 1; under `enumflags` times 2, starting at 1, and 1 after a 0 (`if (!next_i) next_f = next_i = 1;`). Each enum starts its count again. After a value this profile does not compute (FTEF-19.63) the names that follow have no value it compares. A string or vector after `=` is the error `E0227` "Implicit type mismatch. Needed float, got string." (`QCC_SupplyConversion`), a name that is no constant with a value the error `E0228` "enum - NAME is not a compile-time constant", and a base type that is no number with no value the error `E0229` "values for enums of this type must be initialised". An `enumflags` value that is no whole number is the warning `W0225` "enumflags - VALUE not an integer value", and one with more than one bit set "enumflags - 0xV(V) has multiple bits set". A base type before the `{` with no `:` is the warning `W0224` "legacy enum base type. Use \"enum [class] [name_e]:type\" instead", and so is a named enum declared again, whose name `QCC_PR_ParseType` then reads as that base type. A later declaration of an enum's name compares its initialiser with the name's value (FTEF-19.58). The names of an `enum class` are not referable alone (`QCC_PR_DummyDef(..., !strictenum, ...)`), only as `Name::value`, and are of the enum's own type, which casts to no other: `float x = E::A;` is "Cannot cast from enum E:float to float".

A `shared` definition is initialised by its declaration (`if (!def->initialized && shared) ... def->initialized = true;`), and giving it a value, then or later, is the error `E0221` "shared values may not be assigned an initial value". An `extern` function is initialised by its declaration too (FTEF-19.57); `extern` on what is no function is ignored, with the warning `W0214` "extern keyword may only apply to qc functions.".

A `static` global is visible only in its unit, the compiled file and the files it includes (`if ((def->isstatic||(flags&GDF_STATIC)) && strcmp(def->unitn, scope?scope->unitn:s_unitn))`), so another unit's lookup finds the next definition of the name, or none; `static` on a name another file defined is the error `E0231` "can't redefine non-static as static".
A use of a definition marked `__deprecated` is the warning `W0314` "Variable \"NAME\" is deprecated", followed by ": REASON" when `__deprecated("REASON")` gives one.

`QCC_PR_ParseState` reads a state header's frame before its next function, so the frame sees no name the header declares (`[h, h]` with `h` not declared before is "Unknown value \"h\""). The frame is converted to a float, a string or vector being `E0227` "Implicit type mismatch. Needed float, got string."; a next function that is a literal but 0 is the error `E0309` "Type mismatch: string, should be void()".

`Scope::name` defines a member of the class `Scope`, or, with the warning `W0216` "Scope::name is not part of class Scope", a new one (`WARN_MEMBERNOTDEFINED`); of a struct, the global `Scope::name` an earlier definition made, else the error `E0226` "Scope::name is not part of class Scope" (`ERR_NOTDEFINED`); and a scope that is neither, a typedef or an enum included, is the error `E0225` "Scope is not a class". After either error this profile still defines the global `Scope::name`, for navigation (QCD-1.4).

A name is looked up as a definition first and only then as an intrinsic (FTEF-17.4), `random` among them ("returning a float just in case people declare things in the wrong order"). Outside a member function `this` is the error `E0310` "Cannot use 'this' outside of an OO function" and `super` `E0311` "Cannot use 'super' outside of an OO function"; in a member function of a class with no parent `super` is `E0312` "class NAME has no super", where the pinned FTEQCC crashes (signal 11), refusing the program as the profile does. A local named `autocvar_...` is a global, with the warning `W0213` "Autocvar \"NAME\" defined with local scope. promoting to global."; a constant or static one is made neither, with "defined as constant. attempting to correct that for you." or "defined as static. ...". A definition named as an enabled keyword (`var`, `for`, `switch`, `case`, `local`, `default`, `goto`, `continue`, `string`, `float`, `entity`, `vector`, `const`, `asm`, and `break` for what is no function) is the warning `W0221` "\"NAME\" keyword used as variable name - coexisting", the keyword keeping its meaning. `QCC_PR_ParseDefs` warns `W0214` "Conflicting storage classes." for more than one of `extern`, `static`, `shared` and `auto`, "Conflicting constness." for `const` and `var`, and "function modifier on non-function." for `inline`, `wrap`, `weak` or `accumulate` on what is no function, which `accumulate` makes the error `E0230` "accumulate applies only to functions, not NAME".

**Withdrawn** (P2-121, #556): it said attributes, `assumeint` and `assumevar` are not modelled, but the parser and the semantic model read them (FTEF-21.9, FTEF-19.24, FTEF-21.11). Replaced by FTEF-19.30.

The definitions family of `cargo xtask oracles builtins` (`xtask/src/oracles/builtins/declarations.rs`) compiles programs that bind `f` and then make the definitions these statements and QC-11 to QC-13 describe, under both profiles, and the FTEQCC warning programs with `-Werror -Wno-Q208`, for which every warning of the profile is an error, so a warning one compiler gives and the other does not changes the outcome (Q208, "no end_sys_fields defined", is what every program without system definitions gets). Its run of 2026-10-21 (macOS arm64) agrees on every case but the vanilla `float k = 7; float y; float x = y;`, which differs as QC-27.8 says.

The locals a `for` statement defines, in its first clause or anywhere in its body, leave scope at its end: `QCC_PR_ParseStatement_For` keeps `subscopestart = pr.local_tail` and `subscopestop = pr_subscopedlocals?NULL:pr.local_tail->nextlocal`, which is the end of the list whether `subscope` is on or off (FTEF-21.12), and after the statement removes every local after `subscopestart` from `localstable` ("remove any new locals from the hashtable. typically this is just the stuff inside the for(here;;)"). So after the loop the name is the global again, or "Unknown value", and a local of the name is a new definition of any type: `for (float i = 0;;) {} for (string i = "";;) {}` is two locals. A local the statement found again (`float i; for (float i = 0;;) {}`, FTEF-19.1) was not made there and stays. Only `for` does this: a block, `while`, `do`, `if` and `switch` keep their locals.

A name that is a definition's type, or part of it (a field's, a pointer's, a function's return or parameter type), must be a type at that point: C type words (FTEF-2.8), a name `QCC_PR_NewType` registers (`variant`, `__variant`, `__string`, `__vector`, `__entity`, `__bfloat` and the scalars of FTEF-2.8), or a class, struct, union, typedef, enum or accessor declared before it, at file level or, for a local, by a `typedef` earlier in the same body (`QCC_TypeForName` finds a typedef whose `scope` is `pr_scope`). Else `QCC_PR_ParseType` gives the error `E0203` "\"NAME\" is not a type", which ends the declaration, so `foo x;`, `.foo x;`, `foo *p;` and `t x; typedef float t;` are errors and `class C; C c;` is not. In a body FTEQCC reads such a statement as an expression ("Unknown value \"NAME\"", FTEF-2.10); this profile, whose parser cannot tell a type name from a value, reports the same `E0203` there and makes no local, an error either way. A type of more than one word that is no run of C words (`struct tag`, an inline `enum` or `struct`) and the types of a class's or struct's members are not checked (FTEF-19.63).

After a qualifier the type may be left out: `QCC_PR_ParseDefs` sets `hadmodifier` for each storage class or modifier it reads and calls `QCC_PR_ParseType (false, hadmodifier, ...)`, whose `silentfail` returns no type instead of "not a type", and then `if (hadmodifier) { //banned since c99... basetype = type_integer; }`. So `const x = 5;`, `static y;`, `noref z;`, `var v;`, `__register r;` and, in a body, `static y;` define `__int32`s, checked as any definition is (`const x = 5; float x;` is a type mismatch, `const k = "a";` the warning "Implicit cast from string to __int32"). The parser reads the type as left out when a qualifier is followed by a name and then `;`, `,`, `=` or `[`; a name that is a type there (`static t;` after `typedef float t;`) is not told apart, and is read as the name.

The parser's and the semantic model's warnings are reported as FTEQCC's warning settings stand where it gives each (FTEF-14.63, FTEF-14.72): ignored, a warning, or an error, `E0125`. Each is the warning `QCC_PR_ParseWarning` is given its text with: `W0203` `WARN_UNDESIRABLECONVENTION`; `W0204` and `W0313` Q205 (`WARN_POINTLESSSTATEMENT`); `W0205` and `W0215` `WARN_UNEXPECTEDPUNCT`; `W0206`, `W0210`, `W0211` and `W0223` F129 (`WARN_COMPATIBILITYHACK`); `W0207` Q207; `W0208` F306; `W0209` F308; `W0212` F329; `W0213` F310; `W0214` and `W0226` `unimplemented` (`WARN_IGNOREDKEYWORD`); `W0216` F335; `W0217` `WARN_NOTSTANDARDBEHAVIOUR`; `W0218` F321; `W0219` `WARN_NOTCONSTANT`; `W0220` F314; `W0221` `WARN_KEYWORDDISABLED`; `W0222` F320; `W0224` F328; `W0225` F327; `W0312` Q111; `W0314` F326. The five that `warningnames[]` does not name are warnings by default, and no `#pragma warning` names them, but `-Wnone`, `-Wextra` and `-Werror` reach them. A warning is read with the settings at the token it stands at: a definition's at its first token, a local's, a parameter's and a name's use at theirs. `W0201` (vanilla's) and `W0311` (this project's own, QCD-7.17) are no FTEQCC warning and are reported as they are.

A builtin's engine name written as strings (`#"NAME"`, `:"NAME"`, FTE-17.5) is their value as FTEQCC's lexer read them, with the compiler flags in force at the initialiser (FTEF-12.12): with `qcfuncs` off `\101` is C's octal escape, `A`, and with it on Quake's yellow `1` and the digits after it; under `utf8` a `\u` escape writes UTF-8.

`QCC_PR_LexNumber` types a number by the flags in force where it stands (FTEF-12.12). Under `assumeint` a number with no suffix and no `.` is an integer by its magnitude (`if (num > UINT64_C(0x7fffffffffffffff)) pr_immediate_type = type_uint64; else if (num > 0xffffffffu) ... type_int64; else if (num > 0x7fffffffu) ... type_uint; else ... type_integer;`), a number with an `f` suffix staying a float (its branch sets `type_float` first), and a character constant is an `__int32` (`QCC_PR_LexVector`, `if (flag_assume_integer) { pr_immediate_type = type_integer; ...`); under `assumedouble` a number with a `.` is a `__double` (`pr_immediate_type = flag_assume_double?type_double:type_float;`), but after an `f` suffix (`else if (c == 'f' || c == 'F') { pr_immediate_type = type_float;`). A single `l` suffix is 64 bits, and under `ILP32` only two are (`if (islong >= (flag_ILP32?2:1))`). The literal's type is then cast as FTEF-19.31 says: `string s = 5;` under `assumeint` is "Implicit cast from __int32 to string", and `string s = 1.5;` under `assumedouble` "Cannot cast from __double to string". The value is kept as the lexer keeps it, a float's bits (FTEF-13.5).
**Withdrawn** (P2-119, #554): it said the parser reads keywords as written under `-Fcaseinsens`, but it matches them in any case as FTEQCC does (FTEF-20.2). Replaced by FTEF-19.29.

Under `qccx`, `@` before a term is that term read as a string (`QCC_PR_RefTerm`, `if (flag_qccx && QCC_PR_CheckToken ("@"))`, `QCC_PR_RefExpression (retbuf, UNARY_PRIORITY, EXPR_DISALLOW_COMMA)`), a reference that may be assigned; that it applies only to a float or an integer, "'@' operator only functions on floats and ints. go figure.", is the type checker's (FTEF-19.63). Without `qccx`, `@` is no term. `^^` is a token of `pr_punctuation` that no operator of `pr_opcodes` names, so `a ^^ b` ends the expression after `a`.

A module's source in source form, the `progs.src` FTEQCC compiles as code (PRJ-4.4), is read by `Db::parse` past a first line that starts with `#!` (PRJ-4.10), as `qc_syntax::parse_module_source` reads it: the database takes a module's prelude (`ModuleInput::prelude`) to be that file.

FTEQCC names its core types once, before the first pass, with the flags the command line set: `type_string = QCC_PR_NewType(flag_qcfuncs?"string":"__string", ev_string, true);`, and so `vector` and `entity`, then `__string`, `__vector` and `__entity` whatever the flag. So under `-Fno-qcfuncs` or `-Kno-qcfuncs` the words `string`, `vector` and `entity` are no type, "\"WORD\" is not a type" (`E0203`, FTEF-19.20), unless a typedef names the word again, while a `#pragma flag disable qcfuncs`, read after the types are named, keeps them.

**Withdrawn** (P2-132, #569): it said a type name is found in any case, but the type table also holds a scope's, a typedef's redeclaration, a class's members and an enum's names, each searched or compared a way of its own. Replaced by FTEF-19.33.

**Withdrawn** (P2-122, #558): it said the output target's `extern` check and the casts `qccx`, `lax` and `typeexplicit` allow are not modelled, but the semantic model reads them (FTEF-22). Replaced by FTEF-19.32.

A value initialiser, a parameter's default value and a function initialised with a value are cast to the definition's type by `QCC_EvaluateCast(tmp, type, true)`, which refuses with the error `E0213` "Cannot cast from A to B", A and B as `TypeName` writes them (`__int32`, `__double`, `.float`, `void()`, `entity*`; parameter names, which the model does not keep, are left out). A literal's type is `QCC_PR_LexNumber`'s (FTEF-3.1; a character constant is a float); a name's is its definition's, and in a member function a field's name is `this.field`, of the field's type. The C type words name the type FTEF-2.8 makes, and a registered type name its type (`__int32`, `__double`); an 8- or 16-bit integer and `__bint` are types this profile does not follow but as what a pointer points to. `QCC_TryEvaluateCast` with `implicit` set casts, its branches in order: a type to itself; a null, an integer, unsigned or float constant whose word is 0 (`QCC_SRef_IsNull`), to any type but a struct or union; numbers among the float, integer, unsigned, 64-bit and double types; a float or an integer to a vector, with the warning `W0220` "Implicit cast from A to B"; a string to a pointer to an 8-bit integer (`__int8*`, `__uint8*`) and back ("string and char* are the same type"), and a pointer, a function or a string to `void*` and `void*` to them ("can cast any pointer type to void*"), with no warning; a pointer to another, with `W0220` unless they point to one type (`typecmp_lax`, which follows a pointer to what it points to), a type this profile does not follow agreeing with any; pointers, strings, integers, unsigned and functions among themselves, and an integer to an entity and back, the casts "acceptable but probably an error", with `W0220` but between the two integer types. Nothing else casts: `float x = "a";`, `entity e = 1;`, `void() g = 5;`, `string s = 5l;`, `vector v = 5u;` and `entity e = 0d;` are `E0213`, and `entity e = 0;`, `string s = -0;` and `void() g = 0;` cast; `void *p = "a";` and `__uint8 *p = "a";` cast with no word, `float *p = "a";`, `__int16 *p = "a";` and a `float*` initialising a `vector*` with `W0220`. The types are compared with every typedef in them resolved, as `QCC_PR_ParseType` resolves them, and two functions the same part by part (FTEF-17.12) are one type: `typedef float t;` makes a `void(t x)` initialise a `void(float x)` with no word, and `typedef __uint8 byte;` a string a `byte*`. These are the casts with `lax`, `qccx` and `flag_undefwordsize` off, their `-Tid` defaults; FTEF-22 gives what each changes. A string initialised with `_(...)` takes one string literal, else the error `E0232` "_() intrinsic accepts only a string immediate". An initialiser that is no literal and no name is read by the check stage (FTEF-34.9).

**Withdrawn** (P2-136, #587): it said an initialiser of a global that is an expression is checked for no type, and that a function returning a large type is not warned of; the check stage reads such an initialiser (FTEF-34.9) and warns of a large return (FTEF-34.8). Replaced by FTEF-19.63.

Under `-Fcaseinsens`, which only the command line sets (FTEF-14.72), FTEQCC's name tables are searched in any case (`pHash_Get = &Hash_GetInsensitive;`), and `QCC_PR_GetDef` makes two passes, the first taking only a definition whose name is the one written (`if (ins == 0 && strcmp(def->name, name))`), the second, which only a lookup makes (`insmax = allocate?1:2;`), any whose name it is in any case, the newest first (the table's chain). So a use of `foo` finds `Foo` when nothing is named `foo`, the function's locals before the globals, and of `float Foo = 1; string FOO = "a";` the string, the one defined last (`float x = foo;` is "Cannot cast from string to float"); a definition named as another in another case is a definition of its own. `QCC_TypeForName` searches the type table the same way, so a type is found in any case wherever a declaration, a typedef, a parameter or a `Scope::` reads one: the names `QCC_main` registers (`void`, `float`, `string`, `vector`, `entity` when `qcfuncs` was on, `__string`, `__int32`, `__variant`, `variant`, `__bfloat` and the rest of its list) and the typedefs, structs, unions, enums and classes the program names, so `Void() h = #6;`, `VECTOR v;`, `typedef Entity e;` and `enum E {A}; float y = e::A;` are read as their lower case, and `Long x;` is "\"Long\" is not a type" as `long` is, the C words of `QCC_PR_ParseType` being the keywords of FTEF-20.2. A typedef of a name differing in case from one made, with another type, is "Cannot redeclare typedef"; the members of a class found by its name or a parent's are found in any case, `C::F` and `c::f` naming `C::f`; and an enum's value after `Scope::` is the exact one (`strcmp (acc->fieldname, name)`), so `E::a` is `Unknown value "E::a"` while `a` finds `A`. `QCC_PR_ParseEnum` makes each value a new definition with `QCC_PR_DummyDef`, never a redeclaration, which the lookups find before an older one of its name, so `enum {A, B}; #pragma flag enable assumeint` and another `enum {A, B}` make `B` an `__int32`. The keywords `QCC_PR_CheckKeyword` and `QCC_PR_CheckName` then also match in any case (FTEF-20.2); a statement that starts with a type word in another case is the parser's (FTEF-20.6). This profile does not search the preprocessor's macro table in any case, nor follow a class named as a parent in another case or report one not defined.

The scope of `Scope::name` is read as `QCC_TypeForName` reads a type: a class, struct, union, enum or typedef the program defined, or a name `QCC_main` registers, else the error `"Scope" is not a type` (`ERR_NOTATYPE`), as for `Nope::thing()`, `Other::g` after `float Other::g = 1;` ("Other is not a class", FTEF-19.15) and `e::A` after `enum E {A, B};`. `super` is a class's parent and no type name.

A definition's type is read by `QCC_PR_ParseType` even when no declarator follows (`if (QCC_PR_CheckToken (";")) ... return;` comes after the type), so `float (x);` with `qcfuncs` on is `ParseType`'s function type `float(x)` whose parameter `x` is no type, "expected function arg list" (`if (!t) { if (!flag_qcfuncs) t = type_integer; else return NULL; }`), and `S2 (x);` and `void() g = { local float (x); };` likewise; with `qcfuncs` off the parameter is an `int` named x. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseDefs`.

An enumerator given again in a named enum's body with another value is "%s::%s already declared": `enum E { A, A };` (the second is 1), while `enum E { A = 1, A = 1 };` and an anonymous `enum { A, A };` are not, a name given to the enum in an earlier `enum E {` being the base type there (FTEF-19.10) and keeping no names under it. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseEnum`.

An enum's body holds at least one enumerator: `QCC_PR_ParseEnum` reads a name with `QCC_PR_ParseName` before it looks for the `}` (`while(1) { name = QCC_PR_ParseName(); ... if (QCC_PR_CheckToken("}")) break; QCC_PR_Expect(","); if (QCC_PR_CheckToken("}")) break; }`), so `enum E { };` and `enum { , };` are "not a name", and `enum { A, };` is not. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseEnum`.

A type's name is no value: `QCC_PR_ParseValue` finds no definition by the name of a struct, union, class, enum, typedef or accessor, "Unknown value" for `S(1)`, `x = S;` and `local float q = C;`; the operand of `sizeof` is tried as a type first and `spawn(Thing)` takes a class by its name (FTEF-17.1), and `S` in `sizeof(S)` is the type. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_RefTerm`, `QCC_PR_ParseValue`.

An element of a variable, `x[1]`, is no constant initialiser: "initializer for 'y' is not constant" for `float x[2]; float y = x[1];`, with `qcfuncs` on or off. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseInitializerDef`.

A call of a name whose type is a float, vector, string, entity or struct is "not a function". Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseFunctionCall`.

A function with no body is an error (FTEF-17.11) whether it is a global or a member function a class declares and no `Class::member` defines, a `virtual` one included: `class C { void() m; };` and `class C { virtual void() m; };` are "function %s has no body", `class C { void() m; }; void C::m(void) { };` is not. A function whose type a typedef names is one, `typedef float fn(float); fn x;`, and so is C's function pointer typedef (FTEF-21.7) `extern "C" { typedef float (*fp)(float); fp x; }`, a function type with no `*`. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_FinaliseFunction`, `QCC_PR_ParseDefs`.

A state header in a member function names its next function among the members declared before it, and one that is no `void()` is "Type mismatch: %s, should be void()": `class C { float() m = [1, m] { return 1; }; };` and `class C { void() m = [1, n] {}; void() n = {}; };` (`n` a function the header declares) are refused, `class C { void() m = [1, m] {}; };` is not. A next function in another case is the function under `-Fcaseinsens` (FTEF-19.33): `$frame run`, `void() g = [$RUN, G] {};`. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseState`.

A cast's type and `sizeof`'s are read with `QCC_PR_ParseType(false, true, false)`, `silentfail`, so a name that is no type makes no cast and no type: `(T *)0`, `(T)0`, `sizeof(T *)` and `sizeof(T)` with no type `T` are a parenthesised expression and an operand, "Unknown value \"T\""; `sizeof(s)` after `struct S` is the type under `-Fcaseinsens` (FTEF-19.33) and "Unknown value" without, and `(struct s *)0` is a pointer to the struct `s`, a tag, in either case (FTEF-6.8). This profile's parser reads the shapes `(name)` and `(name *)` before an operand, and `sizeof(name *)`, as a type, and the semantic model reports the name as no type, "\"T\" is not a type" (`E0203`): the program is refused either way, and `sizeof(name)` tries the name as a type first (FTEF-19.38). Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_RefTerm`.

`QCC_PR_ParseEnum`'s legacy form reads any type's name before the `{` as the base type (`type = QCC_PR_ParseType(false, true, false)`), a class's or struct's among them, and a base after `:` may be one too; an enumerator of such a base has no number to take (`else QCC_PR_ParseError(ERR_NOTANUMBER, "values for enums of this type must be initialised");` after the `ev_integer`, `ev_uint`, `ev_int64`, `ev_uint64`, `ev_float` and `ev_double` cases) and one given a value is an implicit cast to the class, an error: `class E { float e; }; enum E { A };`, `class E; enum E { A = 1 };`, `struct E { float a; }; enum E { A };` and `struct S { float a; }; enum E : S { A };` are refused, which this profile reports as "values for enums of this type must be initialised" (`E0229`) at the first enumerator. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseEnum`.

A name no definition has, in a body or an initialiser, is made a `variant` and reported `QCC_PR_ParseWarning (ERR_UNKNOWNVALUE, "Unknown value \"%s\".", name)`, an error ending with a full stop (`E0301`, QCD-4.1's message with it), after `QCC_PR_GetDef`'s warning `W0213` "Autocvar \"NAME\" defined with local scope. promoting to global." for an `autocvar_` name in a body; a scoped name `S::n` is `QCC_PR_ParseError (ERR_UNKNOWNVALUE, "Unknown value \"%s::%s\"", ...)` with none. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseRefValue`.
**Withdrawn** 2026-10-28: it counted array sizes among the parts not modelled, which FTEF-19.62 now folds; replaced by FTEF-19.63.

These parts of the path are not modelled by this profile, each for its reason: the values of default values and enum values that are expressions other than a literal, a name or `_()`, which FTEQCC folds as it compiles them, the compiler's work (P2-06, constant folding P2-08); an initialiser of a global that is such an expression is compared by its text (FTEF-17.10), and typed by the check stage (FTEF-34.9); the warnings FTEQCC gives as it writes the program rather than as it defines a name, a definition never referred to ("no references", `WARN_NOTREFERENCED`), a field allocated twice ("Field def already has a value", "Inconsistant field def"), the precache checks ("Sound \"NAME\" was used but not directly precached" and the others of `QCC_WriteData`, from the names `precache_*`, `setmodel`, `sound`, `localsound`, `used_sound` and `used_model` are given) and the end_sys checks, which belong to the compiler's output (QC-25); designated initialisers, `{ .a = 1 }`, whose members are read as written (FTEF-19.47 reads the others), and a definition of a struct type not yet defined ("redeclared with different storage type"), the compiler's (QC-21); and FTEQCC's reacc and hexenc syntaxes (`flag_acc`, `var name : type`, a field `alias`), which `-Tid` does not enable.

A braced initialiser is read against the type element by element (`QCC_PR_ParseInitializerType_Internal`): an array's elements up to its size ("arrays go recursive", each an element of the next dimension or the element type), a vector's as three floats, a struct's one per member in order, but `static` and `virtual` members, and each value as a definition's value is (FTEF-19.31, FTEF-19.3): `float x[2] = {"a", 1};` is "Cannot cast from string to float", `vector x[2] = {1, 2};` warns twice "Implicit cast from float to vector", and `float x[2] = {y, 1};` for a variable `y` is "initializer for 'x' is not constant". A member or element that is an array needs its own braces, else the fatal error "expected {, found X"; a struct member given a value is cast to the struct, "Cannot cast from float to struct S". A struct with a parent takes only `{}` or designated members, else the fatal error `E0354` "inherited structs must use designated initialisers"; a union's members all start at 0, so a second element is the fatal error `E0355` "member U.v was already ininitialised". An element past the size or the members is left to what reads on: inside braces "expected }, found X"; at a global's top level the warning "Missing semicolon at end of definition" and the fatal error `"X" is not a type`; at a local's the warning, "Statement does not do anything" and "expected ;, found }". So `float x[2] = {1, 2, 3};`, `S x = {1, 2};` for a one-member `S` and `float x[2][2] = {{1, 2, 3}, {3, 4}};` are refused, and `float x[2] = {1, 2,};` and fewer elements than members are not.

An initialiser of a global or `static` naming no definition is "Unknown value \"NAME\"." where it is used and then `E0214` "initializer for 'X' is not constant"; an unknown `Scope::name` is the first alone.

A default value is read with the parameter's type, before the declaration's name (FTEF-19.6), so a fatal error in it ends the declaration there: the name is neither defined nor compared with an earlier definition, and a body after it is not read. `void(float a, optional float b = '1 2 3') g;` then `g(1);` is "Cannot cast from vector to float" and "Unknown value \"g\"."; a redeclaration with such a default is that error alone, no "Type mismatch on redeclaration".

A field of a struct, union or class type casts only to a field of the same type or of a `variant` (`typecmp`), any other field or value being the fatal error `E0213` "Cannot cast from A to B": `.S fs; .float fa; fs = fa;` is "Cannot cast from .float to .S", and a field of a class to a field of a class it derives from "Cannot cast from class Other to class Player".

An attribute list is a modifier too: `QCC_PR_ParseDefs` sets `hadmodifier = true;` at the end of each pass of its modifier loop, the `[[...]]` branch included, so after an attribute list alone the type may be left out and is `__int32` (FTEF-19.21): with `attributes` on, `[[eraseable]] x = 5; string s = x;` warns "Implicit cast from __int32 to string".

An item of an enum of an integer base (`int`, `uint`, `__int64`, `__uint64`) is the constant `QCC_MakeIntConst(next_i)` and its kin make of its value, a constant of that type the folding reads: `enum E : int { C = 2, D };` makes `arr[D]` the index 3. A float literal given to one is converted by `QCC_SupplyConversion`, whose `OP_CONV_FTOI` (or `OP_CONV_FU` and the 64-bit ones) folds with its warnings: `enum E : int { C = 1.5 };` is "Numerical overflow. 1.500000 will be rounded to 1" and the value 1.

A braced initialiser for a scalar, a float, string, entity, field or integer, global, local or an array's element, is the error `E0201` "\"{\" - not a name" at the `{`: `QCC_PR_ParseInitializerType` reads the scalar's value as an expression, which `{` cannot start (`float x = { 1 };`, `float a[2] = { {1}, 2 };`); a vector takes braces as three floats.

`QCC_main` makes the core types again under names of their own: `QCC_PR_NewType("__int", ev_integer, ...)`, `"__uint"`, and `"__string"`, `"__vector"` and `"__entity"` when the core type's name has no `_`. Each is the basic type it names and prints by its own name: `__int a; string s = a;` is "Implicit cast from __int to string", `__vector cv; float f = cv;` "Cannot cast from __vector to float", and an argument of `__uint` is named `__uint` in the builtin checks' messages (FTEF-33).

A float or an integer cast to a vector (`QCC_EvaluateCast`, `totype == ev_vector`) is multiplied by `'1 1 1'`, `OP_MUL_FV` or `OP_MUL_IV`, folded, emitted or emulated in turn: on the id target `int i; vector v; v = i;` is "Implicit cast from __int32 to vector" and then `OP_MUL_IV`'s "itof emulation: denormals are unsafe i", in a store, a compound assignment and a local's initialiser alike.

A pointer's braced initialiser (`else if (type->type == ev_pointer && QCC_PR_CheckToken("{"))`) is a nameless array of what the pointer points to, made by `QCC_PR_DummyDef` with `GDF_STATIC` inside a function, whose elements are read as values of a definition named `''`: `float x; float *p = { x };` is `E0214` "initializer for '' is not constant", a local's included, and `{ 1, "a" }` "Cannot cast from string to float". The pointer then takes its address with `QCC_PR_GenerateAddressOf`: a target without `OP_GLOBALADDRESS` refuses it, the fatal `E0331` "Address-of operator is not supported in this form without extensions. Consider the use of: #pragma target fte"; at global scope it is `E0345` "Unable to generate statements at global scope (GLOBALADDRESS)."; and a global's or a `static`'s value is then `E0214` "initializer for 'p' is not constant". A plain or `const` local takes it with no message.

A `static` local whose function already has a local of the name that is not `static` is the fatal error `E0364` "static redefinition of NAME follows non-static definition." (`QCC_PR_GetDef`: `else if (allocate && (flags & GDF_STATIC) && !def->isstatic)`): `void() f = { local float x; static float x; };`. A second `static` is the same definition, an `extern static` one a lookup of it and no error, and a `static` local of a global's name hides the global (FTEF-19.1). Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_GetDef`.

A lookup that passes over a `static` global of another unit (`if ((def->isstatic||(flags&GDF_STATIC)) && strcmp(def->unitn, ...)) { if (!foundstatic) foundstatic = def; ...}`) and finds nothing warns `W0315` "NAME defined static" (`if (foundstatic && !allocate && !(flags & GDF_SILENT))`, `WARN_SAMENAMEASGLOBAL`, `F306`) before FTEF-19.45's "Unknown value": `a.qc` `static float x;` and `b.qc` `void() f = { x = 1; };`. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_GetDef`.

A global or `static` local `__auto` (`isauto`, not in a body unless `static`) is allocated at start-up by `memalloc`, or `malloc`, which `QCC_PR_EmulationFunc` looks up by name; with neither defined it is the fatal error `E0365` "memalloc not yet defined, cannot define __auto NAME at global scope". A local's qualifiers are checked as a global's (FTEF-21.14): two storage classes are `W0214` "Conflicting storage classes." (`static __auto` is), and `const` with `var` "Conflicting constness.". `auto` itself is a keyword only once enabled; `__auto` always is. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseDefs`.

An array's size that is an expression other than a number literal is folded as it is read (`QCC_PR_ParseDefArray`: `QCC_SRef_EvalConst` of `QCC_PR_Expression`, an integer by `QCC_Eval_Int`), a global's at global scope before its definition is made, a local's where it is declared; one that is no constant is the error `E0366` "Array length is not a constant", and the definition's size is the one it folds to, for its bounds (FTEF-31.6), its initialiser and a redeclaration's size (FTEF-19.8). So `const float N = 3; float c[N];` makes `c[3]` "(constant) array index out of bounds (0 <= 3 < 3)" and `float d[N] = {1,2,3,4};` reads the fourth value as the next definition, and `float n; float a[n];`, `float a[n2];` and `float a[n+1];` (with "Unable to generate statements at global scope (ADD_F).") are the error. A local's first dimension is left for the function to allocate (`dynlength`) only on a target with `OP_PUSH` under `qcfuncs` off, when the local is not `static` and has no initialiser. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseDefArray`.

Designated braces, whose first element starts with `.`, name a member in every element (`QCC_PR_ParseInitializerType_Internal`: `if (QCC_PR_CheckToken(".")) ... else QCC_PR_ParseError (ERR_EXPECTED, "designated initialisers require all members to be initialised the same way")`), a `}` after a trailing `,` among them: `S st = { .a = 1, 2 };` and `{ .a = 1, .b = 2, }` are the fatal error `E0372`, at the element. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseInitializerType_Internal`.

Positional struct braces are read member by member, each value followed by `,` or by the closing `}`, and the loop ends at the last member (`for (partnum = 0; partnum < (type)->num_parms; partnum++) { if (QCC_PR_CheckToken("}")) break; ... if (isunion || !QCC_PR_CheckToken(",")) { QCC_PR_Expect("}"); break; } }`). After a value for every member and a trailing `,`, the closing `}` is left to what reads on: a global's or a local's definition is the warning "Missing semicolon at end of definition" and the fatal error `"}" is not a type`, at the `}`; `S st = { 1, 2, };` for a struct of two members. Braces with fewer values end at their `}`. This profile does not follow the `}` of nested braces, which closes the enclosing braces, nor what a local's definition is when more statements follow it. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseInitializerType_Internal`.

A definition may write `CLASS::NAME` with no type: `QCC_PR_ParseDefs` reads the class's name as the type and, with `::` after it, takes it as the scope (`classname = type->name; type = type_invalid;`), and the type is then `void`, so `C::m() = {}` defines a `void()`. Unless the name is the class's, a constructor's, it is the error `E0376` "no type specified for CLASS::NAME. this is only allowed for constructors", which does not end the definition: `C::m = {};` is then also "Type mismatch on redeclaration of C::m. void, should be void()". A scope that names no type is `"D" is not a type`. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseDefs`.

A `(` after a definition's name, and its array suffixes, is a parameter list whatever the type (`if (QCC_PR_CheckToken("("))`), so on a function type the definition is a function returning a function: `float() g()`. When that function type was written inline rather than by a typedef (`type_inlinefunction`), it warns `W0320` "Function returning function. Is this what you meant? (suggestion: use typedefs)" (`WARN_UNSAFEFUNCTIONRETURNTYPE`, which no flag names), a typedef's as a definition's. Such a type prints its return type by the function type's name, `__function()`. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseDefs`.

A typedef's name is looked up among the types FTEQCC defines itself as among the program's (`old = QCC_TypeForName(name)`): `void`, `float`, `vector`, `string`, `entity` and the registered C scalars such as `__int`. A typedef naming another type by one of them is the error `E0219` "Cannot redeclare typedef NAME from NAME to TYPE": `typedef vector float;`; one naming the same type is none, and, being a type, no definition named as a keyword. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseDefs`.

An unknown name in a body (FTEF-19.45) is defined there as a `variant` (`QCC_PR_GetSRef(type_variant, name, pr_scope, true, ...)`): its later uses in the function are that definition and report nothing, another function's report it again, and a later global of the name is no conflict. The checks after the name read it as a `variant`: `nope[1]` and `nope.y` are "expected ;, found [" and "expected ;, found .", `if (nope)` is "conditional type mismatch: variant", `-nope` "type mismatch for -", and a `variant` stores to a struct, as `QCC_SupplyConversionForAssignment` refuses no conversion to or from one. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseValue`, `QCC_PR_GetSRef`, `QCC_SupplyConversionForAssignment`.

A `static` local's value is a constant, as a global's is (`QCC_PR_GenerateInitializerType`: `basedef->isstatic` and `!tmp.sym->constant`), whatever expression gives it: `static float y = x + 1;`, `-x`, `[x, 0, 0]` and `h(1)` of a variable `x` and a function `h` are "initializer for 'y' is not constant"; `1 + 2` and `k * 2` of a constant `k` fold and are accepted. A plain or `const` local is never refused (`basedef->scope && !basedef->isstatic && !basedef->initialized`). Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_GenerateInitializerType`.

At global scope an unknown name in a definition's value is a global `variant`, as in a function it is a local one (FTEF-19.69): `QCC_PR_GetSRef(type_variant, name, pr_scope, true, ...)` with `pr_scope` null defines it, and "Unknown value \"NAME\"." is a warning. The value is then no constant, "initializer for 'u' is not constant", and the checks after the name read a `variant`: `float u = -nope;` is "type mismatch for -", `nope + 1` "Unable to generate statements at global scope (ADD_F).", and `float u = nope[1];` ends at the `[` (FTEF-18.38). Later uses find the global with no message, and `float nope;` after it redeclares it. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseValue`, `QCC_PR_GetSRef`.

A global's value that names a global variable whose type converts to the global's by opcodes (FTEF-22) is read at global scope as any expression is (FTEF-34.9): `int x; float q = x;` on the id target is "itof emulation: denormals are unsafe x", "Unable to generate statements at global scope (DIV_F).", then "initializer for 'q' is not constant"; `float x; int q = x;` the `ftoi` emulation and `MUL_F`; under `#pragma target fte` `CONV_IF`. A constant converts by folding, with no message. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseInitializerType`, `QCC_SupplyConversionForAssignment`.

After a qualifier, `hadmodifier`, `QCC_PR_ParseType` with `silentfail` finds no type at any token that is no name and no field's `.` or `..`, and `QCC_PR_ParseDefs` takes `type_integer` (FTEF-19.21); the token is then the definition's name, which `QCC_PR_ParseName` refuses: `var = 1;`, `const 5;` and `static = 2;` in a body are "\"=\" - not a name" and "\"5\" - not a name", never "is not a type". Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseDefs`; `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_lex.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseName`.

In a body a statement `T x;`, with no `local` or qualifier and `T` a lone name that names no type there, is no definition: `QCC_PR_ParseStatement` finds no type and reads the expression `T`, an unknown name being a `variant` (FTEF-19.69), "Unknown value \"T\".", then at `x` "Expected punctuation", the statement "Statement does not do anything", and the fatal "expected ;, found x"; a name that is a value gives all but the first. So a typedef out of its block, a struct of an inner block, or a type named before its typedef is not "is not a type", which `local T x;` still is (FTEF-19.20). Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseStatement`, `QCC_PR_RefExpression`.

A strict enum, `enum class E : T`, casts to and from no other type wherever a value is cast, stored, passed, or cast explicitly (FTEF-19.10): its item's null constant too, which `QCC_SRef_IsNull` would let any other type take, so `f = E::A;` of a float `f` is "Cannot cast from enum E:float to float", and `e = 1;`, `e = (E)1;` and the global `E e = (E)1;` are "Cannot cast from float to enum E:float"; under `lax` "Implicit lax cast". A plain enum's item is its base type's constant, and its 0 casts to a string with no message. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_TryEvaluateCast`, `QCC_PR_ParseEnum`.

A field defined with a value, `.float b = a;` of a field `a`, names the field `a` names, and takes no field space of its own: `QCC_PR_ParseDefs` gives a field `pr.size_fields` only when it has no initialiser ("fields are const by default, even when not initialised (as they are initialised behind the scenes)", in the branch with no `=`), and `QCC_PR_GenerateInitializerType` copies the value's words into the field's global. The field table lists `b` at `a`'s offset; a vector field's `_x`, `_y` and `_z`, which `QCC_PR_DummyDef` makes at its global's three words, name `a`'s three. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseDefs`, `QCC_PR_GenerateInitializerType`.

The parser reads each keyword with the flags in force at its token. They start as `compiler_flag[]` sets them (`FLAG_ASDEFAULT`, `qc_preproc::Keywords::default`), then as the command line sets them (`-K`, `-F` and `-std=`, FTEF-14.72) and a Hexen II target (FTEF-20.3), then as each `#pragma keyword` or `#pragma flag` sets them (FTEF-12.11) from the token after the directive, which FTEQCC lexes, and so reads the directive, before the parser asks for it; and a definition named as a keyword may turn that keyword off (FTEF-20.4). The preprocessor marks the flags by token (`qc_preproc::FileOutput::keywords`): the first token holds the whole state, and a pragma's mark sets only the flags it names, `kce` and `caseinsens` among them, so a keyword a definition turned off stays off unless a pragma names it again. The flags carry from file to file and into the second autoprototyping pass, as the pragmas' flags do (FTEF-12.11). `QCC_ImportProgs`, which `#merge` runs, turns `wrap` and `weak` on ("these keywords are implicitly enabled by #merge"); this profile opens no file for `#merge` (FTEF-14.47), so it turns none on. Under the vanilla dialect, which has no keyword flags, the parser reads id's words as `qcc` does (QC-14.1).

`QCC_PR_CheckKeyword(enabled, word)` takes a token that starts with `__` when the rest is `word` in any case, whether or not the keyword is on ("lets just always go insensitive with a leading underscore pair": `if (pr_token[0] == '_' && pr_token[1] == '_') { if (stricmp(string, pr_token+2)) return false; ...`), and any other token only when the keyword is on and the token is `word`, in any case under `caseinsens` (`if (flag_caseinsensitive) { if (stricmp (string, pr_token)) return false; }`) and exactly otherwise. `return`, `if`, `else`, `while`, `do` and `not` are `#define`d as 1, always on; `_Bool`, `sizeof`, `_length` and a class's member words (FTEF-20.11) are asked for with `1` or `true`; `deprecated` with `false`, so only `__deprecated` is it. `QCC_PR_CheckName(word)`, which reads an accessor's `get`, `set` and `inline` and an enum's `class`, takes `word`, in any case under `caseinsens`, and never a `__` spelling. So `__FOR` is `for` with the keyword off, `FOR` is `for` only under `-Fcaseinsens`, and `__while` is `while`.

After the command line `QCC_SetDefaultProperties` turns on `thinktime`, `until` and `loop` for a Hexen II target: `if (qcc_targetformat == QCF_HEXEN2 || qcc_targetformat == QCF_UHEXEN2 || qcc_targetformat == QCF_FTEH2) { keyword_thinktime = true; keyword_until = true; keyword_loop = true; }`. The target is the command line's (FTEF-14.72), which `QCC_SetDefaultProperties` sets again before each pass, so a `#pragma TARGET` turns none of them on.

`QCC_PR_DummyDef` warns of a new definition named exactly as a keyword that is on, `W0221` "\"NAME\" keyword used as variable name - coexisting" (`WARN_KEYWORDDISABLED`, which has no name) with `kce` on, and with it off "- disabling" and turns the keyword off (`#define KEYWORD(x) if (!STRCMP(name, #x) && keyword_##x) do{ ... keyword_##x = keywords_coexist;}while(0)`): `var`, `thinktime`, `for`, `switch`, `case`, `local`, `default`, `goto`, `break` for a definition that is no function, `continue`, `state`, `string`, `float` unless the target is `QCF_HEXEN2` or `QCF_UHEXEN2` ("hexen2 requires this..."), `entity`, `vector`, `const` and `asm`. The keyword is off from the token after the name. `QCC_PR_DummyDef` makes every definition: a global, a local, a field, the parameters of a function with a body as `QCC_PR_ParseImmediateStatements` reads it (a prototype's and a builtin's make none), an enum's names, a state header's or `state` statement's next think function when it is new, and a `using` alias; a typedef's name, a struct's members and a class's members are none, and `Class::member` is named so, no keyword. So with `kce` off `float for;` makes `for (;;) {}` a call of the float `for`, the error "not a function", and `for = 1;` an assignment. Two deliberate divergences, both only with `kce` off, as the parser turns the keyword off and the semantic model makes the definitions: a definition named as a keyword turns it off even when it is a redeclaration, which `QCC_PR_GetDef` finds with no new definition; and the keyword is off to the end of the file the definition is in, and on again in the next file and the second autoprototyping pass unless a definition there turns it off, as each file is parsed on its own; and a body whose function type a typedef names defines no parameter, as the parser knows no typedef's parameters.

A statement of `QCC_PR_ParseStatement` is read by its first token, the keywords tried in its order: `{`; `return`; `exit` (`keyword_exit` is `flag_acc`, reacc's, FTEF-20.13, so only `__exit`), `OP_DONE` and a `;`; `loop` and a statement, run again until a `break`; `until` or `while`, a parenthesised condition and a statement; `for`; `do`, a statement, then `until` with its keyword or `while` exactly (`QCC_PR_Expect ("while")`, so `__while` there is "expected while"); `local` and a definition; the definitions of FTEF-20.14; `state`, a state header `[frame, next]` as a function's (FTEF-18.3) and a `;`; `if`, with `not` (FTEF-16.5); `switch`; `using`; `asm`; a `:` label (FTEF-18.23); `goto`; `break`, which before a `(` is a call of the function `break` (`if (!STRCMP ("(", pr_token))`), and else a `;`; `continue`; `case`; `default`; `thinktime`, an expression, a `:`, an expression and a `;`; `;`; a `name:` label; and else an expression.
