Each keyword starts its statement whatever follows it, so with `for` on `for = 1;` is "expected (, found =". `using (a, b = c) s` finds each name as a value is found (`QCC_PR_GetDef (NULL, name, pr_scope, false, 0, 0)`), "NAME is not defined" (`E0313`) when none is, and makes an alias of its type named as it is or, after `=`, as the name after it, from its name until the statement `s` ends; `using a, b = c;` makes them to the end of the function. `asm` takes an instruction, or several in `{ }`: `local` and a definition, or a token that is an `opname` of `pr_opcodes[]` exactly and its operands up to a `;`, which are code generation's (FTEF-19.63); any other token is `E0511` "Bad op code name NAME" (`ERR_BADOPCODE`). `thinktime e : t;` looks up `nextthink` and `time` by name when the target has no `OP_THINKTIME` (`QCC_PR_GetSRef(NULL, "nextthink", ...)`), "Unknown value \"nextthink\"" when there is none: on the standard target, and on every target but `QCF_HEXEN2` and `QCF_UHEXEN2` in this profile, which takes the other targets' opcode sets for code generation's (L-01); that `e` must be an entity and `t` a float ("thinktime type mismatch") is the type checker's (FTEF-19.63). By default `loop`, `until`, `state`, `thinktime` and `using` are off, so only their `__` spellings start these statements.
**Withdrawn** (P2-131, #568): it found a type by its exact name only, and left the types the program defines and a `for` initialiser's types out. Replaced by FTEF-20.14.

`QCC_PR_ParseDefs` reads qualifiers before a type in a loop, each with its keyword: `typedef`, `extern`, `auto`, `register`, `static`, `shared`, `const`, `var`, `nonstatic` (only outside a function: `!pr_scope && QCC_PR_CheckKeyword(keyword_nonstatic, "nonstatic")`), `unused` or `noref`, `used`, `nosave`, `strip` or `ignore`, `inline`, `wrap`, `weak`, `accumulate` and `deprecated` (`QCC_PR_CheckKeyword(false, "deprecated")`). So with its keyword off a qualifier is a type's name, `#pragma keyword disable const` making `const float x = 1;` "\"const\" is not a type", and with it on a qualifier off by default is one, `#pragma keyword enable unused` making `unused float x;` a definition.

`QCC_PR_ParseType` reads, each with its keyword, `const` (with "ignoring unsupported const keyword") and `volatile` before a type and `const` after a `*` (FTEF-2.11); then `accessor` (FTEF-10.1); `class` only with `qcfuncs` on (`if (flag_qcfuncs && QCC_PR_CheckKeyword (keyword_class, "class"))`, at its token, FTEF-12.12); `enum`, `enumflags`, `union` and `struct`; and then a name `QCC_TypeForName` finds or the C type words (FTEF-20.9). With its keyword off each is a type's name, so `#pragma keyword disable struct` makes `struct s { float a; };` "\"struct\" is not a type" while `__struct s { ... };` defines the struct.

The loop over C type words (FTEF-2.8) takes each word with its keyword in force at the type: `register`, `signed`, `unsigned`, `long`, `int` or `integer`, `short`, `char`, `_Bool` (always), `float` and `double`. `_Bool` is `__bint` with `keyword_int` on and `__bfloat` with it off (`if (keyword_int) type = type_bint; else type = type_bfloat;`), and `longbits` is 32 under `ILP32` and 64 otherwise (`#define longbits (flag_ILP32?32:64)`, FTEF-12.12), so with `#pragma flag enable ILP32` `__long l;` is `__int32`. The type the words make is the one FTEQCC registers, named as `QCC_PR_NewType` names it (`__int32`, `__uint64`, `__int16`, `__bfloat`), which the semantic model compares and writes in messages (TypeName). So `#pragma keyword enable long` makes `long l;` an `__int64` and `long int l;` an `__int32`.

`QCC_PR_ParseFunctionType` reads a parameter's qualifiers with their keywords: `optional` (`keyword_optional`, on by default) and `inout`, `out` and `in` (`keyword_inout`, off by default, so only `__inout`, `__out` and `__in`).

`QCC_PR_ParseEntClass` reads a class member's words with `QCC_PR_CheckKeyword(1, ...)`, always on: `nonvirtual`, `static`, `const`, `var`, `virtual`, `ignore`, `strip`, `inline`, `get` and `set`, and `public`, `private` and `protected` before a `:`, so `__STATIC` is `static` there and `STATIC` under `caseinsens`. `QCC_PR_ParseRefValue` takes `this` and `super` as the intrinsics of FTEF-19.16 only with `keyword_class` on (`else if (keyword_class && !strcmp(name, "this"))`), and with it off they are names like any other, "Unknown value" when no definition has them.

`QCC_PR_ParseDefs` takes a `;` right after a declaration's type and defines nothing (`if (QCC_PR_CheckToken (";")) { if (istypedef) ...; return; }`, "type (%s) with no name" commented out), so `float;`, `const float;` and, in a body, `enum { A, B };` and `struct s { float a; };` are definitions of no name; `typedef;` and `typedef float;` are FTEF-19.9's.

The reacc keywords `CodeSys`, `function`, `objdata`, `object`, `pfunc`, `system`, `real`, `external` and `exit` are `#define`d as `flag_acc` (`#define keyword_codesys flag_acc //reacc needs this`), which only `-Facc` and `-std=reacc` set. Their syntax is reacc's, which this profile does not read (FTEF-19.63): it reads the reacc keywords as off, so after a type at file level `__function` and in a function's initialiser `__external`, which `QCC_PR_CheckKeyword` would take, are names, where the pinned FTEQCC reads reacc's function and builtin syntax; `__exit` is FTEF-20.5's.

In a body a statement defines locals when its first token is a name `QCC_TypeForName` finds, not followed by `::` (`strncmp(pr_file_p, "::", 2)`, so with the `::` touching the name), or is exactly one of the words `QCC_PR_ParseStatement` tests with `STRCMP` with its keyword on: `var`, `noref`, `string`, `float`, `double`, `entity`, `vector`, `integer`, `unsigned`, `signed`, `long`, `int`, `short`, `char`, `_Bool` (always), `register`, `volatile`, `static`, `class`, `struct`, `union`, `enum`, `extern`, `auto`, `typedef` and `const`; or is a `.`. No `__` spelling and no other case is among the `STRCMP` words, so `__typedef float t;` and `__long x;` in a body are values, "Unknown value", and `typedef` there starts a typedef only as written. `QCC_TypeForName` searches the table of the names `QCC_PR_NewType` registers (`void`, `float`, `vector`, `string`, `entity`, `__double`, `__int`, `__int32`, `__uint`, `__uint32`, `__int64`, `__uint64`, `__int16`, `__uint16`, `__int8`, `__uint8`, `__bint`, `__bfloat`, `__variant`, `variant`, `__string`, `__vector` and `__entity`) and of the types the program made, a `typedef`'s name and the tag of a `struct`, `union`, `enum`, `class` or `accessor`, a local `typedef`'s in its function only (`t->scope == pr_scope`), and under `-Fcaseinsens` it searches in any case (`pHash_Get = &Hash_GetInsensitive`, FTEF-19.29): `Float x;`, `VECTOR v;`, `Entity e;`, `String s;`, `FLOAT x; x = 1;`, `__Int x;`, `Float;` and `ENTITY:;` are definitions, the last `":" - not a name`, and `float Float; ... Float = 1;` is `"=" - not a name`, and a `typedef float Foo;` makes `Foo = 1;` that error. A name that is such a type starts a definition whatever follows it, `void;` and `__variant;` among them (FTEF-20.12), and a name that is none is a value. The `for` initialiser is no statement: `QCC_PR_ParseStatement_For` reads each of its items, separated by `,`, with `QCC_PR_ParseType (false, true, false)`, which finds those names, the C type words with `QCC_PR_CheckKeyword` (FTEF-20.9, in any case under `caseinsens`), so `for (Integer i; ; )` defines `i` under `-Fcaseinsens` and `for (Float i = 0; ...)` defines it, while a name it finds nothing for is the first item of an expression. In `sizeof (NAME)` and a cast's parentheses such a name is a type, and with `caseinsens` off the same name in another case is a value, "Unknown value".

A `typedef` and a struct's or union's tag a function's body declares last to the end of its block, and are no type after it: `{ { typedef float t; } t x; }` reads `t` as no type, `{ struct S { float a; }; S x; }` defines `x`, and `S y;` after the body is "\"S\" is not a type". An enum a body declares makes its values constants of the function in FTEQCC, not seen after the body (`float x = A;` there is "Unknown value \"A\"."); this profile divergently declares a body's enum as one at file level, its values and name seen after the body too, since the file's enum checks (the legacy base form, a name another type has, FTEF-19.10) read it there.

Each token is lexed, parsed and its definitions made with the flags in force when FTEQCC looks at it: a file starts with the preprocessor's (the command line's, then each pragma's before it, from file to file), each `#pragma flag` or `keyword` sets only the flags it names from the token after it (`*compiler_flag[f].enabled = st;`), and the parser replays them with the changes its `extern` blocks make, at one token in FTEQCC's order: a block's restore (before the token is lexed), a block's start (before `QCC_PR_Lex` lexes the token after its string), then the pragmas in the white space before the token, which `QCC_PR_Lex` runs as it lexes it. The flags kept are those the lexer reads (FTEF-12.12), `cpriority`, `assumevar`, `subscope`, `attributes`, `ifvector` and `vectorlogic` (FTEF-30.2), with the operator priorities (FTEF-21.4) and the defaults of FTEF-21.14; a pragma that names none of them marks nothing, and the others are FTEF-21.20's. A flag read while the parser looks at a token, as FTEQCC reads one after it has lexed the token after what it read, is the flag at that token: `subscope` at a block's end is read at the token after its `}`. The token after an `extern` block is lexed with the block's flags and read with them restored, the pragmas before it applied first and the restore after them, so a pragma there that names one of the six saved flags is undone for the reading and holds for the lexing.

**Withdrawn** (P2-130, #567): it joined every string beside the block's, compared the whole of it, took a `;` before the end of the text or a `}` for a definition, and gave the blocks no nesting level. Replaced by FTEF-21.17.

At a block's end FTEQCC restores the six flags it saved where it started (`flag_qcfuncs = old_qcfuncs; flag_cpriority = old_cpriority; flag_assume_integer = old_assumeint; flag_assume_double = old_assumef64; flag_assumevar = old_assumevar; pr_subscopedlocals = old_subscope;`, "FIXME: reset all flags+keywords?"), so a `#pragma flag` in the block that names one of them holds only to its end, and one that names any other flag holds after it: in `extern "C" { #pragma flag enable qcfuncs }` `qcfuncs` is on to the `}` and off again before it as before the block. Blocks nest, each restoring what it saved, the inner first.

The operator priorities are `QCC_PrioritiseOpcodes`', which reads `flag_cpriority` when it runs: once a compile starts, from `QCC_PR_BeginCompilation` after the command line is read (`-Fcpriority`, `-std=c`), and at each `#pragma flag` that names `cpriority`, at once (`if (compiler_flag[f].enabled == &flag_cpriority) QCC_PrioritiseOpcodes();`). Nothing else runs it: an `extern "C"` block sets `flag_cpriority` and leaves the priorities as they are ("we don't currently change operator precedence"), a pragma in the block that names `cpriority` sets them for the rest of the compile though the block restores the flag, and the priorities hold into the second autoprototyping pass, which `QCC_SetDefaultProperties` starts without `QCC_PR_BeginCompilation`.

With `cpriority` on `QCC_PrioritiseOpcodes` gives each class of `pr_opcodes` C's priority: `priority_class[PC_UNARYNOT] = 1; priority_class[PC_MULDIV] = 2; priority_class[PC_ADDSUB] = 3; priority_class[PC_SHIFT] = 4; priority_class[PC_RELATION] = 5; priority_class[PC_EQUALITY] = 6; priority_class[PC_BITAND] = 7; priority_class[PC_BITXOR] = 8; priority_class[PC_BITOR] = 9; priority_class[PC_LOGICAND] = 10; priority_class[PC_LOGICOR] = 11; priority_class[PC_TERNARY] = 12; priority_class[PC_STORE] = 13;`. The classes are the opcodes' (`*`, `/`, `%`, `*^` and `><` `PC_MULDIV`; `+` and `-` `PC_ADDSUB`; `<<` and `>>` `PC_SHIFT`; `<`, `<=`, `>` and `>=` `PC_RELATION`; `==`, `!=` and `<=>` `PC_EQUALITY`; `&`, `^` and `|`; `&&`; `||`; the assignments `PC_STORE`), so `a == b & c` is `(a == b) & c`, `!a == b` is `(!a) == b` (`NOT_PRIORITY` is 1, the term and its calls), `a || b ? c : d` is `(a || b) ? c : d`, and `x = a ? b : c` assigns the conditional. With it off they are QuakeC's (FTE-19.3, FTE-8.4).

`!` and `~` read their operand with `EXPR_WARN_ABOVE_1`, which every right operand of a binary operator in it is read with too, and an expression in parentheses, an argument and a subscript are not, so each binary operator the operand takes is the warning F304 "suggest parenthesis for unary operator that applies to multiple terms" (`if (priority > 1 && exprflags & EXPR_WARN_ABOVE_1)`, `WARN_UNARYNOTSCOPE`, on by default, `W0227`), given at the token after its right operand: with QuakeC's priorities `!a == b`, `!a * b`, `~a & b` and `!(a) == b` warn, and `!a && b`, `!(a == b)` and `-a == b` do not; with C's none does, the operand being a term.

With `qcfuncs` off `QCC_PR_ParseType` takes no parameter list (`if (flag_qcfuncs && QCC_PR_CheckToken ("("))`), so `void()` is no type where a type is read alone, a parameter's, a member's or a cast's, and `QCC_PR_ParseDefs` reads a declaration's type without its `*`s (`QCC_PR_ParseType (false, hadmodifier, !flag_qcfuncs)`, `ignoreptr`), which each declarator reads: `float *a, b;` makes `a` a pointer and `b` a `float`, where with it on both are pointers. Each declarator then reads `*`s, and parameter lists before its name in a loop (`while( QCC_PR_CheckToken ("("))`), each a function returning the type so far, which the type took before with `qcfuncs` on, so `.void() think;` declares a function returning `.void`, not a field, and a list may stand before any declarator's name whatever the flag (`float a, (float x) g;`); and C's function pointer `(*name)` or `(*name[N])` and a parameter list, a function type with a pointer to it for each `*` past the first, a variable (`isvar |= isptr>0;`) as every declarator after it in the declaration, but in a `typedef`. Where the type took a list, its first declarator's `(*` is a list `QCC_PR_ParseFunctionType` refuses ("expected function arg list"), so `float (*fp)(float);` is an error with `qcfuncs` on.

With `qcfuncs` off `QCC_PR_ParseFunctionType` reads `()` as variadic (`if (!flag_qcfuncs) ftype->vargs = true; //'void name()' is vargs/undefined in C89`), so `void h();` is `void(...)`; a first parameter that is no type, as an `int` named by the word (`if (!flag_qcfuncs) t = type_integer; //c89 assumes int.`), so `void h(x);` is `void(__int32 x)`, where a later one is "\"y\" is not a type", the parser reading a lone name there as such a name, as it cannot tell one a typedef names, which FTEQCC reads as an unnamed parameter of that type, a deliberate divergence; and an array parameter `[N]` as a pointer ("just turn it into a pointer and ditch the top-level size. C style."), as `[]` is whatever the flag ("length omitted. just treat it as a pointer"), where with it on `float a[2]` is a `float`.

`QCC_PR_ParseDefs` reads `[[` among the qualifiers after one of them, `typedef` among them, or with `attributes` on outside a function (`else if ((hadmodifier||(flag_attributes && !pr_scope)) && QCC_PR_CheckToken("["))`), then `QCC_PR_Expect("[")`, attributes and `,`s up to a `]`, and `QCC_PR_Expect("]")`, and counts it a qualifier. Its attributes, each name read with `QCC_PR_CheckName`: `alias(NAME)` or `alias("NAME")`, `accumulate`, `eraseable`, which is `noref`, and `__deprecated` with an optional `("reason")` (`QCC_PR_CheckKeyword(false, "deprecated")`, so a bare `deprecated` is none), whose argument is a string or the error "expected string". Any other token is F321 "Unknown attribute \"NAME\"" (`WARN_GMQCC_SPECIFIC`, `W0228`), and the tokens up to the next `]` or `,` are passed over, so `[[foo(1, 2)]]` warns of `foo` and of `2`; an `accumulate` after one is F321 "accumulating an accumulating accumulation". A definition given `alias(TARGET)` is made with no lookup of its name (`QCC_PR_DummyDef`) and refers to the definition `TARGET` names in its scope, "TARGET not yet defined, cannot create NAME as an alias" (`E0234`) when none does; it may not be initialised, "alias NAME may not be initialised" (`E0235`), and its type may be another's; `alias` counts among the storage classes of FTEF-19.16. With `attributes` off a file-level `[[` is "\"[\" is not a type", and in a body `[[` is an expression's.

`QCC_PR_ParseDefs` tests `extern` against the declaration's type, once it is read (`if (externfnc && !pr_scope && basetype->type != ev_function) { if (flag_qcfuncs) QCC_PR_ParseWarning(WARN_IGNOREDKEYWORD, "extern keyword may only apply to qc functions."); externfnc=false; }`): on a type that is no function's, a C-style declarator's `void h(float x)`, a left out type's and a typedef's of what is no function included, the `extern` is dropped, so the function is no external one and needs a body ("function NAME has no body"), with the warning only when `qcfuncs` is on. With `qcfuncs` off a C function declared in a body is a global constant whose body is elsewhere (`if (!flag_qcfuncs && pr_scope) isconstant = externfnc = true; //in C, a locally defined function refers to an external one.`), made in the global scope (`externfnc?NULL:pr_scope`), so `void h();` in a body declares the global `h`.

With `assumevar` on an initialised global is no constant (`(isinitialised && !flag_assumevar)`, "initialised things are assumed to be consts, unless assumevar is specified"), read once the `=` is: so a name that initialises another global is "initializer for 'NAME' is not constant" (`E0214`), and `const` still makes a constant.

With `subscope` on at a block's end FTEQCC removes the locals made in the block from `localstable` (`if (pr_subscopedlocals) { //remove any new locals from the hashtable.`), so after it their names are the global again or "Unknown value", and a local whose name a local already has is a new one: `QCC_PR_GetDef` passes the old one over for a type mismatch ("assume it was defined in a different subscope") and, but for a `static`, for any other ("subscopes mean that the later one replaces the first, hopefully."), with no "duplicate definition ignored", and from there the name is the new one, the newest in the table first. A local is found from where it is made. A `for` statement's locals leave scope whether the flag is on or off (FTEF-19.19).

With `assumeint` on where `QCC_PR_ParseEnum` starts an enum's base type is `__int32` (`basetype = (flag_assume_integer?type_integer:type_float);`), so its names are integers, which a string may be initialised with, with the warning of FTEF-19.31.

`#pragma noref N`, `#pragma nosave N` and `#pragma defaultstatic N` set the defaults `QCC_PR_ParseDefs` starts each definition with (`pbool isstatic=defaultstatic; ... pbool noref = defaultnoref; pbool nosave = defaultnosave;`, `!!atoi(msg)`), from the token after them, as their marks hold them from file to file; `QCC_SetDefaultProperties` sets `defaultstatic = 0;` before the second autoprototyping pass and leaves the others. Under `defaultstatic` every global is `static` (FTEF-19.12) but one marked `nonstatic`, which only outside a function undoes it, and every local is a `static` local. A `typedef`'s `static`, `noref` and `nosave` are no "bad combination of modifiers with typedef" when the default is on (`||(isstatic && !defaultstatic) ||(noref && !defaultnoref) ||(nosave && !defaultnosave)`), `auto`, `register` and `nonstatic` never are, and under `defaultstatic` a typedef has two storage classes, "Conflicting storage classes.". `QCC_PR_ParseDefs` reads `typedef` among its other qualifiers, before or after them, and after it, a modifier, a type may be left out (FTEF-19.21): `typedef static x;` names an `__int32` and is the error.

**Withdrawn** (P2-122, #558): it said the target's `flag_undefwordsize` and the casts `lax`, `typeexplicit` and `qccx` allow are not modelled, but the semantic model's casts and conversions read them (FTEF-22). Replaced by FTEF-21.18.

The flag family of `cargo xtask oracles builtins` (`xtask/src/oracles/builtins/flags.rs`) compiles programs that bind `f` and then use each of these statements, under the FTEQCC profile, with no option, with `-Werror -Wno-Q208` for those a warning decides, and with the command-line options that set the flags. Its run of 2026-10-21 (macOS arm64) agrees with the pinned FTEQCC on every case.

`QCC_PR_ParseDefs` reads `extern` as its first qualifier, with its keyword, then a string (`if (!hadmodifier && pr_token_type == tt_immediate && pr_immediate_type==type_string)`), as a block: a `{`, definitions up to a `}` (`QCC_PR_ParseDefs(NULL, false)` each), or with no `{` one definition. The string is the one token the lexer read, whose parts `QCC_PR_LexString` joined as any string's (`"" "C"` is `C`); a string beside it that comes from another text is another token, a macro's and the source's or two macros', so with `#define C "C"` the program `extern C C { string s = "\9"; }` is the block `"C"` and a definition that starts with the string `"C"`, `"C" is not a type`, where `#define C "C" "x"` and `extern C { ... }` is the block `"Cx"`. It is compared with `strcasecmp(pr_token, "C")` and `strcasecmp(pr_token, "QC")`, so in any case, and only up to its first NUL, where `pr_token` ends: `"C\x00x"` is `"C"`, and under `qccx` so is `"C":"x"`, whose `:` the lexer writes as a NUL; `"C"` turns `qcfuncs` off and `cpriority`, `assumeint`, `assumevar` and `subscope` on (`flag_qcfuncs = false; flag_cpriority = true; flag_assume_integer = true; ... flag_assumevar = true; pr_subscopedlocals = true;`), `assumedouble` left as it is ("not forced, too annoying"); `"QC"` turns `qcfuncs` on, the others "refrain from changing it"; any other string changes nothing, and the block is read all the same. Each of its definitions is a `QCC_PR_ParseDefs` call, whose first act is `while (QCC_PR_CheckToken(";"))` and whose second is to read a type, so the `;`s may stand before each definition and after none: a block or an `extern "STRING"` that reaches the end of the text with no definition is the error `"" is not a type` (`extern "C"`, `extern "C";`, `extern "C" ;;;`, `extern "C" "QC"`), and one that reaches a `}` is `"}" is not a type` (`extern "C" { ; }`, `extern "C" { float y; ;; }`); a `;` after a definition at the end of the text is the same (`float x;;` and `void() g = {};;` at file level, where the file's loop tests for the end of the text only before a call). The flags hold from the token after the string, which `QCC_PR_Lex()` lexes once they are set, to the token after the block's last, which `QCC_PR_CheckToken("}")` or the definition's end lexes before they are restored: so in `extern "C" { float y; } string s = "\9";` the word `string` is lexed with `qcfuncs` off and `"\9"` with it on, and the definition `string` starts is read with the flags restored (FTEF-21.1), so `extern "C" int a; enum { A };` names a `float` enum. A file that ends in the block is "expected }" (`if (pr_token_type == tt_eof) { QCC_PR_Expect ("}"); break; }`). After another qualifier the string is no block (`const extern "C" {` is "\"C\" - not a name" after the warning of FTEF-21.10). In a body `QCC_PR_ParseStatement` reads `extern` exactly, or `local` and then `extern`, as a definition, so the block's definitions are locals, and `x = 1;` in it is no definition; a `typedef` in the block is a definition of it as at file level. A qualifier alone, `static;`, `const;` or `const *x;`, is a definition of an `int` of no name: the type is left out where the token after the qualifiers is no name (FTEF-19.21). The block is one level of nesting (FTEF-18.32). The parser lexes the text again with the blocks it read, and reports the lexical errors and warnings of the tokens they lex otherwise, in place of the preprocessor's.
**Withdrawn** (P2-06, #587): it listed `ifvector` and `vectorlogic` among the flags the semantic model does not read, but a condition's test reads them (FTEF-30.2). Replaced by FTEF-21.20.

A `break` that no loop or `switch` holds, a `continue` that no loop holds, and a `case` or `default` label that no `switch` holds, are counted (`num_breaks`, `num_continues`, `num_cases`) and left over at the function's end: "%s: function contains illegal breaks", "%s: function contains illegal continues" and "%s: function contains illegal cases" (`QCC_PR_ParseImmediateStatements`): `void() g = { break; };`, `{ continue; }`, `{ switch (1) { case 1: continue; } }`, `{ while (1) { } break; }`, `BREAK;` under `-Fcaseinsens`, `{ case 1: ; }`, `{ default: ; }`, `{ if (1) { case 1: ; } }` and `{ switch (1) { case 1: ; } case 2: ; }` are errors, a `break` in a `switch`, `loop` or `until`, a `continue` in a loop and a label in a `switch` are not. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseImmediateStatements`, `QCC_PR_ParseStatement`.

The flags a pragma may set mid-compile that no token, tree, definition or cast of the semantic model reads are not modelled, each for its reason: `nosave`'s default but for a typedef, and `optimise`, `opcode`, `iffloat`, `ifstring`, `nullemptystr`, `boundchecks`, `fastarrays`, `lo`, `reciprocal-math`, `allowuninit`, `omitinternals`, `embedsrc`, `dumpfilenames`, `annotate`, `brokenarray`, `rootconstructor` and `pythonlogic`, which the compiler's output reads (P2-06 onward); `msvcstyle`, `debugmacros` and `verbose`, which change only what FTEQCC prints; the target's `flag_pointerrelocs`, which `#pragma TARGET` sets with `QCC_OPCodeSetTarget` and only an initialiser that takes an address reads ("preinitialised pointer variables is disabled for this target", `QCC_PR_GenerateInitializerType`), an expression FTEF-19.63 leaves untyped; the dereference of a function `*f`, which `qcfuncs` makes "attempt to dereference function type." in `QCC_PR_RefTerm`, `vargtodouble`, and the `__int32` that `&&` and `||` of constants fold to under `assumeint`, the expression typing's and the compiler's; under `qccx` the field access `e^[f]` and `e[f]` of `QCC_PR_ParseField`, which only the expression's type, an entity's, tells from `^` and a vector or an index, so the parser reads the first as `^` and the second as an index, both accepted as FTEQCC accepts them; and `lax`, `typeexplicit`, `qccx` and `flag_undefwordsize` where an expression's operators, assignments, conditions and pointer arithmetic read them (`QCC_PR_Statement`'s "type mismatch for OP", `QCC_SupplyConversionForAssignment`, `QCC_PR_GenerateLogicalTruth`, `sizeof`), the expression typing's (P2-06).

With `qcfuncs` off a C function a body declares (FTEF-21.10) is defined by a body written with it, `void x() {}`, and needs none elsewhere; C's `(*name)(params)` there is a variable (`isvar |= isptr>0`), no function, so `float (*x)(float); x(1);` and `entity (*x)();` are accepted. After the `)` of `(*name)` the declarator's loop reads further parameter lists (`float (*x)(float)(float);`). A `const` C function pointer is both, "Conflicting constness." (`isconstant+isvar>1`), and a constant, a function needing a body. A function's parameters are those of the last list before its name when the type takes none, `void(float x) h = { x = 1; };`, and so for a struct's or a typedef's parameter type.

A function type whose first parameter's type is a name that is no type, through `*`s, makes `QCC_PR_ParseFunctionType` return none, and its caller the fatal error `E0204` "expected function arg list" (`if (!type) QCC_PR_ParseError(ERR_BADNOTTYPE, "expected function arg list");`): `void(foo a) g;`, `float (x);` and `typedef float (t);`; a later parameter's is `E0203` "\"foo\" is not a type", as a return type's is.

The illegal `break`, `continue` and `case` errors of FTEF-21.19 name the function, `QCC_PR_ParseError(ERR_ILLEGALCASES, "%s: function contains illegal cases", f->name)`, a member function's name being `CLASS::NAME`: `void() g = { break; };` is "g: function contains illegal breaks", once for the function however many it holds.

The `break`s and `continue`s FTEF-21.19 counts are those left in `num_breaks` and `num_continues` when the function ends, after an `if` arm of a constant condition is stripped (`QCC_UngenerateStatements(oldnumst)` forgets the `pr_breaks` and `pr_continues` at or after it): `if (0) { break; }` leaves none and is no error. The continues are checked before the breaks, each a fatal error. The function's name in its end-of-function messages, these and FTEF-34.6's "not all control paths return a value" and "contains unreachable code", is `pr_scope->name`, a member function's `CLASS::NAME`. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseImmediateStatements`, `QCC_UngenerateStatements`.

With `lax` on (`flag_laxcasts`, `#pragma flag enable lax`, `-Flax`) a cast `QCC_TryEvaluateCast` refuses is made by `QCC_EvaluateCast` with the warning `W0229` "Implicit lax cast from A to B" (`QCC_PR_ParseWarning(0, ...)`, warning 0, `WARN_DEBUGGING`, which no name sets and `-Werror` makes an error), in place of "Cannot cast" (`r.cast = cast; //decompilers suck`): `float x = "a";`, `void() g = 5;`, `.float fl = 1;`, `string s = '1 2 3';`, a default value `float a = "a"` and a local's initialiser cast so, and a strict enum's value too, `float x = E::A;` being "Implicit lax cast from enum E:float to float".

With `qccx` on `QCC_TryEvaluateCast` adds a float to an entity or a string, and an entity or a string to a float, to the casts "acceptable but probably an error" (`|| (totype == ev_entity && src.cast->type == ev_float && flag_qccx)` and the three like it), with `W0220`: `entity e = 1;`, `entity e = 1.5;`, `string s = 1;`, `float x = "a";` and a local entity or string initialising a float warn, where without it they are "Cannot cast". An integer to an entity warns either way, and a double to an entity and a string to a vector are refused either way. `-Fqccx` and `-std=qccx` also ignore F314 (FTEF-14.72), a `#pragma flag enable qccx` not.

An enum's value and a state frame are converted by `QCC_SupplyConversion(var, wanted, true)` to the enum's base type and to a float. `QCC_ShouldConvert` needs no conversion for a value of the kind, among the 32-bit and among the 64-bit integers, and for an integer to a function or a pointer; it converts among the numbers but between a double and a 32-bit integer, a float to a vector, and a pointer to a float or an integer to an integer or a float by what it points to; anything else none converts. With `typeexplicit` on any value that is not of the kind already is the error `E0236` "Automatic type conversions disabled. Needed A, got B." (`if (flag_typeexplicit)`, before the test for none, so `enum { A = 0i };`, `enum { A = '1 2 3' };` and `void() g = [1i, g] {};` are errors, and `enum { A = 1 };` is not); `QCC_EvaluateCast` reads no `typeexplicit`, so `float x = 1i;` compiles. A value none converts is the error `E0227` "Implicit type mismatch. Needed A, got B.", or with `lax` on the warning `W0230` of that text (`WARN_LAXCAST`, F314), the value kept as it is: an enum's name then has the value it would have had with no `=`, as `QCC_PR_ParseEnum` reads the value of a number only (`enum { A = "a", B };` makes `B` 1), and a frame of a cycle `[++ a .. b]` is then the error `E0238` "state type mismatch", once, after both frames are converted (`if (s1.cast->type != ev_float || def.cast->type != ev_float)`). `E0236` and `E0227` are fatal, so a state header's first one is its last word. A and B are `basictypenames`' (`integer`, `uint`, `long`, `ulong`, `double`), so under `assumeint` `enum { A = "a" };` is "Implicit type mismatch. Needed integer, got string.". A name's value is converted by its definition's type, before its constness is read, so a `string` constant initialising an enum's name is `E0227` and a variable `float` "is not a compile-time constant".

`QCC_OPCodeSetTarget` sets `flag_undefwordsize` to false, then to true for `QCF_DARKPLACES` only (`flag_undefwordsize = true; //DP insists on using word-aligned pointers`). It runs for each `#pragma TARGET` that names a target (`dp`, `darkplaces`, `dp_1`), at the token after it, and for each `-TNAME` among the command-line options, in their order, so `-Fundefwordsize -Tid` leaves it off and `-Tdp -Tfte` too, and `QCC_SetDefaultProperties` runs it for the standard target before the command line, also before the second autoprototyping pass, which so starts with it off; `-std=gmqcc` sets it, and `#pragma flag` and `-F` name it `undefwordsize`. With it on a string cast to a pointer is the non-fatal error `E0237` "pointer<->string casts were disabled." (`ERR_BADEXTENSION` given as a warning, FTEF-18) and the cast made, before the `char*` and `void*` casts of FTEF-19.31, so `void *p = "a";` is the error too; a pointer cast to a string is not, the C testing `totype == ev_pointer && src.cast->type == ev_string` twice. A `#pragma TARGET` that would switch to or from a Hexen II target after the first statement is ignored with a warning (`numstatements > 1`), which this profile does not model, statements being code generation's: it takes the target.

`QCC_PR_FinishCompilation` reads the target once every file is compiled: unless it is `QCF_FTE`, `QCF_FTEDEBUG` or `QCF_FTEH2`, each function an `extern` made at file level (`def->isextern`, an `extern` `QCC_PR_ParseDefs` kept, FTEF-21.10) is the error `E0239` "extern is not supported with this target format", at its definition. So `extern void(float x) h;` is the error under `-Tid`, and no error under `-Tfte` or after `#pragma target fte` anywhere in the module, the last target holding. It is reported definition by definition with the functions that have no body (QCD-3.11), and, as those are, also when the module has other errors, which FTEQCC's check (`if (pr_error_count) return false;`) never reaches (QCD-1.4); the outcome is the same. A module the semantic model reads without its preprocessing (`Db::module_index`) has no target and is not checked.

Each value is cast or converted with the flags at the token after it: FTEQCC casts it once `QCC_PR_Expression` has read it, which has lexed that token, and the pragmas before it with it (FTEF-21.1). So in `float x = "a"` then `#pragma flag enable lax` then `;` the cast is lax, and a `#pragma flag disable lax` before the next definition holds for it.

The cast family of `cargo xtask oracles builtins` (`xtask/src/oracles/builtins/casts.rs`) compiles programs that bind `f` and then make the casts and conversions of these statements and FTEF-19.31 under the FTEQCC profile, the flags set by `#pragma flag`, `#pragma target` and the command line, and those a warning decides with `-Werror -Wno-Q208`. Its run of 2026-10-22 (macOS arm64) agrees with the pinned FTEQCC on every case.

An implicit cast of a pointer to another pointer (`else if (totype == ev_pointer && src.cast->type == ev_pointer)`), but to or from `void*`, is silent when what the source points to, or a type it derives from (`t = t->parentclass`), is the target's pointee by `typecmp_lax`, and else `W0220` "Implicit cast": a struct is no float, so `S *ps; float *pf; pf = ps;` is "Implicit cast from struct S* to float*", and `float **` to `struct S*` warns too. Two functions are among the casts "acceptable but probably an error", which warn only when `typecmp_lax` tells them apart (`if (implicit && typecmp_lax(src.cast, cast))`): by their return types and the parameters both have, a parameter only one has unless it is `optional`, not by `...` (`typecmp_lax` reads `vargcount`, not `vargs`), so `void(float) f2; void(float, ...) f4; f2 = f4;` is silent and `f2 = f3;` of a `void(int)` is "Implicit cast from void(__int32) to void(float)". Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_TryEvaluateCast`.

The opcodes an operator may be given are the rows of `pr_opcodes[]` whose `name` is its spelling and whose priority class has the operator's priority, in the table's order: `QCC_PrioritiseOpcodes` lists each priority's rows in table order and sorts them by name with `qsort`, and `QCC_PR_RefExpression` starts at the first row of the spelling. The table has 413 rows before its `NULL` name, the opcode numbering, and every row's `opname` is the name `#pragma opcode` takes (FTEF-12). `sort_opcodenames` compares names only, so the order of a spelling's rows is the C library's `qsort`'s, which C leaves unspecified: glibc's keeps table order, and macOS's does not (the pinned FTEQCC on macOS arm64 takes `MUL_FI` as the first `*` row). The order decides only a tie of conversions (FTEF-23.4) and the row used after a mismatch; the semantic model takes table order, and the differential has no case whose outcome the order decides.

`QCC_NumericTypeRanking` ranks the numeric types `double` 15, `float` 10, `__uint64` 6, `__int64` 3, `__uint32` 1 and `__int32` 0 ("large gap, to try to de-prioritize the opcodes that mix float and int types"); every other type is unranked.

`QCC_canConv` gives the cost of converting a value to a basic type, after an accessor or a truth value is taken for its `parentclass`: 0 for the same type; 1 for a field holding the type, in a member function's body (`pr_classtype`); 2 for a constant 0 of an integer, float or pointer type (`QCC_SRef_IsNull`); between two ranked types `3 + (to - from)` up the ranking and `150 + (from - to)` down it; 9 to `variant` and 10 from it; 200 from a float to a vector and 201 from a vector to a float; else no conversion.

`QCC_PR_ChooseOpcode` takes, among the candidates of FTEF-23.1, the first needing no conversion, else the first needing fewest: for an ordinary operator the larger of the two operands' costs, and for an assignment the value's cost, the target's type having to be the row's `type_a` exactly, and for a pointer row what it points at too (`type_pointer` points at `__pointeraux`, a float). A member operator's row must also hold what the field holds. Before choosing, an operand that is a truth value is taken for its `parentclass`, and two operands of one enum type for the enum's base type. When no candidate can take the operands it is the error `E0302` "type mismatch for OP (A and B)", a warning `W0231` (`WARN_LAXCAST`) with `lax` on (FTEF-22.1), and the first candidate is used.

Once an opcode is chosen, an operand whose basic type is not the row's (and the row's is not `variant`) is converted to it, with the warning `W0232` "Implicit conversion from A to B" when the conversion costs 100 or more (FTEF-23.3), the left operand's before the right's: `v < v` for two vectors is `LT_F` with the warning twice, "Implicit conversion from vector to float". A, B are the types' names (`name`, not `TypeName`). The conversion is `QCC_EvaluateCast(operand, row_type, true)`, the implicit cast of FTEF-19.31 and FTEF-22 with its diagnostics: so a vector compared with `<` is then "Cannot cast from vector to float", and after a mismatch (FTEF-23.4) the first candidate's cast of each operand is made or refused, `s * a` for a string `s` being "Cannot cast from string to float" too, or under `lax` "Implicit lax cast".

A refused cast is `QCC_PR_ParseError`: FTEQCC stops the function, skips to the next `;` at file level and reads on from there as declarations. The semantic model, which recovers on its own (QCD-1.4), stops checking the statement and checks the next one; the module fails to compile either way.

A comparison's and a logical operator's value is of the opcode's result type, `type_bfloat` or `type_bint` (`EQ_F`, `NOT_F`, `AND_F`: `&type_bfloat`; `EQ_I`, `NOT_I`: `&type_bint`): a float of the name `__bfloat`, printed so (`string s = (f == 1);` is "Cannot cast from __bfloat to string"), and an `int` printed `__int32`; `_Bool` is `type_bint`, an `int` (`_Bool b; string s = b;` is "Implicit cast from __int32 to string").

`__bint` and `__bfloat` are both `ev_boolean` (`QCC_PR_NewType("__bint", ev_boolean, true)`), one type to `typecmp` and `typecmp_lax` and no other type's: `__bint b; __bfloat b;` redeclares nothing, `_Bool b; int b;` is "Type mismatch on redeclaration of b. __int32, should be __bint", `TypeName` printing `__bint`. A cast to either is `QCC_PR_GenerateLogicalTruth`'s `!=` with zero (`NE_F`, `NE_S`, `NE_E`, `NE_V`, `NE_FNC`, `NE_I` for integers and pointers, `NE_D`, `NE_I64`, `NE_U64`) then that value cast to the boolean's `parentclass`, with no message, implicit or explicit (`else if (totype == ev_boolean)`), and the value is of the parent type; `QCC_StoreSRefToRef` makes the truth again of a number stored into one. So on the id target `__bint c = 1.5;` folds with no overflow warning, `c = f;` and `c = s;` are two "ftoi emulation" warnings, `c = (_Bool)f;` three, and a local's initialiser `_Bool c = f;` one.

An operand converted to the chosen row's type is the cast's result (`QCC_EvaluateCast(lhsd, (*op->type_a), true)`), of the row's type, so the opcode's own checks read that type: a null constant, which converts to any type (FTEF-23.3), compared with a string, an entity or a field is no "'==' type mismatch" (FTEF-28.2): `s == __NULL__`, `e == 0i` and `fld == 0` warn of nothing. An operand of the row's basic type keeps its own type, a class's among them. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_RefExpression`, `QCC_EvaluateCast`.

A value made a boolean, cast to one or stored to one (`QCC_StoreSRefToRef`'s `dest->cast->type == ev_boolean`), is always `QCC_PR_GenerateLogicalTruth`'s comparison, a boolean value too, which it reads as its parent type: on the id target `b = b;` of a `_Bool b` is `OP_NE_I`'s emulation and two "ftoi emulation: denormals are unsafe", and `b = (_Bool)i;` three. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_GenerateLogicalTruth`, `QCC_TryEvaluateCast`, `QCC_StoreSRefToRef`.

Under `lax` a `void` value made a boolean warns "cast to boolean" (`QCC_PR_GenerateLogicalTruth`'s `t == ev_void && flag_laxcasts`, its message given whole) and is `OP_NE_F` against 0: `bb = (_Bool)vf();` of a `void() vf` is that warning, then on the id target three "ftoi emulation". Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_GenerateLogicalTruth`.

On an entity the selector is read as a value with no member expansion (`QCC_PR_ParseRefValue(..., expandmemberfields false)`), or the expression in parentheses after `.`: a field's member is the value it holds, a `variant`'s a `variant`; any other definition is the error `E0318` "NAME is not a field", or "NAME is not a field of class CLASS" when the entity's type is a class (`t->parentclass`).

On a vector `x`, `y` and `z`, or `r`, `g` and `b`, are its components, floats; on a `.vector` field they are `.float` fields (`type_floatfield`). `w` and `a` need a fourth component a vector does not have (`t->size >= 4`), and any other name is the error `E0314` "unsupported vector swizzle '.NAME'".
On a string, `length` is the string's length, an `int`, when the string is a constant, else the error `E0316` "not a constant"; any other name is `E0315` "unsupported string method NAME".
On a struct or union, and on a field of one, the member found in it or its parents (`QCC_PR_FindStructMember`, FTEF-6.11); on a field the member is a field of the member's type (`QCC_PR_FieldType`).
Through a pointer, the member of the struct or union it points at; a pointer to any other type is the error `E0317` "indirection in TYPE - not a struct or union".

On an entity in a body, a member no definition has is made by `QCC_PR_GetSRef(type_variant, name, pr_scope, true, ...)`, a `variant`, and reported with `QCC_PR_ParseWarning(ERR_UNKNOWNVALUE, ...)`, an error that does not end the statement: `E0319` "Unknown field \"NAME\" in class \"CLASS\"", CLASS `entity` for a plain entity and the class for a class's value. The member's value is a `variant`. A class's member is looked up as `CLASS::NAME` in the base's class and its parents, so it is a field of the member's type on a value of the class or one derived from it, and unknown on any other entity: `e.m_a` for a plain `entity e` and a member `m_a` of a class is "Unknown field \"m_a\" in class \"entity\"", whatever the resolver's name lookup (FTEF-17.3) offers for navigation.

Messages print a type as `TypeName` (`qcc_pr_lex.c`) does: a class `class NAME` (an entity type with a `parentclass`), and a field of a class too, the class branch writing over the field's `.`; a struct or union `struct NAME` or `union NAME`; a strict enum `enum NAME:BASE`; a pointer `T*`; a field `.T`; any other type by its name. A function type prints each parameter as `[inout ][optional ]TYPE[ NAME][ = DEFAULT]`, then `...` when it is variadic: the default as `QCC_VarAtOffset` prints the constant, a float `%gf` (`2f`, `0.5f`), an integer `%#xi` (`0x3i`), a vector `'%g %g %g'`, a string quoted. The names are kept beside the types for messages and never tell two types apart (QC-10.10).

An array's only member is `length`, an `int`, the array's size (`QCC_PR_Expect ("length")` after an array's `.`, FTE-13); `LightStyles.length` for an array of strings is the array's length, not the string's.

A member no definition has that names a value FTEQCC declares as it reads it, an intrinsic (`randomv`, `alloca`, `entnum`, `autocvar`, `used_model`, `used_sound`, `va_arg`, `_`, `random`) or `nil`, is that value and no field: the fatal error `E0318` "NAME is not a field", `nil` printed as its constant's name, "IMMEDIATE is not a field".

`QCC_PR_ParseField` reads `.` only after an entity, a value of a type with accessor members, a vector, a `.vector` field, a string, a struct or union, a pointer or a class; after a value of any other type the expression ends before the `.`. The statement goes on with the value it has, `b = a` of `b = a.x + 1` stored with its casts and conversions, and then the `.` is the fatal error `E0204` "expected ;, found ."; inside parentheses, a call's arguments or an index the construct expects its own token at once, "expected ), found .". A fatal error before it, as "Cannot cast from .float to float" for `b = fl.x`, is reported instead.

Some messages print a type by its own name, `type->name`, not by `TypeName`: a pointer a declaration makes is `ptr` (`QCC_PointerTypeTo`), and an array's address `T*` (`QCC_PR_PointerType`); a function `__function` (`type_function->name`); a field `.` and its type's own name (`QCC_PR_FieldType`); a struct, union, class or enum its name with no keyword or base (`s` for `struct s`); any other type by its name. `float *p; void() g = { return p; };` is "'g' returned ptr, expected void".

A named union is made `ev_struct` (`QCC_PR_ParseStruct`, `newt = QCC_PR_NewType(tname, ev_struct, true)`), so `TypeName` prints it as `struct NAME`; a struct or union with no tag is `struct <struct>` or `union <union>` (`QCC_PR_NewType(structtype==ev_union? "<union>":"<struct>", structtype, false)`); and a field of a struct or union prints its own name, `.NAME`.

A typedef of a class is the class (`QCC_TypeForName` gives the typedef's real type), so a value of it has the class's members, and a member it lacks is "Unknown field \"NAME\" in class \"CLASS\"", CLASS the class's own name: `class C { float f; }; typedef C T; T t;` reads `t.f`, and `t.zz` names `C`. A class a typedef writes, `typedef class C2 { float f; } T;`, is declared with it.

A parameter's default prints as `QCC_VarAtOffset` prints a constant of the parameter's type: a float `%gf`, a double `%gd`, an `int` `%#xi`, a `uint` `%#xu`, an `__int64` `%#xill` and an `__uint64` `%#xull` of its bits (C writes `0` for zero, so `0u`), a vector `'%g %g %g'` whatever form it was written in (`[1, 2, 3]` is `'1 2 3'`), a string quoted.

A member of a class declared (`class C;`) but never defined, which has no `parentclass`, is the error `E0371` "Class \"C\" is not defined, cannot access member \"NAME\"" (`QCC_PR_ParseRefValue`: `else if (!assumeclass->parentclass && assumeclass != type_entity)`) in place of FTEF-24.6's "Unknown field"; once the class is defined its unknown member is that error again. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseRefValue`.

After an entity's `.`, a selector that names a class's member through its class, `e.CLASS::name` or `e.(CLASS::name)`, is the global `CLASS::name`, the member function's own body even for a `virtual` one, called with the entity as `self` (`REF_NONVIRTUAL`, for a `REF_GLOBAL` whose name has `::`): "too many parameters on call to C::random" names it, and no "is not a field of class" is given. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseField`.

`QCC_OPCodeSetTarget(format, revision)` holds the revision to the format's highest (6614 for the FTE formats, 20250104 for DarkPlaces, 0 for QSS and the rest) and sets every opcode valid or not by `QCC_OPCodeValidForTarget`. It runs for the command line's last `-T` option, else for the standard format at revision 0, and again at each `#pragma TARGET` that names a target, with the revision after `_` or the row's default (5768 for `fte`, 12901 for `dp`). So a `#pragma TARGET` undoes every `#pragma opcode` before it.

`QCC_OPCodeValidForTarget`: no opcode from `OP_NUMREALOPS` (282) on is valid. The standard, KK7 and QTest formats have the opcodes before `OP_MULSTORE_F`; Hexen II's have those up to `OP_CALL8H` but `OP_SWITCH_V` to `OP_SWITCH_FNC`; the FTE formats have all of them by revision: `OP_PUSH` and those from `OP_STOREP_I16` from 6614, those from `OP_LT_U` from 5768, from `OP_STOREP_I8` from 5744, from `OP_STOREF_V` from 5698, from `OP_IF_F` from 3349 and the rest always; QSS has id's and a list of integer, conditional, field-store, array and Hexen II call opcodes; DarkPlaces has id's, its shifts and unsigned opcodes from revision 20250104, its pointer loads from 20241108, eight opcodes it once got wrong from 12901 and a list of integer and global-array opcodes always.

`#pragma opcode enable NAME...` (or `on`) makes each named opcode valid, and `disable` (or `off`) not, in order, the names an `opname` in any case; an internal one is "opcode NAME is internal" and changes nothing, and an unknown one "opcode NAME not recognised" (FTEF-12). The change holds from the token after the pragma.
A number literal's value is `QCC_PR_LexNumber`'s: its digits accumulated in a 64-bit integer that wraps, the sign applied, then held to the literal's type (FTEF-3); a fraction read with `atof`.

With both operands constant, the logic, bitwise, shift, arithmetic, comparison and 64-bit opcodes fold to a constant of the opcode's result, reading each operand's words as the opcode's operand type (a float's word read as an `int` is its bits). A float division by 0 is "Division of %g by 0" (an `int` dividend "%d"), an integer one "Division by constant 0" and 0, `INT_MIN / -1` "Signed overflow on division by -1" and `INT_MAX`; a remainder by 0 is not folded. A float operand of a bitwise or shift opcode that is not a whole number is "Constant float operand %f will be truncated to %i".

With only the left operand constant: the unary opcodes and conversions fold, a conversion that loses the value being "Numerical overflow. %f will be rounded to %i", for a float with a zero exponent "Denormalized float %g will be rounded to %i. This is probably not what you want.", or "Numerical truncation of %#x to %#x."; the 64-bit and double conversions (`OP_CONV_FI64`, `OP_CONV_DI64`, `OP_CONV_FU64`, `OP_CONV_DU64` and back) fold the same way, with "Numerical overflow" for any fraction lost and "Numerical truncation" as `%#llx`, so `__int64 x; x = 1.5;` warns and `x = 1;` folds; `0 + b`, `0 | b` and `1 * b` are `b`; `0 & b` and a shift of 0 are 0; a false left operand of `&&` is 0 and a true one of `||` 1, as floats.

With only the right operand constant: `a + 0`, `a - 0`, `a | 0`, `a * 1` and `a / 1` are `a`, and `a & ~0` for integers; a division by a constant 0 is "Division by 0"; a false right operand of `&&` is 0. `||` never folds here: `QCC_Eval_Truth(eval_a, ...)` reads the absent left constant, which is false.
**Withdrawn** (P2-07, #63): it said a `length` is a constant whose value the semantic model does not keep, but the model keeps an array's size when it knows it. Replaced by FTEF-26.13.

An unsigned division folds with no check of its divisor (`eval_a->_uint / eval_b->_uint`), a 0 divisor giving 0 as arm64's `udiv` does. A remainder by a constant 0, which is not folded (FTEF-26.2), is emulated as `a - b * (a / b)` in that order (FTEF-27.4), its steps folding in turn, so `13i % 0i` is 13 (`13 / 0` is 0 with "Division by constant 0", ignored by default) and `13.5 % 0.0` is 13 with the truncation warnings of `inf | inf`.

A folded `OP_CONV_FTOI` is `QCC_MakeIntConst(eval_a->_float)`, the float made a `long long` (saturating on arm64) and then an `int`: when the two differ, after the overflow warning, it is `W0234` "Constant int operand %llu will be truncated to %i", the `long long` printed unsigned and the value its low 32 bits. So `i = 1i / 0;` folds `1 / 0.0` to `inf`, warns "Numerical overflow. inf will be rounded to 2147483647" and then "Constant int operand 9223372036854775807 will be truncated to -1", and stores -1.

A folded `OP_CONV_I64I` keeps the low 32 bits (`pint_t d = eval_a->i64;`) and, when they are not the value, warns `W0234` "Numerical truncation of %llx to %#x.", the 64-bit value in hex with no prefix and the 32 bits with C's `%#x` (`0` for 0): `i = 5000000000l;` is "Numerical truncation of 12a05f200 to 0x2a05f200.". Under `ILP32` the `l` literal is 32 bits (FTEF-12.12) and there is nothing to convert.

Two constant doubles fold as C computes them: `OP_ADD_D`, `OP_SUB_D`, `OP_MUL_D` and `OP_DIV_D` to a double with no check of a 0 divisor; `OP_LE_D`, `OP_LT_D`, `OP_EQ_D` and `OP_NE_D` to an `int`; `OP_LSHIFT_DI` and `OP_RSHIFT_DI` shift the double made a `long long` (`(pint64_t)eval_a->_double << eval_b->_int`), and `OP_BITAND_D`, `OP_BITOR_D` and `OP_BITXOR_D` combine both made `long long`s, each result made a double again. `OP_RSHIFT_U64I` shifts the unsigned 64-bit value. `OP_BITEXTEND_I` and `OP_BITEXTEND_U` of two constants are `(a << (32 - bits - ofs)) >> (32 - bits)`, signed and unsigned, `bits` and `ofs` the low byte and the rest of the second. So `arr[(__double)2.5 * 2]` is index 5.

A logical not of a constant folds (`QCC_PR_StatementFlags`, `a is const, b is not`): `OP_NOT_F` and `OP_NOT_V` to the float 1 when the value, or every component, is 0, `OP_NOT_ENT` and `OP_NOT_FNC` of the word, and `OP_NOT_I` to the `int` 1 or 0, before any emulation: on the id target `!1i` is 0 with no "Result of comparison is constant" of an emulated `OP_EQ_FNC`.

A function's definition is a constant whose value no opcode's folding reads, so an opcode of it is emitted, or emulated where the target lacks it, as a variable's is: on the id target `b = (_Bool)fn;` of a `void() fn` is the `OP_NE_FNC` truth and three "ftoi emulation", as of an entity. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_StatementFlags`, `QCC_SRef_EvalConst`.

A value is a constant when it is a literal, a folded result, or a definition that is constant and initialised (`QCC_SRef_EvalConst`), an enum's item and a `length` among them. An array's `length` is its size when the model knows it (FTEF-24.8), an `int`. A constant whose value the semantic model does not keep (an integer constant's initialiser, kept as text, an enum's item, a string's `length`, an array's whose size the model does not know) decides nothing it checks: no folding, no emulation.

A constant operand that an opcode's row converts is the constant its conversion folds to (`QCC_SupplyConversion` emits the conversion opcode, folded as FTEF-26.3 says), so the opcode then folds too: in `(__double)2.5 * 2` the float 2 is converted by `OP_CONV_FD` to the double 2, and `OP_MUL_D` folds.
An opcode the target has is emitted with no diagnostic: on the FTE target the integer and string opcodes, on the standard target id's.

An integer, power or vector remainder opcode calls a helper the program defines before the function, found by name in the function's scope or the globals (`AddInt`, `SubInt`, `MulInt`, `DivInt`, `BitandInt`, `BitorInt`, `ModVec`, `powf` then `pow`, and for `~int` `SubInt`); with none it is the warning `W0235` "NAME function not defined: cannot emulate WHAT" and refused (FTEF-27.5), a power's naming `pow` ("pow function not defined: cannot emulate int*^int"). A mixed integer and float opcode converts its integer operand (`OP_CONV_ITOF`) and emits the float opcode; an integer comparison converts its left operand and emits the mixed one; `==` and `!=` of integers and fields are `OP_EQ_FNC` and `OP_NE_FNC`. The unsigned opcodes are the signed ones, the 64-bit unsigned the 64-bit signed; `OP_EQ_I64` and `OP_NE_I64` compare the two words; the 64-bit bitwise opcodes and loads are emitted as statements of the 32-bit ones with no check of the target.

`OP_ADD_SF` calls `AddStringFloat` when defined; else, for a string that is no constant, it is the warning `W0236` "OP_ADD_SF: string+float may be unsafe", then the float is converted to an integer and added with `OP_ADD_I`. `OP_ADD_SI` and `OP_ADD_IS` warn "OP_ADD_SI: string+int may be unsafe" and add with `OP_ADD_I`. An entity plus a float, unless `qccx` is on, converts the float and adds with `OP_ADD_EI`, which needs the `nextent` builtin ("the nextent builtin is not defined" and refused) and then subtracts with `OP_SUB_I` (`(op == &pr_opcodes[OP_ADD_EF]) ? OP_ADD_I : OP_SUB_I`, never `OP_ADD_EF` there). `<=>` of strings needs `strcmp`, else the fatal error `E0321`.

A conversion folds a constant (FTEF-26.3); else it calls `itof`, `ftoi`, or for `OP_CONV_UF` `utof`, `quake_utof`, `itof` or `quake_itof`, when defined; else it is the warning `W0237` "itof emulation: denormals are unsafe NAME" (NAME the symbol's, `var_a.sym->name`: the value's definition, `IMMEDIATE` for an immediate, and for a temporary `temp_N`, N its slot in `QCC_GetTemp`'s temporaries, which `opt_overlaptemps` reuses; the semantic model does not follow the slots and prints the temporary's type name, `__int32`, where FTEQCC prints `temp_0`) or "ftoi emulation: denormals are unsafe", F313, an error by default, or for `OP_CONV_UF` `W0238` "utof emulation: will break if NAME is big". `%` with no `mod` (or `ModInt`) function is expanded into division, `|`, multiplication and subtraction; `^` into `~`, `&` and `|`; `v / f` into `1 / f` and `OP_MUL_VF`. An integer shift with no `LShiftInt`, `RShiftInt` or `RShiftUInt` is a product or quotient by the constant `QCC_MakeIntConst(1<<n)`, so a shift by 0 folds away, or by `2 *^ n` for a variable `n`; `>>` of an integer tests the sign (`OP_LT_I` against `QCC_MakeFloatConst(0)`), divides the complement (`OP_BITNOT_I`, the division, `OP_BITNOT_I`) and then divides the value itself as a `QCC_PR_SimpleStatement`, which refuses a division the target lacks with the fatal error `E0320` (FTEF-6.14): `i >> 2` ends with "Opcode \"/|DIV_I\" not valid for target". A float shift is the integer one on converted operands when the target has it, else `floor(a * pow(2, b))` when `powf` or `pow` and `floor` are defined, else `bitshift`, else "bitshift function not defined: cannot emulate OP_LSHIFT_F*" and refused.

An opcode FTEQCC does not emulate is refused, `badopcode`: the error `E0320` "Opcode \"OP|NAME\" not valid for target. Consider the use of: #pragma target fte" when the FTE target at its default revision (5768) has it, "... #pragma target fte_6614" when only the newest revision has it, else "Opcode \"OP|NAME\" is not supported.", OP the operator and NAME the opcode's `opname`. It is reported with `QCC_PR_ParseWarning(ERR_BADEXTENSION, ...)` and does not end the statement.
`&&` and `||` are `OP_AND_F` and `OP_OR_F` when the target has no other logic opcode for their operands.

The unsigned, 64-bit and double opcodes the target lacks: `<` and `<=` of unsigned values are the float comparisons of `OP_CONV_UF`'s conversions when the target has no `OP_LT_I`, else the signed ones of the values less `0x80000000`; `>` and `>=` of unsigned, 64-bit and double values are `<` and `<=` of the operands swapped; unsigned division warns `W0235` "OP_DIV_U emulation: assuming the high bit is not set..." and divides as signed; a sign or zero extension of a constant width and offset is two shifts, of any other refused; `&` and `|` of doubles are the 64-bit integer ones between conversions (`OP_CONV_DI64`, `OP_CONV_I64D`); `^` of vectors and doubles is `(a & ~b) | (b & ~a)`; a shift of a double converts it to a 64-bit integer first; `!` of an integer is `OP_EQ_FNC` with 0.

A cast of an operand to its opcode's type (FTEF-23.5) emits the conversion opcodes `QCC_TryEvaluateCast` names for the pair of types, in order: `OP_CONV_UF` for an unsigned value made a float, `OP_CONV_ITOF` for an integer, `OP_CONV_FTOI` back, the double and 64-bit conversions, two of them for a double and a 32-bit integer; each is folded, emitted or emulated in turn. With no `utof`, `quake_utof`, `itof` or `quake_itof`, `OP_CONV_UF` is `OP_CONV_ITOF`, with its warning, then "utof emulation: will break if NAME is big".

Some opcodes are replaced by another, `op = OTHER; break;`, which is emitted with no check of the target, no folding and no helper: the compound stores (`OP_ADDSTORE_F` and the rest, their operands swapped), `OP_STORE_P` and `OP_STORE_I` as `OP_STORE_F`, `OP_LOAD_P` and `OP_LOAD_I` as `OP_LOAD_F`, `OP_STOREP_P` as `OP_STOREP_I`, `~` of a float, vector or 64-bit value as a subtraction from -1, and the pointer comparisons as the entity or integer ones, so `p > q` of pointers on the standard target warns of nothing. `&` and `|` of vectors are three float statements emitted the same way. A bit clear, `a &~ b`, is the target's clearing opcode when it has one, else `a & b` emitted in turn and a subtraction replacing it. A float or string tested by an `if` is compared with 0 (`OP_NE_F`, `OP_NE_S`) and tested as an integer. The commented-out mixed stores (`OP_ADDSTORE_IF` and the like) and the pointer stores under `IAMNOTLAZY`, which the pinned source does not define, are refused (FTEF-27.5).

Pointer arithmetic scales the offset by what the pointer points at: a float offset is first converted to an integer; for `void` it is bytes (`OP_ADD_I`, `OP_SUB_I`), for an 8- or 16-bit type bytes times its width, and for any other type the offset times its size in words is added by `OP_ADD_PIW`, which, emulated, multiplies by `VMWORDSIZE` (4) and adds. A subtraction's size is negated as an unsigned value, `QCC_MakeIntConst(-aux_type->size)`, so it is always the warning `W0234` "Constant int operand 4294967295 will be truncated to -1" (for a size of 1). The difference of two pointers of different types by `typecmp` is the fatal error `E0327` "incompatible pointer types"; of one type it is their byte difference divided by the size. Under `undefwordsize` each assumption is the error `E0326` ("void* maths was disabled.", "pointer* maths was disabled on this type.", "pointer sizes were marked as undefined.", "Making assumptions about pointer sizes was blocked."). A load of 8 or 16 bits reads the word that holds it and shifts; a word load calls `memgetval`, else `W0235` "memgetval function not defined: cannot emulate OP_LOADP_*" and refused. A struct or union pointed at is sized by its layout (FTEF-6.13), so `p + 1` for a `struct S { float a; vector v; } *p` scales by 4 and `p - 1` warns "Constant int operand 4294967292 will be truncated to -4"; a struct whose layout the model does not follow decides no folding and gives no truncation warning.

Some opcodes the target lacks are emitted as plain statements (`QCC_PR_SimpleStatement`), which `QCC_PR_StatementFlags`'s global-scope check never sees: a 64-bit `&`, `|` and `^` as two `OP_BITAND_I`, `OP_BITOR_I` or `OP_BITXOR_I`, a 64-bit field load as two `OP_LOAD_FLD`, each refused on a target without it by the fatal error `E0320` (`force` off); a vector's `&` and `|` as three float ones with `force` on, never refused. So `d & e` of doubles on the id target is the two `OP_CONV_DI64` refusals and then `OP_BITAND_I`'s, which ends the statement before `OP_CONV_I64D`.

An opcode emulated as another (`return QCC_PR_StatementFlags(OTHER, ...)`) gives the other's result, of the other's type: `OP_EQ_I` is `OP_EQ_FNC` and `OP_AND_I` is `OP_AND_F`, so `b = (i == j);` and `b = (i && j);` of ints store a float with no conversion. An unsigned operator emulated by its signed one then casts the result back (`var_c.cast = type_uint;` or `type_uint64`), a comparison's included: `b = !ul;` of a `__uint64` on the id target needs `OP_CONV_U64F`, refused with `E0320`.

`OP_EQ_I64` and `OP_NE_I64` compare word by word: the operands cast to `int`, `OP_EQ_I` (or `OP_NE_I`) of the low words, then of the high words, joined by `OP_AND_I` (or `OP_OR_I`), each emitted or emulated in turn. Each word's comparison gives FTEF-28.1's warnings, so `l == l` of an `__int64` warns "Result of comparison is constant" twice.

A prefix `++` or `--` of a pointer adds `QCC_MakeIntConst(preinc * aux_type->size)` by `OP_ADD_PIW`, the size in words of what it points at, 1 for `void`. The size is unsigned, so `--` adds its negation and warns as FTEF-27.10's subtraction: `--p` of a `vector *` is `W0234` "Constant int operand 4294967293 will be truncated to -3", and on the id target both steps are then `OP_ADD_I`'s helper warning and refusal.

The emulated signed right shift tests its value's sign and jumps: `QCC_Generate_OP_IFNOT` of the `OP_LT_I` against 0 skips the negative form, which `QCC_Generate_OP_GOTO` ends before the positive one. At global scope each jump is a statement too, "Unable to generate statements at global scope (IFNOT)." after the comparison's and "(GOTO)." after the negative form's, as `float q = c;` of an `__int8 c` on the id target gives in the extension of its bits (FTEF-2.12). Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_StatementFlags` (`OP_RSHIFT_I`).

A statement's result is a temporary, named `temp_N` by its word offset among the temporaries (`QCC_GetTemp`): under `opt_overlaptemps`, on by default, the first one no reference holds of the result's size (1 word, 3 for a vector, 2 for a 64-bit value), else a new one after the last; a statement frees its operands' first (`QCC_FreeTemp`), a refused opcode's too (`badopcode`), and a store, a jump or a `void` opcode takes none. The emulation warnings name an operand by `sym->name`, so a temporary's is `temp_N`, as `QCC_VarAtOffset` prints it; the other messages name it by `QCC_GetSRefName`, its type's name (FTEF-27.4). So on the id target `x = c8;` of an `__int8 c8` is "itof emulation: denormals are unsafe temp_0", the `OP_MUL_I` of its shift's result, and `s[i] += x;` of a string's character `temp_1`. FTEQCC keeps the temporaries across the module and those a statement leaves referenced; this profile frees them all at each statement's end, so in a later function a number can differ. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_GetTemp`, `QCC_FreeTemp`, `QCC_PR_StatementFlags`, `QCC_VarAtOffset`.

**Withdrawn** (#84): it said a function's definition is no constant symbol to the comparison warnings; it is one, and a comparison of types `typecmp_lax` tells apart gives no warning, which FTEF-28.4 says, replacing it.
**Withdrawn** (#84): it said a comparison of operands of different basic types is "'OP' type mismatch: A with B"; the warning is never given, and FTEF-28.3 replaces it.

A comparison never warns "'OP' type mismatch: A with B", even with F307 on. When `typecmp_lax(var_a.cast, var_b.cast)` tells the operands apart, the check walks `var_a`'s parents, `for (t = var_a.cast; t; t = t->parentclass) if (typecmp_lax(t, var_b.cast)) break;`, which stops at the first type that differs, `var_a.cast` itself, and `if (t) break;` then leaves before the warning, as the walk of `var_b`'s parents would. So `!u` of a `__uint` and `!p` of a pointer, emulated on the id target as `OP_EQ_FNC` with an `int` 0, warn of nothing, nor do `.float == .vector` or `float() != void()`. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_StatementFlags` (the `OP_EQ_F` to `OP_GT_F` cases).

`OP_AND_F` with one symbol on both sides is "Parameter offsets for && are the same", and with both constant "Result of comparison is constant"; `OP_OR_F` with one symbol is "Parameters for || are the same", and with either constant "Result of comparison is constant". A comparison whose operands' types `typecmp_lax` tells apart leaves the switch before its constant check (FTEF-28.3) and warns of nothing. Any other with both operands constant symbols (`sym->constant && !sym->temp`), or, unless it is a float or vector equality, `<=` or `>=`, with one symbol on both sides, is "Result of comparison is constant": `s == s`, `e == e`, `a < a` and `"x" == "y"` are, `a == a` is not, and two constants of a float comparison fold first (FTEF-26.2). A function's and a field's definitions are constant symbols, so `fn == fn2` of two `void()` and `fl == fl2` of two `.float` warn, where `ff != fn` of a `float()` and a `void()` and `fl == fv` of a `.float` and a `.vector` do not. A null constant converted for the opcode is a constant of the row's type with no statement, `type_function` a `void()` and `type_field` a `.void`: `fn == 0` warns, `ff == 0` and `fl == 0` do not. A `case` value supplied for a function or pointer switch keeps its `int` type (`QCC_ShouldConvert` gives 0), so `switch (ff) { case 1i: }` warns of nothing; any other operand converted for the opcode is a temporary. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_StatementFlags`, `QCC_TryEvaluateCast`, `QCC_SupplyConversion`.

Before the right side is read, an assignment to the result of a postfix `++` or `--` is the fatal error `E0322` "Assignment to post-inc result", and one to a read-only reference the warning `W0241` "Assignment to const". `1 = a`, `~a = 1`, `(a + 1) = 2` and `(a = 2) = 3` are each warned, not refused.

`=` casts the value to the left side's type (`QCC_EvaluateCast(rhs, lhs, true)`, FTEF-19.31), so a value of another type is "Cannot cast from A to B" (`E0213`), a fatal error, and an array named bare is a pointer to its elements: `arr = 1` is "Cannot cast from float to float*". A compound assignment takes the first opcode of its list (`opcodes_addstore` and the others) whose operands are the left side's and the value's basic types, an array named bare its address (`arr += 1` is `ADD_PF`, then FTEF-29.3's "left operand must be an l-value"); with none, the value is cast to the left side's type and the list searched again; with none still it is the fatal error `E0323` "Type mismatch on assignment. A OP B is not supported" (`s += s`), A and B the types' own names (FTEF-24.11), B the left side's when the cast changed the value's type (`ptr *= ptr` for `p *= v` under `lax`, `float* += ptr` for `arr += p`). A field or pointer updated by an in-place opcode the target has (`opcodes_addstorep` and the others) is checked no further.

The store (`QCC_StoreSRefToRef`) to a read-only reference warns `W0241` "Assignment to constant NAME", NAME as `QCC_GetSRefName` gives it (FTEF-27.4), and to an array named bare is "left operand must be an l-value (did you mean NAME[0]?)" (`E0325`). An assignment's value is the value stored, read-only, so `(a = 2) = 3` warns "Assignment to constant IMMEDIATE".

A compound assignment's opcode is emitted (FTEF-27), and its result converted for the store by `QCC_SupplyConversionForAssignment`: an explicit cast (`QCC_TryEvaluateCast` with `implicit` off, which also casts between an entity and a float), else `QCC_ShouldConvert`'s conversion; with none it is the fatal error `E0324` "Implicit type mismatch on assignment to NAME. Needed A, got B." (under `typeexplicit` for any conversion), or under `lax` the warning `W0243`. `a *= v` of a float and a vector is the error: `OP_MUL_FV` gives a vector.

A postfix `++` or `--` of a read-only value is the fatal error `E0322` "postincrement: lhs is readonly" or "postdecrement: lhs is readonly". Otherwise the result is marked as a postfix's, a temporary that messages name by its type (`QCC_GetSRefName`), and the operand is read and updated by adding 1 or -1 (`--` adds -1; `QCC_RefToDef`, or `QCC_PR_DiscardRef` for a value discarded: a statement's expression, a `for` header's first or last clause, a comma's left side), by its basic type: `OP_ADD_F` of a float, `OP_ADD_D` of a double, `OP_ADD_I` of an int for an integer and for a string, `OP_ADD_U` for a uint, `OP_ADD_I64` and `OP_ADD_U64` of an int64; a pointer by `OP_ADD_PIW` of the step times the size in words of what it points at (a word for `void`), or for `__int8` and `__int16` (`aux_type->bits`) by `OP_ADD_I` of the step in bytes, which under `undefwordsize` a value not discarded first makes the fatal error `E0322` "not allowed to make assumptions about pointer sizes. sorry."; any other type (a vector, an entity) is the fatal error `E0322` "post increment operator not supported with this type". A bitfield that does not start its word is first "post increment operator on bitfield"; one that does, and an 8- or 16-bit integer (FTEF-2.12), is read, then "not supported" when its value is used (`ref->cast` is `ev_bitfld`) and stepped as the integer it is read as when discarded. Each opcode is emitted as FTEF-27 says, and the sum stored back as an assignment's (FTEF-29.7, FTEF-6.15): `s++` warns "type mismatch: __int32 __int32 to string s".

An assignment that is the whole condition of an `if`, `while`, `do` or `for`, not parenthesised (`a = 1 && a` is one, `a = (1 && a)`), warns `W0242` "suggest parenthesis for assignment used as truth value" after its right side is read; `if ((a = 1))` does not.

The store checks the value's type against the left side's: unless the value is null, or its type or a parent's is the left side's by `typecmp_lax`, or either is a `variant`, or the value is a `void*` or `variant*` stored into a pointer, a number is converted to the left side's type (`QCC_SupplyConversion`) and anything else is the warning `W0240` "type mismatch: A NAME to B TARGET", TARGET `base.field` for a field. A cast, `lax` included, gives the value the left side's type first, so only a compound assignment's result kept under `lax` (FTEF-29.4) reaches the warning: `a *= v` is "type mismatch: vector vector to float a".

Two names are given to a target. A compound assignment's "Implicit type mismatch on assignment to NAME" and a call's "argument NAME will be ignored" name it by `QCC_GetRefName`: `base.field`, `base[index]` for an element or a string's character, the index `IMMEDIATE` for a constant (`arr[IMMEDIATE]`), `base->index` through a pointer, `TEMP` for no index (`p->TEMP` for `*p`), and the base's name for anything else, an accessor's member included (its branch writes the member's name, then `break`s and returns the base's). The store's "type mismatch" names it as `QCC_StoreSRefToRef` does (FTEF-29.7): `base.field`, `base[index]` but for an `IMMEDIATE` index, else the base.

A constant that is null (`QCC_SRef_IsNull`, an integer, float or pointer 0) casts as a null whatever its definition's type, a `typedef` or `int` one included: `const int zi = 0; string s = zi;` is no cast warning.

So is a global's initialiser that names a constant whose word is 0 (`QCC_SRef_IsNull`): `enum { H }; string s = H;` and `const float z = 0; string s2 = z;` are no error, where a constant 1 is "Cannot cast from float to string"; a struct or union takes no null ("Cannot cast from float to struct S"), and a strict enum's value casts to no other type whatever it is (FTEF-19.10).

A compound assignment or an increment of an array named bare, after its "left operand must be an l-value (did you mean NAME[0]?)" (FTEF-29.3), frees the head a second time: `QCC_StoreSRefToRef` has discarded the reference it read (`QCC_PR_DiscardRef`), and the operator frees it again, `W0319` "INTERNAL: over-freed refcount to NAME" (`QCC_FreeTemp`). So `farr += 1;`, `farr++`, `++farr` and `farr--` of a `float farr[3]` under `#pragma target fte` give both, a local array's too, and the plain store `farr = p;` only the first. A struct's member array frees its offset constants as well, which this profile does not follow. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_StoreSRefToRef`, `QCC_FreeTemp`.

A store to a definition is its `OP_STORE_*` statement, unless the value is the temporary the statement before made, which `opt_assignments` folds the store into; and a postfix `++` or `--` whose value is read copies the old value to a temporary by `OP_STORE_*` first. At global scope each is "Unable to generate statements": `float q = (x = y);` is `STORE_F`, `(x = y + 1)` only `ADD_F`, `float q = x++;` `STORE_F` and `ADD_F`. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_StoreSRefToRef`, `QCC_PR_RefExpression` (`ref->postinc`), `QCC_RefToDef`.

An array named bare, its head, is the pointer to its first element to a prefix or postfix `++` and `--` (`REF_ARRAYHEAD`): read by its address, which the id target refuses (FTEF-31.4), stepped by `OP_ADD_PIW` of its element's size, `--` warning of the truncated negation (FTEF-27.14), and stored as `QCC_StoreSRefToRef` stores to the head, "left operand must be an l-value (did you mean NAME[0]?)" (`E0325`): on the FTE target `--varr;` of a `vector varr[2]` is "Constant int operand 4294967293 will be truncated to -3" then the l-value error, and the value of `farr++` is a `float*`.

`!`, `~` and a value made a truth value emit the opcode of the value's basic type (a truth value taken for its parent's): `!` `OP_NOT_F`, `OP_NOT_S`, `OP_NOT_ENT`, `OP_NOT_V`, `OP_NOT_FNC` and `OP_NOT_I` (for integers and pointers), and `== 0` for a double or 64-bit value; `~` `OP_BITNOT_F`, `OP_NOT_S`, `OP_BITNOT_V`, `OP_BITNOT_I` and the 64-bit and double ones, but nothing for an entity or a function; the truth `!= 0` of each. Each is folded, emitted or emulated (FTEF-27). A `void` value is under `lax` the warning `W0248` with the message and `OP_NOT_F`, else, like any type with no opcode, the fatal error `E0328` "Type mismatch: !TYPE" or "Type mismatch: ~TYPE": `~e` of an entity and `!(void)a`.

A condition is tested by `QCC_Generate_OP_IFNOT`, or `QCC_Generate_OP_IF` for a jump taken when it is true: integers, entities, fields, functions, pointers and truth values as integers; a string warns `W0245` "if (string) tests for null, not empty" (with a full stop for `QCC_Generate_OP_IF`), F322, off by default; a vector is `!v` under `ifvector`, on by default, else `W0246` "if (vector) tests only the first element with the current compiler flags"; a double or 64-bit value is compared with 0; a `variant`, struct, union, strict enum or `void` warns `W0247` "conditional type mismatch: TYPE", TYPE from `basictypenames[]`. The flags `ifvector` and `vectorlogic` are kept for it (FTEF-21.1). The conditional operator's test is checked; the statements' (FTEF-18) are the statement checks'.
