`c ? a : b` tests `c` (FTEF-30.2); `c ?: b` takes `c` as the first arm. An integer arm is made a float when the target has no `OP_STORE_IF`. An integer and a float are a float, the integer converted; an integer and an unsigned value unsigned, and so for 64 bits. Arms whose types `typecmp` tells apart, a truth value taken for its parent's, are then reconciled: a null arm takes the other's type when they are of one size; else arms `typecmp_lax` tells apart (it compares what fields, pointers and functions hold, and parameters and a class's members, but no class names, FTEF-9.14) warn `W0244` "Type mismatch on ternary operator: A vs B", warning 0, and arms it takes as one, two classes with the same members, are the fatal error `E0332` "Ternary operator with mismatching types". `a ? s : 2` warns and the store then refuses the string.

`-e` is `0 - e` of the operand's type (`OP_SUB_F`, `OP_SUB_D`, `OP_SUB_V`, `OP_SUB_I`, `OP_SUB_U` and the 64-bit ones), `+e` the operand; any other type is the fatal error `E0302` "type mismatch for -" or "type mismatch for +". `++e` and `--e` of a read-only value are the fatal error `E0329` "++ operator on read-only value" (or `--`), and of a type with no `+` `E0329` "++ operator on unsupported type"; otherwise the `+` of 1 or -1 of the operand's type, a pointer's by `OP_ADD_PIW`, is emitted and stored, and the value is the operand stored to, read-only, so `itof` of `--i` names `i`.

`*e` of a pointer is what it points at, which may be assigned to; of a string its first character, an integer; under `qccx` of a float or integer an entity; of a function the function, or under `qcfuncs`, on by default, the fatal error `E0330` "attempt to dereference function type."; of anything else `E0330` "Unable to dereference non-pointer type.". Under `qccx`, `@e` of a float or integer is a string, of anything else `E0330` "'@' operator only functions on floats and ints. go figure.".

A cast the program writes, `(TYPE)e`, is `QCC_EvaluateCast(e, TYPE, false)`: it warns of nothing, takes what an implicit cast takes (FTEF-19.31) and also an entity and a float either way (`OP_CONV_ITOF`, `OP_CONV_FTOI`), two types of one basic type and any type to `void`, and under `lax` anything; else it is "Cannot cast from A to B" (`E0213`), a fatal error. Its conversion opcodes are emitted (FTEF-27.8): `(entity)a` is "ftoi emulation: denormals are unsafe" on the standard target.

The vector constructor `[x, y, z]`, and `(vector){x, y, z}`, casts each component that is no float or integer to a float (`QCC_EvaluateCast(x, type_float, true)`, "Cannot cast" for a string or an entity); a component left out, `[x]` or `[x, y]`, is a float 0; three constants are a vector constant; two null components make the vector the third times its axis, `'1 0 0' * x` by `OP_MUL_VF`; else each component is stored, a float with `OP_STORE_F` and an integer with `OP_STORE_IF`, which on the standard target is "itof emulation". Its "Argument not a single numeric value in vector constructor" is not reachable: the cast before it gives every component a float's type or fails.
**Withdrawn** (#84): it said the model keeps no array's length or struct's layout, so their sizes were no known constants; it keeps both, and FTEF-30.11 replaces it.
`?:` compares its arms' types (FTEF-30.3) before it stores the last arm, so "Type mismatch on ternary operator: A vs B" comes before that store's statement.

A conditional's first arm is stored by its size (`switch(r.cast->size)`: three words by `OP_STORE_V`, two by `OP_STORE_I64`, one by `OP_STORE_F`), and one of more than three words is the fatal error `E0370` "oversized ternary result": `struct S { float a, b, c, d; }; S r = c ? s1 : s2;`. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_RefExpression`.

`sizeof(TYPE)` and `sizeof e` are unsigned constants: a string immediate's length with its NUL, a type's bytes, `bits / 8` for an 8- or 16-bit type and 4 per word for any other, and an array's, a member array's included, its element's times its length: `sizeof(farr)` is 16 for `float farr[4]`. Under `undefwordsize` `sizeof` of a type is the error `E0326` "sizeof was disabled, use array.length instead." and of an expression "sizeof was disabled.". `_length(e)` (or `_length e`) is an integer constant: a defined array's length, a constant string's without its NUL, a vector's 3; a struct's member array's length is no constant. A string that is no constant is the fatal error `E0334` "_length(string) requires an initialised constant", any other type "_length() unsupported argument type for intrinsic". Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_RefTerm`.

A truth value as an arm of `?:` is `ev_boolean`: it is not the `int` arm a target with no `OP_STORE_IF` makes a float, nor the `int` promoted to the other arm's `float`, so `x = q ? bb : x;` of a `_Bool bb` warns "Type mismatch on ternary operator: __int32 vs float", and the `?:` is the arms' store, `QCC_PR_DummyDef(type, "ternary", ...)`, which the emulation warnings name `ternary`: "itof emulation: denormals are unsafe ternary" as it is stored to the float. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_RefExpression` (`?`).

A call's value is an alias of `OFS_RETURN` (`QCC_GetAliasTemp`), no temporary, so an arm's store of it is no folded one; and the first arm's store, the condition's under `?:` or the middle arm's, asks for its statement (`&truthstore`), which first copies the aliases to temporaries (`QCC_ClobberDef(NULL)`): at global scope `float q = c ? ff() : y;` is "Unable to generate statements" of `IFNOT`, `CALL0`, two `STORE_F`, `GOTO` and a last `STORE_F`, where `c ? y : ff()` stores the call once. A `?:` with a vector condition under `ifvector`, its default, tests `!v` by `OP_IF_I`, "(IF)". Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_RefExpression` (`?`), `QCC_ClobberDef`, `QCC_Generate_OP_IFNOT`.

`typecmp_lax` compares two function types by their return types and the parameters both have (`minargs`), any more one of them has being `optional`; whether either takes `...` is not compared. So `void(float a, ...)` and `void(float b)` are one type to it, and as `?:` arms, which `typecmp` tells apart, are "Ternary operator with mismatching types"; `void(float a, float b)` and `void(float b)` are not, "Type mismatch on ternary operator"; and `void(float a)` stores to a `void(float a, optional float b)` with no "Implicit cast" (FTEF-22.8). Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_lex.c`, `typecmp_lax`.

At global scope (`pr_scope` null) a conditional whose condition is a constant (`QCC_SRef_EvalConst`) generates nothing: `c ?: b` is `c` when `QCC_Eval_Truth` holds of it, else `b`; `c ? a : b` is `a` when the constant's first word (`eval->_int`) is not 0, so `-0.0` picks `a`, else `b`. The other arm is read and dropped, and the value is the arm's, constant or not ("initializer for 'q' is not constant" only when that arm is not). In a body the jumps are always generated (`if (pr_scope) eval = NULL;`). Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_RefExpression`.

A reference read: a definition or field is the value; an array named bare is its address (FTEF-31.4); an element at an index that is no constant is loaded (FTEF-31.2); what a pointer points at by `OP_LOADP_*` (FTEF-31.3); a string's character by `OP_LOADP_C` for a float index, else `OP_LOADP_U8`.

`base[index]`: of an array, its element, a constant index past its end the warning `W0249` "(constant) array index out of bounds (0 <= I < N)", an index into an element of more than one word scaled by its size (`OP_MUL_F` for a float index, else `OP_MUL_I`); of a class's array member or an array of fields, the field the index selects, the index read as an element's once, when it is parsed, so `arr[i] = 0i` converts `i` once; of a pointer, what it points at; of a string, its character, under `qccx` the string offset (`OP_ADD_I`, or `OP_ADD_F` with "string offsetting emulation: denormals are unsafe" for a float index); of a vector or an entity's `.vector` field, its component, a constant index past 2 the fatal error `E0333` "(vector) array index out of bounds" or "(.vector) array index out of bounds"; anything else is no array, where FTEQCC's parser stops at the `[`: `E0204` "expected ;, found [", `)` inside parentheses or a call's arguments and `]` inside an index. An element at a variable index is read by `OP_LOADA_*` or `OP_GLOAD_*` with the index made an integer when the target has them, by `OP_FETCH_GBL_*` with it made a float for a global array when the target has that, and else by the generated `ArrayGet` function, the index made a float (a vector's divided by 3): on the standard target `arr[i]` of an integer `i` is "itof emulation: denormals are unsafe i".

What a pointer points at is read with the index made an integer, by `OP_LOADP_F`, `OP_LOADP_S`, `OP_LOADP_V`, `OP_LOADP_ENT`, `OP_LOADP_FLD`, `OP_LOADP_FNC`, `OP_LOADP_I` (integers, and pointers when the target has no `OP_LOADP_P`) or `OP_LOADP_I64`, each emulated or refused (FTEF-27.10); a struct, union or double word by word with no check; a `void` or `variant` is the fatal error `E0336` "ptr-to-variants must be cast to a different type before being read". A store through a pointer is by offset, which needs no emulation on the standard target.

An array of fields named after an entity's `.` with no `[` after it, `e.a` for `.float a[2]` or a class's `float a[2]` member, is the array's head, whose address is taken (FTEF-31.4): on the id target the fatal error `E0331` "... Consider the use of either '#pragma target fte' or '#pragma flag enable brokenarray'", stored to or read; `e.a[1]` is the element.

`&e`: under `qccx` a float is a pointer to a float, and a string, field, entity or function a float; a temporary not reached through a pointer is the error `E0335` "Address-of temp on line FILE:LINE", FILE the file's path as the module names it and LINE its line, and stays the value it is; else its address: a field's by `OP_ADDRESS`; a pointer's element's by `OP_ADD_PIW`; a definition's, an element's or an array's by `OP_GLOBALADDRESS`, which a target without it refuses, the fatal error `E0331` "Address-of operator is not supported in this form without extensions. Consider the use of: #pragma target fte", and for an array "Consider the use of either '#pragma target fte' or '#pragma flag enable brokenarray'"; reading an array named bare takes its address, so `arr = arr` and `arr += 1` are that error on the standard target. The address of a local warns `W0250` "Address-of operator on local TYPE NAME is unsafe if recursing (and still bloated when not). Consider use of 'static' or 'auto'.", once per local, off by default; the model counts parameters as locals and does not tell a `static` local. FILE is the file's name as the compiler was given it, `s_filen` (FTEF-14.32), and with LINE follows `#pragma file` and `#pragma line` (FTEF-14.43): `Address-of temp on line foo.qc:40` after `#pragma file foo.qc` and `#pragma line 40`.

A store to an element at an index that is no constant is by its address when the target has `OP_GLOBALADDRESS` or `OP_GSTOREP_F`, the index made an integer, else by the generated `ArraySet` function, the index made a float (a vector's divided by 3); a value of another type than the element's, which only a compound assignment's result under `lax` leaves, is the fatal error `E0337` "Type mismatch on indexed assignment of NAME: A VALUE, needed B.". An element is named `base[index]` in the store's messages, but for an immediate index. A string's character is stored by `OP_STOREP_C` for a float when the target has it, else `OP_STOREP_I8` when it has that, else `OP_STOREP_C` or `OP_STOREP_I8`, the value made a float or an integer for it and the index an integer, added to the string by `OP_ADD_I` on a target whose stores take no offset; the store is emulated as FTEF-6.18 says.

An index on a pointer is scaled as an array's is (`QCC_PR_ParseRefArrayPointer`, `t->size != 1`): by the size in words of what the pointer points at, a vector's 3, a 64-bit value's 2, a struct's or union's its own, by `OP_MUL_F` for a float index, else the index made an integer and multiplied by `OP_MUL_I`; an index of an 8- or 16-bit integer (`t->bits`) is made an integer and multiplied by one, which emits nothing. `pv[i]` of a `vector *pv` is `OP_MUL_I` of `i` by 3, which the id target emulates.

A constant index is read by `QCC_Eval_Int`, a 64-bit integer: C's conversion of a float or double (saturating, as on arm64), an integer, or a 64-bit one, and the bounds check compares its low word as unsigned, so `arr[13.5 / 0.0]` is "(constant) array index out of bounds (0 <= -1 < 1)". A vector or string constant has no value there, `E0360` "Unable to evaluate to numeric constant", twice for an array's, a vector's and a `.vector` field's index (the bounds and the element's read) and 0 for the index; a pointer's index is made an integer instead, a string "Implicit type mismatch. Needed integer, got string.".
A constant vector's component at a constant index is a constant, the component's value: `('13 5 2' + '1 2 3')[1]` is 7, and `vc[1]` of a `const vector vc = '4 9 2'` is 9.

An element of an array, or a vector's component, at a constant index is the array's definition at that word (`ret.ofs += index`), so `iarr[1] == iarr[1]` of `int`s is the same operand twice ("Result of comparison is constant" on the id target) and `iarr[1] == iarr[2]` is not; at an index that is no constant it is loaded into a temporary.

The address of a string's character is no address `QCC_PR_GenerateAddressOf` makes: on any target it is the fatal error `E0361` "Cannot use addressof operator ('&') on a global. Please use the FTE target." (`pw = &s[0];`).

The address of an element through a pointer to an 8- or 16-bit integer (`basetype->align != 32`, "index is bytes or shorts or something small") is the pointer plus the element's byte offset by `OP_ADD_I`, not `OP_ADD_PIW`: a constant index's `index*(align/8)` folded, unless `undefwordsize`, else `OP_MUL_I` of `align/8` and the index made an integer, which folds away for a byte. So on the id target `__int8 *pc; &pc[i]` is only `ADD_I`'s "AddInt function not defined" and "not valid for target" errors, `__int16 *pc; &pc[i]` `MUL_I`'s and then `ADD_I`'s, and `&pc[0]` none. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_GenerateAddressOf`.

Under `qccx`, `&` of a float "casts it to a (pre-dereferenced) pointer" (`QCC_PR_BuildRef(retbuf, REF_POINTER, QCC_RefToDef(r, true), nullsref, type_float, false, 0)`): a float read through the value as an address, by `OP_LOADP_F`, and stored to likewise, so on the standard target `float f; string s; s = &f;` is `OP_LOADP_F`'s "memgetval function not defined" and "not valid for target" errors and then "Implicit cast from float to string". Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_RefTerm`.

A string's character is read and stored through `QCC_SupplyConversion(..., true)`: read at an index that is no float, the index is made an integer, and stored, the value is made a float or an integer for the opcode FTEF-31.5 chooses, then the index an integer. A type that does not convert is the error "Implicit type mismatch. Needed integer, got string." for an index (a warning under `lax`), and the value's cast is the definition's (FTEF-19.31): `s["a"]`, `s[e] = 1` and `s[1] = "b"`, "Cannot cast from string to float". Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_RefToDef`, `QCC_StoreSRefToRef`, `QCC_SupplyConversion`.

An array head has a length prefix for `OP_FETCH_GBL_*` when the target has it, unless it is embedded in another symbol: `def->arraylengthprefix = !rootsymbol && !def->localscope && ...` reads `localscope` before `QCC_PR_GetDef` sets it, so a local array has the prefix too. Read there with an index that is no float (`QCC_LoadFromArray`, `accel == 1`), the index is converted with `QCC_SupplyConversion(index, ev_float, true)`, whose result is not kept: the fetch takes the index as it is and frees it a second time, which for an index that is a named definition warns `W0319` "INTERNAL: over-freed refcount to NAME", as under `#pragma target hexen2` `farr[i]` does for an `int i`. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_LoadFromArray`, `QCC_PR_GetDef`, `QCC_FreeTemp`.

An array of fields, an entity's `e.fa[i]` of a `.float fa[4]` or a class's member array `this.arr[i]`, is indexed in elements of the field's type: an index that is no constant is scaled as an array head's is (FTEF-31.2), so a `.vector` array's `int` index is `OP_MUL_I` by 3, on the id target "MulInt function not defined: cannot emulate int*int" and its refusal, and the scaled index is a temporary. A class's member array is a `QCC_PR_DummyDef` with a root symbol, the class's field, so it has no length prefix (FTEF-31.15): under `#pragma target hexen2` `this.arr[ii]` of an `int ii` warns only "itof emulation", where `e.fa[ii]` of a global array of fields also warns "INTERNAL: over-freed refcount to ii". Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseRefArrayPointer`, `QCC_LoadFromArray`, `QCC_PR_DummyDef`; `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_lex.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseType` (the class's fields).

Under `qccx` the address of a field is the field cast to a float (`r->cast = type_float`), the same symbol, whose word is the field's offset: the module's first field, at offset 0, is then a null constant (`QCC_SRef_IsNull`), which `QCC_TryEvaluateCast` casts to any type with no warning, so `s = &fl;`, `e = &fl;` and `p = &fl;` of the first `.float fl` give nothing, where any later field is "Implicit cast from float to string", "... to entity" and "Cannot cast from float to float*". Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_RefTerm`, `QCC_TryEvaluateCast`, `QCC_SRef_IsNull`.

A string's character read at an index that is no float is the value `OP_LOADP_U8` gives: an `int` on a target that has it, and on one that does not the `__uint32` of the last shift of its emulation (`OP_RSHIFT_U`), so under `#pragma target dp` `x = s[ii];` of a float `x` adds "utof emulation: will break if ... is big". A compound assignment to the character reads it so, and a float value cast to an unsigned type keeps the type its conversion gives (`QCC_TryEvaluateCast` sets no cast on the float to `uint` branch): `s[ii] += x;` there and `u += x;` of a `__uint u` on any target are "Type mismatch on assignment. __uint32 += __int32 is not supported" and "__uint += __int32". Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_StatementFlags` (`OP_LOADP_U8`, `OP_CONV_FU`), `QCC_TryEvaluateCast`, `QCC_PR_RefExpression`.
The callee is read (FTEF-31.1); a value of a type that is no function or `variant` is the fatal error `E0256` "not a function" (FTEF-19.40), whatever names it. A `variant` takes any arguments.

**Withdrawn** (#84): it said a variadic function is no intrinsic and did not say which calls are a method's; FTEQCC's test, `!newself.cast && !t->num_parms`, counts no `...`, and FTEF-32.10 replaces it.

Each argument is read and, when `typecmp` tells its type from its parameter's, cast to it as an assignment's value is (FTEF-29.2), its conversion emitted: `f1(i)` of an integer is "itof emulation". An argument past the last parameter of a function that is not variadic warns `W0252` "too many parameters on call to NAME, argument ARG will be ignored", ARG as `QCC_GetRefName` names it; past the eighth of a variadic one `W0251` "More than 8 parameters on varargs function"; past the 136th (`MAX_PARMS + MAX_EXTRA_PARMS`) the fatal error `E0338` "More than 136 parameters". Missing arguments take their parameters' defaults; an `optional` parameter ends the count; else the warning `W0253` "too few parameters on call to NAME, PARAM will be UNDEFINED" (Q105), "too few parameters on call to NAME" for a parameter with no name. The value is the function's return type.

A local's initialiser is the local's first store: read, converted to the local's type, and its cast reported here for an expression the resolver's initialiser check does not cast itself (a literal, `_()`, a name, a cast of a literal or an element, FTEF-19.31).

In a member function a field named bare is `this.field` (FTEF-17.14), and so is a class's member field, which holds its own type; `::name` and `Scope::name` are the field itself (`expandmemberfields = false;`, "::classname is always usable for eg: the find builtin"), so `find(world, ::targetname, s)` passes the field and `find(world, targetname, s)` is "Cannot cast from string to .string". A field held as a `variant` casts to and from any field type silently.
An `out` argument is stored back after the call (FTEF-29.3); a read-only one, a constant or an immediate, is the error `E0339` "Unable to write to read-only out argument", not fatal.

`va_arg(index, TYPE)` (and `...(index, TYPE)`) reads its index, the `,` ("expected ,, found X" without it) and its second argument as a type (`QCC_PR_ParseType`, `"X" is not a type` for another token; any type, `string`, `vector`, `float*`, `.float`); the parser reads any call of that name so, a function of the name with parameters included. Its index is read as a float times 3 (`OP_MUL_F`), or else made an integer (`QCC_SupplyConversion`, "Implicit type mismatch. Needed integer, got TYPE.") times 3; in a function with no `...`, which has no `__va_list`, it is the fatal error `E0346` "va_arg() intrinsic only works inside varadic functions". Its value is of TYPE.

A call's value is called no further: `QCC_PR_ParseFunctionCall` is reached from a name, and after a call's `)` the expression is read on as a value, so the `(` after it ends the expression. The construct around it then expects its own token: "expected ;, found (" at the end of a statement, and "expected ), found (" in parentheses or a call's arguments, the fatal error `E0204` (FTEF-24.10). `k(g()());` is "expected ), found (". An initialiser `float x = g()();` in a body is FTEQCC's "Missing semicolon at end of definition" and then a parse error; this profile reports "expected ;, found (" there, the same refusal.

An argument may be left empty, a `,` or the `)` where it would start (`else if (arg < t->num_parms && (QCC_PR_PeekToken (",") || QCC_PR_PeekToken (")")))`): `f(1, , 3)`, `f(1, )`. It passes its parameter's default value; a parameter with none, an `optional` one among them, is the fatal error `E0375` "Default value not specified for implicit argument N", counted from 1. Past the parameters, and for a `variant`, which has none, the expression read there is missing, `"," - not a name` or `")" - not a name`. Each default passed so frees its reference once more than it holds it, so FTEQCC warns `W0319` "INTERNAL: over-freed refcount to NAME" (`QCC_FreeTemp`, `WARN_DEBUGGING`), the default as `QCC_VarAtOffset` prints it: `2f` for a float immediate, a constant's name for a constant. Under the vanilla dialect an empty argument is a missing expression. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseFunctionCall`, `QCC_FreeTemp`, `QCC_VarAtOffset`.

A call of a function with no named parameters, `...` or not (`!t->num_parms`), that is no method's is an intrinsic when its name is one, and a name no definition has is called as one (FTEQCC declares them on demand): `_` takes only a string immediate, else the fatal error `E0340` "_() intrinsic accepts only a string immediate"; `random` makes its arguments floats (`QCC_SupplyConversion`, the fatal error `E0227` "Implicit type mismatch. Needed float, got TYPE." for a type with no conversion); `randomv` takes vectors as they are, any other type the fatal error `E0340` "type mismatch on parm N"; `alloca` makes its size an integer, rounds it up to words (`OP_ADD_I` of 3, `OP_DIV_I` by 4) and pushes them by `OP_PUSH`, a plain statement, which only FTE's highest revision has ("Opcode \"<PUSH>|PUSH\" not valid for target. Consider the use of: #pragma target fte_6614"); `alloca`, `used_sound` and `used_model` read their first argument whatever follows the `(` (`QCC_PR_Expression`), so with none they are the fatal error `E0201` "\")\" - not a name"; `entnum(e)` is `(e / 1i) / (nextent(world) / 1i)` by `OP_DIV_I`, and with no `nextent` the fatal error `E0347` "the nextent builtin is not defined"; `used_sound` and `used_model` take a string immediate, else the error `E0340` "Argument to used_sound intrinsic was not a string immediate.". A method's call is one made through an object's member, `c.m()`, or of a member function named bare in another, which passes `this` (`newself`). Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseFunctionCall`.

A call names its callee as `QCC_GetSRefName` does: a definition by its name, a non-virtual member function's `CLASS::name` however it is reached (`QCC_RefToDef` of the member), and a temporary, a field's read and so a virtual method's, by its type's name, which for a function type FTEQCC parses is `__function`: "too many parameters on call to __function, argument IMMEDIATE will be ignored". Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_GetSRefName`, `QCC_PR_ParseFunctionCall`; `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_lex.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseFunctionType`.

`entnum` and `autocvar` are intrinsics only when an argument follows the `(`: `!QCC_PR_CheckToken(")")` takes the `)` of `entnum()` and `autocvar()`, and the call that follows reads its argument from the token after it, so `entnum();` is the fatal error `E0201` "\";\" - not a name". `autocvar` reads its name, a `,`, its default and at most a description: with no `,` after the name it is the fatal error `E0204` "expected ,, found )", and with a fourth argument "expected ), found ,". Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseFunctionCall`.

A constant local's aggregate initialiser, `const string tab[] = { "a", "b" };` in a body, is its value at compile time, as a global's is, with no statement: the generated initialiser copies a constant's words when the definition is a global, a constant or static (`if (basedef && (!basedef->scope || basedef->constant || basedef->isstatic))`), and stores them only otherwise (`finalnotconst`). Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_GenerateInitializerType`.

With `opt_constantarithmatic` on, its default, a call is folded by its function's name, before its arguments are checked, when they are constants (`QCC_PR_GenerateFunctionCallRef`): with one argument, `floor`, `ceil`, `sin`, `cos`, `log` and `sqrt` of its first word read as a float, computed in `double` and made a float (`return QCC_MakeFloatConst(floor(a->_float));`); with two arguments that are floats as written (`arglist[0]->cast == type_float && arglist[1]->cast == type_float`), `pow` as `pow(a, b)`, `mod` as `fmodf((int)a, (int)b)`, `min` and `max` as `progsint.h`'s `((a) < (b) ? (a) : (b))` and `((a) > (b) ? (a) : (b))`, and `bitshift` as `(int)a >> (int)-b` for a negative `b`, else `(int)a << (int)b`. So `static const float m = floor(7 / 2);` at global scope is the constant 3, with no "Unable to generate statements". FTEQCC also folds `strlen` and `stof` of a string constant; this profile does not, as the model keeps no string constant's text where calls are checked, and makes the call. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_GenerateFunctionCallRef`; `engine/qclib/progsint.h`, `min`, `max`.

`sprintf` with a constant format string reads it directive by directive (`%%` is none): an argument position `N$`, flags, a width (`*` takes an argument, `*N$` the Nth, which must be a float, "width modifier requires float at arg N"), a precision (the same, "precision modifier ..."; a `.` with neither is "invalid format string: REST"), length modifiers (`h` a float, `l` and `L` an integer, `q` 64 bits; `j`, `z` and `t` warn "length modifier C is a placeholder"), and a conversion. A conversion assumes a float unless `%i`, `%p` or a modifier says otherwise: `d i c o u x p e f g` and their capitals require a float (a double with `q`), or with `l` an integer ("DIRECTIVE requires int at arg N (got TYPE)", warned twice, an entity taken for `%i`), `%p` a pointer; `%v` a vector, or with `l` "intvector"; `%s` a string; a `variant` is taken by any; another conversion is "invalid format string: REST", which ends the check. Each mismatch warns `W0254` "NAME: DIRECTIVE requires TYPE at arg N (got TYPE)", an argument past the last a `void`. Arguments past the last taken warn "NAME: surplus trailing TYPE argument(s) for format \"FORMAT\"". F324, `WARN_FORMATSTRING`.

`cvar("vid_conwidth")` and `cvar("vid_conheight")` warn that they are deprecated; `setviewprop` and `setproperty` with a constant property check its values' basic types against FTEQCC's table ("NAME(PROPERTY, ...): expected TYPE, got TYPE", then `X, ` and `X, Y, ` for the second and third) and warn "NAME: unknown argument N" for a number not in it; `addstat` and `clientstat` with three arguments compare a constant type number with the field's basic type ("indicated type ev_TYPE does not match passed field type .TYPE", or "is not a basic type"), a field of a `variant` taking any; `sendevent` with a constant type list checks each argument after the second against its letter (`s f F i I u U v e`), "arg type list longer than args", "'C' is not a recognised arg type", "'C' specified, but was passed TYPE", and "cannot pass more than 8 args to a builtin.". Each warns `W0255`, F333, `WARN_ARGUMENTCHECK`.

`return;` in a function whose type is not `void` warns `W0256` "'NAME' returned nothing, expected TYPE" (`WARN_MISSINGRETURNVALUE`, Q203), unless the function is marked `accumulate` or `return =` or an earlier `return;` gave it its return value (`pr_scope->returndef`), so it warns once. `return = e;` reads `e` and stores it with no type check (`QCC_StoreSRefToRef`). `return e;` of `__NULL__` or a null constant returns from any function; a value of another basic type than the function's is cast to it implicitly (`QCC_EvaluateCast(e, type, true)`, FTEF-19.31), and from a `void` function warns `W0257` "'NAME' returned TYPE, expected void" (`WARN_WRONGRETURNTYPE`, Q204) instead.

`if (e)` tests `e` with `QCC_Generate_OP_IFNOT` (FTEF-30.2), `if not (e)` and `if !(e)` with `QCC_Generate_OP_IF`; `if !(e)` of a string or a float tests `!e` (FTEF-30.1) with `QCC_Generate_OP_IFNOT` instead. `if !()` warns `W0261` "if !() is specific to fteqcc", and `if not()` "if not() is specific to fteqcc or hexen2" but on the Hexen II targets (`WARN_FTE_SPECIFIC`, F311, off by default). A constant condition generates no test, and the branch it never takes generates nothing unless it defines a label.

`while (e)` tests `e` as `if` does, `until (e)` with `QCC_Generate_OP_IF`; a constant float condition generates no test, or a `goto` past the loop when it never holds. `do s while (e);` tests `e` with `QCC_Generate_OP_IF`, `do s until (e);` with `QCC_Generate_OP_IFNOT`; a constant condition of any type generates no test, or a `goto` back when it holds.
`for (init; e; step)` tests `e` with `OP_IFNOT_I` and no test of its type; the step is checked before the body and generated after it.

`switch (e)` uses `OP_SWITCH_F`, `_E`, `_V`, `_S` or `_FNC` by `e`'s type when the target has it. A `case` value may generate no code, else the fatal error `E0342` "Case statements may not use formulas"; a read is not generated until the end of the switch, so a field of an entity is a value. After the body each case value of another basic type is made the switch's (`QCC_SupplyConversion`, FTEF-22.3), and without the opcode compared with `e`: by `OP_EQ_F`, `_E`, `_V`, `_S`, `_FNC` (a function or a field), `_P`, `_I` (an integer or unsigned), `_I64` or `_D`, which warn as any comparison does (FTEF-28), and a constant 0 by testing `e` itself; any other type is the fatal error `E0343` "Bad switch type". A range `case a .. b` is `e >= a && e <= b` of a float, a double or an integer of any width, and of any other type warns `W0260` "switch caserange MUST be a float or integer" (`WARN_SWITCHTYPEMISMATCH`, which has no name). A strict enum's opcode and equality are its base type's, its range not, and a value of another type is no enum ("Implicit type mismatch. Needed enum, got TYPE."). Before the comparisons each item of a strict enum switched on that no case covers warns `W0263` "ENUM::ITEM not part of switch" (the warning of code 0), the last item first (each is prepended to the type's `accessors`); a `default`, a range, or a case whose value is no constant of the enum's own type stops the search, covering every item.

When a function is finished (`QCC_PR_FinaliseFunction`), a `return` of the value `return =` set is added, then `OP_DONE`, and `QCC_CheckForDeadAndMissingReturns` reads the layout: a function whose type is not `void` warns `W0258` "NAME: not all control paths return a value" (`WARN_MISSINGRETURN`, Q206) when its last statement before `OP_DONE` is no `return` and no backward `goto`, or when a conditional jump goes to that `OP_DONE`; a statement after a `return` or a `goto` that is no `return`, `goto` or `OP_DONE` and that no jump reaches warns `W0259` "NAME: contains unreachable code (line N)" (`WARN_UNREACHABLECODE`, F323), N its line as `pr_source_line` has it, which `#pragma line` changes. The statement after a `return` or `goto` is not itself tested for a jump to the end. A function whose body had an error, which ends FTEQCC's parse of it (`QCC_PR_ParseError`), is not checked, nor is a function marked `accumulate`, whose parts are finished together. So `float() f = { if (a) return 1; };` warns, and `float() f = { if (a < 0) return 1; if (a) return 1; };` does not: the second test follows the first `return`.
`thinktime e : t;` reads `e`, makes `t` a float (`QCC_SupplyConversion`), and is the fatal error `E0344` "thinktime type mismatch" unless `e` is an entity and `t` a float.

A function returning a type larger than a vector (FTEF-6.13) is passed a pointer to the value by its caller: its body starts by storing it with `OP_STORE_P`, which a target without it refuses ("Opcode \"=|STORE_P\" not valid for target", FTEF-27.5, a fatal error that ends the function's checks), so `return;` "'NAME' returned nothing, expected TYPE" and `return =` "'NAME' not supported when returning TYPE" are the fatal error `E0341`, and the finished function warns `W0262` "Function NAME returns (large) TYPE. This is inefficient." (`WARN_SLOW_LARGERETURN`). The return messages of FTEF-34.1 name a type by its own name (FTEF-24.11), and this one by `TypeName`.

An initialiser of a global that is an expression, no literal, name, cast of a literal or `_()`, is read as a body's expression is at global scope (`pr_scope` null): each statement it generates is the error `E0345` "Unable to generate statements at global scope (OPNAME)." (`QCC_PR_StatementFlags`, `ERR_BADEXTENSION` as a warning, so the read goes on), OPNAME the opcode's: an operator's that is not folded, `LOADF_F` and the like for an entity's field, `STORE_F` for each component of a vector built, the stores of a call's arguments (by their words, `STORE_V`, `STORE_I64` or `STORE_F`; an argument of more than three words copied as it is read, three words a parameter, by the widest store the target has for the words left, and the others stored after every argument is read; on a target with `OP_CALL1H` the first two parameters passed with no store) and `CALLn`, or `CALLnH` with `OP_CALL1H` (`CALL0` with no argument), `IFNOT`, `STORE_*`, `GOTO` and `STORE_*` for `?:` (the first arm stored by its size, `STORE_V`, `STORE_I64` or `STORE_F`, the last by its type as `QCC_StoreToSRef` stores it, a double's with plain statements that report nothing, an `OP_STORE_I64` two `STORE_FLD`s on a target without it, and a store of a temporary the arm's last statement made folded into it, `opt_assignments`), and the `DIV_F` or `MUL_F` of an int conversion's emulation. The value is then cast to the global's type, and a value that is no constant is `E0214` "initializer for 'NAME' is not constant". So `float b = a + 1;` gives both, `float b = 1 + 2;` neither, and `const vector v = [19, 20];` is a constant.

A `switch`'s cases are compared in order after its body is read, and a second `default` is the fatal error `E0352` "Duplicated default case" there (`if (defaultcase >= 0) QCC_PR_ParseError(ERR_MULTIPLEDEFAULTS, "Duplicated default case");`), after the errors of the cases before it: `switch (1) { default: case 1: default: ; }` is refused, and `switch (1) { case "a": default: default: ; }` reports the string case's mismatch instead.

An opcode `QCC_PR_StatementFlags` refuses (FTEF-27.5, `badopcode`, an error but no fatal one) is still emitted, so at global scope it is also "Unable to generate statements at global scope (OPNAME).": `string t = s + 1;` on the id target is "OP_ADD_SF: string+float may be unsafe", `AddInt`'s and `ADD_I`'s refusals, and "Unable to generate statements at global scope (ADD_I).".

At the end of each function, before the illegal `case`, `continue` and `break` checks, every `goto` read since the last function's end must name a label read since then (FTEF-18.23): `for (i = 0; i < num_gotos; i++) { for (j = 0; j < num_labels; j++) if (!strcmp(pr_gotos[i].name, pr_labels[j].name))`, and otherwise `QCC_PR_ParseError(ERR_NOLABEL, "Goto statement with no matching label \"%s\"", pr_gotos[i].name);`, the fatal error `E0308` at the function's closing `}` for the first such `goto`, which ends the function's checks. A `goto` in a stripped `if` arm is no longer among them (`QCC_UngenerateStatements` takes back `num_gotos`), where a label there stays. A function defined inside another ends the same way, checking the enclosing function's `goto`s read before it and its own against the enclosing function's labels read before it and its own, and then forgets both: a label after the inner function does not help them, and a `goto` after it does not find a label before it; its error ends the enclosing function's checks. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseImmediateStatements`, `QCC_UngenerateStatements`.

NAME: contains unreachable code (line N) (FTEF-34.6) is given at the line of the unreachable statement (`statements[st].linenum`), and "not all control paths return a value" at the function's end. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_CheckForDeadAndMissingReturns`.

These differences from FTEQCC's messages are not modelled by this profile, each for its reason. Code generation's, which the compiler (QC-25) owns, as the checks report nothing a program's meaning depends on: the slots `QCC_GetTemp` keeps across functions, so a later function's `temp_N` may be numbered higher (FTEF-27.16); a narrow integer read again in a function, whose extension FTEQCC emulates only the first time; a `__double` stored to a `_Bool`, which FTEQCC follows with one more "ftoi emulation"; and the offset constants a struct's member array frees again (FTEF-29.12). The text of an error in a program both refuse: `typedef ;` warned at the line of the token after the `;`; `(T *)0` and `typedef for x;` with `T` and `for` no type; `[x, 0, 0]_x`; and `spawn(float)`, whose type keyword the semantic model reads as a value. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`.

A `float` or `vector` constant whose initialiser expression folded to a value is that value wherever it is named, as a literal constant is: after the initialiser is read, `if (!def->nofold && def->constant && def->initialized && def->symbolheader == def && def->ofs == 0 && !def->arraysize)` the definition takes the immediate's place, `base = QCC_MakeFloatConst(val->_float).sym;` (`QCC_MakeIntConst`, `QCC_MakeVectorConst` for the others) and `def->ofs = base->ofs; def->symbolheader = base->symbolheader;`. So `const float P = 1 << 8; const float R = P - 1;` folds `R` to 255, and `const vector cv = [1, 2, 3];` is a known vector, whose `cv[1]` is the immediate 2. An array, a shared definition (`nofold`) and an initialiser that does not fold stay as they are. Source: fte-team/fteqw@f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e, `engine/qclib/qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseDefs`.

A differential run executes one scenario (DIFF-2) in the oracle runner, whose VM is id's `PR_ExecuteProgram`, and in QuakeC Studio's runner, whose VM is `qc-vm`. Each writes one trace ([`trace.md`](trace.md)) of the whole scenario, and the two traces are compared by DIFF-9. Neither program links, calls or generates code from the other: this page and the specs it cites are the whole contract between them.

The oracle's VM is `WinQuake/pr_exec.c` compiled unchanged, built as [`vm.md`](vm.md) "Reference build" requires. Everything around it is the mock engine of this page, written by each side on its own: the edicts, the system globals, the builtin table (`pr_builtins`, 79 entries), the host that calls `PR_ExecuteProgram`, and the `Host_Error` and `Sys_Error` that `PR_RunError` and the builtins call.

Where this page or [`edicts.md`](edicts.md) and [`builtins.md`](builtins.md) say the mock does what an id function does, the oracle may compile that function from the pinned commit (for example `ED_Alloc`, `ED_Free`, `ED_LoadFromFile`, `SV_RunThink` or a class pure `PF_` function), and QuakeC Studio uses its own port. Where those specs fix an answer that id's C leaves undefined or platform-dependent (BUILTIN-2.5, BUILTIN-2.7, BUILTIN-2.10, BUILTIN-7.5, BUILTIN-7.6, BUILTIN-7.7, BUILTIN-8.3, BUILTIN-12.6, BUILTIN-16.3, EDICT-8.3), both mocks implement the fixed answer, so for that case the oracle does not run id's code. The float to integer conversion of BUILTIN-2.2 is the exception: its fixed answer is what id's code gives on x86, so the oracle may use C's conversion. `pr_exec.c` is never changed, so the VM's own undefined cases stay id's and are expected divergences (DIFF-10.1).

A run is deterministic: its trace depends only on the scenario's files. It reads no clock, environment variable, system random source or file the scenario does not name, and running the same scenario twice in the same program writes the same bytes.

The mock engine stands in for id's server; it does not model it. Nothing moves and nothing collides (DIFF-5.8, DIFF-7), so a scenario shows that the two VMs execute the same QuakeC the same way, not that a mod behaves as it does in Quake. The server simulation (`qs-sim`, [#238](https://github.com/quakecstudio/editor/issues/238)) is checked against id's engine by its own suite ([#239](https://github.com/quakecstudio/editor/issues/239)).

A scenario file is lines of bytes ended by a line feed, or a carriage return and a line feed. A `#` and everything after it on the line is a comment. A line that is empty after removing the comment, spaces and tabs is skipped. Every other line is a directive: a key, then its arguments, separated by one or more spaces or tabs. A path is relative to the directory holding the scenario file and cannot contain a space, a tab or a `#`.
The directives are:

**Withdrawn** 2026-10-16: it did not say which texts are numbers, so the two runners could read one scenario differently: C's `strtod` and Rust's `f64` parsing both accept `+0.1` and `inf`, and `strtod` accepts hexadecimal; replaced by DIFF-2.7 (integers), DIFF-2.8 (numbers) and DIFF-2.9 (refusal).

The mock's settings are `skill`, `deathmatch`, `coop` and `teamplay`, with the texts `1`, `0`, `0` and `0`, and each name a `cvar` line gives; a `cvar` line for one of the four replaces its text, and a later line for a name replaces an earlier one. A setting's value is its text read by `Q_atof` (BUILTIN-11.7). There are no other settings: `cvar` of any other name returns 0 and `cvar_set` of it changes nothing (BUILTIN-11.8).

The entities file holds the text of a BSP entity lump, read as `ED_LoadFromFile` reads it (EDICT-8), byte for byte, with a NUL after its last byte. How the runner makes it, for example from a `.map` file with the brushes removed, is not part of this spec: both runners read the same file.

An `input` line is `input <frame> <edict> <field> <values>`: `<frame>` from 1 to `frames`; `<edict>` from 1 to `clients`; `<field>` one of `button0` and `button2` with one value, 0 or 1, `impulse` with one integer from 1 to 255, or `v_angle` with three numbers.

An integer (the arguments DIFF-2.2 and DIFF-2.6 call integers, and the values of `button0`, `button2` and `impulse`) is an optional `-` followed by one or more of the digits `0` to `9`, and nothing else: no `+`, no `.`, no exponent. Its value is the digits read in base 10, leading zeros included, and a value outside the argument's range is refused.

A number (the argument of `frametime`, the six of `model` and the three of `v_angle`) is, in order: an optional `-`; one or more digits, with at most one `.` before, among or after them; and optionally an exponent, `e` or `E`, then an optional `+` or `-`, then one or more digits. Nothing else is a number: not a leading `+`, `inf`, `infinity` or `nan` in any case, hexadecimal, or a `.` without a digit. `frametime` is the `double` nearest the exact decimal value of the text, and a `model` or `v_angle` number the `f32` nearest it, ties to even, each rounded once (never through `double` on the way to `f32`); a value whose magnitude rounds below the smallest subnormal is a zero with the text's sign. A `model` or `v_angle` number whose nearest `f32` is infinite is refused, so every number a scenario gives is finite; `frametime` is refused unless its `double` is greater than 0 and at most 1.

A scenario with an unknown key, a missing or extra argument, a value that is not an integer or a number as DIFF-2.7 and DIFF-2.8 say or is out of range, a repeated key that may appear once, a model name repeated, or no `progs`, is refused before anything runs, and no trace is written.

The runner loads the progs by [`progs.md`](progs.md) with the header CRC checked (PROGS-3). A progs that is refused, or that has fewer than 92 global slots or 105 field slots (EDICT-2.4, EDICT-3.3), ends the scenario with that error before the trace header: no trace is written.

The runner then writes the trace header (TRACE-1.3, TRACE-2.1), and sets the engine state: the setting `deathmatch` becomes `0` when the value of `coop` is non-zero; the skill is `(int)(skill + 0.5)` clamped to 0 to 3 and becomes the value of `skill`; the 600 edicts are all zero with none free and `freetime` 0 (EDICT-1.8); `num_edicts` is `maxclients + 1`; the clock is 1.0; the server is loading; no `changelevel` has been issued; no client slot is active; the 64 lightstyles hold no string; the three message buffers of DIFF-6.5 are empty; `checkclient`'s last choice and its time are 0 (DIFF-7.3); and the random state is the seed (DIFF-6.2).

The sound precache list holds only entry 0, the empty string. The model precache list holds entry 0, the empty string; entry 1, `maps/<map>.bsp`; and entries 2 to `submodels + 1`, the names `*1` to `*<submodels>` (BUILTIN-10.3).

The world's fields are set by EDICT-4.1, its `model` an engine string with the text `maps/<map>.bsp`. Then the globals of EDICT-11.4: `coop` to the value of the `coop` setting when it is non-zero, and otherwise `deathmatch` to the value of the `deathmatch` setting; `mapname` to an engine string with the text `<map>`; `serverflags` to 0. These writes, and `time` set to 1 by EDICT-8.1, appear in the change set of the trace's first run record (TRACE-4.1), after the string records of their engine strings (TRACE-4.10).

The map's entities are spawned from the entities file by EDICT-8, using the value of the `deathmatch` setting and the skill of DIFF-3.2 for EDICT-8.4. Each spawn function is a run. The messages EDICT-8 prints are console output and are not compared.

The server then becomes active and runs the two settle frames of EDICT-8.9 as physics frames of 0.1 seconds (DIFF-5.3), without setting `frametime`, emptying a buffer or clearing muzzle flashes. Then the clients enter (DIFF-4), then `frames` server frames run (DIFF-5.1), and the scenario ends.

A scenario that ends normally runs no more QuakeC: no `ClientDisconnect`, no `SetChangeParms`. What the host writes after the trace's last record, such as the last frame's muzzle-flash clearing, is in no change set and is not compared.

Each engine string (EDICT-13.1) gets a value outside the string table, by EDICT-13.3, and a string record when its text is set (TRACE-4.10). Its number is each runner's own; DIFF-9.4 compares the text.

DIFF-3.8 holds for the strings a builtin sets as for the host's: `ftos` and `vtos` write their one buffer (BUILTIN-7.4) and return its value, so each call whose text differs from that value's latest string record writes a string record before the `CALL`'s step record, whose change set first shows the value in `OFS_RETURN`. A call that sets the same text again writes none, as the oracle's `qs_emit_string_records` skips an unchanged text (`oracles/vm/host.c`). Without the record the value has no text in its trace (TRACE-7.3), and DIFF-9.4 compares the two runners' different numbers as bits.

Client slots 0 to `clients - 1` enter in order. For each, as `SV_ConnectClient` does: run `SetNewParms`, with nothing set before it (EDICT-9.1), then copy the globals `parm1` to `parm16` into the slot's spawn parms. Then, as `Host_Spawn_f` does: set every field of the slot's edict to 0 without changing its free flag; set `colormap` to the edict's number, `team` to 1 (the colours are 0, EDICT-5.2) and `netname` to an engine string with the text `player` (`DIFF_CLIENT_NAME`); copy the spawn parms to `parm1` to `parm16`; set `time` to (f32)clock and `self` to the edict; run `ClientConnect`; then run `PutClientInServer` with nothing set between the two.

A slot whose player has entered is active and spawned from then on: it counts as connected for the builtins (BUILTIN-11, BUILTIN-12.7), the physics frame (DIFF-5.4) and `checkclient` (DIFF-7.3). The other slots never have a player.

At the start of server frame `k` (DIFF-5.1), the `input` lines for frame `k` are applied in file order to their edict, as `SV_ReadClientMove` stores a move: `button0` and `button2` set that field to the value, `impulse` sets `impulse` to the value, and `v_angle` sets its three slots to the three values. Nothing else of client input runs: no `SV_ClientThink`, so no field other than these is written.

A server frame of length `T` (the `frametime` directive): sets the global `frametime` to (f32)`T`; empties the unreliable datagram; applies the frame's input (DIFF-4.3); runs a physics frame of length `T` (DIFF-5.3), never paused; empties the reliable datagram; and clears `EF_MUZZLEFLASH` in `effects` on edicts 1 to `num_edicts - 1` (EDICT-10.7), converting `effects` to an integer and back (BUILTIN-2.1, BUILTIN-2.2).

Server frames are numbered from 1. Frame `k` starts with the clock at 1.0 plus 0.1 twice (the settle frames) plus `T` `k - 1` times, each addition made in `double` at the end of a physics frame (DIFF-5.3), so about 1.2 when frame 1 starts.

A physics frame of length `T`, as `SV_Physics`: set `self` and `other` to the world and `time` to (f32)clock, and run `StartFrame`. Then for `i` from 0 while `i` is less than `num_edicts`, read again after each edict: skip edict `i` if it is free; link it (DIFF-5.7) if `force_retouch` is not 0; then give it its turn: an edict from 1 to `maxclients` by DIFF-5.4; otherwise one whose `movetype` equals 7 (`MOVETYPE_PUSH`) by DIFF-5.5; otherwise one whose `movetype` equals 0, 8, 4, 6, 10, 5 or 9 by thinking (DIFF-5.6) and nothing else; otherwise the fatal error `SV_Physics: bad movetype <n>`, `<n>` the integer conversion of `movetype`. The comparisons are of floats, so a `movetype` of 7.5 is a bad movetype. After the last edict, when `force_retouch` is not 0 it is decreased by 1 in `f32`; then the clock advances by `T`.

A client edict's turn does nothing when its slot has no player. Otherwise, as `SV_Physics_Client` without the move: set `time` to (f32)clock and `self` to the edict and run `PlayerPreThink`. Then, by the integer conversion of `movetype`: 0, 3, 5 or 8 thinks (DIFF-5.6) and ends the turn if the edict is then free; 6 or 10 thinks and goes on even if the edict is then free, because `SV_Physics_Toss` returns into the turn; any other value is the fatal error `SV_Physics_client: bad movetype <n>`. Then link the edict (DIFF-5.7), set `time` to (f32)clock and `self` to the edict, and run `PlayerPostThink`.

A `MOVETYPE_PUSH` edict's turn, the world's included, is `SV_Physics_Pusher` with `SV_PushMove` reduced to its branch for a pusher with zero velocity, whatever the velocity is: in `f32`, `oldltime` is `ltime` and `thinktime` is `nextthink`; if `thinktime` is less than `ltime + T` (in `double`), `movetime` is `thinktime - ltime`, or 0 if that is negative, and otherwise (f32)`T`; if `movetime` is not 0, `ltime` becomes `ltime + movetime`. Then if `thinktime` is greater than `oldltime` and not greater than `ltime`, set `nextthink` to 0, `time` to (f32)clock, `self` to the edict and `other` to the world, and run `think`. Nothing moves or is pushed, and `solid` is not changed.

Thinking is `SV_RunThink` (EDICT-10.3): when `nextthink` is greater than 0 and not greater than `clock + T` (in `double`), set `time` to `nextthink`, or to (f32)clock if `nextthink` is less than the clock, then `nextthink` to 0, `self` to the edict and `other` to the world, and run `think`. A `nextthink` of exactly (f32)`(clock + T)` can be just above `clock + T` and then waits a frame.

Linking an edict, from a turn or a builtin, is `SV_LinkEdict` without the area tree: for an edict that is not the world and not free it writes `absmin` and `absmax` by EDICT-12.2, and it runs no `touch` function, even where id's call would touch triggers.

The mock frame leaves out everything that needs the map or another entity's box: client movement (`SV_ClientThink`), gravity, `SV_CheckVelocity`, water checks, the moves of every movetype, pushing and blocking, trigger and impact touches and `blocked` functions, and the client updates. So `origin`, `velocity`, `angles`, `groundentity`, `flags`, `waterlevel` and the other fields of EDICT-12 that physics writes change only when QuakeC or a builtin writes them; `touch` and `blocked` are never called; and nothing runs `ClientKill`, `SetChangeParms` or `ClientDisconnect` except DIFF-8.3.

The mock's builtin table has the numbers 0 to 78 of BUILTIN-5. Builtins of class pure, state and output (BUILTIN-4) behave as [`builtins.md`](builtins.md) says, with the engine state of DIFF-2 to DIFF-5 and DIFF-6.3 to DIFF-6.5 as the fixture BUILTIN-4.2 names; the class world builtins behave as DIFF-7 says; the numbers with no builtin fail as BUILTIN-1.2 says.

The C library's `rand` is replaced by a 32-bit unsigned state, which starts at the scenario's seed: each call sets the state to `state * 1103515245 + 12345` modulo 2^32 and returns `(state >> 16) & 0x7fff`. `random` (BUILTIN-6.6) is the only mock builtin that calls it, once per call.

`precache_model` never fails to load a model (BUILTIN-10.4's fatal error does not happen). The bounds of a model list entry, for `setmodel` (BUILTIN-9.4), are: for entry 0, `'0 0 0'` and `'0 0 0'`; for a name given by a `model` directive, its bounds; for any other name ending in the four bytes `.mdl`, `'-16 -16 -16'` and `'16 16 16'`; and for every other name, the world, the submodels and sprites among them, `'0 0 0'` and `'0 0 0'`.

The command buffer that `localcmd` and `changelevel` append to (BUILTIN-11.5, BUILTIN-11.6) is never run: no command executes and the map never changes. `changelevel` still records that it was issued.

The mock keeps the size in bytes of three buffers and nothing else of the output: the unreliable datagram (`MSG_BROADCAST`, `sound`, `particle`), the reliable datagram (`MSG_ALL`), each of `LIMIT_MAX_DATAGRAM` bytes, and the signon buffer (`MSG_INIT`, `ambientsound`, `makestatic`) of `BUILTIN_SIGNON_SIZE` bytes. It counts what BUILTIN-11 to BUILTIN-13 append, so it drops a sound or particle and fails with `SZ_GetSpace: overflow without allowoverflow set` where id's buffers would (BUILTIN-12.2, BUILTIN-12.5, BUILTIN-13.3). A client slot's reliable message is not kept, never overflows and never drops the client. No output, console text included, is compared.

The errors that builtins.md fixes where id's C is undefined are runtime errors (VM-19.7) with these messages in the mock, so both mocks write the same error record: `invalid entity` (BUILTIN-2.7), `invalid string` (BUILTIN-2.5), `invalid field` (BUILTIN-8.3) and `invalid lightstyle` (BUILTIN-12.6).

No mock builtin starts a nested run: `walkmove` and `movetogoal` touch nothing (DIFF-7.7, DIFF-7.8). `traceon` and `traceoff` change only the trace flag (BUILTIN-16.4), which does not change what a runner writes to the trace.

`traceline(v1, v2, nomonsters, forent)` writes `trace_allsolid` 0, `trace_startsolid` 0, `trace_fraction` 1, `trace_endpos` a copy of the three slots of PARM1, `trace_plane_normal` `'0 0 0'`, `trace_plane_dist` 0, `trace_ent` the world, `trace_inopen` 1 and `trace_inwater` 0, and nothing else.
`pointcontents(v)` returns -1 (`CONTENTS_EMPTY`).

`checkclient()` chooses as `PF_checkclient` and `PF_newcheckclient` do, with no PVS: when the clock minus the time of the last choice (both `double`, 0 at map start) is at least 0.1 (`BUILTIN_CHECKCLIENT_INTERVAL`), it takes `check`, the last choice clamped to 1 to `maxclients`, and looks at edicts from `check + 1` (from 1 when `check` is `maxclients`), wrapping from `maxclients + 1` to 1 and stopping at `check`, for the first that is not free, has `health` above 0 and has no `FL_NOTARGET` (128) in its `flags` converted to an integer; the choice is that edict, or `check` when none qualifies, and its time is the clock. It returns the world when the chosen edict is free or its `health` is 0 or less, and the chosen edict otherwise. It does not read `self`.
`checkbottom(e)` returns 1. `aim(e, speed)` returns a copy of the three slots of `v_forward`.

`droptofloor()` leaves `self`'s `origin` as it is, links `self` (DIFF-5.7), sets `flags` to the integer conversion of `flags` with `FL_ONGROUND` (512) set, converted back to a float, sets `groundentity` to the world, and returns 1.

The step of `walkmove` and `movetogoal` along a yaw `a` by a distance `d` is: `y = (f32)(a * M_PI * 2 / 360)` computed in `double`; `move_x = (f32)(cos(y) * d)` and `move_y = (f32)(sin(y) * d)`, in `double`; and `origin_x` and `origin_y` of `self` become `origin_x + move_x` and `origin_y + move_y` in `f32`. `origin_z` is not written.

`walkmove(yaw, dist)` returns 0 and changes nothing when `self`'s `flags`, converted to an integer, has none of `FL_ONGROUND` (512), `FL_FLY` (1) and `FL_SWIM` (2). Otherwise it steps along `yaw` by `dist` (DIFF-7.6), links `self` (DIFF-5.7) and returns 1. It writes no other field.

`movetogoal(step)` writes 0 to `RETURN` and changes nothing else when `self`'s `flags` has none of the three flags of DIFF-7.7. Otherwise it turns `self` as `ChangeYaw` does (BUILTIN-15.4); computes the step along `ideal_yaw` by `step` (DIFF-7.6), applied only when `angles_y - ideal_yaw` (`f32`) is not strictly between 45 and 315; links `self` (DIFF-5.7); and writes nothing to `RETURN`. It does not read `goalentity` or `enemy`, and does not call `rand`.

Every error writes an error record (TRACE-4.6): a runtime error (BUILTIN-3.1), a host error (BUILTIN-3.2, and VM-2.1 raised by `PR_ExecuteProgram`) and a fatal error (BUILTIN-3.3). For an error raised by a statement or by the builtin it called, the function and statement are TRACE-4.7's, which for a builtin is the `CALL`. For an error the host raises outside any run (DIFF-5.3's and DIFF-5.4's bad movetype, EDICT-8.8's parse errors, `ED_ParseEdict: parse error`, `ED_Alloc: no free edicts` while spawning the map), the function is 0 and the statement is -1.

The message is the error's text: for a runtime error, the message `PR_RunError` is given (TRACE-4.8); for `error` and `objerror`, the joined text of BUILTIN-7.3, not id's `Program error`; for VM-2.1, `PR_ExecuteProgram: NULL function`; for a fatal error, the text `Sys_Error` is given.

After a runtime or host error, when the server is active (from the settle frames on), the host shuts the server down as `Host_ShutdownServer` does: for each client slot in order whose player has entered, it saves `self`, sets `self` to the slot's edict, runs `ClientDisconnect` and restores `self` (EDICT-9.2). Then the scenario ends. While the map is loading the server is not active, and the scenario ends after the error record.

The shutdown's runs start where the error left the VM. After a runtime error the call depth is 0 (VM-19.1); after a host error it is still the depth at the error, since neither `Host_Error` nor `PF_error` resets it (BUILTIN-3.2, VM-2.1). Either way the local stack keeps the slots the aborted functions saved (VM-19.6). Each `ClientDisconnect` run takes that depth as its exit depth (VM-2.3), so after `error` called 30 calls deep its first QC call reaches `LIMIT_MAX_STACK_DEPTH` and fails with `stack overflow`.

An error during the shutdown writes its error record and ends the scenario at once: id's `Host_Error` is then entered a second time and calls `Sys_Error ("Host_Error: recursively entered")`, so the later slots' `ClientDisconnect` does not run.
A fatal error writes its error record and ends the scenario with no shutdown: `Sys_Error` prints, calls `Host_Shutdown`, which runs no QuakeC, and exits.

Two traces of one scenario are equal when their headers have the same version, `progs_crc`, `entityfields` and `numstrings` (`edict_size` and `field_offset` may differ), they have the same number of change-carrying records (TRACE-3), and each pair of corresponding change-carrying records, the `n`th of each, agrees by DIFF-9.2 and DIFF-9.3. String records are not paired with each other; they are used only to read values (TRACE-7.3).

Corresponding records have the same tag, and: run records the same function; step records the same function, statement, opcode and builtin number, or both no builtin; error records the same function, statement and message, byte for byte.

After each pair, every global slot and every field (edict number and field slot) listed in either record's change set has equivalent values in the two traces (DIFF-9.4). A trace's value of a slot at a record is the value in the latest change set up to and including that record that lists the slot; if none does, it is the progs file's value for a global (PROGS-12.1) and 0 for a field (TRACE-3.4).

A value `a` of trace A and `b` of trace B are equivalent by the first rule that applies: if each is an engine string of its trace (a value from outside 0 to `numstrings - 1` with a string record before the record being compared, TRACE-7.3), they are equivalent exactly when the latest texts are the same bytes; otherwise they are equivalent when their bits are equal, when both are NaNs (VM-4.3), when both name the same edict `n` below `LIMIT_MAX_EDICTS` by TRACE-7.1, or when both name the same field slot of the same edict `n` below `LIMIT_MAX_EDICTS` by TRACE-7.2, each through its own trace's header.

The first divergence is the first pair of corresponding records that fails DIFF-9.2 or DIFF-9.3, or, when one trace has fewer change-carrying records, the first record the shorter one lacks. Comparison stops there. A divergence in a run record's change set is a difference in the host's own writes, which are the mock engine's (TRACE-4.1), not the VM's.
A divergence that DIFF-10.1 lists is reported as expected; any other is a failure.
These are the expected divergences between the oracle and QuakeC Studio:
NaN payloads (VM-4.3), the edict header size (EDICT-1.3) and engine string numbers (EDICT-13.3) are not divergences: DIFF-9.4 compares through them.

No other divergence is expected. One that DIFF-10.1 does not list is a defect in `qc-vm`, `qc-edict`, the mock engine or the oracle runner, and is fixed there. A row is added only with a statement elsewhere in `docs/spec/` that makes the divergence deliberate and gives its reason ([`../porting.md`](../porting.md)).
A statement is executed in a trace when a step record has its index. The statements of a progs are 1 to `numstatements - 1`.

The statement coverage of a progs over a set of scenarios is the number of distinct statements executed in any of their traces divided by `numstatements - 1`. It is measured on QuakeC Studio's traces, counting only the records before the first divergence of each, so a statement counts only once both VMs agree on it.

For the report, a QC function's statements are those from its `first_statement` up to, not including, the next larger `first_statement` of a QC function (`first_statement` above 0), or `numstatements` for the last; a statement before the first QC function belongs to none.

Each progs is loaded (DIFF-3.1) and set up as a world for each scenario of the VM differential's corpus set (`qs-differential`'s `runner::scenarios`): the map's entities are spawned and the settle frames run (DIFF-3), and the scenario's clients enter (DIFF-4); no scenario frame runs. A progs that is refused, or a setup that ends in an error in either progs, stops the run with an error. The two worlds are then compared as DIFF-12.3 compares two calls; a difference there is the run's one divergence, and no function is called.

Every function of the first progs with a body (`first_statement` above 0) is called in `rounds` rounds, each from the world as the setup left it, through `PR_ExecuteProgram` (EDICT-9.1). The second progs' call is to its function of the same name. Round `r` of the function named `n` draws its context with SplitMix64 seeded by the FNV-1a hash of `n` followed by `r` as four little-endian bytes, so a run is deterministic (DIFF-1.4). The context is drawn from the first progs' world and written into each world by name: - `self` is a client one time in four and `other` one time in two, else an edict in use; - each parameter by the type of its definition: a vector for a three-slot parameter, an entity, a string, else a float; - with a share by `r % 4` of 0, 1 in 16, 1 in 4 and 1 in 2, each float, vector, entity or string field of `self`, `other`, each entity parameter and, one time in four, the world; and with a quarter of that share each float or string global named in the definitions whose value in the progs is 0; - the server is loading (VM-12.2, BUILTIN-10.1) when `r % 8` is 7, else active.

Two calls agree when they end the same way (both return, or both stop with the same run error message), call the same builtins in the same order, leave the mock engine in the same state (precaches, lightstyles, buffers, command buffer, engine strings, the random source), and leave the same values in every named global and in every named field of every edict in use, with the same edicts free. A named global is a global definition whose name is not empty and not `IMMEDIATE`, taken in definition order; a named field is the first field definition of each name. The two progs must name the same globals in the same order and the same fields, or they differ in their definitions. A value is compared through its definition's type: a string by its text (an engine string's, else the progs' string at that offset), a function by its name, a vector by its three slots, an entity by its edict's number (its bits divided by the progs' edict size, as two progs with other fields have other edict sizes), a field by the name of the field at its slot (as two progs may lay their fields out in another order), and a float or pointer, or an entity or field value that names none, by its bits. When the two progs have the same global and field definitions, functions and strings, two worlds whose global and field slots hold the same bits agree without that reading.
When the two progs have the same statements, two calls agree only if they also execute the same statements in the same order (each with its function and builtin).

The coverage of a codebase is the number of distinct statements of the first progs executed by its setups and calls in any scenario, divided by `numstatements - 1` (DIFF-11.1). A codebase passes with no divergence between the two progs and a coverage of at least 90% (TEST-6).

`cargo xtask compiler-diff` compiles each vanilla corpus codebase (`id-1.01`) with id's `qcc` and with `qc-codegen` with `--opt fold` off and on (QC-27.20), and compares `qcc`'s progs with each of the two. `--fast`, which CI runs on every change, makes 32 rounds; `--full`, which the nightly differential workflow runs, makes 128.

When the two progs' definitions, functions or strings differ, a call's return value is compared too, since the return slot is named by neither. A version 6 progs does not record a function's return type, so the slot's first word is read as a float, a string, an entity and a function, and the two agree when any reading does: the same bits, the same text, the same edict, or the same function. A vector's other two words are compared only through the globals and fields they are stored to. A QuakeC function of the first progs that the second has no QuakeC function of the same name for is a divergence.

`cargo xtask compiler-diff --full` also compares the rerelease (COMP-8): `rerelease` is compiled with the pinned FTEQCC as `cargo xtask oracles rerelease` compiles it, the oracle progs, and with `qc-codegen` in the FTEQCC dialect, with `--opt fold` off and on, and each pair is held to DIFF-12.5's bar. The other five rerelease codebases are compared when a run names them, Dawn of the Machine with `-Fautoproto`'s prototypes as FTEQCC is given it (FTE-1.2), and each joins the nightly set once it passes. Every pair compared adds a row to the results table `target/compiler-diff/summary.md`: the codebase, the oracle's progs and ours, the divergences, the statements executed, and whether it passes; the nightly differential workflow publishes it as the run's summary.

When the first progs is the pinned FTEQCC's (DIFF-12.8), its definitions are compared with ours by these rules, which replace DIFF-12.3's same names in the same order. FTEQCC names fewer globals: `QCC_WriteData` writes no definition nothing uses (`if (def->strip || !def->symbolheader->used) continue;`), no vector component, and no local of a function whose locals it overlaps (`if (def->scope && !def->isstatic && !def->scope->privatelocals) continue;`), and `QCC_FinaliseDef` gives a symbol nothing uses no slot (`if (!def->symbolheader->used) { ... return; }`), so a definition it writes for one is at slot 0. So: (1) the fields must have the same names, as DIFF-12.3 says; (2) a global of either progs inside a QuakeC function's locals (from `parm_start`, `locals` slots) is a local and is not compared, unless it is a function definition whose value is the QuakeC function of its name, as a state's `[frame, next]` declares `next` inside the body; (3) every other named global of the first progs at a slot other than 0 must be found among ours in the same order, the next one of its name, and is compared with it; ours may name more. FTEQCC also gives named constants of one value one slot, so DIFF-12.2's draw leaves out a float or string global whose slot another float or string definition names, or slot 0, for either oracle; the progs of id 1.01, qcc's and ours, have no such global; and it writes a global by name to its first definition outside every QuakeC function's locals, else to its first, for either oracle. And two calls that both stop with `runaway loop error` (VM-2.3) agree, with nothing else compared: where a loop is stopped depends on how many statements each pass takes, which two compilers need not share.

An edict is `EDICT_HEADER_SIZE` (96) bytes of engine state followed by `entityfields` 4-byte field slots (PROGS-13.1). The edict size is `96 + 4 * entityfields` bytes; for id 1.01's 105 field slots it is 516.

The header holds, in order: the free flag, the area links, the BSP leaf count and up to 16 leaf numbers (`LIMIT_MAX_ENT_LEAFS`), the network baseline, and `freetime`, the server time the edict was last freed (an `f32`). QuakeC cannot address the header: field slot 0 is the first byte after it.

id computes the header size as `sizeof(edict_t) - sizeof(entvars_t)`, which depends on the build. This spec fixes 96, the size on the 32-bit x86 build id shipped; a 64-bit build of the same code has 108. The header size is visible to QuakeC only through entity and pointer values (EDICT-1.5, EDICT-1.6), so a comparison with an oracle built for 64 bits compares those values as edict numbers and field slots; the trace header records each VM's edict size and field offset for this (TRACE-2.1).

The array has `LIMIT_MAX_EDICTS` (600) edicts, numbered from 0. Edict 0 is the world (EDICT-4) and edicts 1 to `maxclients` are the client slots (EDICT-5). `num_edicts` starts at `maxclients + 1` (EDICT-1.8) and grows by one each time allocation takes a new edict (EDICT-6.2); it never shrinks, and edicts at or above it have not been used on this map.
An entity value is the edict's number times the edict size (PROGS-17.4): with 105 field slots, edict 3 is 1548. Edict 0 is 0, so the world is the "null" entity.
A pointer value made by `OP_ADDRESS` for field slot `f` of edict `n` is `n * edict size + 96 + 4 * f` (PROGS-17.7).

Turning a number into an edict fails with `EDICT_NUM: bad number <n>` when the number is negative or not less than 600. Turning an edict back into a number fails with `NUM_FOR_EDICT: bad pointer` when the number is negative or not less than `num_edicts`. An entity value is not checked when QuakeC uses it (`PROG_TO_EDICT` only adds); what one that names no edict (EDICT-1.9) does is in VM-11.4, VM-12.5 and BUILTIN-2.7.

Every map gets a new array: `SV_SpawnServer` reloads the progs, which resets every global to its value in the file (PROGS-12.1), and allocates the edicts zero-filled, so every field of every edict is 0 and no edict is free until the map's entities are spawned (EDICT-8). `num_edicts` starts at `maxclients + 1`.

An entity value **names an edict** when it is `n` times the edict size for a whole number `n` from 0 to `LIMIT_MAX_EDICTS - 1` (599); it names edict `n`. It does so whether or not `n` is below `num_edicts` and whether or not edict `n` is free: the array holds all 600 edicts (EDICT-1.4), so id's code reads and writes such an edict as any other. Any other value, negative, not a multiple of the edict size, or 600 edicts or more, names none: id's `PROG_TO_EDICT` (`(edict_t *)((byte *)sv.edicts + e)`) then gives an address that is not the start of an edict in the array, so what it reaches depends on the header size (EDICT-1.3) or lies outside the array. The edict size is the VM's own (TRACE-2.1), so the same edict number is a different value in a 32-bit and a 64-bit build.
The engine's system globals are the 64 slots from 28 (`PROGS_RESERVED_OFS`) to 91, at these slots, with these types:

The only check that a progs puts these globals at these slots is the header CRC (PROGS-3.2, PROGS-5): qcc's `progdefs.h` lists, in order, every global declared before the one named `end_sys_globals`, so a progs whose CRC is 5927 declared exactly these names and types in this order. `end_sys_globals` itself is not a system global, and the engine does not use its slot.

When the CRC check is skipped (PROGS-15.8), the system globals are still the slots of EDICT-2.1, whatever the progs' definitions say is there, as id's engine would read them; they are never resolved by name.

A progs with fewer than 92 global slots cannot hold the system globals. id's engine would read and write past the end of the globals, which is undefined; this spec fixes the answer: such a progs is refused with a typed error when the edict store is set up. A progs id's qcc wrote with CRC 5927 always has at least 92.
The engine's system fields are the 105 field slots from 0 to 104, at these slots, with these types; a mod's own fields follow from slot 105:

As for globals, only the header CRC ties a progs' field definitions to these slots: `progdefs.h` lists every field declared before the one named `end_sys_fields`. The engine never looks a system field up by name, and with the CRC check skipped (PROGS-15.8) the system fields are still the slots of EDICT-3.1. `end_sys_fields` takes a field slot of its own (QC-21.3) that the engine does not use.

A progs whose `entityfields` is less than 105 cannot hold the system fields. id's engine would write them past the edict's fields into the next edict, which is undefined; this spec fixes the answer: such a progs is refused with a typed error when the edict store is set up. A progs id's qcc wrote with CRC 5927 always has at least 105.

The engine reads these non-system fields by name, and only if the progs defines them: `gravity` (scales gravity, `SV_AddGravity`), `items2` (`SV_WriteClientdataToMessage`), and the mission-pack ammo fields set by the `give` cheat (`Host_Give_f`). Lookup is by exact name over the field definitions, first match (`ED_FindField`); a missing field is skipped, not an error.

With more than 894760 field slots, `LIMIT_MAX_EDICTS` edicts of EDICT-1.1's size take more than 2147483647 bytes, so an entity value (EDICT-1.5), a 32-bit integer, cannot name every edict, and id's `PR_LoadProgs` computes `entityfields * 4` as an `int`, which overflows for a large enough count, which is undefined. This spec fixes the answer: a progs whose `entityfields` is greater than 894760 is refused with a typed error when the edict store is set up, whether or not the header CRC was checked. No progs a compiler writes comes near it. 894760 is `(2147483647 / 600 - 96) / 4`, each division rounded down.

Before the map's entities are parsed, the engine zeroes edict 0's fields, clears its free flag, and sets `model` to the world model's name (`maps/<map>.bsp`), `modelindex` to 1, `solid` to `SOLID_BSP` (4) and `movetype` to `MOVETYPE_PUSH` (7).

The map's first entity is parsed into edict 0 without clearing it first, so the four fields of EDICT-4.1 keep their values unless the entity's keys set them. Every later entity is cleared first (EDICT-8.2).

QuakeC may store into the world's fields only while the map is loading; once the server is active, `OP_ADDRESS` on edict 0 fails with `assignment to world entity` (VM-12.2; a pointer made while loading still writes later, VM-12.6). Engine code writes the world's fields at any time.
The world is never handed out by allocation (EDICT-6.1), is never linked into the area tree, and gets physics like any other edict: `MOVETYPE_PUSH` (EDICT-10.4).
